item.title: Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Leads Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Awareness Programme at Solan, Himachal Pradesh
item.description:
An awareness programme under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) was organized today at the Vertex Institute, Solan , an authorized partner of National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology , Government of India (NIELIT) Shimla, in collaboration with the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of Himachal Pradesh.
Shri Sudhansh Pant Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India , graced the programme as the Chief…
item.content:encoded:
An awareness programme under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) was organized today at the Vertex Institute, Solan, an authorized partner of National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology, Government of India (NIELIT) Shimla, in collaboration with the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of Himachal Pradesh.

Shri Sudhansh Pant Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, graced the programme as the Chief Guest.

Shri Divyanshu Singal, Additional District Commissioner, Solan; Shri Keshav Nand Gautam, Deputy Director (SCDP), Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of Himachal Pradesh; and Shri Vivek Arora, District Welfare Officer, Solan, were also present.

The programme was aimed at strengthening awareness among young people about the adverse consequences of substance abuse and encouraging active youth participation in the collective endeavour towards a healthier, safer and drug-free society.

A key feature of the programme was the interaction of Shri Sudhansh Panth, IAS, with students pursuing Computer Applications and Artificial Intelligence under PM-AJAY at Vertex Institute.

During the interaction, the Secretary encouraged students to focus on acquiring industry-relevant skills, strengthening digital capabilities and making effective use of emerging technologies in the Information Technology sector.  He highlighted the importance of equipping young people with contemporary skills and enabling them to take advantage of emerging opportunities in the Information Technology sector.

Shri Pant also distributed certificates to meritorious students in recognition of their academic performance and achievements. He appreciated the efforts of Vertex Institute in providing job-oriented and skill-based IT programmes, including courses in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, and acknowledged the role of such initiatives in enhancing the employability and strengthening the skill ecosystem for young people.

The programme also featured a Nasha Mukt Bharat pledge ceremony, during which Shri Pant administered the pledge to the participating students. The students pledged to stay away from drugs and substance abuse and to contribute towards creating a healthier, safer and drug-free society.

The pledge reaffirmed the importance of transforming awareness into individual and collective responsibility, particularly among young people, who are central to the long-term success of the Nasha Mukt Bharat initiative.

A range of educational and creative activities were organised to engage students and reinforce the message of prevention and awareness against substance abuse. These included painting, slogan writing, debate, declamation and a thematic skit centred on the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

Around 96 students participated in the programme with enthusiasm.

Students also presented cultural performances conveying messages on healthy lifestyles, responsible decision-making and the importance of remaining free from substance abuse. The active participation of students reflected the critical role of youth in carrying the message of prevention and awareness to families and communities.

Representatives from various departments and organisations participated in the programme. Smt Minaxi and Shri Dilip from NIELIT Shimla, along with Shri Rohan and Shri Om Prakash from the District Welfare Office, Solan, extended their support to the awareness initiative.

The programme was supported by the Vertex Institute team, including Shri Subhash Attri, Shri Shashi Bhaskar, Smt Manisha Attri, Ms. Neha Kamal, Shri Kuldeep Kashyap, Ms. Samriti, Ms. Jyoti, Shri Rohit Tomar, Ms. Nidhika, Shri Gaurav and other members of the institute.

The programme concluded with a reaffirmation that sustained awareness, youth engagement, community participation and coordinated institutional efforts are vital to advancing the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

The enthusiastic participation of students and stakeholders provided a meaningful platform for strengthening preventive awareness and promoting responsible, healthy and substance-free lifestyles among young people.

It is pertinent to mention that Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) was launched on 15 August 2020 by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi with the objective of creating greater awareness about the harmful effects of substance abuse and strengthening preventive efforts against drug dependence.

The Department of Social Justice & Empowerment is the nodal department for NMBA, with emphasis on awareness generation, preventive education, youth and community participation, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration.

The Abhiyaan adopts a comprehensive and participatory approach involving government departments, educational institutions, civil society organisations, communities and other stakeholders.

Youth-focused awareness programmes such as the one organised at Vertex Institute, Solan, are an important component of efforts to build informed communities and strengthen the collective resolve towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

***

PR-153- TAR/KV/RK

item.description:

The first tour of Yuva Sangam Phase VII was flagged off from Sikkim University , the nodal institution, on 25 September 2026 , marking the commencement of the Sikkim–Rajasthan exchange . The Rajasthan leg is being hosted by Indian…
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, is organising Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat programme to strengthen people-to-people connections and promote mutual understanding among the youth of India.

The first tour of Yuva Sangam Phase VII was flagged off from Sikkim University, the nodal institution, on 25 September 2026, marking the commencement of the Sikkim–Rajasthan exchange. The Rajasthan leg is being hosted by Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur.

The Sikkim delegation arrived in Jodhpur on 29 September 2026 and is participating in a series of cultural and educational engagements to experience Rajasthan’s heritage, traditions and history.

As part of the visit, the delegation visited Mehrangarh Fort on 1 October 2026. The delegates explored the fort’s historic architecture, courtyards and heritage spaces, gaining insights into Rajasthan’s history and architectural legacy.

The delegation also interacted with Shri Gaj Singh II on 1 October 2026. The interaction provided the young participants an opportunity to learn about Rajasthan’s heritage, traditions and historical legacy, further enriching their understanding of the State’s cultural heritage.

The Sikkim–Rajasthan exchange reflects the objectives of Yuva Sangam by providing young Indians an opportunity to travel beyond their home States, engage with local communities and experience India’s diverse cultural traditions. Through such exchanges, the programme seeks to foster mutual understanding among youth and strengthen the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat and unity in diversity.

***

item.title: AGARTALA MILITARY STATION OBSERVES SWACHHATA HI SEVA CAMPAIGN
item.description:
In continuation with the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, the troops of Indian Army’s Spear Corps and students of Army Public School Agartala, organized a multi-day series of structured educational, creative and community outreach activities from 29 September to 02 October 2026. The campaign aimed to foster deep environmental consciousness, personal hygiene and active community responsibility among young students.
The four-day initiative culminated on 02 October 2026 with an…
item.content:encoded:
In continuation with the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, the troops of Indian Army’s Spear Corps and students of Army Public School Agartala, organized a multi-day series of structured educational, creative and community outreach activities from 29 September to 02 October 2026. The campaign aimed to foster deep environmental consciousness, personal hygiene and active community responsibility among young students.

The four-day initiative culminated on 02 October 2026 with an outdoor cleanliness drive at the iconic Albert Ekka War Memorial, alongside a station-wide Shramdaan (voluntary cleanliness drive) conducted by Spear Corps Volunteers across Agartala Military Station.

 

To embed sustainable habits early in life, APS Agartala featured five structured events engaging students across various grade levels, kickstarting the campaign by designing and preparing colorful awareness banners carrying slogans on environmental hygiene, poster-making activities focused on the central theme of 'Swachh Bharat Campaign', an Essay Writing Competition wherein students expressed their ideas, perspectives and practical solutions regarding cleanliness, public health and hygiene, a Drawing Competition centered around the theme 'Clean, Green & Sustainable Station', showcasing creative visions for eco-friendly military garrisons and an Outdoor Cleaning Drive at Albert Ekka War Memorial, extending cleanliness efforts directly to historic community spaces, paying homage to national heroes through active community service.

Complementing the school activities, Indian Army volunteers participated in a extensive Shramdaan drive across Agartala Military Station. Soldiers mobilized across garrison premises, key public transit routes, residential lines and green belts to clear waste, maintain landscaping and promote eco-friendly waste management practices.

"Inculcating environmental responsibility and civic pride in our youth is as vital as maintaining operational readiness. The active involvement of our students at APS Agartala alongside the dedicated Shramdaan by our troops reflects the true spirit of Swachhata Hi Seva-turning civic duty into a shared, lifelong commitment", told a defence spokesperson on the extensive campaign.

Spear Corps of the Indian Army is responsible for defending the Borders and maintaining peace in the North-East. Alongside its operational duties, Spear Corps actively leads ecological preservation, disaster relief and community welfare initiatives across the region.

***

PS/KMD

item.title: Madhya Pradesh–Karnataka Delegation of Yuva Sangam Phase VII Embarks on a Journey of Cultural Discovery and Youth Exchange
item.description:
The Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education, is organising Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat programme to strengthen people-to-people connections and promote national integration among the youth.
The Madhya Pradesh–Karnataka delegation , with School of Planning and Architecture (SPA), Bhopal as the nodal institute, was flagged off on 26 September 2026 . The delegation is visiting Karnataka, hosted by the Central University of Karnataka ,…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education, is organising Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat programme to strengthen people-to-people connections and promote national integration among the youth.

The Madhya Pradesh–Karnataka delegation, with School of Planning and Architecture (SPA), Bhopal as the nodal institute, was flagged off on 26 September 2026. The delegation is visiting Karnataka, hosted by the Central University of Karnataka, to experience the State’s rich heritage, traditions, cuisine, landscapes and cultural diversity.

A key highlight of the visit was the interaction of the Madhya Pradesh delegation with Governor of Karnataka Shri Thawar Chand Gehlot on 1 October 2026. The interaction provided the young delegates an opportunity to learn about Karnataka’s cultural heritage and the role of youth in strengthening national unity and people-to-people connections.

As part of their cultural and educational immersion, the delegates visited Bidar Fort and Indian Institute of Management Bengaluru (IIM Bengaluru).

On 30 September 2026, the delegation also interacted with Padma Shri Rasheed Ahmed Quadri, renowned for his contribution to the traditional art of Bidriware. The interaction offered the delegates an opportunity to understand the craft, its rich legacy and the importance of preserving India’s traditional knowledge and cultural heritage.

The delegates also visited Gurudwara Sri Nanak Jhira Sahib, where they experienced the spiritual and cultural traditions associated with the historic site. The visit provided an opportunity to appreciate the diverse religious and cultural heritage of the region.

Yuva Sangam is a flagship youth exchange initiative of the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat programme. It aims to promote mutual understanding and strengthen connections among youth from different States and Union Territories through experiential learning and cultural exchange.The initiative provides young participants an opportunity to experience the cultural traditions, educational institutions, innovation ecosystems and developmental initiatives of different States and Union Territories.

The programme is centred around five thematic pillars — Paryatan (Tourism), Parampara (Traditions), Pragati (Development), Paraspar Sampark (People-to-People Connect) and Prodyogiki (Technology). These pillars enable participants to explore the diverse cultural, social, educational, technological and developmental dimensions of different regions.

*****

AM/AV

item.content:encoded:
Ha ka sngi ba rakhe ia ka Gandhi Jayanti, la pynlong ia ki Special Gram Sabha ha kylleng ka ri, ha kaba palat 2.42 lak tylli ki Special Gram Sabha la pynlong ha ka GPDP Portal (https://gpdp.nic.in) bad ka Panchayat NIRNAY Portal (https://meetingonline.gov.in). Kine ki Gram Sabha ki la sakhi ia ka jingiashim bynta kaba shit rhem bad kaba radbah jong ki nongshong shnong, ki nongmihkhmat, ki nongtrei jong ki Panchayat bad ki heh sorkar. Kine ki Special Gram Sabha ki la long ruh ka dak jong ka jingsdang jong ka People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, ha kaba ki Panchayat kin pynkhreh ïa ki Panchayat Development Plan jong ki na ka bynta u snem mang tyngka 2027-28. Ha kine ki 2.42 lak tylli ki Gram Sabha ba kyrpang, ki skhim bad ki sienjam ba prat lynti jong ka Sorkar India, kata na ka Tnat Panchayati Raj; Rural Development; ka Tnat Drinking Water and Sanitation; ka Tnat Consumer Affairs; ka Tnat Food and Public Distribution; ka Tnat Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; bad ka Tnat Land Resources; bad la don ha ka bynta ba pdeng jong ki jingiakren.

Ki Gram Sabha ba kyrpang ki la ai ia ki nongshong shnong nongkyndong ia ka lad ban iashim bynta ha ki jingiakren halor ki jingthmu ba kongsan jong ka sorkar bad ki mat kiba iadei bad ka thain. Ki jingiakren ki kynthup ia ka jingpynkhlain ia ka jingai bor jong ka Central Finance Commission sha ki Panchayat, ka jingshaniah ha ka liang ka pisa tyngka lyngba ka khajna, ka hok longtrai bad jaka, ka jingpynthikna ia ka kam bad ka jingim, ka um dih kaba khuid bad ka jingkhuid jingsuba, ka jingpynbiang ia ka ioh ka kot na ka bynta ki kynthei, ka jingpynbiang ia ka ioh ka kot, ka jingbam, ka jingiada ia ki nongthied jingthied bad ka jingpynkupbor ia ki kynthei ha ki kam pisa ha ryngkat kiwei kiwei ki bynta. La pule bad pyrkhat ia ki agenda bad ki jingpynsngewthuh kiba pynpaw ia ki jingthmu ba kongsan jong ka sorkar, kynthup ia ki jingpynkylla ha ka rukom synshar ba wanrah jingkylla bad ki lad ki lynti kiba pynshong nongrim ha ki nongshong shnong ba la shim ha kine ki shiphew snem ba la dep. Ki nongshong shnong, ki nongmihkhmat, ki nongtrei jong ki Panchayat bad ki heh sorkar ki la ïashim bynta shitrhem, da kaba batai shaphang ki jingshem, ki jingïohi bad ki jingai jingmut jong ki, ki ban ïarap ban pynriewspah ïa ki jingpynkhreh jong ki Gram Panchayat ban wanrah ia ka roi ka par. Ia ka jingpyniaid ia kine ki Gram Sabha ba kyrpang ha ka ri baroh kawei la kyrshan da ka jingpyrshang ba iatreilang jong ki Tnad Sorkar, ryngkat bad ki nongtrei jong ki bad ki nongtrei mon sngewbha jong ka MY Bharat. Ka jingiatreilang jong ki ha ki Jylla, District, Block bad Gram Panchayat ka la iarap ban pynsuk ia ka jingiakren kaba don jingmut halor ki skhim bad ki jingthmu kiba pynshong nongrim ha ki nongshong shnong, katba ka dang pynkhlain ia ka Jan Bhagidari bad ka Samvaad ha ki shnong. Da kaba shim ïa ka rukom treikam jong ka sorkar baroh kawei, u Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary ka atnat Panchayati Raj, ha ryngkat kiwei kiwei ki ophisar jong ka Tnat bad kiwei kiwei ki Tnat Sorkar India kiba iatrei lang  ki la iakren man ka por bad ki ophisar na ki Jylla bad Union Territory baroh shi sngi, ha kaba ki la peit ia ka jingpyniaid ia ki Special Gram Sabha ha kylleng ka ri bad ki la plie lad ia ka jingiatreilang hapdeng ka Sorkar Pdeng bad ki Sorkar Jylla.  Ki sienjam jong ki Jylla bad ki Union Territory, ba la kyrrshan lang da ka Tnat Panchayati Raj, ki bor pyniaid distrik bad ki nongtrei, ki la pynthikna ia ka jingiaid beit iaid ryntih jong kane ka prokram ha kylleng ka ri ha ka jingiar kaba ym pat ju iohi mynno mynno ruh.

People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27 ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’

Ka People’s Plan Campaign, ba la ïalam da ka Tnat Panchayati Raj ryngkat ka jingïatreilang bad ki 21 tylli ki Tnad jong ka Sorkar India, ka pyni ïa ka rukom treikam jong ka Sorkar Baroh Kawei hapoh ka jingïalam jong u Myntri Rangbahduh ka ri u Narendra Modi. Ka Tnat ka la pyntreikam ïa ka People’s Plan Campaign ha baroh ki Jylla bad ki Union Territory naduh u snem 2018 ban plie lad ïa ki Panchayat ban pynkhreh ïa ki plan kiba pynshong nongrim ha ki sakhi sabut, kiba pura bad kiba ïashim bynta lang. Hapoh ka Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, ka tnad ka kyrshan ia ka jinghikai bad ka jingpynkhlain bor ha kylleng ki khyndai tylli ki phang pdeng jong ka roi ka par ha ki thain. Palat 2.55 lak tylli ki Gram Panchayat ki pynkhreh ïa ki Gram Panchayat Development Plan bad buh ïa ki ha ka rynsan eGramSwaraj, katba ka Panchayat Advancement Index ka ïarap ïa kawei pa kawei ka Gram Panchayat ban ithuh ïa ki jingjop bad ki jingduna jong ka. Halor kane ka nongrim, ka Gram Sabha ka lah ban shim ïa ka Sankalp halor ki bynta ba donkam eh, ban pynïaid shakhmat ïa ka Jingpyntreikam ha ki jaka ïa ki thong jong ka roi ka par ba iaineh bad ka jingthmu jong ka Viksit Bharat.

Ki jingpynkylla bad ki jingjop ba kongsan ba la wanrah ha ki Special Gram Sabha

Ki Panchayat kiba la pynkupbor bad kiba lah ban Shaniah ha lade (Ka Tnat Panchayati Raj). Ka Sixteenth Finance Commission ka la ai jingmut ban ai pisa T 4,35,236 klur na ka bynta ki Rural Local Body na ka bynta u snem 2026-31, kaba kiew haduh 84 percent ban ia kaba la ai ha ka Fifteenth Finance Commission, ha kaba ka annual per capita grant ka la kiew na kumba T 400 sha jan T 950. Ka SAMARTH Panchayat Portal ka la pynrung kyrteng palat 57 lak ki nongsiew khajna bad 15 lak ki jaka, bad ka khusnam Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award ka ai ki jingmyntoi kiba haduh T 1 klur. Ki jingkheiñ jingdiah jong ki Panchayat mynta ki bud ïa ka rukom treikam ba don hynriew kyrdan ba la pyndonkam da ka Sorkar Pdeng bad ki Sorkar Jylla, bad palat 2.5 lak tylli ki jaka treikam jong ki Panchayati Raj ki la ïasoh bad ka AuditOnline system. Hapoh ka skhim Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA), la pynmih 3.33 klur ki kard jaka na ka bynta 2.06 lak tylli ki shnong, da kaba ai ram kumba T 1,713 klur kiba la mynjur bad ka jingithuh ia ki kynthei kum ki trai jaka.

Ka Jingioh kam bad ki lad kamai ja kpoh (Department of Rural Development). Ka Viksit Bharat Guarantee and Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), kaba treikam naduh ka 1 tarik u Naitung 2026, ka kular iban ai ka bylla sngi 125 sngi man la u snem mang pisa sha ki longiing nongkyndong kiba dei hok ban ioh, ryngkat ka jingbuh jingtip shaphang ka jingwan bylla lyngba ka Face Authentication bad ki jingai jingsiew lyngba ki lad digital. La pynmih ia ki sngi bylla na ka bynta palat 31.69 klur ngut ki briew, palat 2.81 klur ki nongtrei na kumba 2.23 klur ki longïing ki la ïoh kam ïoh jam, bad ki kam ki dang ïaid shakhmat ha jan 2.31 lak tylli ki Gram Panchayat. Ka jingmang pisa shipor kaba T 93,841 klur ka dei kaba la mang na ka bynta ki Jylla bad ki Union Territory na ka bynta u snem 2026-27, bad ka Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan ka plie lad ïa ki Gram Sabha ban jied ïa ki kam katkum ki jingdonkam ha ka thaiñ.

Ka umdih kaba shngain bad ka jingkhuid jingsuba (Ka Tnat Drinking Water and Sanitation). Hapoh ka Jal Jeevan Mission, ka jingpynpoi um kor ha ki jaka nongkyndong ka la kiew na kumba 3.23 klur tylli ki longing (17 percent) sha palat 16 klur (palat 80 percent), bad la pynpaw ruh ia ka Jal Arpan, ka jingaiti ia ki skhim sam um ba la pyndep sha ki Gram Panchayat bad ki shnong ki thaw. Hapoh ka Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), la shna 12.22 klur tylli ki paiñkhana ha ki ïing bad palat 5.25 lak tylli ki shnong (89.6 per cent) ki la pynbna ïalade kum ki Open Defecation Free Plus (Model). La ïakren shaphang ki kyndon Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 ha ki jingïalang gram sabha, katba ka Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 ka dang kut.

Ka Jingshngain ha kaba iadei bad ka Um (Ka Tnat Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation). Lyngba ka Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain, la shna palat 1.55 klur tylli ki jaka pyndap um bad buh um da kaba iashim bynta lang ki paidbah, bad ha ka jingpeit ia ka jingktah jong ka bynta ba nyngkong la antad ba ka jingpyndap um kaba don hapoh khyndew kan long 2.43 billion cubic metre. Ki kyndon kyntiew ia ki wah ba la pynkylla thymmai ki la kyntiew ia ka pisa sha ka T 22,000 shi hectare ha ki jaka madan bad T 28,000 ha ki jaka lum bad ki jaka ba eh ban poi, bad la pynduna ia ka por jong ka projek na ka hynniew sha ka san snem. Ki kam Gram Sabha hapoh ka Catch the Rain ki la pynleit jingmut ha kaba pynsngewthuh shaphang ka jinglum ia ka um slap, ka jingpyndap biang ia ka um kaba don hapoh khyndew bad ka jingpynneh pynsah ia ka um ba la ialam da ki paidbah. Ki nongshong shnong, ki nongmihkhmat jong ka Panchayati Raj bad ki heh jong ka district ki la ïashim bynta shitrhem ha kane ka prokram, ha kaba la pynïaid ïa ki jingialam lynti ha kaba iadei bad ki teknoloji, ka jingpyni ïa ki video pynsngewthuh, ka jingthung dieng bad ki kam Shramdaan, ha ryngkat ka jingpynïaid ïa ka Jal Shapath. La pynsawa bad pyni ruh ia ka Jingrwai Catch the Rain (CTR) ban pynskhem ia ka khubor ban pynneh pynsah ia kawei pa kawei ka jingjaw um slap bad ban pynlong ia ka jingtreilang na ka bynta ka jingpyndonkam ia ka um ha ka rukom kaba lah ban iaineh.

Ka Jingshngain ha ki mar bam bad ka jingiada ia ki nongthied jingthied (Ki Tnat Food and Public Distribution, bad Consumer Affairs). Hapoh ka One Nation One Ration Card, kumba 3.27 klur ki jingai jingsiew ki jia man la u bnai, bad ka Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana ka ai khaw khlem jingsiew sha 81.35 klur ngut ki nongioh jingmyntoi, ia kaba la pynjlan haduh u snem 2028. Ka National Consumer Helpline, kaba lah ban ioh ha ki 17 jait ki ktien, ka la ioh 3,42,371 tylli ki jingphone ha u Nailar 2026 haba ianujor bad ki 78,477 tylli ki jingphone ha u Nailar 2019, bad ka la plie lad ia ka jingpynphai pisa kaba palat T 105 klur naduh u Iaiong 2025. Ka rynsan e-Jagriti ka la pyndep palat 2.55 lak na ki 2.81 lak tylli ki case bad ka la ïoh ïa ka khusnam Silver Award ha ka National Award for e-Governance 2026.

Ki kot khyndew lyngba ki lad Digital (Ka Tnat Land Resources). Hapoh ka Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme, 99.90 per cent ki Record of Rights bad 97.4 per cent ki Cadastral Map ki dei kiba la pynkylla digital. Ki nongshong shnong ha ki 31 tylli ki Jylla bad ki Union Territory ki lah ban ioh ia ki kot jaka online, bad ha ki 24 tylli ki jylla/UT ki lah ban shim ia ki kot ba la soi da ki lad digital, kaba iada ia ki trai na ki jingpynkylla thok bad pynsuk ban ioh ia ka ram.

Ka Jingai jingtip bad kiwei kiwei ki sienjam ba kongsan ha ka ri

Katto katne ki Tnad Sorkar ki la ai ka jingkyrshan kaba kordor ha kaba pynthikna ia ka jingpynsngewthuh ha ki shnong. Ka tnad kam pohiing ka la pynsuk ia ka jingpynsngewthuh halor ki ain pynshitom ia ki kam bein kiba thymmai, kata ka Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, ka Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita bad ka Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam; ka Tnat Kam Iaterilang halor ka Jingkylla Digital bad Jingpynkhlain ia ki Kam Iatreilang,; Ka Tnat Women and Child Development halor ka Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat; bad ka Tnat Social Justice and Empowerment halor ka Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan na ka bynta ki shnong kiba shngain, kiba koi tba khiah bad kiba lait na ka jingshongkha jong ki khynnah bad ka jingpyndonkam ia ki drok. Kine ki Special Gram Sabha ki la pynskhem biang ia ka Gram Sabha kum ka nongrim jong ka synshar paidbah kaba iashim bynta lang bad ka jingsynshar shnong. Ka tnat Panchayati Raj ka khmih lynti ban pynkhreh ia ki Panchayat Development Plan kiba pynshong nongrim ha ki paidbah na ka bynta u snem 2027-28 hapoh ka People’s Plan Campaign, na ka bynta ka jingtei ia ki Sashakt, Atmanirbhar bad Viksit Panchayat ha ka sienjam kaba kham heh jong ka Viksit Bharat.

Ban ioh jingtip shaphang ki jingpynkylla bad ki Tnat ba Iashim bynta: Shon hangne

item.title: 2.42 Lakh Special Gram Sabhas Across India Put Citizen-Centric Initiatives at the Heart of Grassroots Discussions on Gandhi Jayanti
item.description: On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country, with more than 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas scheduled on the GPDP Portal (https://gpdp.nic.in) and Panchayat NIRNAY Portal (https://meetingonline.gov.in). The Special Gram Sabhas also marked the commencement of the People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana,…
item.content:encoded:
On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country, with more than 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas scheduled on the GPDP Portal (https://gpdp.nic.in) and Panchayat NIRNAY Portal (https://meetingonline.gov.in). These Gram Sabhas witnessed enthusiastic and active participation of local residents, elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and officials. The Special Gram Sabhas also marked the commencement of the People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, under which Panchayats will prepare their Panchayat Development Plans for the Financial Year 2027-28. In these 2.42 lakh special Gram Sabhas, schemes and pioneering initiatives of the Government of India, namely from the Ministry of Panchayati Raj; the Department of Rural Development; the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation; the Department of Consumer Affairs; the Department of Food and Public Distribution; the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation; and the Department of Land Resources were placed at the center of the discussions.

The Special Gram Sabhas provided rural citizens with a direct platform to participate in discussions on key government initiatives and issues of local relevance. The wide-ranging deliberations covered enhanced devolution of Central Finance Commission grants to Panchayats, financial self-reliance through Own Source Revenue, secure property and land rights, assured employment and livelihoods, safe drinking water and sanitation, water security, food security, consumer protection and women’s economic empowerment, among other areas. Agenda and awareness material highlighting key government initiatives, including transformative governance reforms and citizen-centric measures undertaken over the last twelve years, were read out and deliberated upon. Local residents, elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and officials actively participated, sharing their experiences, perspectives and suggestions, which will contribute to enriching the Gram Panchayat Development Plans. The nationwide conduct of these Special Gram Sabhas was supported by the coordinated efforts of partner Ministries and Departments, along with their field and grassroots-level functionaries and MY Bharat volunteers. Their engagement across State, District, Block and Gram Panchayat levels helped facilitate meaningful dialogue on citizen-centric schemes and initiatives, while strengthening Jan Bhagidari and Samvaad at the grassroots. Adopting a Whole-of-Government approach, Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, along with senior officers of the Ministry and participating Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, remained in continuous touch with officials of States and Union Territories throughout the day, reviewing the progress of Special Gram Sabhas across the country and facilitating close coordination in the spirit of cooperative federalism. The coordinated efforts of States and Union Territories, supported by their Panchayati Raj Departments, district administrations and field functionaries, ensured the seamless conduct of this nationwide exercise on an unprecedented scale.

People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27 ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’

The People’s Plan Campaign, led by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in collaboration with 21 Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, reflects the Whole-of-Government approach under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Ministry has been rolling out the People’s Plan Campaign in all States and Union Territories since 2018 to enable Panchayats to prepare evidence-based, holistic and participatory plans. Under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, the Ministry supports training and capacity building across nine themes of local development. More than 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats prepare participatory Gram Panchayat Development Plans and upload them on the eGramSwaraj portal, while the Panchayat Advancement Index helps each Gram Panchayat identify its achievements and gaps. On this basis, the Gram Sabha can take a Sankalp on priority areas, advancing the Localisation of Sustainable Development Goals and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Key reforms and achievements presented in the Special Gram Sabhas

Empowered and self-reliant Panchayats (Ministry of Panchayati Raj). The Sixteenth Finance Commission has recommended ₹4,35,236 crore for Rural Local Bodies for 2026-31, an increase of nearly 84 per cent over the Fifteenth Finance Commission, with the annual per capita grant rising from about ₹400 to nearly ₹950. The SAMARTH Panchayat Portal has registered over 57 lakh taxpayers and 15 lakh properties, and the Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award carries incentives of up to ₹1 crore. Panchayat accounts now follow the six-tier structure used by the Union and State Governments, and more than 2.5 lakh Panchayati Raj Institutions have joined the AuditOnline system. Under the Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA) Scheme, 3.33 crore property cards have been generated for 2.06 lakh villages, with loans of about ₹1,713 crore sanctioned and recognition of women as property owners encouraged.

Employment and livelihoods (Department of Rural Development). The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), in force since 1 July 2026, guarantees 125 days of wage employment every financial year to eligible rural households, with attendance through Face Authentication and digital payments. More than 31.69 crore person days have been generated, over 2.81 crore workers from about 2.23 crore households have received employment, and works are under way in nearly 2.31 lakh Gram Panchayats. An interim allocation of ₹93,841 crore has been made to States and Union Territories for 2026-27, and the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan enables the Gram Sabha to decide works according to local needs.

Safe drinking water and sanitation (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation). Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, rural tap water connections have grown from about 3.23 crore households (17 per cent) to more than 16 crore (over 80 per cent), and Jal Arpan, the handing over of completed water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and communities, was also highlighted. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), 12.22 crore household toilets have been built and over 5.25 lakh villages (89.6 per cent) have declared themselves Open Defecation Free Plus (Model). The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 were discussed during the gram sabhas, as Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 culminates.

Water security (Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation). Through Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain, more than 1.55 crore artificial recharge and storage structures have been constructed with community participation, and an impact study of the first phase estimated groundwater recharge of 2.43 billion cubic metres. Revised watershed development norms have raised funding to ₹22,000 per hectare in plain areas and ₹28,000 in hilly and difficult areas, and reduced the project period from seven to five years. The Gram Sabha activities under Catch the Rain focused on raising awareness about rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and community-led water conservation. Local communities, Panchayati Raj representatives and district officials participated actively in the programme, which featured technical guidance, screening of awareness videos, tree plantation and Shramdaan activities, along with the administration of the Jal Shapath. The Catch the Rain (CTR) Anthem was also played and displayed to reinforce the message of conserving every drop of rainwater and mobilising collective action towards sustainable water management.

Food security and consumer protection (Departments of Food and Public Distribution, and Consumer Affairs). Under One Nation One Ration Card, about 3.27 crore portability transactions take place every month, and the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides free foodgrains to up to 81.35 crore beneficiaries, extended up to 2028. The National Consumer Helpline, available in 17 languages, received 3,42,371 calls in August 2026 against 78,477 in August 2019, and has facilitated refunds of over ₹105 crore since April 2025. The e-Jagriti platform has disposed of more than 2.55 lakh of 2.81 lakh cases instituted and received the Silver Award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026.

Digital land records (Department of Land Resources). Under the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme, 99.90 per cent of Records of Rights and 97.4 per cent of cadastral maps have been digitised. Citizens in 31 States and Union Territories can access land records online, and in 24 states/UTs can download digitally signed records, safeguarding owners against fraudulent mutations and facilitating access to credit.

Awareness on other key national initiatives

Several Ministries/Departments extended valuable support in ensuring awareness at the village level. The Ministry of Home Affairs facilitated awareness on the new criminal laws, namely the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam; the Ministry of Cooperation on the Digital Transformation and Strengthening of Cooperatives; the Ministry of Women and Child Development on Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat; and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, in pursuit of safe, healthy, child marriage free and drug free villages. These Special Gram Sabhas reaffirmed the Gram Sabha as the foundation of participatory democracy and local governance. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj looks forward to the preparation of people-centred Panchayat Development Plans for 2027-28 under the People’s Plan Campaign, towards building Sashakt, Atmanirbhar and Viksit Panchayats in the larger endeavour of Viksit Bharat.

item.title: Department of Telecommunications Launches Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6
item.description:
The conclusion of the Swachhata Hi Seva- 2026 Campaign witnessed the launch of implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 with tree plantation by Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia and a commitment to resolve pending public issues & other related matters.
The Department of Telecommunications is actively participating in Special Campaign 6. During the identification phase of the campaign (up to…
item.content:encoded:
The conclusion of the Swachhata Hi Seva- 2026 Campaign witnessed the launch of implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 with tree plantation by Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia and a commitment to resolve pending public issues & other related matters.

 

The Department of Telecommunications is actively participating in Special Campaign 6. During the identification phase of the campaign (up to 30.09.2026) the Department has already identified targets on disposal of pending MP references, State Government References, Public Grievances (PG), PG Appeals, Parliamentary Assurances etc. The Department has set target to review/weed out 12,513 physical files and dispose of following pending matters:

VIP references: 55

Public grievances: 2270

Public grievances Appeals: 640

The Department has identified more than 450 campaign sites across its organizations/ field offices/ PSUs pan India during the campaign to resolve pending matters. The Department and its PSUs/Attached Offices/Autonomous Bodies/field offices have identified the scrap and e-waste which shall be disposed of during the implementation phase of the Campaign (2.10.26 -31.10.26) to free up office space, generate revenue and foster a clean and healthy workplace to keep employees focused, safe and productive.

The Department is fully dedicated to driving the campaign's success and aims to deliver impactful results and contribute meaningfully to the overarching vision of the initiative.

item.title: Department of Telecommunications concludes Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
item.description: Department of Telecommunications (DoT) celebrated Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign from 17.09.2026 to 02.10.2026 with the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” . The campaign drove a widespread national movement by actively rallying citizens and mobilizing government personnel—ranging from senior officials to staff across the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) headquarters, regional offices, field units, and associated public sector undertakings. Together, the…
item.content:encoded:
Department of Telecommunications (DoT) celebrated Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign from 17.09.2026 to 02.10.2026 with the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”. The campaign drove a widespread national movement by actively rallying citizens and mobilizing government personnel—ranging from senior officials to staff across the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) headquarters, regional offices, field units, and associated public sector undertakings. Together, the Department and its PSUs/field offices organized extensive cleanliness drives specifically dedicated to transforming and restoring neglected areas and designated Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) throughout the country.

 

The Swachhata Campaign culminated on 02.10.2026, being observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas, with Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region planting a tree sapling as part of “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative.

item.title: "Context Matters, Care Matters, Compassion Matters": CEO BHASHINI at MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave
item.description: The Military Nursing Service (MNS) organised the Scientific Conclave on “Digital Innovations in Nursing Practice: Harmonizing Technology with Compassionate Care” as part of the closing ceremony of its Centenary Year 2026 at Manekshaw Centre, Delhi Cantt. The conclave brought together senior leadership, nursing professionals, healthcare practitioners and technology stakeholders to deliberate on the evolving role of digital innovation in strengthening healthcare delivery and nursing…
item.content:encoded:
The Military Nursing Service (MNS) organised the Scientific Conclave on “Digital Innovations in Nursing Practice: Harmonizing Technology with Compassionate Care” as part of the closing ceremony of its  Centenary Year 2026 at Manekshaw Centre, Delhi Cantt. The conclave brought together senior leadership, nursing professionals, healthcare practitioners and technology stakeholders to deliberate on the evolving role of digital innovation in strengthening healthcare delivery and nursing practice.

Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, BHASHINI, was invited as the Keynote Speaker at the inaugural ceremony of the Scientific Conclave, where he delivered a keynote address titled “Wired in Wellness: The Scope of Opportunities of Digital Health in Transforming the Healthcare Landscape.”

General Dhiraj Seth, PVSM, UYSM, AVSM, Chief of the Army Staff, was the Chief Guest for the inaugural ceremony. The programme also witnessed the release of the MNS Diary and the Nursing Research Compendium, along with the e-release of the scientific souvenir titled “Digital Pulse of Nursing: Connecting Technology, Transforming Care.”

In his keynote address, Shri Nag highlighted the transformative potential of digital technologies in healthcare, emphasising that language, context and healthcare-specific data are essential to building technology that is accessible, accurate and responsive to the needs of patients and healthcare professionals.

He outlined the four pillars of BHASHINI and its growing role in healthcare, including speech, translation and other language technologies, which can reduce communication barriers and make healthcare systems more inclusive across India's diverse linguistic landscape.

He stressed the need for medical and nursing glossaries as foundational language resources for healthcare-focused AI systems. While medical terminology requires consistency, patients often describe symptoms in everyday language, and the same condition may be expressed differently across languages, regions and contexts. AI systems therefore need healthcare-specific language data to understand this diversity accurately. A well-developed glossary can connect clinical terminology with everyday language, creating a common language layer between healthcare professionals, patients and AI systems.

Shri Nag also underlined the importance of language in care delivery. Since healthcare communication spans diverse linguistic and social contexts, language, datasets, digital literacy and clinical accuracy are key to the effective adoption of digital health technologies.

He spoke about the BHASHINI Domain Innovation Challenge in Healthcare, which encourages technology-led solutions to practical challenges in healthcare communication. Among the solutions highlighted was an AI-powered voice-to-text tool for OPD prescriptions, demonstrating how speech and language technologies can support clinical workflows and enable more efficient documentation. He noted the potential of voice-first and multilingual technologies to bridge the gap between technology and the realities of healthcare delivery, particularly where communication must move seamlessly between clinical terminology and the language patients use.

Speaking on language in compassionate healthcare, Shri Nag said, "Context matters, care matters, compassion matters, and healthcare, all three become even more important when we are communicating with people in a language they understand."

The discussions at the Scientific Conclave reflected the growing intersection of nursing, healthcare, digital technologies and AI, while underscoring the need to keep technological advancement grounded in the human dimensions of care.

The participation of CEO, BHASHINI, at the MNS Centenary Scientific Conclave highlighted the importance of building digital health solutions that recognise India's linguistic diversity and support healthcare professionals and patients through technologies that are accessible, context-aware and designed around real-world communication needs.

The Scientific Conclave formed an important part of the closing celebrations of the Centenary Year of the Military Nursing Service, commemorating a century of dedicated service and recognising the evolving role of nursing in an increasingly technology-enabled healthcare ecosystem.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, enabling greater accessibility to digital services through Language AI.

item.title: Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme: Empowering Entrepreneurs and Driving Inclusive Growth Across India
item.description: PMEGP, a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) plays a crucial role in promoting self-employment by enabling the establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. Under the scheme, prospective entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance in the form of Margin Money (MM) subsidy on bank-sanctioned loans providing much needed…
item.content:encoded:
PMEGP, a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) plays a crucial role in promoting self-employment by enabling the establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. Under the scheme, prospective entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance in the form of Margin Money (MM) subsidy on bank-sanctioned loans providing much needed impetus to enterprise creation.

Since FY 2014-15, around 8.12 lakh micro entrepreneurs have been assisted with MM Subsidy to the tune of Rs. 24,398.61 crore under PMEGP for generation of sustainable employment opportunities to ~73.08 lakh persons.

Turning Aspirations into Enterprises: PMEGP Driving Grassroots Transformation

PMEGP is transforming the aspirations of ordinary individuals into successful enterprises by providing easy access to credit supported by MM subsidy. It enables first-generation entrepreneurs to establish viable businesses, turning job seekers into job creators.

The success of PMEGP is best reflected in the inspiring journeys of its beneficiaries, who have transformed their entrepreneurial aspirations into thriving enterprises:

Skinkaanti Ayurveda – From Micro Enterprise to National Leader: Founded by Smt. Pooja Sharma based in Parwanoo, Himachal Pradesh, Skinkaanti Ayurveda exemplifies remarkable growth from a modest micro-enterprise into India’s largest handmade soap manufacturing unit. Established with a project cost of Rs. 25 lakh and supported by State Bank of India, the enterprise today records an impressive annual turnover of Rs. 30 crore and provides employment to 300 individuals, of which 95% are women. By blending Ayurvedic principles with modern scientific techniques, the unit has achieved significant technological breakthroughs, including improved manufacturing efficiency and cost reduction, while supplying products across India through diverse retail and institutional channels.

M/s Ess Pee Quality Products – From PMEGP Support to Global Recognition: Established by Shri Surender Pal Singh Nagi in Mohali, Punjab, M/s Ess Pee Quality Products has evolved into a globally competitive food processing enterprise. With an initial project cost of Rs. 21 lakh financed by Bank of Baroda, the unit has grown into a Rs. 38 crore turnover business, generating employment for around 130 individuals. The enterprise manufactures honey, cookies, and fruit jams, and exports to 26 countries, including the USA, Australia, and France. Its achievement of the prestigious AA+ BRCGS certification highlights its adherence to global quality and safety standards.

The success stories of the PMEGP entrepreneurs demonstrate the transformative impact of the scheme in fostering entrepreneurship, promoting scaling up of micro-enterprises and a key driver of employment generation and inclusive growth across the country.

Prospective beneficiaries can know more about the scheme and submit their applications through the official PMEGP portal at: https://pmegp.msme.gov.in/

item.content:encoded:
Infusing  new energy to the call of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for 'Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi' and 'Vocal for Local', Shri Manoj Goyal, Chairman,  Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, purchased Khadi products at Gramodyog Bhawan, Gram Shilpa Emporium and launched nationwide special discount sale. On this occasion, he purchased Khadi and Village Industries products and made digital payments through UPI. Many dignitaries shopped at the showroom at Connaught Place on Gandhi Jayanti. Addressing the media on the occasion, Chairman KVIC Shri Manoj Goyal said that KVIC is making continuous efforts to take Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's call of 'Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi' to the masses and Gen-Z.

Chairman KVIC informed that on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, a special discount campaign has been launched across the country including Khadi Bhawan at Connaught Place in New Delhi. The discount will be available from October 2 to November 16, 2026. During this period, up to 20 per cent discount will be available on Khadi products and 10 per cent discount on village industry products. He further reiterated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Khadi has attained a new dimension. Today, Khadi is becoming a powerful medium to realize the resolutions of Atmanirbhar Bharat, Vocal for Local, Local to Global and Developed India-2047. He said that Khadi is not just a apparel, but the livelihood of crores of artisans and weavers, the cultural heritage of India and a symbol of sustainable development.

Shri Goyal speaking on this occasion said that as a result of the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and Village Industries sector has also made unprecedented progress. The turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector stood at over Rs 1.87 lakh crore in the financial year 2025-26, while more than 2.04 crore people are getting employment through this sector. He expressed confidence that the sector will also achieve the turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore in the coming time.

item.title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar And Shri B. L. Verma Distribute 662 Aids, Assistive Devices Costing Over ₹10 Lakh Distributed To 114 Senior Citizens In Delhi-NCR Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana
item.description:
The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, organised a distribution programme under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital here today.
During the programme, 662 aids and assistive devices, costing over ₹ 10 lakh, were distributed to 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizen…
item.content:encoded:
The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, organised a distribution programme under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital here today.

During the programme, 662 aids and assistive devices, costing over ₹10 lakh, were distributed to 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizen Homes across Delhi-NCR.

The aids and assistive devices were distributed by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, and Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment.

 

Shri Sajeesh Kumar N., Joint Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri Praveen Kumar, Chairman and Managing Director, Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), were also present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar recalled that the International Day of Older Persons was observed across the country yesterday (October 1, 2026) and aids and assistive devices were distributed to 904 senior citizens at Bhavnagar, Gujarat on the occasion. He appreciated the contribution of youth, NGOs and civil society organizations in facilitating such initiatives and supporting senior citizens.

Dr. Virendra Kumar observed that senior citizens often experience difficulties relating to hearing, mobility and vision with advancing age. He stated that the Ministry has decided to expand the distribution of assistive devices to beneficiaries residing in Senior Citizens’ Homes across the country, in consonance with the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on the completion of 25 years in governance.

The Minister emphasized that access to appropriate assistive devices can help senior citizens become more self-reliant in carrying out their daily activities and lead their lives with greater dignity and confidence.

Highlighting the significant contributions made by senior citizens in diverse fields, including agriculture, literature and the armed forces, Dr. Virendra Kumar noted that many elderly persons also face challenges arising from loneliness and social isolation. He emphasized the need for collective efforts to ensure that senior citizens are able to live their lives with dignity, respect and honour.

He called upon youth, corporates, NGOs and organizations working for the welfare of senior citizens to come forward and contribute towards building an inclusive society, in keeping with the vision of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas outlined by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Dr. Virendra Kumar further noted that, according to Census 2011, India has 10.38 crore senior citizens, with approximately 70 per cent residing in rural areas. Emphasising the Government’s efforts to improve accessibility to welfare services, he stated that the Ministry plans to increase the number of PM-Divya Asha Kendras from 109 to 300 so that senior citizens can access assistive devices and related services more conveniently and without undue waiting.

Addressing the gathering, Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, welcomed the senior citizens and highlighted the importance of the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, launched by the Department on April 1, 2017, under the guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister to benefit senior citizens in need of aids and assistive devices.

Shri B. L. Verma lauded the invaluable contributions and sacrifices made by senior citizens in the nation-building process. He also highlighted the initiatives being undertaken by the Department to promote inter-generational bonding and reduce the generation gap, while ensuring greater social inclusion and participation of senior citizens.

Shri Verma expressed the hope that senior citizens across the country would continue to contribute their experience, knowledge and wisdom towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Shri Praveen Kumar, Chairman and Managing Director, ALIMCO, highlighted the performance and efficiency of ALIMCO in implementing the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana under the guidance of Dr. Virendra Kumar. He also underscored the use of Artificial Intelligence by ALIMCO to better serve senior citizens in the coming years.

The programme concluded with the Hon’ble Ministers, along with the invited senior citizens, offering floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi , Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri & Dr B R Ambedkar.

The programme reflects the Government’s continued commitment towards ensuring the dignity, independence and well-being of senior citizens, while strengthening access to aids and assistive devices and enabling them to lead a more self-reliant and dignified life.

The programme reflects the Government’s continued commitment to promoting the dignity, independence, inclusion and well-being of senior citizens. Through initiatives such as the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, the Government is strengthening access to assistive devices and enabling senior citizens, particularly those in need, to lead more independent, self reliant, dignified and fulfilling lives.

It is pertinent to mention that Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) is an initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at providing physical aids and assisted-living devices to senior citizens in need, thereby supporting their mobility, independence and quality of life. The programme seeks to facilitate greater social inclusion and enable senior citizens to participate more independently in everyday life.

item.title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 in New Delhi
item.description:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 as the Chief Guest in New Delhi and presented the Sant Eshwar Seva Samman to individuals and organisations recognised for their exemplary and selfless service to society.
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the Sant Eshwar Samman is a recognition of the spirit of selfless service and a celebration of India’s culture of compassion and responsibility. He extended his greetings and…
item.content:encoded:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 11th Sant Eshwar Samman-2026 as the Chief Guest in New Delhi and presented the Sant Eshwar Seva Samman to individuals and organisations recognised for their exemplary and selfless service to society.

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the Sant Eshwar Samman is a recognition of the spirit of selfless service and a celebration of India’s culture of compassion and responsibility. He extended his greetings and congratulations to all the awardees for their extraordinary contributions to the nation.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the Sant Eshwar Foundation and Rashtriya Sewa Bharati for instituting the awards and sustaining the initiative for 11 consecutive years. He said that by recognising countless individuals who work silently to strengthen society and make the nation more inclusive, the awards motivate others to follow the path of Seva.

Highlighting the timeless Indian tradition of service, the Vice-President said, “Our civilisational ethos has always taught us, ‘Nar Seva is Narayana Seva’.” He noted that the great saints and thinkers of Bharat have inspired people to rise above narrow boundaries of self and dedicate themselves to the welfare of others.

Referring to the goal of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Vice-President emphasised that development cannot be measured only through economic growth, infrastructure or technological advancement. A truly developed India, he said, is one where every citizen experiences dignity, opportunity and hope.

He said that every citizen is a stakeholder in the nation’s progress and that the work of service organisations and individuals constitutes nation-building at the grassroots. Citing the Swachh Bharat Mission as an example, he said the initiative demonstrated how Jan Bhagidari can transform a government programme into a people’s movement.

The Vice-President also highlighted the serious threat posed by narcotic drugs and substance abuse to the health and future of the youth. He recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan in August this year, while Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah launched the Nasha Mukt Bharat 2029 Roadmap. He said that both initiatives are important steps towards building a drug-free India.

Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan called for development to be accompanied by compassion, character and social responsibility, and congratulated all the awardees. He expressed the hope that their lives would inspire more citizens, particularly the youth, to dedicate themselves to the welfare of society and strengthen the spirit of Seva Bhav and Kartavya Bodh.

 

 

***

PR/ASM/VM

item.title: CAQM Reviews Enforcement Status Across NCR; 197 Inspections Conducted in 17 Days
item.description:
The 140th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 01.10.2026 to review enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period 08.09.2026 to 24.09.2026.
140th Meeting of Enforcement Task Force (ETF) reviews enforcement actions, compliance status and inspections across NCR. For more details, visit: …
item.content:encoded:
The 140th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 01.10.2026 to review enforcement actions, inspections and compliance status across the National Capital Region (NCR) for the reporting period 08.09.2026 to 24.09.2026.

 

140th Meeting of Enforcement Task Force (ETF) reviews enforcement actions, compliance status and inspections across NCR.

For more details, visit: https://t.co/HtYWEMQFN5 pic.twitter.com/S2l5uBGLrd

— Commission for Air Quality Management (@CAQM_Official) October 2, 2026

 

During the 17-day reporting period, a total of 197 inspections were reported, comprising 10 inspections at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites, 111 inspections in the Industrial Sector and 76 inspections related to Diesel Generator (DG) sets. The industrial sector inspections included 22 inspections conducted as part of a special inspection drive. Based on the inspections, violations were reported in 85 cases, comprising 8 C&D cases, 49 industrial cases and 28 DG-related cases.

As per the violations reported by the concerned sectors, various enforcement actions have been proposed. These include closure of 4 C&D projects and 1 industrial unit; sealing of 28 DG sets; issuance of orders/directions for compliance in 17 cases, including 4 DG sets; and Environmental Compensation (EC) in 10 cases. Other proposed actions include issuance of letters to project proponents, re-inspection, forwarding of cases to CPCB/SPCB, advisories and other appropriate follow-up measures.

The ETF was apprised of the action taken during the special inspection drive conducted in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh on 15.09.2026 by 7 teams of the Flying Squads of the Commission, along with District Administration and Police personnel and officers of UPPCB. A total of 22 premises were inspected, of which 05 were found compliant and 1 had already been sealed by UPPCB. The actions suggested in the remaining cases include closure of 4 units, sealing of 1 DG set, issuance of orders in 5 cases, imposition of EC in 4 cases, and re-inspection and prosecution in 2 cases.

The status of resumption orders issued after the previous ETF meeting was also reviewed. As on 30.09.2026, a total of 9 resumption orders had been issued, comprising 2 industrial units and 7 C&D sites. State-wise, 1 resumption order was issued in Delhi, 3 in Haryana and 5 in Uttar Pradesh. Further, 1 case was transferred to the concerned State Pollution Control Board for final decision, pertaining to an industrial unit in Uttar Pradesh.

The updated cumulative enforcement status as on 01.10.2026 was also reviewed. It was noted that the Flying Squads of the Commission have so far carried out inspections at 28,744 units/projects/entities across NCR. Based on these inspections, 1,831 Closure Directions have been issued, out of which 1,488 Resumption Orders have been issued after verification of compliance. Further, 127 cases have been transferred to the respective State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) for final decision, while 216 entities remain for issuance of resumption orders.

In addition, a special inspection drive of industrial units in Loni, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh was conducted on 29.09.2026 by 7 inspection teams to assess compliance with applicable environmental norms and directions of the Commission. A total of 21 units/ locations were inspected and all 21 were found non-compliant. The major non-compliances observed included operation of furnaces without adequate stack/chimney and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), operation without valid Consent to Operate (CTO), operation of industrial units in non-conforming areas, use of unapproved fuel including coal, operation of pit furnaces without stack, APCD and OCEMS, non-compliance related to DG sets, and waste processing activities without CTO and adequate APCDs. In some previously sealed premises, indications of continued operation, including sounds of metal activity and/or smoke emissions, were also observed. Necessary corrective action(s) have been directed.

The Commission reiterated the need for continued strengthening of enforcement, timely verification of compliance and close coordination among implementing agencies for effective implementation of the prescribed norms. The Commission also emphasized expeditious enforcement action, strict compliance monitoring and continued inspections across priority sectors, including Industrial Units, C&D activities and DG sets, to ensure effective mitigation of air pollution across the NCR.

VM/GS/SK

item.title: Cleanliness Drive at Kasimedu Fishing Harbour
item.description:
Export Inspection Agency – Chennai (Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India), in association with the Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu, the Export Inspection Agency (EIA)–Chennai organized a Hygiene Awareness Programme for the Fishermen Community at Kasimedu Fishing Harbour, Chennai as a part of the celebration of “ Swachh Bharat Divas” on 2nd October 2026, under the “Swachhata Hi Seva – 2026” campaign of the Government of India.
…
item.content:encoded:
Export Inspection Agency – Chennai (Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India), in association with the Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu, the Export Inspection Agency (EIA)–Chennai organized a Hygiene Awareness Programme for the Fishermen Community at Kasimedu Fishing Harbour, Chennai as a part of the celebration of “Swachh Bharat Divas” on 2nd October 2026, under the “Swachhata Hi Seva – 2026” campaign of the Government of India.

On behalf of Export Inspection Agency- Chennai, Incharge Shri. Jayapalan G, Deputy Director (In charge) organised the event along with Shri. John Becker, Assistant Director of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Chennai Fishing harbour management wing. The officials from both the office and other members of Seafood Exporter Association of India, Tamil Nadu Chapter, students from Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences (TANUVAS), Dr. M.G.R. Fisheries College and Research Institute (TNJFU) and Fishermen’s of Kasimedu Fishing harbour around 100 personals participated in this Fishermen’s Awareness programme. All participants actively took part in the harbour cleaning drive, promoting the spirit of Swachhta and collective responsibility towards a cleaner and safer fishery environment.

The Program primarily focused on;

The event witnessed enthusiastic participation from the fishermen community of Kasimedu Fishing Harbour, who actively engaged in learning about hygienic handling of fish on board and at the landing centres to prevent contamination by pathogens. The session emphasized that the safety of fishery products begins at the landing centres, and maintaining clean and hygienic fishing harbours is crucial for ensuring the safety and quality of seafood.

Maintaining hygiene in fishing harbours forms an essential part of the Swachhta Abhiyan, ensuring cleanliness, food safety, and environmental protection. As fishing harbours are busy areas where large quantities of fish are landed and handled daily, unclean surroundings can cause contamination, foul odour, pest infestation, and the spread of diseases. Regular waste disposal, proper drainage, sanitation, and clean working platforms help ensure that the fish remain safe, fresh, and of exportable quality.

A clean harbour not only protects the marine environment and improves the health and safety of workers but also enhances the global image of India’s seafood sector. The program also highlighted the harmful impact of single-use plastics on the marine environment and the threat caused to the marine animals, aquatic life and eventually to the human beings. Participants were encouraged to avoid the use of single-use plastic materials such as plastic bags, cups, and bottles, which often end up in the sea and harm aquatic life. The initiative promoted the use of eco-friendly alternatives and emphasized the need for collective responsibility in reducing plastic waste at the harbour premises to protect both marine biodiversity and the quality of seafood.

As a regulatory body under the Export Inspection Council (EIC), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, the Export Inspection Agency – Chennai holds the responsibility of ensuring that all certified seafood products are safe for human consumption and meet international hygiene standards.

item.title: CSIR-NEERI Celebrates 85th Foundation Day; Chandrayaan Missions and Future Lunar Exploration Highlighted
item.description:

item.content:encoded:
Nagpur, 2 October 2026

CSIR-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) celebrated its 85th Foundation Day on October 1, 2026, at the NEERI Auditorium in Nagpur, with a series of programmes highlighting India's scientific achievements and the institute's contributions to environmental research. 

Dr. Prakash Chauhan, Director, National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), ISRO, Hyderabad, was the Chief Guest, while Dr. S. Venkata Mohan, Director, CSIR-NEERI, was also present.

Delivering the Foundation Day Lecture on ‘Exploring Earth’s Moon with Indian Lunar Missions’, Dr. Chauhan said that India had emerged as a major space-faring nation, making remarkable progress from its early space programme to advanced lunar and planetary missions.


Tracing India's space journey from the establishment of the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station in 1963 to the development of indigenous launch vehicles, satellites and space infrastructure, he highlighted the growing participation of public and private organisations and start-ups in the space sector.

Dr. Chauhan outlined the scientific and technological achievements of India's lunar exploration programme, from Chandrayaan-1 to Chandrayaan-3. He also discussed Chandrayaan-4, the planned lunar sample-return mission, and the technological challenges involved in collecting, preserving and safely bringing lunar samples back to Earth.

He highlighted Chandrayaan-5/LuPEX, the planned ISRO-JAXA mission to explore the Moon's southern polar region and study lunar volatiles, including water in permanently shadowed regions.

Emphasising that several mysteries of the Moon remain unexplored, Dr. Chauhan said that future lunar missions would deepen scientific understanding of the Moon's origin, evolution, surface and resources, while strengthening India's capabilities in space science and technology.

In his welcome address, Dr. S. Venkata Mohan highlighted CSIR's contribution to building a knowledge-driven and globally competitive India. He outlined CSIR-NEERI's research on key environmental challenges, including water, air quality, climate change, waste management and carbon circularity, with emerging applications of artificial intelligence. He also highlighted initiatives such as NEERI-ZAR for flood-affected areas of Assam, eco-rejuvenation of around 110 hectares of degraded land and research on emerging contaminants.

On the occasion, the CSIR-NEERI Newsletter for April–September 2026 and a policy brief on ‘A Roadmap for Climate-Attributed Economic and Non-Economic Ecosystem Loss and Damage Reporting for India’ were released. Employees completing 25 years of service and those who retired on superannuation between September 2025 and August 2026 were also honoured. Meritorious children of CSIR-NEERI employees were felicitated.

As part of the celebrations, the institute opened its campus to the public, with around 1,000 students from 20 schools and colleges visiting to learn about CSIR-NEERI's research and development activities through laboratory demonstrations.

The programme was conducted by Dr. Shalini Dhyani, Scientist-F, while Shri Prakash Kumbhare, Scientist-F, proposed the vote of thanks.
