item.content:encoded:
Hidayatullah National Law University (HNLU), Raipur, inaugurated the International Trade Law Summit (ITLS) 2026 on 2 October 2026, bringing together academics, policymakers, legal practitioners, researchers and students for a three-day engagement on “The WTO@30: Reimagining Multilateralism in International Trade Law.” The Summit is being organised by the School for Law & Technology and the Centre for WTO & WIPO Studies, HNLU, in collaboration with its academic and institutional partners.


The inaugural ceremony had Prof V. C.Vivekanandan, Vice Chancellor of HNLU delivering the opening remarks, Shri Prabhat Malik, IAS, Director of Industries& Aviation of Gov of Chhattisgarh as the Chief Guest; Prof. (Dr.) James J. Nedumpara, of the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, New Delhi  as the Guest of Honour addressing the gathering.


In his inaugural address, Prof. (Dr.) V. C. Vivekanandan situated the Summit within a changing international environment marked by geopolitical rivalry, technological competition, supply-chain concerns and declining institutional trust. He emphasised that trade has significance beyond the movement of goods and services, as it can contribute to either the management of confrontation or the cultivation of habits of cooperation.


Reflecting on the WTO at thirty, the Vice-Chancellor observed that the international economic landscape has evolved considerably, with emerging economies acquiring greater influence and new questions arising from digital trade, artificial intelligence, environmental measures and global value chains. He framed the Summit around four questions: how multilateralism can be reimagined without abandoning its foundational legal principles; how development concerns can be accommodated; how national policy space can coexist with global economic interdependence; and how established and emerging powers can work towards a renewed equilibrium.
Calling for a reform-oriented rather than merely diagnostic conversation, Prof. Vivekanandan concluded: “I hope this summit will not merely diagnose the fractures in the trading system. I hope it will imagine the architecture of repair.”
Addressing the gathering as Guest of Honour, Prof. (Dr.) James J. Nedumpara, Head, Centre for Trade and Investment Law, IIFT, stressed that international trade cannot be examined in isolation from wider social and economic concerns. Referring to human rights, environmental protection, sustainability and labour conditions, he observed that “Trade cannot actually work in silos” and emphasised that WTO agreements extend beyond trade liberalisation alone.
Prof. Nedumpara further highlighted the need to reform the WTO rulebook in response to emerging challenges while retaining the centrality of the multilateral system and its judicial function. He underlined the responsibility of all actors within the system, observing that “Everyone has to behave like a responsible actor,” and emphasised that “The judicial function of the WTO has also to be maintained.”
Shri Prabhat Malik, IAS, Chief Guest, brought a state-level perspective to the Summit, highlighting the ways in which international trade rules intersect with industries, businesses and citizens at the regional level. In the context of governance and administrative reform, he stated: “Either you improve the rules, either you enforce compliance, or you make the process easy.” He also encouraged students and researchers to examine international trade through the lens of Chhattisgarh and to consider how regional industries and communities can engage with and benefit from the multilateral economic system.
The inaugural session concluded with a forward-looking observation from Shri Malik: “While we might not change the world, we can optimise the processes within ourselves to become a net gainer in the economy.”
The programme also featured a welcome address by Dr. Deepak Srivastav, Registrar in Charge; an overview of the Summit by Dr. Ankit Awasthi; the release of the Abstract Book; and a Vote of Thanks by Dr. Mayank Srivastava. The programme was anchored by Ms Satvika and Ms Prajna. The academic proceedings commenced with a training session on “Mastering WTO Trade Negotiations”, followed by technical sessions and other engagements scheduled over the three-day Summit.
A major feature of the inaugural day was a panel discussion bringing together trade law professors from different jurisdictions to examine the relationship between academia and the WTO in the context of public policy. The eminent professors included Prof. Dorotea López Giral, Director, Institute of International Studies, Universidad de Chile (Chile, WTO Chair); Prof. Poppy Sulistyaning Winanti, Professor of International Relations, Center for World Trade Studies, Universitas Gadjah Mada (Indonesia, WTO Chair); Prof. Vu Kim Ngan, Deputy Head, Department of Planning and Finance, Foreign Trade University (Vietnam, WTO Co-chair); Mrs Varsha Mooneeram-Chadee, Senior Lecturer and Member, WTO Chair at the University of Mauritius and Centre of Excellence for International Trade and Investment, University of Mauritius (Mauritius, WTO Chair); Prof. Victor Saco, Associate Professor of International Economic Law, Maestría en Derecho Internacional Económico (MDIE), Escuela de Posgrado PUCP (Peru, WTO Chair); and Prof. (Dr.) James J. Nedumpara, Head, Centre for Trade & Investment Law, IIFT, New Delhi (India, WTO Chair).

The session opened with remarks by Vice-Chancellor Prof. Vivekanandan and featured Dr. Navneet Roy, Ms. Aditi Singh and Dr. Priyanka Dhar, with Ms. Yaashita Gupta, student volunteer, anchoring the discussion.
The discussions on the opening day set the intellectual context for the Summit’s wider examination of the future of multilateral trade, including development, sustainability, technology, digital trade, governance and dispute settlement. Rather than treating the WTO@30 moment simply as a celebration of institutional continuity, the deliberations placed emphasis on the need to examine how the multilateral trading system can respond to a more complex and changing international environment while retaining the legal predictability and cooperative framework that underpin international trade.
The three-day International Trade Law Summit 2026 continues at HNLU with further academic and policy-oriented deliberations on the future of multilateralism in international trade law.

item.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment takes “Shram Samvad” outreach to industrial clusters in Delhi, Haryana and Uttarakhand
item.description: The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, continued its nationwide “Shram Samvad” initiative with District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes held on October 1, 2026 at Haridwar in Uttarakhand, Naraina Industrial Area in New Delhi and Sonipat in Haryana . The programmes brought together government officials, industry associations, employers, HR and legal professionals and other stakeholders to enhance awareness of the four Labour Codes, employer compliance…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, continued its nationwide “Shram Samvad” initiative with District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes held on October 1, 2026 at Haridwar in Uttarakhand, Naraina Industrial Area in New Delhi and Sonipat in Haryana. The programmes brought together government officials, industry associations, employers, HR and legal professionals and other stakeholders to enhance awareness of the four Labour Codes, employer compliance requirements and key employment and social-security initiatives of the Government.

The Shram Samvad campaign, launched nationwide on September 28, 2026, is a 90-day outreach initiative under which the Ministry is undertaking district-level engagement across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories, with a focus on industrial clusters. The initiative seeks to provide employers and other stakeholders with greater clarity on the provisions, applicability and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes and facilitate effective implementation at the ground level.

At Haridwar, the programme was organised in partnership with SCOPE at the BHEL Admin Building. Around 125 participants, including representatives of industry associations and business establishments, employers, industrialists, professionals and officials from EPFO, ESIC and the Central Labour Commissioner’s office, participated in the programme. Shri Govind Ram, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, provided an overview of the four Labour Codes and the basic employer compliance chain, including establishment and workforce parameters, applicability thresholds and principal compliance areas. Shri Venkanna Banothu, Director of Mines Safety, DGMS, and senior representatives of the Uttarakhand Labour Department also participated.

At Naraina Industrial Area, New Delhi, the programme was organised in collaboration with Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and Naraina Industries Association and was attended by around 80 participants representing employers, industry, HR, legal and finance professionals and other stakeholders. Shri Ashok Kumar Singh, IAS, Director General, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), delivered the keynote address, highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes and the importance of stakeholder awareness, compliance readiness and effective implementation.

At Sonipat, the Ministry organised the Shram Samvad programme in collaboration with Laghu Udyog Bharati at Wyndham Garden. The programme witnessed participation of around 70 stakeholders, including employers, State authorities and representatives from the labour and employment ecosystem. Shri P.B. Verma, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), delivered the inaugural address. The technical sessions included an overview of the new Labour Codes by Shri Minhaz Ahmed, Director, Ministry of Labour & Employment.

Across the three programmes, technical discussions covered the Code on Wages, 2019; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Code on Social Security, 2020; and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Dedicated sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) were also conducted.

Senior officials and representatives of EPFO, ESIC and the Central Labour Commissioner’s Office actively participated in the programmes across all venues. A key component of the programmes was the interactive Question-and-Answer sessions, enabling participants to raise practical issues concerning applicability, statutory compliance, records and returns, employee benefits and implementation of the new framework. The sessions provided stakeholders with an opportunity to seek clarifications directly from officials of the Ministry and its attached and subordinate offices.

***

Rini Choudhury

item.content:encoded:
PIB Mumbai | Mumbai, October 2, 2026

Mumbai Port Authority observed Swachhata Abhiyan 2026 at Grey Gate, Indira Dock, today, marking the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. The programme was led by Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Shri Sarbananda Sonowal, in the presence of Dr. M. Angamuthu, IAS, Chairperson, Mumbai Port Authority, and Shri Ravish Kumar Singh, IRTS, Deputy Chairman, Mumbai Port Authority.

The programme commenced with the lighting of the lamp and floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi, followed by the administration of the Swachhata Pledge. A short film showcasing the cleanliness initiatives undertaken by Mumbai Port over the past year was also screened. The Union Minister and the Chairperson felicitated the port's Safai Karmis in recognition of their contribution to maintaining cleanliness and ensuring smooth port operations.

In a significant step towards sustainable port operations, Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal, operated by Mumbai Port Authority, was declared a plastic-free oil terminal.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Sarbananda Sonowal highlighted the importance of cleanliness in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Swachh Bharat and appreciated Mumbai Port Authority's continued efforts towards plastic reduction and effective waste management. The Minister also interacted with Safai Karmis, listened to their experiences and attended a tea reception organised in their honour. He also dedicated the OSR facilities to the nation.

As part of the campaign, the Union Minister led a cleanliness drive at various locations within the port, including South of 18ID, OSR facilities, the sea-cleaning area, the wharf at BPX North Area and the Mooring Staff toilet facility, reinforcing the message of collective responsibility towards cleanliness.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. M. Angamuthu said that Swachhata Abhiyan provided an opportunity to recognise the valuable contribution of the port's sanitation workforce and reaffirmed the Authority's commitment to sustainable and responsible port operations.

Mumbai Port Authority reiterated its commitment to sustaining cleanliness drives across its docks, residential colonies and coastal areas throughout the year, alongside ongoing efforts to reduce single-use plastic. The Authority reaffirmed its focus on integrating cleanliness, sustainability and employee welfare into its day-to-day operations.

item.title: India and Netherlands Discuss Deepening Agricultural Cooperation
item.description:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, held bilateral talks with Mr. Silvio Erkens, Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, Netherlands, in New Delhi on 28th September 2026.
The meeting focused on reviewing ongoing cooperation in agriculture sector, and strengthening agricultural cooperation by exploring new areas of cooperation. Both sides reiterated their resolve to enhance productivity through modern technology,…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, held bilateral talks with Mr. Silvio Erkens, Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, Netherlands, in New Delhi on 28th September 2026.

The meeting focused on reviewing ongoing cooperation in agriculture sector, and strengthening agricultural cooperation by exploring new areas of cooperation. Both sides reiterated their resolve to enhance productivity through modern technology, innovation and knowledge exchange.

Both sides discussed progress on establishment of 25 Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in the agriculture and horticulture sectors. Further, both sides agreed to explore cooperation in the seed sector though a work plan outlining key areas of cooperation for a clear framework for effective implementation.

In the area of agricultural innovation, both sides discussed identifying potential areas of cooperation, recognising the significant progress and advancements made by both countries in this field.

In addition to the Agriculture Minister, the Dutch delegation included Mr. Marten van den Berg, Director General, and other senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature, along with Ms. Marisa Gerards, Ambassador, and other officials from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in India.

The Indian side included Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Dr. M L Jat, Secretary, DARE and other senior officials of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

item.title: MoEFCC Guwahati organises cleanliness drive at Khamrenga under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign
item.description:

The programme included a cleanliness drive at Khamrenga Wetland, environmental awareness activities and a roadside plantation programme near Sarusajai Stadium, Guwahati.
The activities were undertaken by officers and staff of MoEF&CC, Sub-Office Guwahati, along with staff members of the…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Sub-Office Guwahati, organised a two-day programme on 1 and 2 October 2026 under the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ (SHS) 2026 campaign. The programme included a cleanliness drive at Khamrenga Wetland, environmental awareness activities and a roadside plantation programme near Sarusajai Stadium, Guwahati.

 

The activities were undertaken by officers and staff of MoEF&CC, Sub-Office Guwahati, along with staff members of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), with a focus on cleanliness, responsible waste management, wetland conservation and environmental awareness.

 

On the first day, a cleanliness drive was organised at Khamrenga Wetland, an ecologically significant wetland in the Guwahati landscape associated with Aamchang Wildlife Sanctuary. Prior to the cleanliness drive, Dr. Hemen Hazarika, Scientist E, MoEF&CC, sensitised the participants on the importance of wetland conservation and highlighted the role of wetlands as significant natural carbon sinks that contribute to long-term carbon sequestration and climate regulation. He stressed the need to keep wetlands free from waste, particularly plastic waste and create greater awareness among people for their preservation and restoration. Dr. T. James Singh, Research Officer, MoEF&CC, highlighted the important role of wetlands in supporting biodiversity, particularly birds, fish and other aquatic and terrestrial fauna and emphasised the need to prevent habitat degradation and indiscriminate dumping of waste in and around wetland areas. Dr. Diana Ethel Amonge, Consultant, MoEF&CC, spoke about the range of ecosystem services provided by wetlands, including water retention, groundwater recharge, carbon storage and flood moderation, besides providing important habitats for local biodiversity. Ms. Agatha Ch. Momin, Wildlife Biologist, NTCA, emphasised the importance of individual and collective responsibility in maintaining clean and healthy wetlands and encouraged the participants to adopt responsible waste-disposal practices and promote greater environmental awareness in the community.

 

The sensitisation session was followed by a cleanliness drive at Khamrenga Wetland, in which the officers and staff actively participated.

 

On the second day, a roadside plantation programme was conducted along National Highway 27 near Sarusajai Stadium, Guwahati. Legerstromia speciosa (Ajar) saplings were planted in the vacant spaces along the median row to enhance greenery and contribute to a cleaner environment. The officers and staff also undertook a cleanliness drive at the office premises, promoting cleanliness and responsible environmental practices at the workplace.

 

The programme highlighted the importance of collective participation in maintaining clean surroundings, protecting wetlands and promoting environmental responsibility.

item.content:encoded:
Ka Tnad pathai Information and Broadcasting ka la pynpaw ka jingsngewsih kaba khraw ïa ka jingkhlad syndet ki lai ngut ki dkhot jong ka tnat Information and Broadcasting kiba la duh noh ïa la ka jong ka jingim ha ka jingjia aksiden kali ha Mizoram ha ka 1 tarik u Risaw, 2026. Ka kali kaba kit ïa kine ki ophisar ka la hap sha riat katba ki dang don ha ka kam.

Kiba la khlad noh ki long u Dr. Engam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau bad Central Bureau of Communication, Imphal; u Nampibou Marinmai, IIS, Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra bad All India Radio, Aizawl; bad u H. Lianvela, MTS, Central Bureau of Communication, Field Office, Aizawl.

Ka jingduh noh ia ki lai ngut ka la pynsngewsih jur ia ka Tnad. Ka jingkhlad syndet jong ki ka long ka jingduh kaba khraw ia la ki jong ki jong ki jaka treikam jong ki bad ia ka kynhun jong ki ophisar bad ki riew shemphang kiba trei ia ka kam ai jingtip paidbah bad jingpynsaphriang ia ki jingtip ha kylleng ka ri.

U Dr. Engam Pame, 58 snem ka rta, u la rung sha ka Indian Information Service ha u snem 1994 hadien ba u la pyndep ia ka MA ha ka International Relations na ka School of Social Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. Ha ki lai phew snem ba u la shakri, u la trei ha ki kyrdan bapher bapher ha Delhi, Imphal, Pune bad Shillong, da kaba noh synniang ha ka jingai jingtip ka sorkar, ka jingpynbiang ia ki jingtip bad ka jingai jingtip paidbah.

Kum u Additional Director General, PIB Imphal, u Dr. Pame u la don ka bynta kaba kongsan ha kaba pynkhlaiñ ïa ka kam ai jingtip bad jingïatreilang bad ki kynhun pathai khubor bad ki tnad sorkar ha kylleng ka thaiñ Shatei lammihngi. Uwei na ki ophisar jong ka Information Service Group A uba la shakri slem tam na ka thaiñ shatei lammihngi, u la wanrah ïa ka jingshemphang kaba khraw ha ka kam bad ka jingsngewthuh kaba jylliew shaphang ka jingïakren bapher bapher jong ka thaiñ sha ki kam jong u. U Dr. Pame u dei na ka jaidbynriew Zeme Naga jong ka Tamenglong district, Manipur. U la iehnoh shadien ïa ka tnga jong u, ka Ajuna Pame bad uwei u khun shynrang bad kawei ka khun kynthei.

U Nampibou Marinmai u dei u ophisar jong ka Indian Information Service bad u dang trei kum u Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra bad ka All India Radio, Aizawl. U la long ruh u Chairman jong ka Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC). Hashuwa kane u la trei kum u Public Relations Officer bad ka Tnad ïada ri jong ka sorkar India, ha kaba u la don bynta ha ki kam ïadei bad ki jingai jingtip shaphang ki kam ïada ri, ka jingpynbna khubor ha ki lad pathai khubor bad ka jingïakren.

Lyngba ka jingiadei kaba la slem jong u bad ki kam pathai khubor bad ki jingpynbna paidbah, u Nampi u la nohsynniang shibun ha ka kam ai jingtip ia ki paidbah bad ka jingpynsaphriang jingtip. Ka jingshemphang jong u ha ka kam ai jingtip shaphang ka kam iada ri bad ka jingpynbna paidbah ka la plie lad ia u ban pynsuk ia ka jingai jingtip hapdeng ki jaka treikam bad ki lad pathai khubor. Yn kynmaw burom ia ka jingaiti lut jong u ha ka kam, ka jingshakri ba aiti lut bad ka jingiadei kaba jan bad ki paralok bad ki nongtrei ha ki lad pathai khubor. U la iehnoh shadien ia ka tnga, u khun shynrang bad ka khun kynthei.

U H. Lianvela, MTS, CBC Field Office Aizawl, u la rung sha ka kam sorkar ha u snem 1998. U la don 52 snem ka rta bad u la iehnoh shadien ia ka kurim, ka khun kynthei bad u khun ksiew.

U Gojendra Dey, Driver, CBC, Field Office, Aizawl ruh u la mynsaw ha katei ka jingjia aksiden bad u dang shah sumar ha kawei ka Hospital. U la tip briew bad u don hapoh ka jingsumar jong ki doktor.

Ka Tnad Information and Broadcasting ka don ryngkat bad kiba haïing hasem, ki para ba iatreilang bad ki paralok ba la duh noh ïa ki lai ngut ki heh ophisar ha kane ka por jong ka jingsngewsih kaba khraw. Yn kynmaw da ka burom bad jingsngewnguh ia ki na ka bynta ki snem ba ki la trei shitom na ka bynta ka Sorkar bad ka jingnoh synniang jong ki ha ka jingai jingtip paidbah.

item.title: Architect Riyaz Tayyibji delivers the 52nd Gandhi Memorial Lecture at the Raman Research Institute
item.description:
Riyaz Tayyibji, principal architect and partner at Anthill Design, Ahmedabad, delivered the 52nd Gandhi Memorial Lecture (GML) at the historic auditorium of the Raman Research Institute (RRI) today.
Delivered at RRI by a person of high eminence, typically on Mahatma Gandhi’s birthday, or on some occasions, on the day of his martyrdom, the lectures have become a highlight event in the Institute’s calendar. The lecture is jointly organised by RRI and the RRI Trust.
…
item.content:encoded:
Riyaz Tayyibji, principal architect and partner at Anthill Design, Ahmedabad, delivered the 52nd Gandhi Memorial Lecture (GML) at the historic auditorium of the Raman Research Institute (RRI) today.

Delivered at RRI by a person of high eminence, typically on Mahatma Gandhi’s birthday, or on some occasions, on the day of his martyrdom, the lectures have become a highlight event in the Institute’s calendar. The lecture is jointly organised by RRI and the RRI Trust.

Professor Tarun Souradeep, Director, RRI, welcomed the guests to the lecture. Professor Jyotsna Dhawan, Chair, RRI Trust, welcomed Tayyibji on behalf of the RRI trust and introduced him to the audience.

In his address titled “What is modern about Gandhi's Buildings? Reconsidering Modern Architecture in India”, Tayyibji, who is also a visiting tutor at the Faculty of Architecture, CEPT University, Ahmedabad, said that though most of us are aware of the philosophical and political ideas of Gandhi, very few know of how they affected the built environment around him.

He talked about a project that he was associated with under the Ministry of Culture, the “Gandhi Heritage Sites mission”, that dealt with documenting built heritage that Gandhi was associated with.

Under this project, the team that involved him as the Project Coordinator documented around 20 sites, and the 10-year project culminated with the book “Gandhi’s Places: An Architectural Documentation”.

He went on to talk about his experiences documenting the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, and the Sevagram Ashram in Wardha. “It would be difficult to convince you that this is one of the most modern buildings of the time because the image of the building is vernacular,” Tayyibji said about the Sevagram Ashram.

Tayyibji talked about a fascinating experience he had while documenting the Magan Sangrahalaya in Wardha, where he said Gandhi arguably organised the “first international design competition” to develop portable working charkhas in 1919.

The competition demanded a charkha that was more performative than aesthetic, and though the reward was a handsome sum of Rs 5000, a big amount for the time, due to the lacklustre response, he refloated the competition in 1929 with a reward of a whopping sum of Rs 1 lakh.

He went on to say that Gandhi was someone who used machines in the way a user understands it, rather than a producer. The lecture turned out to be a huge insight into how Gandhi’s buildings gave an insight into the man and his exploration of materiality.

The talk was also live-streamed on RRI’s official YouTube channel.

 

******

item.title: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Mourns the Untimely Demise of Dr. Engam Pame (IIS), ADG, Shri Nampibou Marinmai (IIS), Director and Shri H. Lianvela, MTS
item.description:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting deeply mourns the untimely demise of three members of the Information and Broadcasting fraternity who lost their lives in a tragic road accident in Mizoram on October 1, 2026. The vehicle carrying the officials fell into a gorge while they were on official duty.
The deceased are Dr. Engam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau and Central Bureau of Communication, Imphal; Shri Nampibou Marinmai, IIS, Director (News),…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting deeply mourns the untimely demise of three members of the Information and Broadcasting fraternity who lost their lives in a tragic road accident in Mizoram on October 1, 2026. The vehicle carrying the officials fell into a gorge while they were on official duty.

The deceased are Dr. Engam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau and Central Bureau of Communication, Imphal; Shri Nampibou Marinmai, IIS, Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl; and Shri H. Lianvela, MTS, Central Bureau of Communication, Field Office, Aizawl.

The tragic loss of three colleagues has deeply saddened the Ministry. Their untimely demise is a profound loss to their respective organisations and to the larger family of officials and professionals engaged in public communication and information dissemination across the country.

Dr. Engam Pame, 58, joined the Indian Information Service in 1994 after completing his MA in International Relations from the School of Social Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. During his more than three decades of service, he served in various capacities in Delhi, Imphal, Pune and Shillong, contributing to government communication, media coordination and public outreach.

As Additional Director General, PIB Imphal, Dr. Pame played an important role in strengthening communication and coordination with media organisations and government departments across the Northeast. One of the longest-serving Information Service Group A officers from the Northeast, he brought extensive field experience and a deep understanding of the region’s diverse communication landscape to his assignments. Dr. Pame belonged to the Zeme Naga community of Tamenglong district, Manipur. He is survived by his wife, Ajuna Pame, and a son and daughter.

Shri Nampibou Marinmai was an Indian Information Service officer and was serving as Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl. He was also Chairman of the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC). He had earlier served as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, where he was associated with defence-related public relations, media reporting and communication.

Through his long association with news and public broadcasting, Shri Nampi made valuable contributions to public communication and information dissemination. His experience in defence public relations and broadcasting enabled him to facilitate communication between institutions and the media. His professional commitment, dedicated service and cordial association with colleagues and media professionals will be remembered with respect. He is survived by his wife, son and daughter.

Shri H. Lianvela, MTS, CBC Field Office Aizawl, had joined government service in 1998. He was 52 and is survived by his wife, daughter and grandson.

Shri Gojendra Dey, Driver, CBC, Field Office, Aizawl, also sustained injuries in the accident and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. He is conscious and under medical care.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting stands with the bereaved families, colleagues and friends of the three officials in this hour of profound grief. Their years of dedicated service to the Government and their contribution to public communication will be remembered with respect and gratitude.

***

Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash

item.description:
The Indian Institute of Technology Indore (IIT Indore) celebrated the birth anniversaries of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri on Friday, October 2, 2026, alongside the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, reaffirming its commitment to cleanliness, environmental conservation and community engagement.
The programme was graced by Prof. Kanhaiya Tripathi, Special Monitor, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), and hosted by Prof. Suhas Joshi, Director, IIT Indore. The celebrations…
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Institute of Technology Indore (IIT Indore) celebrated the birth anniversaries of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri on Friday, October 2, 2026, alongside the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, reaffirming its commitment to cleanliness, environmental conservation and community engagement.

The programme was graced by Prof. Kanhaiya Tripathi, Special Monitor, National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), and hosted by Prof. Suhas Joshi, Director, IIT Indore. The celebrations commenced with the inauguration of an exhibition organised by the Centre for Rural Development and Technology (CRDT), IIT Indore, to mark the occasion. Prof. Sandeep Chaudhary, Professor-in-Charge, CRDT, introduced the programme and presented an overview of the Centre's activities.
A plantation drive under the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative was a key highlight of the celebrations. Conducted in the gracious presence of Prof. Kanhaiya Tripathi, the initiative underscored IIT Indore's commitment to environmental conservation and sustainability. Participants also took the Swachhata Pledge, reaffirming their commitment to maintaining cleanliness and promoting responsible practices. Prof. Kanhaiya Tripathi felicitated the awardees for their contributions to cleanliness under the campaign.

Addressing the gathering, Prof. Kanhaiya Tripathi extended his greetings on the birth anniversaries of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri. Emphasising the relevance of Gandhian philosophy, he remarked that only an individual with a universal outlook can truly understand the essence of Swaraj. He also highlighted the importance of self-respect for individual growth and societal progress.

Prof. Suhas Joshi congratulated the awardees recognised for their contributions to cleanliness under Swachhata Hi Seva Abhiyan 2026. Highlighting the importance of cleanliness in everyday life, he remarked that cleanliness is next to godliness and encouraged everyone to embrace it as a personal responsibility and collective commitment.

As part of the visit, Prof. Kanhaiya Tripathi also interacted with Prof. Suhas Joshi, Director, IIT Indore, Deans, Heads of Departments, Faculty members and other senior officials in a meeting that provided a platform for meaningful interaction and discussion on key institutional matters.

The celebration reflected the enduring values of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri, inspiring the IIT Indore community to contribute towards a cleaner, greener and more responsible society.

***

item.content:encoded:
The Office of the Controller of Communication Accounts (CCA), Maharashtra and Goa, organised a fortnight-long cleanliness campaign from September 17 to October 2, 2026, under the national initiative Swachhata Hi Seva 2026. The campaign was conducted in line with this year's theme, “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, with a focus on promoting cleanliness, environmental sustainability and public participation.

As part of the campaign, officers and staff members took the Swachhata Pledge, committing themselves to contributing voluntary hours towards cleanliness and sanitation. A tree plantation drive was also organised to promote environmental conservation and enhance green cover.

To raise public awareness about waste management and civic responsibility, employees took out an awareness march through local areas carrying banners and placards. A mass Shramdaan drive was also conducted at the BSNL Administrative Building Compound on Juhu Tara Road, Mumbai, during which litter was cleared and weeds were removed from the premises.

The campaign was organised under the guidance of Dr. Satish Chandra Jha, Controller of Communication Accounts, Maharashtra and Goa, and coordinated by Shri Khandagale Dhammapal Anil, Joint CCA, and Shri Vishnu Bhanudas Borade, Assistant CCA.

Addressing the participants, Dr. Jha emphasised that cleanliness should be adopted as a continuous habit rather than a seasonal activity. He encouraged officers and staff to sustain their efforts and actively contribute towards building a cleaner and healthier India.

***

Saurabh Khekde/Parshuram Kor

item.description:
Indian Naval Ship Trishul, a frontline guided missile stealth frigate, arrived at Valencia, Spain, on 30 Sep 2026 as part of her ongoing deployment to the Mediterranean, Atlantic and adjoining maritime regions.
During the port call, INS Trishul will undertake professional interactions, cross-deck visits, sporting and cultural engagements with the Spanish Navy . The engagements will provide opportunities for exchange of operational experiences and foster greater mutual understanding…
item.content:encoded:
Indian Naval Ship Trishul, a frontline guided missile stealth frigate, arrived at Valencia, Spain, on 30 Sep 2026 as part of her ongoing deployment to the Mediterranean, Atlantic and adjoining maritime regions.

During the port call, INS Trishul will undertake professional interactions, cross-deck visits, sporting and cultural engagements with the Spanish Navy. The engagements will provide opportunities for exchange of operational experiences and foster greater mutual understanding between the two Navies.

The port call is part of the Indian Navy’s sustained maritime engagement with friendly foreign countries and partner navies. Earlier during the deployment, INS Trishul participated in the 24th edition of Exercise VARUNA with the French Navy at Toulon, comprising professional engagements during the harbour and sea phases. (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2317552)

The deployment underscores the Indian Navy’s commitment to operational readiness, maritime engagement and international outreach, contributing towards a secure and stable maritime environment.

***

VM/AS

The National Academy of Direct Taxes – Regional Campus (NADT-RC), Mumbai, observed the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign with a series of activities on its campus to promote cleanliness, civic responsibility and respect for sanitation workers.

In the spirit of ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’, officers and staff of the Academy joined the drive with enthusiasm to clean the campus premises, and also planted saplings, reinforcing the message that clean surroundings are a shared responsibility.

An awareness skit titled ‘Swachhata Kurukshetra’, headed by Shri Madan Kumar, Income Tax Inspector, was also staged at the Academy. Through an engaging performance, the team conveyed the importance of keeping our premises and surroundings clean, and paid tribute to sanitation and cleaning workers, highlighting the need to recognise and respect their essential role in maintaining public hygiene.

The ‘Swachhata Kurukshetra’ skit team

item.description:

Goa has all the ingredients to emerge as a model of growth, opportunity and achievement, Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said on Friday, describing the state as a place where “growth and glory”, “opportunity and optimism” and “aspirations and achievement” come together.
The minister was addressing the 'Seva Ki Kahani – Atmanirbhar Bharat – Swayampurna Goa' programme organised by the…
item.content:encoded:
Ponda, Goa

02 October 2026

Goa has all the ingredients to emerge as a model of growth, opportunity and achievement, Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said on Friday, describing the state as a place where “growth and glory”, “opportunity and optimism” and “aspirations and achievement” come together.

The minister was addressing the 'Seva Ki Kahani – Atmanirbhar Bharat – Swayampurna Goa' programme organised by the State government to celebrate the spirit of self-reliance, service and rural development, at Betoda, Ponda.

“G stands for Growth and Glorious, O for Opportunity and Optimism, while A stands for Aspirations and Achievement. Swayampurna Goa is reflected in these three words,” the minister said.

At the event, the minister also launched the 'Goa Fresh' brand, describing it as an important step towards giving Goa’s agricultural produce a distinct identity and expanding its recognition.

“Goa Fresh is an important step towards giving a new identity to Goa’s agricultural products,” he said, highlighting the state’s natural advantages for farming.

“Goa’s soil, land, climate and adequate rainfall are extremely favourable for agriculture. Coconut, cashew and spices are the identity of Goa’s agricultural wealth. While Goa is a small state geographically, its potential is much larger," he said and assured that the Central government led by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will leave no stone unturned in transforming the agriculture of Goa and will not allow any shortage of funds for the farmers.

The Union minister also praised the state’s development trajectory, referring to it as “Golden Goa” and saying the progress being made in the state was drawing appreciation from across the country. “On one hand, the BJP government is building a Golden Goa, and on the other, the entire country is saying, ‘Well done Goa’,” he said.

The minister said Goa’s development experience offered lessons for others. “Goa is doing very well, and the world needs to learn from it,” he said.

Referring to the state’s political and development history, the minister said the foundation laid by former chief minister Manohar Parrikar had been carried forward under Chief Minister Dr Pramod Sawant.

“Parrikar ji laid the foundation of Goa’s development, and now CM Pramod Sawant ji has built a palace of development on that foundation,” he said. He cited Goa’s roads, flyovers and governance as examples of the state’s development, saying, “Everywhere here, one can see good governance.”

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shripad Naik, Union Minister of State for Power, New and Renewable Energy, said every section of society has contributed towards the mission of Swayampurna Goa. “For transforming the mission into reality, large-scale employment opportunities have been created, besides the launch of various schemes for farmers, rural youth, women and small entrepreneurs. With the collective efforts of all, we will soon be a self-reliant state,” he said.

The programme, held under the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, showcased initiatives aimed at strengthening agriculture, rural livelihoods, entrepreneurship and community-led development across Goa. Alongside the launch of Goa Fresh, the programme included the launch of the FPO Policy, signing of an MoU between the National Institute of Hydrology and the Directorate of Agriculture, Goa, and distribution of agricultural subsidies.

The event, which also marked the sixth anniversary of ‘Swayampurna Goa’ initiative, also featured the launch of the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme, felicitation of Lakhpati Didis, financial assistance through bank loans to self-help groups, seed-capital support to food enterprises under the PM-FME scheme, sanction of pink electric rickshaws to SHG members and support for integrated farming clusters.

Dr Pramod Sawant, Goa Chief Minister, was also present at the event, along with Shri Sadanand Shet Tanavade, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha; MLAs and officials from various government departments.  

Earlier, as part of Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, participated in a cleanliness drive KTC Bus Stand, Ponda, along with the diginitaries and students of PES Ravi Naik College of Arts and Science, Farmagudi, Ponda.

***

Nana Meshram/Riyas Babu/Parshuram Kor

item.title: Historic First for Jammu & Kashmir (UT): Mining Development Begins with Successful Auction of Two Mineral Blocks
item.description:
In a historic first, two mineral blocks in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir (UT) have been successfully auctioned through the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Central Government’s mineral auction process. The successful auction marks an important step towards unlocking the mineral potential of Jammu & Kashmir and initiating a new phase of organised mineral development in the Union Territory.
The development comes as Jammu & Kashmir continues to witness greater…
item.content:encoded:
In a historic first, two mineral blocks in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir (UT) have been successfully auctioned through the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Central Government’s mineral auction process. The successful auction marks an important step towards unlocking the mineral potential of Jammu & Kashmir and initiating a new phase of organised mineral development in the Union Territory.

The development comes as Jammu & Kashmir continues to witness greater focus on infrastructure, investment and economic development following the abrogation of Article 370. The auction of these mineral blocks adds a new dimension to this development journey by enabling systematic exploration and development of the Union Territory’s mineral resources.

The Government of Jammu & Kashmir (UT) had entrusted the auction of mineral blocks to the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. The successful completion of the auction reflects the use of a transparent and competitive mineral auction process for the systematic development of mineral resources.

Details of the Blocks

Koot–Kapran Limestone Block, Anantnag

Located in Koot and Kapran villages of Dooru Tehsil in Anantnag district, the Koot–Kapran Limestone Block covers 22.43 hectares and has estimated limestone resources of 4.75 million tonnes. The block has been explored up to the G-4 stage, providing scope for further detailed exploration and development.

Wantrag Limestone Block, Anantnag

The Wantrag Limestone Block covers 5.36 hectares and has estimated limestone resources of 10.853 million tonnes. The block has been explored up to the G-3 stage, including 159 metres of drilling, providing an important geological basis for further exploration and development.

The auction of the two limestone blocks is expected to catalyse new investment and economic activity in the Union Territory. As mining and associated activities develop, they are expected to generate a large number of direct and indirect employment opportunities and create avenues for local businesses, entrepreneurs, service providers and allied industries.

The development of the mineral sector will also contribute to greater value creation from Jammu & Kashmir’s mineral resources and support new opportunities for local participation in the emerging mining ecosystem. This marks another step towards strengthening the economic foundations of a Viksit Jammu & Kashmir.

The Ministry of Mines will continue to work in coordination with the Government of Jammu & Kashmir to facilitate transparent, sustainable and responsible development of the Union Territory’s mineral resources.

***

Prajith Kumar MV

item.title: Union Tribal Affairs Minister Shri Jual Oram Interacts with Students at Eklavya Model Residential School, Bazpur; Emphasises Development of the School as a Centre of Excellence
item.description:
Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram participated in cleanliness and awareness activities with students at the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS), Bazpur, in Udham Singh Nagar district of Uttarakhand on Friday.
On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, the Union Minister paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. He thereafter participated in a cleanliness drive organised in the school premises along with students, teachers and…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram participated in cleanliness and awareness activities with students at the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS), Bazpur, in Udham Singh Nagar district of Uttarakhand on Friday.

On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, the Union Minister paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. He thereafter participated in a cleanliness drive organised in the school premises along with students, teachers and members of the local community and administered the cleanliness pledge. He also planted a sapling under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative.

Interacting with the students, Shri Jual Oram emphasised the importance of maintaining cleanliness in the school, hostel and surrounding areas. He sensitised the students towards cleanliness, environmental conservation and responsible citizenship and called upon them to encourage positive behavioural change in their families and villages as well. He said that cleanliness is not merely an activity but a value to be adopted throughout life, contributing significantly to better health, dignity, environmental protection and sustainable development.

During the programme, the Union Minister held an interaction with the students and enquired about their studies, interests and future aspirations. He encouraged them to study diligently and strive to achieve their goals. Shri Oram also visited exhibitions and displays prepared by the students on waste management, waste segregation, sustainable development and environmental conservation, and appreciated their efforts.

Addressing the students, the Union Minister said that children possess immense talent and that providing them with quality education, adequate resources and sufficient opportunities to progress is a shared responsibility of the Government and society. He said that ensuring quality education, better facilities and equal opportunities for children from tribal areas and connecting them with the mainstream of development is a priority of the Government.

Shri Jual Oram said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Central Government is continuously working to strengthen the quality of education and facilities in remote and tribal areas and to provide better opportunities to children and youth. He said that the endeavour is to enable talented children from tribal communities to achieve new heights in education and play an important role in nation-building.

The Union Minister said that efforts would be made to equip Eklavya Model Residential School, Bazpur, with the necessary facilities and resources and develop it as a centre of excellence. He emphasised creating an academic environment in the school that, in terms of facilities and educational quality, moves towards the standards of reputed institutions such as Sainik Schools and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.

Shri Oram urged the students to adopt responsible behaviour in their daily lives and actively contribute to building a clean and healthy nation. He said that inculcating the values of cleanliness, environmental conservation and civic responsibility among tribal students is an important step towards strengthening the collective resolve of ‘Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’.

He said that inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of transforming cleanliness into a nationwide people’s movement and the vision of ‘Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’, the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ campaign is promoting cleanliness, environmental conservation and public participation across the country.

Students, teachers, school staff and representatives of the local community participated enthusiastically in the programme. Various activities relating to personal hygiene, waste segregation, environmental awareness and public participation were promoted during the event. The programme also demonstrated the ‘Whole-of-Government’ approach and community participation in the cleanliness campaign.

The Union Minister inspected the cleanliness and arrangements at the school premises and held discussions with officials and public representatives on various issues related to the development of the school. District Magistrate, Udham Singh Nagar, Shri Nitin Singh Bhadauria, Chief Development Officer Shri Divesh Shashani, officials of the district administration, representatives of the State Government, the Principal, teachers and staff of the school, and representatives of the local community were present on the occasion.

The visit of the Union Minister for Tribal Affairs to Uttarakhand is providing an opportunity for interaction with local stakeholders and officials on issues related to tribal education and welfare through Eklavya Model Residential Schools. During his visit, the Minister is also participating in various programmes related to senior citizens’ welfare, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and tribal education.

Shri Jual Oram is on a four-day visit to Uttarakhand. During the visit, he will participate in various programmes and also attend the Uttarakhand Aadi Rangotsav.

item.title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches 'Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0' Across Personnel, Science & Technology and Earth Sciences Ministries, Expanding Swachhata into a Wider Movement of Efficiency and Resource Management
item.description: Swachhata has evolved from an appeal for cleanliness into a sustained culture of good governance, efficient utilisation of public resources, reduction of pendency and responsible management of waste, said Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, While launching the Implementation…
item.content:encoded:
Swachhata has evolved from an appeal for cleanliness into a sustained culture of good governance, efficient utilisation of public resources, reduction of pendency and responsible management of waste, said Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, While launching the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 today.

Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for Swachhata from the Red Fort in 2014, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the initiative gradually transformed into a people’s movement and subsequently became an institutional practice across Government offices. He said the campaign has continuously acquired new dimensions, from toilets and cleanliness to disposal of old files, redundant furniture, e-files and electronic scrap, thereby linking Swachhata with administrative efficiency, optimum use of public space and productive management of resources.

Dr. Jitendra Singh began the day by participating in the launch activities of Special Campaign 6.0 at the venue designated by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). He participated in Shramdaan, plantation under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, and the symbolic commencement of weeding out old records, besides honouring Safai Mitras by distributing safety kits and sweets.

Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG; Smt. Rachna Shah, Secretary, DoPT; and Dr. Surendrakumar Bagde, Director General, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), were among the senior officers present. DARPG is the nodal department for the Special Campaign.

The Minister thereafter proceeded to CSIR Headquarters, where he took forward Special Campaign 6.0 across the scientific and technological ecosystem. Dr. Jitendra Singh led a mass cleanliness drive, participated in the Swachhata Signature Campaign and plantation drive, and felicitated Safai Mitras. Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR; Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology (DST); and Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), along with senior officials from DST, DBT and CSIR, participated in the programme. The activities at CSIR included review and disposal of obsolete records and scrap, workplace improvement and effective management of office spaces, with emphasis on Jan Bhagidari.

Speaking during the launch activities, Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled how the Swachhata movement, after its initial focus on sanitation, gradually entered Government offices and addressed the large accumulation of files and records that were no longer required but continued to occupy valuable space. He recalled that the exercise subsequently evolved into a dedicated annual campaign from 2 October to 31 October, with each successive campaign adding new dimensions. From physical files and discarded furniture, the exercise has expanded to e-files and e-scrap, reflecting the changing nature of Government workplaces and the growing need for responsible management of electronic assets.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the experience of the Special Campaigns has demonstrated that systematic disposal of redundant material can create both financial value for the public exchequer and usable space for Government offices. Over the last five years, ₹5,102.91 crore has been generated through disposal of e-waste and scrap, while more than 1,049.54 lakh square feet of office space has been cleared and put to productive use. More than 180.48 lakh files have also been closed or weeded out and 24.20 lakh cleanliness sites identified and cleaned across the country.

The Minister said the space released through the campaign can subsequently be put to productive use, including creation of green areas and restoration of spaces that had remained blocked or underutilised. He said the annual campaign serves as a renewed commitment to a practice that should continue throughout the year, while the repeated campaigns have helped make Swachhata part of the working culture of Government institutions.

The Minister subsequently visited the Ministry of Earth Sciences, where e-waste and obsolete equipment from Prithvi Bhavan and Mausam Bhavan were taken up for disposal under Special Campaign 6.0. Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, was present during the programme and briefed the Minister on the items identified for disposal.

The inventory comprises 705 items in all. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the exercise at the Ministry of Earth Sciences is part of a wider campaign across the scientific ecosystem, with similar activities being undertaken by institutions under Earth Sciences, CSIR and DST. He said more than 100 science institutions have commenced the campaign from 2 October, taking the message of Swachhata and responsible disposal of obsolete material across the country's scientific institutions.

The Minister also connected the campaign with the larger Waste-to-Wealth dimension of India's scientific ecosystem, where the objective goes beyond disposal of waste to developing technologies that can convert waste into useful products, materials, energy and new economic opportunities. The CSIR portfolio includes technologies for municipal solid-waste management, recycling of plastic waste, recovery of critical metals and rare earth elements from e-waste, recycling of lithium-ion batteries, biomethanation, conversion of agro-waste into biodegradable products, wastewater resource recovery and utilisation of industrial waste for value-added products. These technologies have been transferred to industry and other organisations for application and further development.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the experience of Special Campaigns demonstrates how a cleanliness initiative can progressively become an instrument of administrative reform, resource optimisation and institutional efficiency. In the scientific ecosystem, this approach is being extended further through technologies that enable waste to move through a larger value chain, from identification and disposal to recovery, recycling, innovation and wealth creation.

The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 will run from 2 October to 31 October 2026, following the preparatory phase undertaken by Ministries and Departments during September. The campaign focuses on Swachhata, reduction of pendency, review and weeding of records, efficient utilisation of office space, scientific disposal of e-waste and redundant material, and improved record management across Government offices. The campaign is being implemented as a whole-of-government effort, with institutional goals across Ministries and Departments.

***

 

NKR/AK

item.title: Robotics to Become an Accelerating Tool in Every Specialty of Medicine: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
item.description:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, who is also a noted Physician and diabetologist, today said robotics is set to become an accelerating tool in every specialty of medicine, covering diagnostics as well as treatment and therapy.
He said robotics, together with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and nanoscience, would create a…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, who is also a noted Physician and diabetologist, today said robotics is set to become an accelerating tool in every specialty of medicine, covering diagnostics as well as treatment and therapy.

He said robotics, together with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and nanoscience, would create a larger ecosystem for precision health delivery and precision medicine, with emerging technologies enabling increasingly personalised healthcare based on an individual’s genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns.

Dr. Jitendra Singh was delivering inaugural address at the International Conference of the "Society of Robotic Surgery" here. He said robotics should not be viewed as a technology confined to surgery but as a tool that would increasingly become part of different branches of medicine. “It’s a tool. It will happen everywhere,” he said, adding that while the present conference is focused on robotic surgery, the future could see the emergence of robotic medicine, robotic endocrinology and robotic cardiology, just as AI is finding applications across different medical specialties.

The Minister said medicine is entering an exciting phase of frontier practices, with the 21st century witnessing the emergence of AI, biotechnology, nuclear medicine and other technology-driven solutions. He said the next phase would see greater application of genetically driven diagnostic solutions, alongside advances in quantum technologies, nanomedicine and robotics.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said precision medicine would increasingly require treatment approaches tailored to individual patients, even when they are diagnosed with the same disease. Genetic profile, environmental conditions, lifestyle and dietary patterns, he said, would increasingly shape medical decision-making, making technology-enabled and personalised healthcare an important part of the future of medicine.

Referring to the Genome India Programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said 10,000 individuals have already been sequenced and expressed the hope that India could eventually move towards gene sequencing for every newborn. He said undertaking such detailed genetic sequencing for a population of 1.4 billion would require the optimal use of AI and robotics.

The Minister also spoke about the potential of nanomedicine in addressing longstanding healthcare challenges. Referring to efforts towards developing oral insulin, he said advances at the nano level could help overcome limitations associated with conventional drug delivery and open new possibilities for therapeutic interventions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s size, diversity and geographical spread make technologies such as AI, robotics and tele-robotics particularly relevant for healthcare delivery. Sharing his experience with robotic ultrasonography, he said he had performed an ultrasound on a person located 10,000 kilometres away in Antarctica, demonstrating the possibilities of remotely enabled medical technologies.

Describing the potential transformation in the traditional model of specialist healthcare, Dr. Jitendra Singh said, “Instead of the patient being referred to the doctor, it will be the doctor being referred to the patient.” He said tele-robotics could enable specialist expertise to reach patients across geographical boundaries, allowing advanced medical capabilities to be delivered without the patient necessarily having to travel to the specialist.

The Minister also spoke about India’s evolving disease profile, where infectious diseases continue to coexist with metabolic and lifestyle-related disorders. He said diseases traditionally associated with later stages of life are increasingly being seen among younger people, creating a complex healthcare landscape that requires both advanced technological tools and a more integrated and holistic approach.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the scale and diversity of India’s healthcare requirements make the adoption of new technologies particularly important. AI and robotics can serve as powerful facilitatory tools for health delivery across the country, while also supporting the transition towards precision and personalised medicine.

Dr. Jitendra Singh congratulated the organisers of SRS India 2026 for bringing robotic surgery into the domain of institutional learning, academics and professional conference platforms. He said the adoption of emerging technologies such as robotics would be essential to keep pace with the rapidly evolving landscape of medical science.

***

 

NKR/AK

item.title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Leads Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam Tree Plantation Drive At Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation; Hon’ble Minister Of State For Social Justice And Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma Joins The Drive
item.description:
As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign , the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment organised a tree plantation activity under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative at the Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation (BJRNF) in National Capital here today.
The plantation drive was led by Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, in the presence of Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and…
item.content:encoded:
As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment organised a tree plantation activity under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative at the Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation (BJRNF) in National Capital here today.

The plantation drive was led by Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, in the presence of Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Dr. Virendra Kumar led the tree plantation activity along with officials of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation.

Drawing a parallel between the nurturing of nature by Mother Earth and the nurturing of human life by mothers, Dr Kumar emphasised the importance of protecting and nurturing the environment.

The Officers and officials of the Ministry and BJRNF actively participated in the plantation drive, reaffirming their collective commitment towards environmental conservation and the creation of a clean and green environment.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Virendra Kumar highlighted the vision behind the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam initiative, which was initiated by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Dr. Virendra Kumar called upon all participants to contribute towards keeping Mother Earth Clean And Healthy, emphasising that collective efforts towards environmental conservation will help create a healthier and more sustainable environment for generations to come.

On the occasion, Dr. Virendra Kumar and Shri B. L. Verma paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. The dignitaries also paid their respects to Babu Jagjivan Ram.

Dr Virendra Kumar also administered a pledge to the officers and participants to contribute towards a clean and green environment.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the plantation drive reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and the broader vision of Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

He said the initiative also highlights the importance of nurturing urban green spaces and encouraging collective participation in environmental conservation.

The Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam plantation activity reinforces the message of environmental responsibility and sustainable development, while encouraging citizens and institutions to contribute towards building a cleaner, greener and healthier India.

***

PR-151-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.title: Department of Health and Family Welfare Launches Special Campaign 6 to Institutionalise Swachhata, Reduce Pendency and Strengthen Citizen-Centric Governance
item.description:
The Department of Health and Family Welfare (DoHFW), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, has commenced implementation of Special Campaign 6 from October 2, 2026, across its Central Government Hospitals, Attached and Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Bodies, CPSUs and other organisations. The campaign will continue till October 31, 2026, with a focus on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency and promoting efficient and citizen-centric governance.
The campaign, spearheaded by…
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Health and Family Welfare (DoHFW), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, has commenced implementation of Special Campaign 6 from October 2, 2026, across its Central Government Hospitals, Attached and Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Bodies, CPSUs and other organisations. The campaign will continue till October 31, 2026, with a focus on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency and promoting efficient and citizen-centric governance.

The campaign, spearheaded by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), aims to promote cleanliness and improve workplace efficiency while ensuring timely disposal of pending matters. Under Special Campaign 6, DoHFW has set comprehensive targets covering cleanliness, disposal of records and unserviceable items, review of files, resolution of public grievances and simplification of rules and processes.

As part of the cleanliness campaign, 2,017 sites have been identified across various offices and institutions under DoHFW for cleanliness activities. The initiative is aimed at creating cleaner, more organised and hygienic workplaces. Special emphasis is also being placed on the identification and disposal of e-waste and unserviceable items. Besides ensuring responsible disposal, the exercise is expected to generate revenue and release valuable office space for productive use.

 

 

Office of Assistant Drugs Controller (India), CDSCO, JNPT Sea Port, Panvel

Cleanliness activities under the campaign are being undertaken across institutions and offices of the Department. These include the Office of the Assistant Drugs Controller (India), CDSCO, JNPT Sea Port, Panvel; Central Health Education Bureau (CHEB), Delhi; Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh; and International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, among others.

 

Central Health Education Bureau (CHEB), Delhi

To address pendency and strengthen responsive governance, a number of public grievances and associated appeals have been earmarked for prompt resolution under the campaign. The exercise seeks to ensure timely disposal of grievances and reinforce transparent and citizen-centric administration.

Further, 60,012 physical files and 10,020 e-files have been identified for review. The review is aimed at reducing unnecessary records, improving record management and streamlining office functioning.

 

Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh

In addition, 12 rules/processes have been identified for simplification with a view to removing procedural bottlenecks, improving efficiency and promoting ease of governance.

Through Special Campaign 6, the Department of Health and Family Welfare is undertaking a coordinated effort towards cleaner workplaces, effective record management, reduction of pendency, simplification of processes and responsive administration.

   

Cleanliness drive at International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai

The Department reaffirms its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, enhancing administrative efficiency and strengthening citizen-centric service delivery across its offices and institutions.

*****

SR

HFW/ DoHFW commenced Special Campaign 6 /02 October 2026/1

item.title: PRIME MINISTER AND LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAY TRIBUTES TO MAHATMA GANDHI AND SHRI LAL BAHADUR SHASTRI
item.description: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi; Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla; Union Minister of Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh; Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda; Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju; Leader of the Opposition in Rajya Sabha Shri Mallikarjun Kharge; Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Shri Rahul Gandhi; Shri Nitin Nabin, MP; Members of Parliament, former Members, and other…
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi; Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla; Union Minister of Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh; Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda; Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju; Leader of the Opposition in Rajya Sabha Shri Mallikarjun Kharge; Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Shri Rahul Gandhi; Shri Nitin Nabin, MP; Members of Parliament, former Members, and other dignitaries paid floral tributes at the portraits of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, on the occasion of their birth anniversaries, in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan today.

Secretary-General of Lok Sabha Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and Secretary-General of Rajya Sabha Shri P.C. Mody also paid floral tributes on the occasion.

On this occasion, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla, addressing students from different parts of the country in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan as part of the ‘Know Your Leader’ Programme, called upon the youth to draw inspiration from the lives, ideals, and public service of Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, and to contribute with determination, discipline, and a strong sense of responsibility toward building a developed India.

Welcoming the young participants, the Speaker said that their presence in the historic Central Hall was an opportunity to connect with India's democratic and constitutional heritage. Mentioning Mahatma Gandhi, he noted that his life demonstrated the power of truth, morality, non-violence, and Satyagraha. At a time when much of the world was under colonial rule, Mahatma Gandhi showed that a movement based on truth and non-violence could give direction to the struggle for freedom. His ideas and philosophy subsequently inspired movements for freedom and justice across the world. Invoking the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, he urged the youth to study his life and ideas, saying that the more one understands his life and philosophy, the more one gains insight, courage, and a new perspective to face adversity and challenges. He said that Mahatma Gandhi's life teaches that even through simple means, lasting change can be brought about in the lives and minds of people. Self-reflection, discipline, perseverance, and firmness of purpose were integral to his life and remain relevant for the youth today.

Referring to former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, Shri Birla highlighted his simplicity, honesty, high ideals, sense of duty, and firmness in decision-making. He recalled Shastriji’s inspiring call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan”, which gave direction to the nation during a challenging period and underlined the importance of national and food security. he said that although today's youth have access to technology, knowledge, and enormous resources, these alone cannot ensure the achievement of one's goals. Patience, ethical conduct, discipline, determination, and continuity of effort are equally essential. He called upon the youth to remain steadfast in their goals and not allow disappointment, fatigue, or setbacks to weaken their resolve. He stated that social responsibility must remain at the heart of the youth's journey and that their aim should be not merely personal achievement, but also contributing to the development and progress of the country. He urged them to use their knowledge, energy, and capabilities to help build and lead a new and developed India.

Concluding his address, Shri Birla called upon the participants to carry the message and inspiration of the programme to their schools, communities, and wherever they go. He said that they should leave the historic Constituent Assembly Hall with new inspiration, energy, and confidence, and with a renewed commitment to fulfill their duties and contribute to nation-building.

More than 500 school students from different parts of the country participated in the programme and witnessed the floral tributes paid to Mahatma Gandhi and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri in the historic Constituent Assembly Hall. Thirty-six selected young participants also spoke on the lives, ideals, thoughts, and contributions of the two national leaders, sharing their understanding of how their lives continue to inspire generations in India and across the world.

Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha Speaker also visited Rajghat and Vijay Ghat to pay his respects at the samadhis of Mahatma Gandhi and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri, respectively.

राष्ट्रपिता महात्मा गांधी जी और ‘जय जवान, जय किसान’ का अमर मंत्र देने वाले देश के पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री स्व. श्री लाल बहादुर शास्त्री जी की जयंती पर आज संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में ‘Know Your Leader’ कार्यक्रम के तहत देशभर से आए युवा विद्यार्थियों के विचारों को सुना। मैंने महसूस किया कि आज की पीढ़ी गांधी जी और शास्त्री जी के जीवन दर्शन को आत्मसात कर रही है। सत्य, अहिंसा और सत्याग्रह पर उनके सारगर्भित विचारों को सुनकर बड़ा संतोष हुआ। ‘एक भारत – श्रेष्ठ भारत’ की भावना को साकार करते इन नौजवानों को संबोधित करते हुए राष्ट्र के प्रति समर्पण भाव को सर्वोपरि रखने का आह्वान किया। पूज्य गांधी जी और शास्त्री जी के जीवन में एक समान संदेश स्पष्ट दिखाई देता है - राष्ट्र सबसे पहले। अपने कर्तव्यों को ईमानदारी से निभाना, समाज और देश के प्रति जिम्मेदारी को समझना और अपने प्रत्येक कार्य को राष्ट्रहित से जोड़ना ही उनके प्रति हमारी सच्ची श्रद्धांजलि है। युवा विद्यार्थी इस ऐतिहासिक Central Hall से केवल महान नेताओं की स्मृतियां लेकर न लौटें, बल्कि उनके विचारों और आदर्शों को अपने जीवन का हिस्सा बनाने का संकल्प लेकर जाएं। विकसित भारत केवल एक लक्ष्य नहीं, बल्कि करोड़ों भारतीयों के सामूहिक संकल्प और परिश्रम से पूरा होने वाला सपना है। इस सपने को साकार करने के लिए हर युवा को अपने क्षेत्र में उत्कृष्टता, नवाचार, अनुशासन और राष्ट्रसेवा की भावना के साथ आगे बढ़ना होगा। आइए, गांधी जी के सत्य, अहिंसा और मानवता के आदर्शों तथा शास्त्री जी की सादगी, कर्तव्यनिष्ठा और राष्ट्रसेवा से प्रेरणा लेकर हम संकल्प लें कि अपने हर प्रयास से भारत को और मजबूत, आत्मनिर्भर, समृद्ध एवं विकसित बनाने में योगदान देंगे। जय हिंद। #GandhiJayanti2026 #LalBahadurShastriJayanti

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) October 2, 2026

महात्मा गांधी जी की प्रेरणा से दुनिया के कई देश आज़ाद हुए। गांधी जी का दर्शन व उनके विचार आज भी दुनियाभर के लिए प्रेरणा है। https://t.co/2XfrF9wgsn

item.description:
