item.title: Dignity by Design: Innovation Reshapes India's Public Toilets
item.description:
Over the years, India’s cities have made significant strides in expanding access to public sanitation facilities. From improving availability and cleanliness to enhancing safety and accessibility, cities are adopting innovative approaches to make public toilets more inclusive and user-friendly.
Building on these efforts, the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) , launched on 2 October 2014 , has advanced sanitation innovation across India. Cities built toilets, raised awareness and worked…
item.content:encoded:
Over the years, India’s cities have made significant strides in expanding access to public sanitation facilities. From improving availability and cleanliness to enhancing safety and accessibility, cities are adopting innovative approaches to make public toilets more inclusive and user-friendly.

Building on these efforts, the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), launched on 2 October 2014, has advanced sanitation innovation across India. Cities built toilets, raised awareness and worked towards becoming Open Defecation Free (ODF). Many went further, achieving ODF+ and ODF++ status. In 2022, the Toilets 2.0 initiative under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U) raised the bar again. Its aim was to make Community and Public Toilets (CT/PTs) safe, clean and inviting for everyone. Citizens can now find the nearest facility through the ‘SBM Toilet Locator’ on the Swachhata app.

Today, the change is visible in unexpected places. An old bus has become a women's toilet. Plastic waste has turned into building material. A busy market now hosts a smart lounge. A small city has found a safe way to handle sanitary waste. Pilgrim towns offer facilities open to all. Together, these stories trace the journey from basic access to dignity, safety and innovation.

New Age Toilets: A Scrap Bus Becomes a Safe Space for Women

Women travelling through crowded bus terminals often struggle to find a clean and private toilet. In Bengaluru, Karnataka, an old bus found a new purpose to meet this need. The Sthree Toilet was set up at the Majestic bus terminal of the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC). Built from a scrap vehicle, it serves women exclusively.

The toilet has three Indian-style and two Western-style commodes. A sanitary napkin vending machine and an incinerator support menstrual hygiene. A dedicated space lets mothers feed their babies and change diapers. Sensor lights run on solar power generated by the facility itself. Waste drains into the nearest sewage chamber at the bus station. The toilet has proved especially helpful for mothers travelling with young children.

Navi Mumbai’s Sustainable Toilets: A Model of Eco-Conscious Urban Design

Can a public toilet be built from what a city throws away? Navi Mumbai has shown that it can. The Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) has developed Aspirational Toilets at Sector 14, Koparkhairane. The site lies near the Nisargudyan urban garden, a busy public space. Around 8,000 to 9,000 visitors use the facility every day.

The structure uses 426 square metres of recycled plastic sheeting. This includes 5.3 metric tonnes of single-use plastic, 11,700 plastic bottles and 35,200 bottle caps. Builders also reused 85 repurposed computer keyboards and 284 kg of scrap metal. The project puts the principle of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle into everyday practice.

Safety and comfort are built into the design. Separate sections for men and women ensure privacy. Units for children and persons with disabilities, baby care stations and sanitary pad vending machines serve all users. A fountain running on treated sewage water completes its green design. The complex now stands as a symbol of environmental innovation and civic pride.

Swachh Smart Toilets: Freshrooms Bring Comfort to Bhopal

Shoppers, vendors and commuters crowd Bhopal’s 10 Number Market every day. The Bhopal Municipal Corporation has set up ‘Freshrooms’, smart and luxury public convenience centres. They follow a Design-Build-Operate-Transfer (DBOT) model under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP). The Smart Lounge at the market covers 800 to 1,000 square feet. It serves 500 to 1,000 visitors daily.

Technology lies at the heart of the facility. It offers sensor-based toilets and touch-free urinals. Visitors can also use hot and cold showers, lockers and Wi-Fi. A café, vending machines and baby-changing rooms add to the comfort. A digital information wall keeps users informed. Separate, accessible facilities serve men, women and persons with disabilities. By integrating technology, comfort and sustainability, Freshrooms demonstrate how innovative models can deliver world-class sanitation while ensuring financial self-sufficiency.

Smart Sanitary Solutions in Karad: Safe Disposal, Safer City

Clean toilets are one part of the sanitation story. Safe disposal of sanitary waste is another. Used napkins and diapers, if dumped openly, harm health and the environment. Stigma often keeps the issue hidden. Karad, a small city in Satara district of Maharashtra, has tackled this challenge head-on. It ensures 100% segregation, collection and processing of sanitary and biomedical waste. Nearly 300 to 350 kg of sanitary waste is collected daily from hospitals, clinics, households and other facilities.

The first step was to break the taboo around sanitary waste. Workshops, community outreach and public announcements explained the risks of careless disposal. The Karad Municipal Council (KMC) worked with women residents to form awareness groups. These groups carried the message across residential areas. Separate red bins were placed in public toilets to make safe disposal easier for women.

Schools were encouraged to install sanitary pad vending machines and disposal systems. The city’s Information, Education and Communication (IEC) team urged users to wrap used pads in paper. Many schools have since installed incinerators. Their residue goes to the biomedical waste treatment plant.

Garbage collection vehicles carry a separate bin for sanitary waste. Staff sort this waste so that only suitable material reaches the incinerator.

KMC has partnered with the Karad Hospital Association to treat this waste. KMC allocated land for construction of the biomedical waste treatment plant, while the association operates and maintains it. This is a 600 kg/day Common Biomedical Waste Treatment Facility (CBWTF). It processes the sanitary waste collected by the council free of charge. Its central incinerator reaches temperatures of up to 1,200°C. Gases are filtered to remove harmful substances. Emissions are monitored in real time and linked to the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) system.

This PPP partnership has eased the council’s financial burden, as it bears only collection and transport costs. High-temperature incineration of sanitary waste has reduced health risks and protects sanitation workers handling the waste. Open dumping has been eliminated, preventing environmental contamination and reducing the spread of diseases. It has improved residents’ quality of life, particularly for women affected by sanitary waste disposal challenges.

Comfort, Cleanliness & Care for Tirupati’s Pilgrims

Places of faith draw lakhs of visitors, making clean toilets a daily necessity. Tirupati is among India’s busiest pilgrimage destinations. The Tirupati Municipal Corporation has built modern toilet complexes for devotees, tourists and residents.

A dedicated Pink Toilet Complex for women stands near the bus station. It links key points such as Srinivasam, Vishnuvasam, the railway station and the bus terminal. Women can use Indian and Western toilets, restrooms, and mother care and changing rooms. Incinerators and sanitary napkin vending machines support menstrual hygiene. The complex serves 12,000 to 15,000 users daily. A structured three-shift cleaning system maintains the facility.

A Common Public Toilet Complex near the railway station caters to 20,000–25,000 devotees visiting the Govindarajaswamy Temple area daily. Designed for universal access, it provides dedicated facilities for men, women, transgender persons, Divyaang, and children. Ramps, handrails, child-friendly fixtures, and bathing rooms ensure greater comfort, hygiene, and accessibility for pilgrims.

Road Ahead

Under SBM-U 2.0, the focus has moved beyond building toilets. The goal now is to keep them clean, safe, inclusive and sustainable. These stories show how cities are reaching that goal in their own ways. A scrap bus, recycled plastic, sensor-based fixtures and a high-temperature incinerator each play a part. Partnerships with private operators, hospitals and communities keep these facilities running well. Dedicated workers and caretakers give them life every day. As the Swachh Bharat Mission completes twelve years, the direction is clear. Every citizen, whatever their gender, ability or location, deserves a clean and dignified toilet. From markets to monuments, Indian cities are turning that promise into reality.

 

Reference:

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

item.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal Calls for WTO-Compliant Approach to Correcting Global Trade Distortions at the Concluding Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, U.S.
item.description:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the concluding day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and spoke in sessions on structural excess capacity and production, updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, ending forced labour in global supply chains, and the closing session.
Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Shri Goyal said that India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the concluding day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and spoke in sessions on structural excess capacity and production, updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, ending forced labour in global supply chains, and the closing session.

Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Shri Goyal said that India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a domestic-demand-driven economy serving 1.4 billion people, and is building manufacturing value chains from design to finished goods as a trusted link in global supply chains. He said India’s manufacturing capacity serves its domestic and global needs and that, in the sectors identified by the G20 Presidency, India does not have structural excess capacity.

Shri Goyal said India shares the concerns of many Members that trade-distorting support in some economies can lead to dumping and predatory pricing. He said such concerns are addressed through WTO-consistent measures, including anti-dumping and countervailing duties, based on evidence and subject to judicial review. He emphasised that industrial capacity in itself is not the issue, while distortions can arise where geographical concentration of production is driven by hidden subsidies and support. He said diversification of production and supply chains is a legitimate objective, but cannot be used as a pretext for measures outside WTO rules or for shifting the burden of adjustment onto developing countries, which must retain policy space to industrialise. He also said that sharing of statistics and data should take place within existing mechanisms.

On updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, Shri Goyal said that India’s trade with G20 members depends on a transparent, non-discriminatory and rules-based trading system. He said Most-Favoured-Nation treatment is a key guarantee of this system, ensuring that the same terms apply to the smallest trader and the largest trader. He emphasised that consensus remains central to the WTO and that special and differential treatment must be preserved to enable developing countries to catch up with developed economies. He also called for restoration of the two-tier dispute settlement system.

Speaking on ending forced labour in global supply chains, Shri Goyal said India’s commitment to the elimination of forced labour is absolute and unconditional. He noted that Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits forced labour as a fundamental right, enforceable by the Supreme Court. He said India has ratified ILO Conventions 29 and 105 and, in July 2026, amended its Foreign Trade Policy to prohibit the import of goods produced using forced labour.

Shri Goyal said measures at the border must be based on specific and verifiable evidence rather than presumptions about entire countries, regions or sectors, and must respect due process and WTO rules. He said the International Labour Organization is the competent, universal and tripartite body for labour standards. India supports the objective of eliminating forced labour and voluntary exchange of good practices among G20 members, provided that such cooperation does not involve monitoring of members, create new obligations or result in information being used as a basis for unilateral trade action.

Shri Goyal thanked Ambassador Greer and the United States G20 Presidency for the arrangements and hospitality extended in Milwaukee. Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s words that issues that cannot be resolved together should not come in the way of those that can, Shri Goyal said India participated in the Meeting in that spirit and, across all four themes, shared its concerns and offered constructive inputs.

The Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment to a rules-based, fair, equitable, non-discriminatory, transparent, open, inclusive and multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core. He emphasised the importance of preserving policy space for developing countries to grow and feed their people, while upholding decision-making by consensus. Shri Goyal extended India’s full support to the United Kingdom for its G20 Presidency in 2027.

On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal held bilateral meetings with the Minister for Trade and Tourism of Australia, the Minister of Commerce of Saudi Arabia, the Minister Delegate for Foreign Trade and Economic Attractiveness of France, the Minister for Trade of the Republic of Korea and the Minister of International Trade of Canada.

Gandhi Jayanti was observed as Shramdan Day on 2 October 2026 at the CSIR-Structural Engineering Research Centre (CSIR-SERC), CSIR Madras Complex (CMC), Chennai, and the Tower Testing Research Station, Thirusulam.

The observance commenced with floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi, followed by the administration of the Swachhata Shapath (Cleanliness Pledge) to the staff. A cleanliness drive was subsequently conducted near CSIR- NML and adjacent to CMC departmental canteen, with enthusiastic participation from employees of CSIR-SERC and CMC.

As part of the programme, saplings were planted in front of the CMC departmental canteen and near the Garage to promote environmental sustainability and encourage a greener campus.

Dr. N. Anandavalli, Director, CSIR-SERC and Co-ordinating Director CMC, actively participated in the programme along with staff members of CSIR-SERC and CMC.

The observance highlighted the relevance of Mahatma Gandhi's values and reinforced the importance of cleanliness, collective responsibility, environmental awareness and sustainable practices.

item.content:encoded:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today paid floral tributes and offered homage to Mahatma Gandhi Ji, former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Thiru K. Kamaraj Ji.

Paid tributes to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi Ji, at Rajghat on his birth anniversary. His unwavering faith in truth and non-violence, steadfast commitment to justice, and profound belief in the dignity of every individual continue to inspire humanity. Mahatma Gandhi Ji’s life and message remain an enduring beacon of peace, compassion, selflessness and service. On this solemn occasion, let us reaffirm our commitment to the values he cherished and dedicate ourselves to building a just, harmonious and inclusive society.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

At Raj Ghat, the Vice-President paid floral tributes and offered homage to Mahatma Gandhi Ji on his birth anniversary. Recalling his enduring legacy, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that Mahatma Gandhi Ji’s unwavering faith in truth and non-violence, steadfast commitment to justice and profound belief in the dignity of every individual continue to inspire humanity.

He said that Mahatma Gandhi Ji’s life and message remain an enduring beacon of peace, compassion, selflessness and service. He called upon everyone to reaffirm their commitment to the values cherished by Mahatma Gandhi Ji and dedicate themselves to building a just, harmonious and inclusive society.

Paid tributes to former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji on his birth anniversary at Vijay Ghat today. A leader of quiet strength and extraordinary resolve, Shastri Ji exemplified humility, integrity and an unwavering commitment to the nation. At a defining moment in India’s journey, his leadership instilled confidence and unity, while his call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” gave enduring recognition to the sacrifices of our soldiers and the vital contribution of our farmers. His life remains a powerful reminder that true leadership is rooted in simplicity, courage and service to the nation.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

At Vijay Ghat, the Vice-President paid floral tributes and offered homage to former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji on his birth anniversary.

Describing Shastri Ji as a leader of quiet strength and extraordinary resolve, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he exemplified humility, integrity and unwavering commitment to the nation. He recalled that, at a defining moment in India’s journey, Shastri Ji’s leadership instilled confidence and unity, while his call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” gave enduring recognition to the sacrifices of the nation’s soldiers and the vital contribution of its farmers.

The Vice-President said that Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji’s life remains a powerful reminder that true leadership is rooted in simplicity, courage and service to the nation.

On the death anniversary of Thiru K. Kamaraj Ji, I paid my humble tributes to him at Uprashtrapati Bhavan today. A towering statesman and a true people’s leader, Kamaraj Ji devoted his life to the service of the nation and the welfare of the common people. His transformative contribution to education, particularly in expanding opportunities for children from underprivileged backgrounds, remains a defining legacy of his public life. His dedication to public welfare and his selfless approach to public life continue to inspire generations.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

At Uprashtrapati Bhavan, the Vice-President paid tributes to Thiru K. Kamaraj Ji on his death anniversary and recalled his outstanding contribution to public life and nation-building.

Describing Kamaraj Ji as a towering statesman and a true people’s leader, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he devoted his life to the service of the nation and the welfare of the common people.

He said that Kamaraj Ji lived his entire life guided by Gandhian thought and made lasting contributions to the development of Tamil Nadu by expanding roads and educational institutions, introducing the midday meal programme and bringing new hope to the lives of the poor.

The Vice-President also recalled Kamaraj Ji’s contributions to irrigation and industrial development through the construction of dams and establishment of industrial estates, which laid foundations for the growth of agriculture and industry in Tamil Nadu.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan paid respectful tributes to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi Ji and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Ji at Uprashtrapati Bhavan today. He recalled their sacrifices and invaluable contributions to the freedom struggle, nation-building and the welfare of society.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 2, 2026

தேசியப் பெருந்தலைவர் காமராஜர் அவர்கள் இந்த தேசத்துக்காகவே வாழ்ந்தவர்; மக்கள் நலனைத் தவிர வேறொன்றையும் அறியாதவர். தன் வாழ்நாள் முழுவதும் காந்திய சிந்தனையோடு வாழ்ந்த அவர், சாலைகளை அமைத்தார்; கல்விச்சாலைகளை உருவாக்கினார்; மதிய உணவுத் திட்டத்தை வழங்கினார். ஏழைகளின் வாழ்வில் ஒரு புதிய ஒளியை ஏற்படுத்தினார். அணைகளைக் கட்டினார்; தொழிற்பேட்டைகளை அமைத்தார். இந்த மண்ணில் தொழில் வளர்ச்சியும், விவசாய வளர்ச்சியும் ஓங்கி வளர்வதற்கு அவரது திட்டங்களே அடித்தளமிட்டன. தமிழகம் இன்று இந்தியாவிலேயே இரண்டாவது வேகமாக வளர்ந்து வரும் பொருளாதாரமாக வீறுநடை போட மிக முக்கிய காரணம் பெருந்தலைவர் காமராஜர் அவர்கள். பெருந்தலைவர் அவர்களின் புகழ் இந்த மண்ணில் என்றென்றும் நிலைத்து நிற்கும். பெருந்தலைவர் வாழ்க! அவர் புகழ் ஓங்குக!

item.title: Urban Transformation: Building Greener, More Sustainable Cities
item.description: A city’s growth is visible not only in its buildings and roads, but also in how it responds to everyday challenges. The way waste is handled, communities participate and services are delivered can shape the quality of urban life. The Swachh Bharat Mission has given this everyday transformation a strong foundation across the country. Over time, the focus has moved beyond simply collecting and disposing of waste. Cities are finding ways to recover value from discarded material, encourage…
item.content:encoded:
A city’s growth is visible not only in its buildings and roads, but also in how it responds to everyday challenges. The way waste is handled, communities participate and services are delivered can shape the quality of urban life. The Swachh Bharat Mission has given this everyday transformation a strong foundation across the country. Over time, the focus has moved beyond simply collecting and disposing of waste. Cities are finding ways to recover value from discarded material, encourage responsible habits and make municipal services more efficient. Green practices are also gaining ground as segregation, recycling, reuse and recovery become integral to local systems. Digital monitoring, data-driven systems and better service delivery are helping local bodies to work with greater precision. These efforts are gradually creating urban spaces that balance environmental responsibility with the needs of everyday life.

Cities Leading the Way in Sustainable Urban Transformation

Across different regions, cities are demonstrating how local solutions can translate into meaningful environmental outcomes. Their experiences show that sustainable urban transformation can take many forms. These include converting dumping grounds into integrated waste management facilities and promoting zero-waste practices. Technology is also improving everyday sanitation services and strengthening urban systems. The following stories highlight these diverse approaches.

A Greener Goa: Turning Waste into Energy

Located in the valleys of Saligao, Goa, the Integrated Waste Management Facility Center promotes environmental sustainability. Spread across 113,000 square metres, it is operated by the Goa Waste Management Corporation (GWMC). The facility was formerly used as a garbage dump. It has now been transformed into an integrated, eco-friendly waste management hub for Goa. The center manages 250 metric tons of wet and dry waste every day. At this plant, organic matter is separated from waste and converted into biogas, which helps generate electricity. This energy supports the needs of the local community by alleviating power shortages in the area.

Wet waste from restaurants is converted into valuable bioproducts, including methane-rich biogas. Recyclable materials are recovered from 100 metric tons of dry waste processed at the facility. The remaining dry waste is sent to cement factories for co-processing. Additionally, 1.32 kilowatts of electricity is generated from wet waste at the facility. This electricity powers 35 units, with half supplied to the Goa Electricity Department. The plant also generates 7–8 tons of compost daily. Local panchayats use this compost for gardening and reforestation projects.

The integrated solid waste management facility is strengthening Goa’s waste management system, processing approximately one-third of the state's total waste. People who once merely collected waste are now part of the plant's trained workforce. This provides livelihood opportunities for several families in the region while benefiting the environment. The plant operates continuously throughout the year, aiming to make the city "zero waste”.

Gandhinagar’s Zero-Waste Journey: Citizens Driving Change

Gandhinagar in Gujarat stands as a strong example of swachhata and sustainability. Through its commitment to the Swachh Bharat Mission and participation in Swachh Survekshan, the city promotes a culture of cleanliness. Inspired by the global Zero Waste Week movement, the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation organised impactful activities from 2nd to 7th September, 2026. These initiatives aimed to encourage behavioural change and promote the 3R principles: Reduce, Reuse and Recycle. Activities were conducted at 25 locations across the city, directly engaging more than 600 citizens. Targeted social media campaigns further reached and sensitised over 40,000 individuals during the week. The My Theli stalls became vibrant spaces for community participation and sustainable action across Gandhinagar. Citizens were encouraged to donate used clothes. Skilled women from local self-help groups transformed these donations into reusable carry bags.


The “Swachhata Se Shuruvat” campaign was launched to encourage responsible practices among school students. Quiz competitions were organised to raise awareness about environmental concerns and responsible practices. Engaging and interactive games were designed through which students gained practical insights into sustainability. The Reduce, Reuse, Recycle van visited residents at their doorsteps to collect old clothes, plastic and electronic waste. Participants received rewards for their donations, encouraging greater community involvement. Citizens were also invited to share their personal efforts and daily practices through online testimonials. Through these initiatives, Gandhinagar is advancing its zero-waste vision. The city continues to strengthen resource-conscious practices while working towards the goal of Garbage Free Cities.

Kakinada’s Smart Approach to Efficient Waste Management

In Andhra Pradesh’s East Godavari District, Kakinada has emerged as a notable example of technology-enabled waste management. Kakinada generates around 144 tons of waste daily, comprising wet, dry and hazardous materials. The Kakinada Municipal Corporation manages this operation across 50 wards, which are further divided into 382 micro pockets. Each micro pocket covers 250 to 350 households and is managed by two sanitation workers.

 

With around 112,993 households, over 973 sanitation workers have been employed to manage waste. These households are strategically organised into 40,661 designated waste collection points across the city. Digital tools are used to streamline waste collection and transportation. The Online Waste Management System (OWMS) tracks the process in real time. Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), facial recognition, GPS and a human resource management system (HRMS) further support workforce and transportation management. RFID chip-enabled tags are installed at the gates of every waste generator. Collectors scan these tags when waste is picked up. The scanned information is recorded in the OWMS, enabling officials to monitor collection progress. Continuous monitoring and dedicated sanitation staff have helped the system achieve 100% door-to-door collection.

 

The Municipal Corporation has deployed 108 hopper vehicles equipped with GPS tracking devices. These monitor the transportation and report deviations during waste collection and transportation to processing plants. It has also introduced a Facial Recognition System (FRS) for all SafaiMitras. Workers can now record their attendance using facial recognition technology. This eliminates the need for manual attendance registers or fingerprint scanners. All these technologies are integrated into a Central Command Centre for close monitoring. Around 60% of residents now segregate waste at source. The combined efforts of sanitation workers and residents are strengthening Kakinada’s ability to manage its waste efficiently.

 

Ghaziabad: Turning Waste into Carbon Value

Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, is advancing cleanliness and urban development while taking steps to reduce carbon emissions. The Ghaziabad Municipal Corporation (GMC) has registered for an international carbon credit project. The initiative is verified by the United Nations and combines environmental protection with potential financial benefits. Improved solid waste management under the Swachh Bharat Mission can reduce greenhouse gases such as methane from dumping sites.
Greater use of clean fuels and energy sources can also lower dependence on fossil fuels and reduce carbon emissions. In line with these efforts, the Ghaziabad Municipal Corporation has demonstrated its commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals. It has been accredited under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), supported by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

The GMC has replaced old streetlights across the city with energy-efficient LED lights. This measure reduces carbon emissions while also lowering electricity consumption. It is also adopting "wet waste composting" to produce compost from wet waste. This process supports faster waste management and helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Following Indore in Madhya Pradesh, Ghaziabad is set to become the first urban local body (ULB) in Uttar Pradesh and the second in the country to turn waste into a new source of value.

Together, these measures are expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 2.7 lakh tonnes. This reduction corresponds to 2.7 lakh carbon credits, with one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent to one credit. Certified credits can be converted into revenue by being sold on the international carbon market. The initiative supports cleanliness, environmental protection and economic opportunities for Ghaziabad.

 

 

Building Cities That Value Every Resource

The transformation underway across cities reflects a broader shift in the way urban resources are managed. Technology is strengthening everyday sanitation services while citizens are becoming active participants in sustainable practices. Local solutions are creating visible improvements in everyday urban life. They also show the value of combining innovation with people’s efforts for effective waste management. Together, these approaches point towards urban systems that are not only cleaner, but also more circular and resource-efficient

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

item.title: APEDA Facilitates Export of Bihar’s Makhana from Purnea to Greece
item.description:

The consignment, sourced by Indo Global Export, Belouri, Purnea, is being exported to Greece…
item.content:encoded:
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a consignment of 1 MT of Popped (Phool) Makhana from Purnea, Bihar, for export to Greece, marking another step towards expanding international market access for Bihar’s traditional Makhana and creating opportunities for improved farmer realisation through export-oriented value chains.

The consignment, sourced by Indo Global Export, Belouri, Purnea, is being exported to Greece through S. S Foods Exports Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi. The shipment will move from Mundra Port in India to Piraeus Port in Greece.

The export has also resulted in higher price realisation compared with the prevailing domestic market selling price, highlighting the potential of international markets to create additional value for Makhana producers. Such export-led market access can strengthen linkages between producers and international buyers while creating opportunities for improved returns to farmers.

India is the global leader in Makhana production, with Bihar contributing around 80-85% of the country’s production. Makhana cultivation in Bihar spans over 35,000 hectares across 10 districts. The sector is supported by technical interventions at the grassroots level from Bihar Agricultural University (BAU), Sabour, and ICAR-National Research Centre for Makhana, Darbhanga.

The flag-off programme was chaired by Agriculture Minister, Government of Bihar, Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha, in the presence of Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev, and Director, Horticulture, Agriculture Department, Government of Bihar, Shri Abhishek Kumar, along with senior officers of the Government of Bihar and other stakeholders associated with the Makhana export value chain.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Vijay Kumar Sinha said, “The export marks an important milestone for Bihar’s Makhana sector as the product continues to reach international markets. India exported more than 7000 MT of makhana and value-added makhana products valued at USD 22 million during FY 2025-26 across more than 20 international destinations.”

He further stated that the Government of Bihar is working towards an Agri Export Policy aimed at supporting farmers and improving their incomes through export promotion. He also highlighted that packhouses have been developed to support the Makhana export value chain. He commended APEDA for its continued efforts towards expanding Makhana exports and improving farmer realisation.

The export from Purnea to Greece is part of growing efforts to connect Bihar’s Makhana producers and exporters with international markets. With its strong traditional and cultural association with Bihar, Makhana has emerged as an important product in India’s agricultural export basket.

APEDA has been facilitating market linkages and supporting exporters in taking Indian Makhana to international markets. Makhana exports are also expanding into European markets, with growing opportunities for Indian producers and avenues for diversification beyond traditional destinations. These efforts are helping connect Makhana producers in Bihar with international demand while creating opportunities for improved farmer realisation and greater participation of producer groups in the export value chain.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Abhimanyu Panwar

item.title: Department of Pharmaceuticals Commences Special Campaign 6 with Focus on Scientific E-Waste Management and Pendency Liquidation
item.description:
In pursuance of the guidelines issued by the Government, the Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), along with its attached and subordinate organizations - including the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs), and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) - officially commenced Special Campaign 6, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, on October 2, 2026 .
…
item.content:encoded:
In pursuance of the guidelines issued by the Government, the Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), along with its attached and subordinate organizations - including the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs), and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) - officially commenced Special Campaign 6, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, on October 2, 2026.

Following an intensive Preparatory Phase (September 15–30, 2026) where baseline targets, site identifications, and record inventories were successfully completed, the Department has now transitioned into the active implementation phase running upto October 31, 2026.

Campaign Metrics & Baseline Targets for Special Campaign 6:

  1. Cleanliness Campaigns: 12,208 cleanliness and outstation office drives scheduled across organizational units.
  2. Pendency & Grievance Redressal Targets: Active resolution tracking is underway for 4 MP references, 2 Parliamentary Assurances, 1 Inter-Ministerial Cabinet proposal, 58 State Government references, 2 PMO references, 72 Public Grievances (CPGRAMS), 18 Public Grievance Appeals, and 20 Easing of Rules/Process items.
  3. Record Management: Review of 2,716 physical files and 20 e-files to optimize workspace and streamline documentation.
  4. Scientific E-Waste Management: Systematic disposal targeting an aggregate of 1,011 quantities of obsolete equipment - including 602 units of IT & telecommunication equipment, 196 consumer electrical/electronic & photovoltaic units, 53 large/small electrical appliances, 5 laboratory instruments, 154 other electronic assets, and electrical tools, through MoEFCC - empanelled recyclers.

Key Focus Areas:

  1. Scientific E-Waste Management: Safe segregation and disposal, compliant with E-Waste Management Rules.
  2. Pendency Liquidation: Swift closure of public grievances, parliamentary assurances, and official references.
  3. Space Optimization: Promoting clean, clutter-free working environments through systematic record reviews and scrap clearance.

The Department remains committed to institutionalizing Swachhata and elevating governance standards throughout this month-long nationwide initiative. Daily progress updates and best practices will be shared via the national SCDPM portal.

The FPO-led export includes green peas, mixed vegetables, peas and carrots, sweet corn, samosa, among other products. The…
item.content:encoded:
The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a consignment of 24 MT of frozen food products from Sonipat, Haryana to Canada on 1st October 2026. The shipment, exported by Aterna Foods Producer Company Limited, comprises 2,295 boxes of frozen food products with a total shipment value of CAD 35,140.

The FPO-led export includes green peas, mixed vegetables, peas and carrots, sweet corn, samosa, among other products. The exporting unit was supported by APEDA under its Financial Assistance Scheme. The shipment marks another step towards expanding international market opportunities for Indian processed food products and connecting Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) with global buyers and markets.

The export highlights the growing role of Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) in developing export-oriented value chains and enabling farmers to access international markets. APEDA has been facilitating linkages between FPOs/FPCs and exporters through initiatives aimed at strengthening market access and connecting farmer groups with export opportunities. By linking agricultural produce with processing and international markets, the FPO-led model can support improved returns for producers and strengthen the participation of farmer groups in the export value chain.

Addressing the gathering, Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev congratulated the exporter and stakeholders, noting that the direct export by the FPO would significantly enhance value realisation for the producers. He also acknowledged NIFTEM’s valuable contribution and expressed optimism about expanding exports to the Canadian market.

APEDA, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, continues to facilitate market linkages and export opportunities for Indian agricultural and processed food products while supporting the integration of farmer groups into global value chains.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Abhimanyu Panwar

item.title: NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on SDG Budgeting in Kolkata under the State Support Mission, in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and UNDP
item.description: NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and with technical support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), organised a National Workshop on SDG Budgeting in Kolkata on 29 September 2026 under the State Support Mission (SSM) initiative of NITI Aayog. The Workshop focused on strengthening the alignment of planning and budgeting processes with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with emphasis on institutionalising SDG budget tagging and translating…
item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and with technical support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), organised a National Workshop on SDG Budgeting in Kolkata on 29 September 2026 under the State Support Mission (SSM) initiative of NITI Aayog. The Workshop focused on strengthening the alignment of planning and budgeting processes with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with emphasis on institutionalising SDG budget tagging and translating financial commitments into measurable development outcomes at the sub-national level.

The Workshop brought together participants from 32 States and Union Territories, along with senior officials from NITI Aayog, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) and its offices, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), UNDP, UN Resident Coordinator Office (UNRCO), development partners, and representatives from FICCI, CII, SEBI, Tata Steel Foundation, Intellecap and GIZ. Government representatives from Haryana, Odisha, Meghalaya and West Bengal shared experiences on the implementation and institutionalisation of SDG Budgeting, reflecting the whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to SDG localisation.

The inaugural session was graced by Dr. Swapan Dasgupta, Hon'ble Finance Minister, Government of West Bengal; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Hon'ble Member, NITI Aayog; Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Comptroller and Auditor General of India, virtually; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Government of India, virtually; Shri Prabhat Kumar Mishra, Additional Chief Secretary, Finance, Government of West Bengal; Shri Stefan Priesner, United Nations Resident Coordinator; Dr. Angela Lusigi, Resident Representative, UNDP; and Shri Rajib Kumar Sen, Programme Director (SDGs), NITI Aayog.

Delivering the Chief Guest Address, Dr. Swapan Dasgupta said, "What we have not always had is a clean line running from a goal, to a target, to an allocation in the budget, to a unit that will actually spend. Without that line, the SDGs remain an aspiration on the asset side of the ledger with no corresponding entry on the liability side. SDG budget tagging is the discipline of drawing that line."

In his keynote address, Dr. R. Balasubramaniam said, "Mapping the SDGs to State expenditure is a significant step. Whole-of-society and whole-of-government can sound like slogans, but with the finance department, political leadership, multilateral institutions and the private sector together today, the idea becomes real. The task ahead is to guide every State so that money spent can be shown to be money spent wisely”.

Shri Prabhat Kumar Mishra, Additional Chief Secretary, Finance, Government of West Bengal, highlighted that the State has, for the first time, mapped its budget to the goal level of the SDGs and integrated the exercise into its Integrated Financial Management System.

Shri Stefan Priesner highlighted India’s enabling framework for private sector engagement, including CSR, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting, ESG in capital markets and the Social Stock Exchange, and emphasised the need to integrate sustainability into core business decision-making. Dr. Angela Lusigi highlighted the value of SDG budget tagging in linking expenditure with specific SDG targets and assessing whether resources are reaching those who need them most, while also aligning CSR, investment and philanthropy with development priorities. She also noted the joint standards launched by ISO and UNDP to support public and private organisations in placing the SDGs at the core of decision-making.

The discussions emphasised that SDG budget tagging can enable governments to make expenditure visible against development goals, identify gaps and strengthen evidence-based planning. The “Guide on Mapping State Budgets to the SDGs”, developed jointly by NITI Aayog, the CAG of India and UNDP, was discussed as a practical framework for aligning State budgets with the Goals. The deliberations also underscored the importance of embedding SDG priorities within the annual budget cycle and establishing the institutional arrangements required to move from measurement to mission-mode implementation.

The workshop comprised four technical sessions covering the design elements of SDG budget tagging, including the identification of expenditure to be tagged, the appropriate level of tagging, linkage with the Head of Accounts, tagging to SDG Targets, attribution through NITI Aayog’s Scheme-SDG mapping and value assignment.

States including Haryana, Odisha, Meghalaya and West Bengal shared their experiences of implementation and institutionalisation. Discussions on integrating SDG budgeting into the annual budget cycle covered institutional responsibilities, reconciliation, quality assurance, reporting and performance audit.

The session on “Making It Happen: SDG Budgeting in the Annual Budget Cycle”, led by Shri Navneet Gupta, Principal Accountant General (A&E), examined the integration of SDG budget tagging into budget preparation, institutional responsibilities, and accountability mechanisms including reconciliation, quality assurance, reporting and performance audit, including the role of the CAG

A dedicated session on private sector engagement examined enabling policy frameworks, innovative financing and responsible business conduct to strengthen sustained private sector engagement with the SDGs. Representatives from Tata Steel Foundation, Intellecap, IICA, MoSPI, FICCI, GIZ, ITC Limited, CII and SEBI participated in the session.

As India advances towards Viksit Bharat@2047, with 2030 as a critical milestone for the SDGs, the workshop reaffirmed NITI Aayog’s commitment to strengthening cooperative federalism and supporting States and Union Territories in embedding the SDGs within their planning, budgeting and governance processes. The deliberations underscored the need to strengthen the linkage between public expenditure, development priorities and measurable outcomes, and to accelerate the transition from measurement to implementation.

***

MJPS/SS/PRK

item.content:encoded:
The second edition of the biannual Naval Commander's Conference 2026 was conducted from 29 Sep - 01 Oct 2026 at New Delhi. The apex level conference served as an avenue for a comprehensive review of the Navy's operational and materiel preparedness at the military-strategic level. During the three-day conference, Shri Rajnath Singh, Hon'ble Raksha Mantri, Shri Jitin Prasada, Hon'ble Minister of State for Electronics and IT, Gen NS Raja Subramani, Chief of Defence Staff, and Gen Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff interacted with the Naval Commanders. (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2316492®=3&lang=1 )

The conference brought together the naval commanders to deliberate on operational preparedness, logistics and maintenance milestones, and reforms undertaken in the field of training and HR management. These aspects were discussed in the backdrop of the evolving global security environment, and rapid advances in technology, including absorption of AI, and the growing role of autonomous and uncrewed systems.

Shri Jitin Prasada, Hon'ble Minister of State for Electronics and IT, highlighted the importance of accelerating technology adoption, and strengthening domestic capabilities in key sectors such as semiconductors, AI and quantum technologies.

 

Addressing the Naval Commanders, Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics & IT, lauded the #IndianNavy’s role in ensuring India’s energy security and highlighted the GoI’s focus on strengthening sovereignty in semiconductor and chip production towards a more robust… https://t.co/wDqVkp3ajM pic.twitter.com/RP1FX5BonF

— SpokespersonNavy (@indiannavy) October 1, 2026

 

Gen NS Raja Subramani Chief of the Defence Staff underscored the Navy's role as a strategic force multiplier in safeguarding national interests and commended the Indian Navy's operational commitment to maintaining energy security, along with its sustained efforts towards technology absorption, and indigenisation. He also emphasised the need for technology-driven transformation, resilience, and greater integration among the Defence Forces.

 

Gen NS Raja Subramani, #CDS, addressing the #IndianNavy Commanders’ Conference on 29 Sep 2026, acknowledged the Navy as a strategic force multiplier.

He commended the Navy’s efforts in technology absorption, #Aatmanirbharta, and ongoing operations to maintain energy security.… https://t.co/YAIlHts5y8 pic.twitter.com/yWC0VTEnkQ

— SpokespersonNavy (@indiannavy) September 30, 2026

 

Gen Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff outlined the preparedness of the Indian Army to address regional security challenges.

 

Gen Dhiraj Seth, #COAS, interacted with the Naval Commanders on 29 Sep 2026 and shared perspectives on the contemporary security environment.

The interaction focused on further strengthening Tri-Service synergy, interoperability and integrated responses to emerging security… https://t.co/YAIlHtrxIA pic.twitter.com/A5CwrXWtYb

— SpokespersonNavy (@indiannavy) September 30, 2026

 

The key deliberations during Commanders' Conference emphasised jointness, interagency coordination, optimal utilisation of resources and strategic alignment towards building a Combat Ready, Credible, Cohesive and Future Ready force.

item.title: Government Extends Operational Timelines of RELIEF (Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) Intervention to Support Exporters Amid West Asia Logistics Disruptions
item.description:
In view of the continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and its impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions, the Department of Commerce has vide Notification No.37/2026-27 dated 30 th September 2026 extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF – Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM).
Component II of the RELIEF scheme encourages exporters to obtain ECGC cover…
item.content:encoded:
In view of the continued geopolitical disruptions in West Asia and its impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions, the Department of Commerce has vide Notification No.37/2026-27 dated 30th September 2026 extended the timelines under Component II of RELIEF – Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM).

Component II of the RELIEF scheme encourages exporters to obtain ECGC cover for upcoming shipments to the specified regions, with 95% risk coverage. The component is available for Stand Alone Policies or Whole Turnover Policies obtained on or after 16 March 2026. The types of cargo covered under the benefits include Full Container Load (FCL), Less than Container Load (LCL), and Reefer containers (excluding energy shipments). Further, this component of RELIEF ensures that the premium paid by exporters shall not be increased beyond the pre-disruption level for the eligible period.

RELIEF was launched on 19 March 2026 as a targeted intervention to support Indian exporters affected by extraordinary freight escalation, heightened insurance premia and war-related export risks arising from disruptions in the Gulf and wider West Asia maritime corridor.

The above extension reflects Government of India’s commitment to ensure export resilience, sustaining trade flows and supporting exporters amid the prevailing geopolitical and logistics uncertainties.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Abhimanyu Panwar

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Commerce, has vide Notification No. 41/2026-27 dated 30th September 2026 extended the continuation of Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme upto 31st December 2026  and shall be available for exports made by Domestic Tariff Area  (DTAs) Units, Advance Authorisation (AA) Holders, Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Units and Export Oriented Units(EOUs).

The RoDTEP Scheme refunds embedded, un-rebated Central, State and local duties, taxes and levies borne on exported products — including prior-stage cumulative indirect taxes

The existing RoDTEP rates and value caps, as notified in Appendix 4R and Appendix 4RE as applicable on 30th September 2026 shall continue unchanged during the aforesaid period.

The above measure reflects the Government's commitment to provide support to the exporters by creating a level playing field in international markets vis-à-vis competing economies.

The Preparatory Phase of the campaign, from 15th September to 30th September 2026, has been completed. During this phase, the Ministry and its CPSEs completed the necessary preparations and set targets for the Implementation Phase.
During the Implementation…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Steel and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) are actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6, being conducted from 2nd October to 31st October 2026.

The Preparatory Phase of the campaign, from 15th September to 30th September 2026, has been completed. During this phase, the Ministry and its CPSEs completed the necessary preparations and set targets for the Implementation Phase.

During the Implementation Phase from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, the Ministry and its CPSEs will focus on the following activities:

  • Cleanliness Campaign: 301 cleanliness activities will be undertaken at various offices and locations.
  • Disposal of Files: Efforts will be made to dispose of 20,763 physical files and 9,056 e-files.
  • Public Grievances: Special focus will be given to the disposal of 37 pending public grievances, with the aim of bringing the pendency down to zero.

The campaign will focus on timely disposal of pending matters, including references from MPs, PMO, VIPs, Cabinet and State Governments. It will also focus on cleanliness, disposal of old files, proper record management and better use of office space.

Through SCDPM 6, the Ministry of Steel and its CPSEs will work towards reducing pendency, faster disposal of matters, better service delivery and maintaining a clean and efficient working environment.

*****

AG

item.title: On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, MoEFCC commences Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 to Institutionalize Swachhata, minimize pendency and promote scientific E-Waste Management
item.description: On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti on October 2, 2026, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) today commenced the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 with an emphasis on sanitation and hygiene. The Campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency across all its subordinate offices, autonomous organisations, regional offices and other field and outstation offices with particular focus on offices having public interface or providing public…
item.content:encoded:
On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti on October 2, 2026, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) today commenced the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 with an emphasis on sanitation and hygiene. The Campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency across all its subordinate offices, autonomous organisations, regional offices and other field and  outstation offices with particular focus on offices having public interface or providing public services.

The Campaign also seeks to promote sustained behavioural change inspired by Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), with a focus on conserving energy and water, saying no to single-use plastics, promoting sustainable food systems, reducing waste and e-waste, and encouraging the adoption of healthy and environmentally responsible lifestyles.

Special Campaign 6 is being undertaken in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). This year's Campaign focuses on “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-Waste”, along with cleanliness of campaign sites, disposal of pending matters, records management, space management, process simplification and disposal of redundant items and furniture.

MoEFCC has identified the following targets under various parameters, including cleanliness, pendency liquidation and record management for implementation during this Phase:-

Nodal Officers have been designated to coordinate and monitor the activities, ensure timely reporting and facilitate achievement of the identified targets. The Ministry will continue to monitor progress during the Implementation Phase through the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) Portal of DARPG, which will be updated regularly during this Phase.

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has said that the entire life of revered Bapu stands as a beacon of truth, non-violence, compassion and service. He noted that his life and ideals will continue to illuminate the path of humanity in every era.

The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam-

“अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।

निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी॥”

item.content:encoded:
As part of the Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026, the Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice, organised a Tree Plantation Drive on 01.10.2026 at the India International Arbitration Centre (IIAC), Vasant Kunj, New Delhi under the theme of "Ek ped Maa ke naam" on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti.

The Plantation drive was led by Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice. Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs and Chairperson  IIAC, along with senior officers / officials of the Department and IIAC participated in the event. The  Hon’ble Minister, Law Secretary &  Chairperson  IIAC, Senior officers of the Department  and IIAC planted  saplings on the IIAC campus.

“True cleanliness begins in the mind (Mann ki Swachhta),” says the Minister, recalling Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran experience

Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Minister said that cleanliness is not limited to keeping streets and public spaces clean; it must begin with a clean mind, pure thoughts and a sense of duty towards society.

He said that Swachhata Hi Seva is a people’s movement in which every individual has a role to play. He noted that 2 October, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, reminds the nation that cleanliness, discipline and service were integral to Bapu’s vision of a free and self-reliant India.

Recalling Mahatma Gandhi’s stay in Champaran in 1917, the Hon’ble Minister highlighted how Gandhiji initiated efforts towards sanitation and hygiene, which became part of a wider mass movement and contributed to addressing the grievances of indigo farmers.

The Minister said that the lesson from Champaran remains relevant today: Swachhata is a mission of empathy and shared responsibility, and not merely a campaign.

Shri Meghwal expressed confidence that, through the collective efforts of all stakeholders, IIAC would develop into a global, efficient and credible centre for arbitration. He said that the Centre should reflect the same values of transparency, discipline and service that Swachhata Hi Seva represents.

Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs and Chairperson, IIAC, said that cleanliness has two dimensions — the cleanliness of our surroundings and the cleanliness of the mind — and one remains incomplete without the other. He appreciated the efforts of IIAC and stressed that institutions have a responsibility to adopt sustainable practices and contribute meaningfully to the objectives of the Swachh Bharat Mission. He assured that IIAC is committed to establishing itself as a global, efficient and credible institution, contributing to India’s emergence as a preferred seat for international arbitration.

The event was organized with the objective of promoting cleanliness, hygiene and civic responsibility, and spreading the message that cleanliness is a collective responsibility and an essential part of a healthy and progressive society with the theme of Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath.

The event of sharmdaan was led by Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Minister of State (I/c) along with Dr Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Shri Chetan Sharma, ASG and other senior officers of the Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs including its attached offices i.e. Vidhi Sahitya Prakashan and Official Language Wing and advocates of Supreme Court and High Court, New Delhi.

During the event, he actively participated in the Shramdaan and interacted with the officials and sanitation workers present at the site.

The Hon’ble Minister emphasized the significance of the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign and the importance of maintaining cleanliness not only in government offices and public places but also in our homes and communities. He called upon all officials and employees to adopt cleanliness and hygiene as a regular habit and to contribute actively towards creating a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable environment. He also highlighted the significance of the International Day of older person which also falls on the 1st October and recognizes their valuable experience and guidance in inspiring the younger generation towards cleanliness and a better nation.

item.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code has strengthened credit discipline, improved recovery climate and contributed to ease of doing business: Harsh Malhotra, MoS, Corporate Affairs Ministry
item.description:
Minister of State for Corporate Affairs Ministry and Road Transport and Highways, Shri Harsh Malhotra inaugurated the 10th Annual Day celebrations of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, marking ten years of IBBI since its establishment on 1st October, 2016.
Chief guest Shri Harsh Malhotra in his inaugural address, observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) has strengthened credit discipline, improved the recovery…
item.content:encoded:
Minister of State for Corporate Affairs Ministry and Road Transport and Highways, Shri Harsh Malhotra inaugurated the 10th Annual Day celebrations of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, marking ten years of IBBI since its establishment on 1st October, 2016.

Chief guest Shri Harsh Malhotra in his inaugural address, observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) has strengthened credit discipline, improved the recovery climate and contributed to the ease of doing business in the country. He noted the Government’s commitment to keep the Code responsive to emerging needs, including through the recent legislative amendments, and urged all stakeholders to work towards faster and value-maximising resolutions in the decade ahead.

MoS Shri Malhotra highlighted the need for improved adoption of emerging technologies, including AI, in IBC ecosystem. He noted that the efforts should be made towards faster resolutions and value maximisation as way forward.

Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal, reflected to the role of the Adjudicating Authority in the IBC framework. He highlighted the steps being taken to reduce delays in disposal of cases and recent improvements in speedier disposal of resolution plans. He noted various areas of reforms that may be considered in coming times including revision in admission thresholds, use of mediation, sector specific carveouts, etc.

Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal shared his perspective on the evolution of insolvency jurisprudence over the decade and the issues that may be considered in coming times. He highlighted that the IBC has seen seven sets of amendments to the Code in the last ten years. While noting the constraints involved in amending laws, he appreciated that amendments to the Code and regulations are being carried out in line with emerging needs in a timely manner. While noting the positive outcomes of IBC, he emphasised the need for timelines to be respected by all stakeholders.

Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while noting the achievements of the IBC, highlighted the policy reforms undertaken to strengthen the Code, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026. He noted key aspects of the amendment act and outlined the areas for the next phase of reforms in IBC framework and ecosystem.

Welcoming the guests, Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI, reflected on the ten-year journey of the Code and the Board. He noted that IBC has enabled substantial recoveries for creditors, rescued viable businesses across sectors, and brought about a lasting change in

debtor–creditor behaviour. He observed that the ecosystem now comprises over 4,400 Insolvency Professionals and over 6,000 Registered Valuers, highlighting the responsive, participative and evidence-based approach to regulation-making being adopted by IBBI.

As part of the Tenth Annual Day celebrations, an annual publication, “Shaping the Next Decade of IBC: The Road Ahead”, was released during the event. On this occasion, winners of the 7th National Online Quiz on the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, were also felicitated.

The event was also graced by imminent dignitaries like Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal; and Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional  Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs also honoured the occasion with their gracious presence. The event was also attended by Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI; Shri Sandip Garg, whole Time Member, IBBI; and Shri Bhushan Kumar Sinha, whole Time Member, IBBI. The event witnessed participation of eminent dignitaries and key stakeholders of the insolvency ecosystem.

*****

SR/ONP

item.description:
The District Opium Office, Mandsaur Second Division, Mandsaur, organised an awareness programme under “ Mission Yuva Raksha ” at Sharda Public School, Pipliya Mandi, with the objective of sensitizing students about the harmful effects of drug abuse and creating awareness regarding the importance of a drug-free life.
At the beginning of the programme, the participants were provided with information about the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), its role, functions and…
item.content:encoded:
The District Opium Office, Mandsaur Second Division, Mandsaur, organised an awareness programme under “Mission Yuva Raksha” at Sharda Public School, Pipliya Mandi, with the objective of sensitizing students about the harmful effects of drug abuse and creating awareness regarding the importance of a drug-free life.

At the beginning of the programme, the participants were provided with information about the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), its role, functions and contribution towards prevention of drug abuse and enforcement of narcotics-related laws.

Thereafter, a Question-and-Answer Competition was organized to make the awareness activities more effective, interactive and participatory. Through the competition, students were sensitized about the manner in which drug abuse can adversely affect an individual’s physical and mental health, family life, education, career and overall future. Important information was also shared regarding the harmful effects of various addictive substances, preventive measures and the role of youth in building a drug-free society.

At the conclusion of the programme, the participating students and other participants took a Drug-Free India Pledge, committing themselves to staying away from drugs and contributing actively towards the creation of a healthy and drug-free society.

The programme was successfully conducted with the coordination and cooperation of the Principal of Sharda Public School, Pipliya Mandi. Approx 150 students participated enthusiastically in the programme, and the participants gave highly positive and encouraging feedback regarding the awareness activities.

The programme aimed to create awareness among young people about the dangers of drug abuse and to motivate them to contribute towards building a drug-free, healthy and responsible society. The programme concluded successfully with active participation and positive engagement from the students.

item.title: Cooperation between the Nalanda University and the CSIR-Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit for research and capacity-building in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage
item.description: Nālandā University (NU) and the CSIR–Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit have signed a Memorandum of Understanding today to establish a structured collaboration for academic, research and capacity-building cooperation in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage, including Traditional Cultural Expressions (TCEs). The MoU was signed by Prof. Sachin Chaturvedi, Vice Chancellor, Nālandā University and Dr.…
item.content:encoded:
Nālandā University (NU) and the CSIR–Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit have signed a Memorandum of Understanding today to establish a structured collaboration for academic, research and capacity-building cooperation in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage, including Traditional Cultural Expressions (TCEs). The MoU was signed by Prof. Sachin Chaturvedi, Vice Chancellor, Nālandā University and Dr. Viswajanani J Sattigeri, Scientist-H and Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit, in the presence of the faculty members of the Nālandā University and senior officials of the CSIR-TKDL Unit.

 

Through the collaboration, the two organizations, Nālandā University and CSIR-TKDL Unit shall draw together their individual strengths to address their common interests on matters of TK, IPR, cultural heritage including the TCEs of Bihar. The cooperation shall focus on academic and research activities and intellectual exchanges, trainings, student internship and exchange visits and networking, among others.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Chaturvedi, Vice-Chancellor, Nālandā University, appreciated the significant efforts of the CSIR on the TKDL and its role in preventing the misappropriation India’s TK. He further noted that this collaboration would strengthen efforts to identify, document and disseminate TK and TCEs while creating greater awareness about IPRs and also training the younger generation on the matter. He highlighted the importance of systematically documenting, preserving, and making TK across subject areas such as ecological knoweldge of the communities, folklore, music, and others. He also opined that the TK may be made accessible in a manner that safeguards the interests of knowledge holders and communities, as well as the organizations’ commitment to evidence based R&D in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS). He observed that the collaboration with TKDL would provide an important platform for integrating TK with contemporary academic research, documentation, IP awareness and interdisciplinary scholarship.

Dr. Sattigeri, Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit stated that India has been leading globally on all matters of TK, be it policies or initiatives such as the TKDL. She stated that the ancient Nālandā University speaks of the importance of collaboration between organizations, both nationally and internationally. This collaboration between CSIR-TKDL Unit with the new Nālandā University is envisaged to rejuvenate the past glory of Nalanda as both educational and research hub, with specific focus on the cultural heritage of India, and particularly, Bihar. 

The Parties are confident that the collaboration between Nālandā University and CSIR-TKDL Unit will contribute to the attainment of the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and National IPR Policy 2016 on TK, IPR and cultural heritage.

About Nālandā University:

Nālandā University has been established as an International University of “National Importance” under the aegis of the Ministry of External Affairs, Govt of India, at Rajgir, District-Nalanda, Bihar. The objectives of Nālandā University, deriving on its ancient heritage value and strong international cooperation,  are focused on the pursuit of intellectual, philosophical, historical and spiritual studies and others. The revival of Nālandā University aims at improving regional understanding and the appreciation of one another’s heritage and history, to build a community of learning where students, scholars, researchers and academicians can work together symbolizing the spirituality that unites all mankind.

About TKDL:

The TKDL database, first of its kind worldwide, was established in 2001 by the Government of India, through a collaboration between CSIR and Ministry of AYUSH. The key objective of the TKDL is to prevent the erroneous grant of patents on Indian traditional knowledge (TK) and deter misappropriation of the country’s heritage. Currently, the TKDL contains information on over 5.2 lakh formulations and practices of Indian Systems of Medicine such as Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa Rigpa as well as Yoga from the traditional texts. The TK information from diverse languages and subject areas are transcribed into value-added information correlated with modern terminologies.

The TKDL information is presented in a digitized format in five international languages including English, German, French, Japanese and Spanish, therein breaking language and format barriers for ease of use by patent examiners. Currently, the TKDL database is available to 18 international patent offices through Non-Disclosure Agreements.

The TKDL is a global benchmark in the defensive protection of traditional knowledge and has been successful in protecting India’s interest against any possible misuse of its heritage. The impact has been significant, with over 375 patent applications world-over being revoked, rejected, amended, withdrawn or abandoned, based on the prior art evidences presented from the TKDL database.

********

NKR/AK/NM
