The activities aimed to foster a culture of cleanliness and collective responsibility while encouraging sustainable practices in the workplace and the wider community.
As part of the initiatives, and array of…
item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, October 1, 2026:

 

The Geological Survey of India (GSI), Eastern Region, Kolkata, undertook a series of Swachhata initiatives today, to promote cleanliness, hygiene, environmental awareness and responsible waste management among its officers and staff. The activities aimed to foster a culture of cleanliness and collective responsibility while encouraging sustainable practices in the workplace and the wider community.

 

As part of the initiatives, and array of activities, including cleanliness drives, Shramdaan, cleaning and beautification of office premises, awareness programmes on sanitation and hygiene, proper waste disposal, environmental conservation activities, and the felicitation and health check-up of Safai Mitras, were organised. Officers and staff actively participated in the activities, reaffirming their commitment to maintaining a clean, healthy and hygienic workplace.

 

Special emphasis was laid on maintaining cleanliness in office premises, laboratories and common areas, promoting responsible waste management and reducing the use of single-use plastics. Plantation initiatives and environmental awareness activities were also undertaken to contribute towards creating a cleaner and greener workplace.

 

Speaking on the occasion, Additional Director General and Head of Department, GSI, Eastern Region, Shri Lalit Mohan Singh Maura, appreciated the enthusiastic participation of the officers and staff in the Swachhata initiatives. He emphasised that cleanliness should become an integral part of everyday life and workplace culture rather than remain limited to periodic campaigns.

 

As part of its environmental responsibility initiatives, GSI, Eastern Region, also organised an e-waste collection drive, encouraging citizens to responsibly dispose of discarded electronic items. The drive aimed to promote awareness about sustainable e-waste management and encourage environmentally responsible practices for a cleaner and greener environment.

 

In another initiative under the “Swachh Pathshala – Swachhata Gyan Yatra” campaign, a team from the State Unit of SU: WBAN, GSI, Eastern Region, led by DDG, Dr. Santanu Bhattacharjee visited AG Primary School, Baisakhi. With the support of Safai Mitras of GSI, Eastern Region, the initiative focused on promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental awareness among students and strengthening efforts towards creating a cleaner and healthier school environment.

 

The Swachhata initiatives provided an opportunity to sensitise employees and the wider community about the importance of maintaining cleanliness not only in workplaces but also in homes, schools and public spaces. The activities reinforced the message that cleanliness is a continuous collective responsibility that requires active participation and sustained efforts from every individual.

 

 

*****************

item.content:encoded:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu in her message on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti says: -

“On behalf of all citizens, I pay my respectful tribute to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti.

Gandhiji’s life and ideals are widely respected by the global community. Today, an atmosphere of war and conflict prevails in many parts of the world, affecting all nations. In these circumstances, Mahatma Gandhi’s message of peace and non-violence becomes even more relevant.

Our country is advancing towards the national goal of becoming Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. In this journey, priority is being given to the values ​​of empathy and inclusion to ensure that no citizen is deprived of the benefits of development. This vision reflects the spirit of Mahatma Gandhi’s ideal of ‘Sarvodaya’, based on the principle of the welfare and upliftment of all.

On the auspicious occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, let us reaffirm our commitment to building an empowered, developed and Atmanirbhar Bharat through our ethical conduct and active participation”.

 

****

item.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan calls for making cleanliness a part of everyday public behaviour, not limiting it to campaigns
item.description: Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today emphasised that cleanliness should not remain confined to the duration of a campaign, but should become an integral part of people’s behaviour and everyday lives. Addressing a virtual meeting with the Secretaries and senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and the Ministry of Rural Development, he called for active participation by officials and employees in…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today emphasised that cleanliness should not remain confined to the duration of a campaign, but should become an integral part of people’s behaviour and everyday lives. Addressing a virtual meeting with the Secretaries and senior officials of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and the Ministry of Rural Development, he called for active participation by officials and employees in cleanliness activities and urged them to lead by example. He also stressed the need to continuously strengthen awareness and participation around cleanliness in offices, workplaces, field offices and rural areas. Shri Chouhan said that sustained efforts, rather than activities limited to a defined campaign period, are essential to make cleanliness a lasting practice and a shared responsibility across institutions and communities.

Shri Chouhan said that Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 requires extensive public participation to ensure that cleanliness activities are both effective and sustainable. He directed officers and employees to give priority to cleanliness within their respective areas of work and to take the initiative themselves rather than treating such activities merely as an official requirement. He placed particular emphasis on effectively connecting rural areas, panchayats and field-level offices with cleanliness activities and ensuring the participation of farmers, rural communities, sanitation workers, the media and other relevant stakeholders. He stressed that the involvement of these groups is important for taking cleanliness efforts beyond government offices and making them more visible and meaningful at the grassroots level. Active participation by all concerned, he said, would help create greater awareness and encourage cleanliness to become part of routine practices in communities.

The Union Minister directed that cleanliness activities should not be reduced to a formality, but should produce clear and measurable outcomes. He emphasised the need for systematic documentation of the work undertaken as part of the campaign so that the results and impact of the activities can be properly assessed. Wherever possible, he called for achievements to be recorded through before-and-after photographs, enabling the changes brought about through cleanliness initiatives to be clearly documented. He stressed that such documentation would help demonstrate the tangible results of the campaign and ensure that the work undertaken is properly recorded for future review. The focus, he said, should remain on visible improvements, measurable outcomes and sustained efforts rather than simply completing activities within the stipulated campaign period.

During the meeting, Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare; Dr Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR); Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development; and Shri P Narhari, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, briefed the Union Minister on cleanliness activities being undertaken by their respective departments and shared details of their forthcoming action plans. The officials outlined the work already undertaken as well as the proposed activities and priorities for the next phase. Their presentations covered the participation of officials and employees, activities at field and institutional levels, and measures being planned to further strengthen cleanliness efforts across the departments and their associated offices and institutions.

The meeting was informed about various activities undertaken by the Department of Agriculture under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 from September 16 to October 2. These included cleanliness pledges, Swachh Pathshala activities, participation of young people, solid waste management, cleanliness drives across office premises, and intensive cleaning of corridors, canteens and toilets at headquarters and field offices. Activities also included the disposal of old furniture and electronic waste as part of efforts to improve cleanliness and make more effective use of available office space. The meeting was also informed about initiatives undertaken to honour sanitation workers, conduct health check-ups for them and organise various activities for their children. These efforts were aimed at recognising the contribution of sanitation workers while also supporting their welfare and encouraging wider participation in cleanliness-related activities. The meeting also reviewed efforts to involve employees directly in cleanliness work and to strengthen awareness around responsible waste management.

It was informed during the meeting that the disposal and auction of old furniture and electronic waste had generated revenue of approximately Rs 15 lakh. In addition, officials and employees participated in collective cleanliness drives through shramdaan (volunteering), contributing their time and effort to activities undertaken as part of the campaign. A plan was also shared to take forward activities under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. The initiatives discussed during the meeting reflected efforts to combine cleanliness activities with responsible disposal of unused material, greater participation by officials and employees, and activities aimed at creating a cleaner and more organised working environment. The revenue generated through the disposal and auction of old furniture and electronic waste also highlighted the value of identifying and appropriately disposing of material that is no longer required.

Regarding the Special Campaign to be conducted from October 2 to October 31, 2026, all departments shared details of the targets set for the disposal of pending files and cases, reduction in the number of pending matters, disposal of scrap and e-waste, better utilisation of office space and removal of unusable material. As part of the campaign, unused computers, printers and other electronic equipment will be identified and processed for disposal in accordance with the prescribed rules and procedures. The progress made against the identified targets will be reviewed regularly, while achievements will be appropriately documented. The exercise will focus not only on physical cleanliness but also on improving the efficiency and organisation of offices by addressing pending matters, removing redundant material and ensuring better use of available space. Regular monitoring and documentation will help departments assess progress against their respective targets and record the outcomes of the campaign in a systematic manner.

The Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) informed the meeting that a large-scale cleanliness campaign was being conducted at the Pusa campus, with officers, employees and students actively participating in the activities. Similar cleanliness-related activities are also being conducted across all ICAR institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). Through the KVK network, efforts are being made to connect farmers and rural communities with cleanliness, waste management and environmental awareness. These activities are intended to extend the message of cleanliness beyond institutional premises and strengthen awareness among farming and rural communities. The participation of students, employees, officers, farmers and rural communities is also helping to create wider engagement with cleanliness and responsible waste management at different levels. The meeting was informed that the network of ICAR institutions and KVKs is being used to support these efforts and encourage greater awareness of cleanliness and environmental responsibility among people in rural areas.

Shri Chouhan called upon all concerned officers and employees not to limit cleanliness to the prescribed duration of the campaign, but to make it a continuous part of everyday behaviour in offices, villages, panchayats and workplaces. He said the success of a cleanliness campaign should not be measured only by the physical cleaning of premises. Its real impact must be reflected through behavioural change, public participation and sustainable outcomes that continue beyond the campaign period. He emphasised that cleanliness should become a regular practice and a shared responsibility rather than an activity undertaken only during designated campaigns. By encouraging participation, maintaining awareness and ensuring measurable and lasting results, cleanliness efforts can have a sustained impact across workplaces, rural areas and communities. The Union Minister stressed that the objective should ultimately be to make cleanliness an enduring part of daily life and public behaviour.

***

SS/MS/MK

item.title: High-Level Jordanian Delegation Meets Secretary (Textiles) in New Delhi
item.description:
A high-level delegation from the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, led by H.E. Mr. Zaher Al Qatarneh, Secretary-General, Ministry of Investment, met Ms. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary (Textiles), Government of India, at the Ministry of Textiles, New Delhi, today to discuss avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation in textiles and apparel sector.
The Jordanian delegation included H.E. Mr. Yousef Abdelghani, Ambassador of Jordan to India; Ms. Haya Iman, Director of Investment Promotion;…
item.content:encoded:
A high-level delegation from the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, led by H.E. Mr. Zaher Al Qatarneh, Secretary-General, Ministry of Investment, met Ms. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary (Textiles), Government of India, at the Ministry of Textiles, New Delhi, today to discuss avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation in textiles and apparel sector.

The Jordanian delegation included H.E. Mr. Yousef Abdelghani, Ambassador of Jordan to India; Ms. Haya Iman, Director of Investment Promotion; and Ms. Noor Murad, Investment Promotion Officer. Senior officials from the Ministry of Textiles and the Ministry of External Affairs, along with representatives of the textile industry, also participated in the meeting.

The discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, sourcing, investment and industry partnerships including Joint Ventures in the sector. Jordan’s textile and apparel imports from the world stood at around USD 2 billion in 2025, while India’s exports to Jordan were around USD 48 million, accounting for a 2.4% share and making India Jordan’s fourth-largest supplier.

The Indian side highlighted the potential for enhanced cooperation in apparels, fabrics, technical textiles, cotton textiles and made-ups, including opportunities for greater sourcing, investment and industry partnerships.

The two sides also explored opportunities for strengthening institutional and knowledge partnerships between leading fashion, design and textile institutions in India and Jordan, including student and faculty exchanges, design innovation and cooperation in AI-enabled fashion forecasting.

Both sides also discussed the possibility of reinvigorating the established institutional mechanism  to facilitate structured and sustained engagement and follow-up on identified areas of cooperation in textiles & apparel.

The meeting concluded on a positive note, with both sides agreeing to bilaterally engage and take forward the areas of cooperation identified during the discussions.

********

MAM/VN

item.title: Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Chaired Review meeting on National Surveillance Programme for Aquatic Animal Diseases (NSPAAD)
item.description:
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, MoFAH&D, GoI chaired review meeting on National Surveillance Programme for Aquatic Animal Diseases (NSPAAD) on 1 st October 2026 in New Delhi . The meeting focused on strengthening aquatic animal health surveillance through a review of NSPAAD Phase-I and Phase-II, assessment of the Disease Report App, and discussions on the way forward.
The Review meeting was held through video conference and witnessed…
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, MoFAH&D, GoI chaired review meeting on National Surveillance Programme for Aquatic Animal Diseases (NSPAAD) on 1st October 2026 in New Delhi. The meeting focused on strengthening aquatic animal health surveillance through a review of NSPAAD Phase-I and Phase-II, assessment of the Disease Report App, and discussions on the way forward.

The Review meeting was held through video conference and witnessed participation from State fisheries department, fisheries ICAR institutions including ICAR- National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), Export Inspection Council (EIC), Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA), National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) and other relevant fisheries stakeholders.

During the review meeting, Dr Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary (Fisheries), Department of Fisheries, MoFAH&D highlighted the role of NSPAAD program in strengthening disease diagnostics, surveillance networks and laboratory infrastructure to achieve export targets. The Secretary stressed the need for stronger engagement of State Governments, improved convergence among stakeholders and wider adoption of disease reporting mechanisms to enhance disease preparedness and safeguard export competitiveness. He noted that, implemented under PMMSY, the National Surveillance Programme for Aquatic Animal Diseases (NSPAAD) is being executed in two phases to establish a robust aquatic animal disease surveillance and reporting framework in the country. He further suggested examining the transition of NSPAAD from a project-based intervention to a long-term programme under PMMSY to ensure continuity, institutionalization and sustained support for aquatic animal health management in the country. The secretary also sought suggestions from ICAR scientists, state officials to further improve the program outreach.

The stakeholders highlighted the critical role of aquatic animal disease surveillance in sustaining aquaculture growth and supporting India’s expanding seafood exports. Representatives from MPEDA and EIC emphasized the need for closer convergence with NSPAAD to strengthen disease monitoring, ensure compliance with international sanitary requirements and facilitate access to emerging export markets. EIC informed that regular disease reporting and coordinated engagement among regulatory agencies have contributed to easing export certification requirements in key markets such as the Republic of Korea.

ICAR, NFDB, CAA and participating States underscored the need to institutionalize NSPAAD as a long-term programme, strengthen State-level disease surveillance systems and expand farmer participation through the ReportFishDisease mobile application. States shared progress in laboratory strengthening, disease diagnostics, awareness generation and farmer outreach, while also highlighting the need for greater adoption of disease reporting tools and enhanced capacity building at the grassroots level. Stakeholders further recommended leveraging Matsya Seva Kendras, Sagar Mitras and fisheries extension networks to improve disease reporting, early warning and rapid response mechanisms across the country.

India’s seafood exports have more than doubled over the past decade, increasing from ₹30,213 crore in FY 2013-14 to ₹73,890.46 crore in FY 2025-26, reinforcing the country’s position as one of the world’s leading seafood exporters. Recognizing that aquatic animal health is integral to export competitiveness, the Department is simultaneously strengthening disease surveillance, biosecurity and compliance systems to ensure sustainable growth, improved market access and greater acceptance of Indian seafood products in global markets.

The Department is implementing the National Surveillance Programme for Aquatic Animal Diseases (NSPAAD) as the country’s flagship aquatic animal disease surveillance initiative. Operational since 2013 and expanded to pan-India coverage under PMMSY since 2022, the programme has established a national network of aquatic animal health laboratories, strengthened diagnostic capacity for WOAH-listed and emerging pathogens, and institutionalised a transparent disease reporting framework aligned with international standards. NSPAAD has conducted over 1,100 awareness programmes covering nearly 48,000 fish farmers and 177 training programmes for stakeholders, while the multilingual ReportFishDisease mobile application has enabled timely reporting of disease incidences and rapid scientific response. The programme has facilitated the first-time detection and confirmation of 15 emerging and exotic aquatic animal diseases in the country, strengthened early warning and response mechanisms, and significantly enhanced India’s credibility in international aquatic animal health reporting, thereby supporting the sustainability, resilience and export readiness of the fisheries sector.

 

*********

JP

item.title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Hosts Water Warriors from Across India at His Residence
item.description: Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Paatil today interacted with Water Conservation Warriors and River Rejuvenation Warriors from different parts of the country who have been leading grassroots initiatives in water conservation, river and water-body rejuvenation and environmental protection. The interaction, organised by the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) under Namami Gange, provided a platform for these grassroots champions to share their journeys, learn from one another and…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Paatil today interacted with Water Conservation Warriors and River Rejuvenation Warriors from different parts of the country who have been leading grassroots initiatives in water conservation, river and water-body rejuvenation and environmental protection. The interaction, organised by the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) under Namami Gange, provided a platform for these grassroots champions to share their journeys, learn from one another and discuss how successful community-led models can be strengthened and replicated across the country.

The participants shared first-hand experiences of restoring rivers and ponds, undertaking Shramdaan, promoting rainwater harvesting, removing plastic and other waste near water bodies, carrying out plantation drives and mobilising women, youth, volunteers and local communities. Their stories highlighted how individual initiative, when combined with collective action and community ownership, can translate into visible and sustained improvements on the ground.

Among those who shared their work was Ramveer Tanwar, popularly known as the ‘Pondman of India’, who spoke about rejuvenating more than 100 ponds and establishing 10 mini urban forests. Kamini Kumari from Bihar highlighted her initiative in mobilising 500 women to construct 500 groundwater recharge pits along the Baya River in a single day, linking water conservation with groundwater recharge, sustainable agriculture and livelihood opportunities for women.

Surendra Singh Chaudhary, popularly known as ‘Bittu Tabahi’, shared his journey of taking up the clean-up of the polluted Ajnar River at Biaora in Rajgarh district of Madhya Pradesh. A young B.Sc. student, he began the effort on 26 January 2026 and undertook hands-on removal of plastic, weeds, sludge and other waste from the river, largely through his own initiative. His work, which began as a local effort, drew wider public attention and has inspired greater participation in the cleaning and restoration of local water bodies.

Anand Malligavad from Bengaluru spoke about his work in restoring 33 lakes and planting more than one lakh native trees. Jagdish Singh Negi from Uttarakhand shared his work in water conservation, forest restoration and converting plastic waste into eco-bricks. Subham Kumar highlighted the role of youth and volunteers in river cleanliness and his efforts to mobilise communities to remove more than 2.47 lakh kilograms of waste from the banks of the Ganga and its tributaries.

The interaction also highlighted the role of water volunteers and community groups in sustaining clean rivers and ghats. Akash Yadav from Uttar Pradesh shared how his 15-member volunteer group has contributed to the rejuvenation of four Ganga ghats and the removal of more than one tonne of plastic waste. Dr. Sanjivini Sharma from Kanpur spoke about mobilising more than 900 volunteers for Ganga conservation campaigns and removing over 120 metric tonnes of waste, besides promoting plastic recycling, reuse of discarded materials and livelihood opportunities for women through community-led waste management.

The other water warriors included Ms. Kusum Gildiyal, Sh. Jagdish Negi, Ms. Rama Tiwari, Dr. Suman Pandey, Ms. Kumari Sunita Singh, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Singh, Sh. Ajay Kumar Tivare, Sh. Nitish Kumar Singh, Sh. Kamlesh Bhai Shastri, Sh. Sandeep Chaudhary, Ms. Sirkunwar, Ms. Phoolbati and Sh. Vivek Bhat. The work of these warriors were highly appreciated by Hon’ble Minister Jal Shakti.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Archana Varma, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, appreciated the role played by the Water Warriors in taking the message of water conservation and cleanliness beyond government programmes and into communities. She praised their ability to bring people together and mobilise collective action around rivers, ponds and other water bodies, and emphasised that such citizen-led participation is essential for sustaining water conservation and river rejuvenation efforts over the long term.

Addressing the participants, Shri C. R. Paatil congratulated them for their commitment and said that listening directly to their experiences was an opportunity to understand the scale, diversity and impact of grassroots action taking place across the country. He acknowledged that many of them had worked through difficult local circumstances and had nevertheless succeeded in bringing people together for the protection of water and the environment. Referring to the larger national movement, Shri Paatil said that under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, water conservation has evolved into a nationwide Jan Andolan anchored in Jan Bhagidari. He said that the Prime Minister's consistent emphasis on conserving every drop of water has inspired citizens and communities across the country to take ownership of water conservation, and that the work of the Water Warriors and reflects this spirit of collective action.

The Minister emphasized that the next step should be to translate this energy into focused, measurable and sustained outcomes. He encouraged the participants to identify specific rivers, ponds, ghats and other water bodies, set clear targets and demonstrate visible improvement on the ground. He also stressed the importance of involving women, youth, schoolchildren, senior citizens and other sections of society so that water conservation and cleanliness become enduring people’s movements rather than one-time activities.

Shri Paatil encouraged the Water Warriors to remain connected with one another, regularly share their work and learn from successful models being implemented in different parts of the country. He said that good local initiatives should not remain confined to one place, but should be adapted and expanded wherever they can help communities address similar challenges.

The Water Warriors expressed happiness at being invited by the Minister to his residence and at the opportunity to share their stories directly with him. They also valued the chance to interact with fellow grassroots champions from different parts of India, exchange experiences, understand different approaches to community mobilisation and explore ways to remain connected and collaborate in future.

The interaction reaffirmed that protecting rivers and conserving water cannot be achieved through infrastructure and government programmes alone. Sustained Jan Bhagidari, Shramdaan, responsible community behaviour and committed grassroots leadership are equally important. The experiences shared during the meeting demonstrated how citizens, volunteers and local communities can become powerful partners in the national effort for clean rivers, conserved water resources and a cleaner, more sustainable environment.

***

ND/HM

item.title: Postcard completed a 157-year journey: First Postcard was issued in Austria on October 1, 1869- Postmaster General Krishna Kumar Yadav
item.description: The knock of the Postman at the doorstep and the Postcard handed over in his hands once filled the entire family with anticipation. A few words written on a postcard felt like the voice of a loved one living far away. That is why the postcard became more than just a piece of paper—it evolved into a medium that connected emotions and relationships. With time, modes of communication continued to evolve. Telephone, mobile phones, the internet and social media began delivering messages within…
item.content:encoded:
The knock of the Postman at the doorstep and the Postcard handed over in his hands once filled the entire family with anticipation. A few words written on a postcard felt like the voice of a loved one living far away. That is why the postcard became more than just a piece of paper—it evolved into a medium that connected emotions and relationships. With time, modes of communication continued to evolve. Telephone, mobile phones, the internet and social media began delivering messages within seconds. Yet, the historical and emotional memories associated with postcards continue to endure. From politicians to litterateurs and social reformers, many have made effective use of postcards to convey their messages and ideas. On October 1, 2026, the postcard marked 157 years of its existence globally. Postmaster General of North Gujarat Region, Shri Krishna Kumar Yadav, said that the world's first postcard was issued in Austria on October 1, 1869.

Regarding the story behind this, Senior Officer of Indian Postal Service Shri Krishna Kumar Yadav, Postmaster General said that the idea for the postcard first occurred to an Austrian representative named Kolbensteiner, who shared it with Dr. Emanuel Herrmann, a professor of economics at the Military Academy in Wiener Neustadt. Finding the idea quite appealing, Dr. Herrmann wrote an article about it in a newspaper on January 26, 1869. The Austrian Postal Authority acted swiftly on the idea, and the first postcard was issued on October 1, 1869, marking the beginning of the postcard’s journey around the world. The world’s first postcard was yellow in colour, measuring 122 mm in length and 85 mm in width. One side was designated for writing the recipient’s address, while the other side was left blank for writing the message.

Renowned as distinguished writer, Postmaster General Shri Krishna Kumar Yadav mentioned in his book "India Post : 150 Glorious Years" that the first postcard in India was issued in 1879. Printed in a light brown colour, the postcard was priced at 3 paise and bore the inscription “East India Postcard.” The Royal Coat of Arms of Great Britain was printed in the centre, while the upper-right corner featured a red-brown portrait of Queen Victoria wearing a crown. This medium of expression became so popular among the people that postcards worth approximately ₹7.5 lakh were sold during the first three quarters of the year alone.

It is noteworthy that until now, four types of postcards—Meghdoot postcards, ordinary postcards, printed postcards, and competition postcards—were available at post offices, priced at 25 paise, 50 paise, ₹6, and ₹10, respectively. With effect from December 20, 2024, all these categories have been merged into a single “Postcard” category.

It is worth mention that More than 1.11 crore postcards were written by people associated with the cooperative sector in Gujarat to express gratitude to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, setting a new Guinness World Record in the process. In all, 1,11,75,000 postcards were written to the PM, thanking him for GST reforms and several other measures. Postmaster General Shri Krishna Kumar Yadav said that the campaign emerged as a remarkable example of the power of postcards as a medium of collective expression and public participation. This initiative was undertaken under the aegis of the Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation in collaboration with Department of Posts at Gujarat. For the first time in the world such a large number of postcards were written simultaneously, and Guinness World Records officials awarded a certificate for the achievement on 14 October, 2025 after the counting at a venue on Sabarmati Riverfront. According to Guinness World Records, the previous record was held by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) / Section Water (Switzerland) Basel, Switzerland with 6,666 postcards.

item.title: Industry-Academia Synergy Takes Centre Stage at 85th CSIR Foundation Day Celebration at CSIR-CSMCRI
item.description:
CSIR-Central Salt & Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSIR-CSMCRI), Bhavnagar, celebrated the 85th Foundation Day of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) on October 1, 2026, with enthusiasm and scientific spirit. The programme commenced with the National Song and…
item.content:encoded:
CSIR-Central Salt & Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSIR-CSMCRI), Bhavnagar, celebrated the 85th Foundation Day of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) on October 1, 2026, with enthusiasm and scientific spirit. The event brought together scientists, staff members, students, and distinguished guests to commemorate the significant milestone in the history of India's premier scientific research organization.

The programme commenced with the National Song and the CSIR Song, followed by welcome address by Dr. J. R. Chunawala, Chief Coordinator of the Foundation Day Celebration Committee. Delivering the distinguished lecture, Mr. Amit Raj Sinha, Managing Director and CEO of Sigachi Industries, Hyderabad, shared insights on industry-driven innovation and the role of research institutions in fostering technological advancement. The Foundation Day Lecture was delivered by Chief Guest Mr. Digvijaysinh D. Jadeja, IAS, Mission Director, Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission, Gandhinagar, who emphasized the importance of science, biotechnology, and innovation in achieving sustainable growth.

A highlight of the programme was the felicitation ceremony and the release of the CSIR-CSMCRI Annual Report 2025-26. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Arup Ghosh, Director, CSIR-CSMCRI, reflected on the institute's scientific achievements and ongoing contributions in the areas of salt science, marine chemicals, advanced materials, biotechnology, and sustainable technologies. He highlighted the importance of CSIR's contributions to national development and the challenges ahead.

Dr. Kanti Bhooshan Pandey, a principal scientist at CSIR-CSMCRI informed that the celebrations also included an Open Day programme, providing visitors and schools students under CSIR-Jigyasa program, coordinated by Dr. D.R. Chaudhary with an opportunity to learn about the institute's research activities, facilities, and technologies developed for societal and industrial benefit. The event concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Mr. Biranchi Sarang, Controller of Administration with the remark that the celebrations underscored CSIR's unwavering commitment to scientific excellence, societal outreach, and visionary leadership. Dr. Shilpi Kushwaha anchored the event.

item.title: BHASHINI Showcases Multilingual AI Solutions at GatiSheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0
item.description: The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India , participated as an Associate Partner in the three-day national exhibition “GatiSheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0” , held from 28 to 30 September 2026 in Jammu. The exhibition brought together government departments, institutions and organisations to showcase initiatives, technologies and citizen-centric services contributing to the…
item.content:encoded:
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, participated as an Associate Partner in the three-day national exhibition “GatiSheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0”, held from 28 to 30 September 2026 in Jammu. The exhibition brought together government departments, institutions and organisations to showcase initiatives, technologies and citizen-centric services contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

BHASHINI showcased its multilingual language technology ecosystem through an exhibition stall, providing visitors with an opportunity to experience how Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based language technologies can support multilingual digital access and citizen-facing services. The participation also provided a platform to engage with government stakeholders, students, technology enthusiasts, industry representatives and members of the public.

As part of the exhibition, the BHASHINI team conducted live demonstrations of its multilingual Language AI capabilities and use cases, showcasing applications across governance, citizen services, access to justice and multilingual digital communication. The demonstrations highlighted how technologies such as speech recognition, speech synthesis, translation, transliteration and voice-enabled interaction can be integrated into digital services to enable more accessible and inclusive interactions across languages.

The BHASHINI stall witnessed good footfall and strong visitor engagement throughout the three-day exhibition. Visitors interacted with the team, explored the BHASHINI application and participated in the selfie booth, providing an opportunity to create greater awareness about BHASHINI’s multilingual language technologies and their applications in everyday digital services.

The exhibition also facilitated interactions with stakeholders from diverse sectors, enabling discussions around Language AI, multilingual digital services and potential avenues for institutional outreach and collaboration. The engagement provided opportunities to understand stakeholder requirements and explore areas where BHASHINI’s language technologies could support wider adoption of multilingual digital services.

The participation also witnessed visits by dignitaries, including Shri Jugal Kishore Sharma, Hon’ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Jammu & Kashmir, and Ms. Ansuya Jamwal, Additional Deputy Commissioner, Jammu, who visited the BHASHINI stall and interacted with the team. The presentation of a memento to BHASHINI in recognition of its association as an Associate Partner during the concluding day marked a significant acknowledgement of its participation in the exhibition.

The three-day engagement at GatiSheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0 provided BHASHINI with an opportunity to demonstrate the role of Language AI in enabling inclusive digital governance, while strengthening awareness of its multilingual technology ecosystem among citizens and stakeholders in the region.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is building a national ecosystem for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, and enables the integration of Language AI capabilities across government and public-facing digital services. Its ecosystem includes technologies for translation, speech recognition, speech synthesis, transliteration and other language services, helping make digital information and services more accessible across India’s linguistic diversity.

   ****

Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma / Dhanya Ranjan

item.title: Department of Health Research to participate in Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026 to promote Swachhata and reduce pendency
item.description:
Reaffirming its commitment to Swachhata, the Department of Health Research (DHR) will undertake Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. The Campaign will focus on institutionalising cleanliness, reducing pendency, improving record management and promoting the efficient utilisation of office resources across DHR, ICMR Headquarters and its 27 Institutes across the country.
As part of the ongoing Preparatory Phase from 15th to 30th September, 2026, the Department has completed…
item.content:encoded:
Reaffirming its commitment to Swachhata, the Department of Health Research (DHR) will undertake Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. The Campaign will focus on institutionalising cleanliness, reducing pendency, improving record management and promoting the efficient utilisation of office resources across DHR, ICMR Headquarters and its 27 Institutes across the country.

As part of the ongoing Preparatory Phase from 15th to 30th September, 2026, the Department has completed the preliminary exercise for identifying suitable locations for cleanliness drives, assessing requirements for space management and beautification of office premises, identifying scrap and redundant items for disposal in accordance with the applicable provisions and identifying pending references.

The Department has also undertaken a review of its record management practices, including identification of files and records due for reviewing and weeding, as well as e-files requiring closure, in accordance with the prescribed procedures.

With the preparatory exercise providing a clear roadmap for focused interventions, the Department is gearing up for the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. During the Campaign period, the identified targets will be taken up in a time-bound manner, with emphasis on cleanliness and space management, disposal of e-waste and redundant items, liquidation of identified pendency, simplification of processes and strengthening of record management.

The progress of the Campaign will be regularly monitored by the Nodal Officer to ensure timely implementation of the identified activities and achievement of the Campaign objectives.

***

SR/PY

item.title: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs concludes Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026 with active participation and collective commitment towards cleanliness
item.description:
The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (MoPA) actively participated in the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) Campaign 2026, observed from 17th September to 2nd October 2026 across Ministries and Departments of the Government of India. The campaign focused on promoting cleanliness, hygiene, civic responsibility, environmental responsibility and public participation towards realizing the vision of a Swachh Bharat.
The campaign commenced on 17th September 2026, with Secretary,…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (MoPA) actively participated in the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) Campaign 2026, observed from 17th September to 2nd October 2026 across Ministries and Departments of the Government of India. The campaign focused on promoting cleanliness, hygiene, civic responsibility, environmental responsibility and public participation towards realizing the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

The campaign commenced on 17th September 2026, with Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal, administering the Swachhata Pledge to all officers and officials of the Ministry. During the fortnight, the Ministry undertook a series of activities in accordance with its action plan, including special cleanliness drives and Shramdaan, cleanliness inspections by senior officers, the “Swachh Air” initiative with placement of indoor plants in Sections and officers’ cabins, health check-up of Safai Mitras, and thanking and felicitation of Safai Mitras.

The campaign also emphasized environmental responsibility through plantation activities under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam Abhiyan”, alongside efforts to strengthen cleanliness and hygiene practices within the Ministry's office premises.

A major highlight of the campaign was the “Ek Din – Ek Ghanta – Ek Saath Shramdaan” organized by the Ministry at Navyug School, Peshwa Road, New Delhi. The programme was led by Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs & Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju, and witnessed participation of Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal; Chairman, NDMC, Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi; Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. Satya Prakash; Principal, Navyug School, Ms. Meenakshi Kaushik, along with officers and officials of the Ministry, teachers and students of the school.

During the programme, the Swachhata Pledge was administered to all participants, reaffirming their collective commitment towards cleanliness and hygiene. As part of the event, Shri Kiren Rijiju, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal, Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi and Dr. Satya Prakash planted saplings under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam Abhiyan” in the school campus.

The programme witnessed active participation of officers and officials of the Ministry, teachers and students of Navyug School, reflecting the spirit of collective participation and shared responsibility towards Swachhata.

The campaign concluded with a closing ceremony, during which Safai Mitras were felicitated in recognition of their dedicated contribution towards maintaining cleanliness and hygiene. Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. Satya Prakash, while addressing the gathering, highlighted the tagline of the campaign and called upon everyone to celebrate its spirit by making Swachhata a regular ritual, beginning from one’s own immediate surroundings and vicinity.

Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal, reiterated the importance of sustaining the spirit of Swachhata beyond the campaign period. He emphasized that cleanliness is a collective responsibility and encouraged officers and officials to continue adopting cleanliness and hygiene as an integral part of their everyday practices.

Through the various activities undertaken during the campaign, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs reaffirmed its commitment to the vision of Swachh Bharat and to fostering a sustained culture of cleanliness, hygiene, environmental responsibility, civic participation and dignity of labour.

The campaign concluded with a commitment to continue these efforts and make Swachhata an integral part of everyday life.

***

ISA

item.description:

The Yatra was launched simultaneously from four cities — Delhi, Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Bengaluru — with the objective of taking awareness about NPS Sanchay to the last mile of the society and facilitating on-the-spot enrolment of eligible beneficiaries. …
item.content:encoded:
State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) Gujarat, in collaboration with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), flagged off the NPS Sanchay Van Yatra from Ahmedabad on the occasion of NPS Diwas on October 1, 2026.

The Yatra was launched simultaneously from four cities — Delhi, Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Bengaluru — with the objective of taking awareness about NPS Sanchay to the last mile of the society and facilitating on-the-spot enrolment of eligible beneficiaries.

The Ahmedabad launch event was attended by Shri Raveesh Kumar, Convenor, SLBC Gujarat & General Manager, Bank of Baroda; Shri Ranjeet Kumar Das, Deputy General Manager, Bank of Baroda, Ahmedabad Zone, along with representatives of PFRDA, senior bank officials, Banking Correspondents and other stakeholders.

NPS Sanchay is a simplified variant of the National Pension System introduced by PFRDA with a focus on expanding pension coverage among the informal sectors. It is particularly relevant for people engaged in agriculture and allied activities and other informal-sector occupations.

The Van Yatra will travel across 15 districts of Gujarat from October 1 to October 15, 2026, covering three locations in each district. During the Yatra, awareness sessions will be conducted to explain the features and benefits of NPS Sanchay, while eligible individuals will also be facilitated for on-the-spot subscriber enrolment.

The initiative seeks to strengthen pension awareness and financial security among farmers, agricultural and allied-sector workers, rural entrepreneurs and other eligible members of the informal sector, while leveraging the extensive network of banks and grassroots financial inclusion functionaries.

The launch of the NPS Sanchay Van Yatra marks another significant step towards taking pension awareness and access to the last mile and strengthening inclusive social security coverage across Gujarat.

The drive was conducted under the guidance of Shri Sanjay Pant, Inspector General, Tactical HQ (Special Operations), BSF, Chhattisgarh.

Officers, Subordinate Officers, and Jawans of the Border Security Force, along with the medical team from the Government District Hospital, Durg, actively participated in the event.

item.content:encoded:
Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) operationalized a new state-of-the art Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Koppal, on Thursday, 01 October 2026 marking another step towards strengthening resident-centric Aadhaar services in the city of Koppal. The ASK Koppal was inaugurated by a Shri Siddrameshwar, Additional Deputy Commissioner as a chief guest in the presence of Senior Accounts Officer, UIDAI RO Bengaluru and other officials, M/s BLS and ASK Staff among others.

He appreciated the UIDAI’s effort and interacted with residents who visited ASK as well as the centre staff present there. Also, enquired about the Aadhaar enrolment and update procedures, and reviewed the various Aadhaar services being provided at the centre.

The ASK Koppal is equipped with 4 operational kits to provide seamless Aadhaar-related services to thousands of residents. The ASK is functional on all days except public holidays, thereby ensuring greater accessibility & convenience. The Aadhaar Seva Kendra offers Aadhaar enrolment, demographic and biometric updates, grievance redressal and other Aadhaar related services under one roof. In addition to the enrolment and update transactions, ASK Koppal will also receive grievances from Aadhaar number holders for their resolution through the Regional Office.

With the inauguration of the Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) at Koppal, UIDAI has now operationalised 18 Aadhaar Seva Kendras across Karnataka. A further 07 ASKs are scheduled to become operational in the coming days across various districts, increasing the total 25 UIDAI-run Aadhaar Seva Kendras in the State.

The ASKs run by UIDAI, are designed to be fully inclusive and resident-friendly with facilities such as wheelchair accessibility, accessible restrooms, and a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism. Residents can also book appointments online for Aadhaar services at ASKs through UIDAI’s appointment portal: https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/.

 

*****

item.title: HEADQUARTERS INTEGRATED DEFENCE STAFF CELEBRATES 25 YEARS OF JOINTNESS AND INTEGRATION
item.description:
Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) today marked its Silver Jubilee, commemorating 25 years since its establishment on 01 October 2001 in New Delhi, observed as ‘Tri-Service Day’.
As part of the Silver Jubilee celebrations themed “Future readiness through jointness & Integration”, HQ IDS organised ‘Trishakti Manthan’ featuring addresses by the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) & Secretary Department of Military Affairs General N. S. Raja Subramani, and the Chief of…
item.content:encoded:
Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) today marked its Silver Jubilee, commemorating 25 years since its establishment on 01 October 2001 in New Delhi, observed as ‘Tri-Service Day’.

As part of the Silver Jubilee celebrations themed “Future readiness through jointness & Integration”, HQ IDS organised ‘Trishakti Manthan’ featuring addresses by the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) & Secretary Department of Military Affairs General N. S. Raja Subramani, and the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) Air Marshal Tejinder Singh. The deliberations highlighted HQ IDS’s contribution to operational preparedness through joint operational doctrines, joint training frameworks, integrated exercises and enhanced coordination of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mechanisms.

In recognition of its distinguished contributions to strengthening jointness and integration, HQ IDS released a Silver Jubilee Book chronicling its evolution and achievements over the past 25 years, along with a film showcasing key milestones since its establishment. The prestigious CDS Unit Citations were conferred to personnel in recognition of their contributions towards strengthening jointness and integration. A Wreath Laying Ceremony at the National War Memorial & Museum was conducted to honour the brave hearts who made the supreme sacrifice in service of the Nation.

HQ IDS has played a significant role in preparing the Defence Forces for emerging domains, including Cyber, Space and Artificial Intelligence, while promoting collaboration with research organisations, academia and industry to accelerate indigenous capability development in line with Atmanirbharta in Defence. It has also strengthened institutional mechanisms for jointness through platforms such as Ran Samwad, Joint Commanders’ Conference (JCC) and Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE) Programme, facilitating structured deliberations on contemporary security challenges and enhancing joint warfighting capabilities across land, maritime, air, space, cyber and cognitive domains.

Over the past two-and-a-half decades, HQ IDS has evolved as the apex institution driving jointness, integration and synergy among the three Services, with a focus on capability enhancement and joint employment of combat power in line with national security objectives.

******

SR/Sumitra

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Government of India, along with its PSUs, attached and subordinate offices, participated in the nationwide cleanliness initiative ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ on October 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The initiative was undertaken as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign across various locations in the country.

The DFPD organised a cleanliness drive at the outer premises of Hanuman Mandir, Baba Kharak Singh Marg, New Delhi. Officials and employees of the Department enthusiastically participated in the one-hour Shramdaan. The initiative aimed at promoting cleanliness, improving sanitation and creating awareness among citizens about hygiene and responsible waste disposal. Through collective participation, the Department reaffirmed its commitment towards a cleaner, healthier and garbage-free India.

Besides DFPD, various PSUs and attached/subordinate offices of the Department also undertook cleanliness activities at multiple locations across the country.

 

The Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) demonstrated its unwavering commitment to community welfare by actively participating in the national cleanliness drive – “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath – Shramdaan at Siri Fort Sports Complex and MCD Parking, August Kranti Marg, opposite NFDC, New Delhi where a highly motivated team came together with energy, enthusiasm, and true team spirit to devote one hour towards cleaning and beautifying the public spaces. This impactful effort reflects their shared vision of a cleaner, healthier, and more responsible India. Through collective action and civic pride, they continue to support the mission of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.

The Food Corporation of India (FCI) conducted special cleanliness drives across its Headquarters, Regional and District offices throughout the country. Senior officials and staff actively participated in the campaign. As part of the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative, a rally was also organised to the nearest Central Park in Connaught Place, New Delhi, to promote awareness about cleanliness and civic responsibility.

 

The Indian Grain Management and Research Institute (IGMRI) organised cleanliness drives at Hyderabad and Ludhiana, with active participation of its officials and staff.

Collective Shramdaan activity was performed by Quality Control Cells of DFPD by organizing cleanliness drives at Bhubaneshwar, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkatta, Guwahati, Patna, Pune, Lucknow, Bhopal and Hyderabad

National Sugar Institute (NSI), Kanpur also organized a cleanliness drive in the office complex.

item.title: NSO Launches October 2026 Survey Drive, Appeals to Citizens and Enterprises for Cooperation
item.description:

Information is collected by trained officers of the NSO using hand-held digital devices (tablets) equipped with e-Sigma software and secure web portals designated for…
item.content:encoded:
The Field Operations Division of National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India is engaged in collecting information from households and establishments since 1950 which is used for planning and policy formulation both at National and State level. 

Information is collected by trained officers of the NSO using hand-held digital devices (tablets) equipped with e-Sigma software and secure web portals designated for enterprise surveys. All information collected in these surveys is kept strictly confidential. The identity of households and enterprises participating in the survey is not disclosed in any report or published data. The data is used only for statistical purposes. 

The detail of surveys undertaken by NSO (FOD) during the month of October, 2026 in various Districts is attached as Annexure-I. Further, for Wholesale Price Index, Purchaser Price Index, Index of Industrial Production and Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises, selected units have been sent notices and are contacted by NSO (FOD) officials for data collection time to time.

item.description:
The Scholarship for Education Transformation and Upliftment (SETU) National Scholarship Portal (NSP) App, a dedicated mobile application, is providing all information and guidance aimed at making scholarship-related services more accessible, convenient and student-friendly for eligible beneficiaries of the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships for Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes, under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment.
A Senior Ministry Official said the…
item.content:encoded:
The Scholarship for Education Transformation and Upliftment (SETU) National Scholarship Portal (NSP) App, a dedicated mobile application, is providing all information and guidance aimed at making scholarship-related services more accessible, convenient and student-friendly for eligible beneficiaries of the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships for Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes, under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment.

A Senior Ministry Official said the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), Government of India, has already launched the App in April this year, by the Ministry.  He said the SETU NSP App has been developed as a simple, secure and transparent digital platform to provide students with convenient access to a range of scholarship services through a single interface.

The Official said the application is designed to reduce procedural difficulties and facilitate students in completing various scholarship-related activities without having to navigate through multiple platforms. He said through the SETU NSP App, eligible students can register for scholarship schemes, complete biometric authentication, submit scholarship applications and track the status of their applications. The application also provides access to user guides and support services, enabling students to obtain relevant information and assistance during the scholarship application process.

The Official further said the application also provides digital services for key stakeholders involved in scholarship administration, including Institutional Nodal Officers (INOs), District Nodal Officers (DNOs) and State Nodal Officers (SNOs). These functionalities are intended to support the effective processing, monitoring and management of scholarship applications at different levels, thereby strengthening the overall scholarship delivery mechanism.

It is pertinent to mention that the introduction of the SETU NSP App is part of the Department's continuing efforts to leverage digital technology and citizen-centric solutions for improving public service delivery. By providing essential scholarship services through a mobile application, the initiative seeks to make the process more convenient for students and improve access to information and application-related services. The availability of services through a mobile platform will enable students to access important information, complete required processes and monitor their applications more conveniently.

The SETU NSP App also reinforces the Department's focus on transparency, accessibility and efficiency in the administration of scholarship schemes. Digital access to application and tracking services can help students remain informed about the progress of their applications and access relevant guidance whenever required.

The Department continues to undertake measures aimed at simplifying processes and strengthening the delivery of welfare and scholarship benefits through technology-enabled solutions. The launch of the SETU NSP App represents another step towards creating a more accessible, efficient, transparent and student-centric scholarship ecosystem.

The Department remains committed to adopting innovative and technology-driven solutions that simplify scholarship-related processes, improve transparency and facilitate the timely and effective delivery of benefits to eligible students.

The SETU NSP App is available for download on the following platforms:

item.title: ICAR and FCI signs MoU for Safe and Sustainable Foodgrain Storage
item.description:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 30 September 2026 to undertake research on alternative fumigation technologies for safe and sustainable management of storage pests in wheat and rice. The research study is supported by the Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD), Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution.
The two-year Phase-I project will be implemented by…
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Food Corporation of India (FCI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 30 September 2026 to undertake research on alternative fumigation technologies for safe and sustainable management of storage pests in wheat and rice. The research study is supported by the Department of Food & Public Distribution (DFPD), Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution.

The two-year Phase-I project will be implemented by ICAR–Central Institute of Post-Harvest Engineering and Technology (CIPHET), Ludhiana.

For decades, India's critical grain reserves have relied heavily on aluminium phosphide (ALP) and malathion for post-harvest pest control. However, widespread and repeated use has led to severe consequences, including pest resistance frequencies reaching 72-100% in key Indian states and escalating fumigation cycles that drive up operational costs. Furthermore, current chemical methods pose significant respiratory threats to workers and long-term ecological risks. This initiative seeks to directly address these challenges by standardizing the commercial use of nitrogen gas, carbon dioxide (CO2), and a synergistic combination of CO2 and phosphine. The following three major trials will be conducted in Phase-I:

  • Nitrogen gas (>99%) fumigation for effective management of storage pests in wheat stored in metal silos.
  • Combined carbon dioxide and phosphine gas fumigation for managing/controlling storage pests in wheat and rice stored in bags at FCI/CWC warehouses.
  • Carbon dioxide fumigation for managing/controlling storage pests in wheat and rice in bags enclosed in hermetic covers.

Following the two-year Phase-I pilot, Phase-II will expand into a one-year multi-location trial across varied agro-climatic zones to establish region-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

The initiative aims to develop scientifically validated, scalable and sustainable alternatives to conventional chemical fumigation, addressing concerns related to increasing pest resistance, occupational exposure, environmental impacts and fumigant residues.

The MoU was signed in the presence of the Dr. M. L Jat, Secretary, DARE & Director General, ICAR; Dr. Rajbir Singh, Deputy Director General (Agricultural Engineering), Dr. D.K. Yadav Deputy Director General (Crop Science), Dr. K. Narsaiah, Assistant Director General (Processing Engineering); ICAR. The MoU was signed by Dr. Nachiket Kotwaliwale, Director, ICAR-CIPHET and Dr. A.K. Sinha, Executive Director (Quality Control), FCI. The event was also attended by Ms. Priya Jacob, Director, DFPD, Sh. Rajagopal General Manager QC-FCI, Dr. Devinder Dhingra, Pr. Scientist, ICAR; Dr. Sandeep Mann Pr. Scientist and Lead Investigator of project, ICAR-CIPHET; Shri Gautam Kumar, Deputy General Manager (Quality Control), FCI; Sh CP Saharan and Ms. Sarika Pritam, Assistant General Manager (Quality Control), FCI.

item.description: Under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the Department of Justice is implementing the Special Campaign 6 for clearing pendency and focusing on Swachhata of the office premises. As in the previous years, this year too, this campaign has been spread over two phases, with Phase-I (from 15.09.2026-30.09.2026) being the identification phase, wherein various pending matters (like References from MPs, Parliamentary Assurances, References from the…
item.content:encoded:
Under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the Department of Justice is implementing the Special Campaign 6 for clearing pendency and focusing on Swachhata of the office premises. As in the previous years, this year too, this campaign has been spread over two phases, with Phase-I (from 15.09.2026-30.09.2026) being the identification phase, wherein various pending matters (like References from MPs, Parliamentary Assurances, References from the State Governments, Inter Ministerial references, Public Grievances etc.) and also, sites requiring sprucing, cleaning and beautification were identified. Phase-II from 02.10.2026 to 31.10.2026 is being devoted to the clearance of the identified pendency and cleaning/ sprucing up and beautification of identified sites/areas.

During the just concluded Phase-I of the said campaign, 211 Public Grievances and 309 number of appeals under Public Grievances were detected. Apart from this, 4 sites requiring sprucing, cleaning and beautification were also identified within the premises of the Department.

With regard to the implementation phase of the Special Campaign which is scheduled from 02.10.2026 to 31.10.2026, the main focus is to liquidate the pendency identified in the phase-I. In addition to the above, 49 e-waste equipment/items, were identified and the same will be disposed off during the main/second phase of the campaign. The amount so generated from disposal of these items will be deposited into the Government treasury. As far as sites requiring sprucing, cleaning and beautification, 4 sites have been identified and the same will be cleaned with the shramdaan giving by the officials of Department of Justice during the second / implementation phase.

The Department is committed to disposal of the pending matters/ items ripe for disposal and upkeep and improvement of sites selected for cleaning and beautification, as identified during the first phase, in the second phase of the Special Campaign 6.

item.title: NIELIT Imphal Celebrates 38th Foundation Day
item.description:
NIELIT Imphal celebrated its 38th Foundation Day at its Akampat campus on Thursday, 1 October 2026. The programme was attended by dignitaries, faculty members, staff, students, retired employees, technology partners, invitees and members of the media.
The celebration was graced by Smt. Adhikarimayum Sharda Devi, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, as the Chief Guest. Prof. Nilanjan Dey, Techno International New Town, Kolkata, and Dr. Manish Arora, Registrar, NIELIT (Deemed to be…
item.content:encoded:
NIELIT Imphal celebrated its 38th Foundation Day at its Akampat campus on Thursday, 1 October 2026. The programme was attended by dignitaries, faculty members, staff, students, retired employees, technology partners, invitees and members of the media.

The celebration was graced by Smt. Adhikarimayum Sharda Devi, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, as the Chief Guest. Prof. Nilanjan Dey, Techno International New Town, Kolkata, and Dr. Manish Arora, Registrar, NIELIT (Deemed to be University) attended as Guests of Honour. Dr. Yumnam Jayanta Singh, Executive Director & Dean, NIELIT Imphal, presided over the function.    

The programme began with the National Anthem, National Song and State Song of Manipur, followed by felicitation of the dignitaries and ceremonial candle lighting.

Welcoming the gathering, Dr. Yumnam Jayanta Singh greeted the dignitaries, retired employees of the institute, faculty members, students, and technology partners and media representatives. He said that NIELIT has 56 centres across the country and highlighted that NIELIT Imphal is celebrating 38 years of its existence.

He said that over the years, NIELIT Imphal has grown into one of the important technology institutions in the North Eastern Region. Referring to the laboratories and facilities being developed at the institute, he said that NIELIT Imphal has been providing significant technological services to both the State and the nation. He also expressed confidence that the institute would continue to strengthen its role in education, skill development and emerging technologies.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Nilanjan Dey drew attention to the rapid changes taking place in the field of Artificial Intelligence. He referred to earlier predictions about an “intelligence explosion”, where machines would eventually become capable of creating even more intelligent machines. He observed that many developments which were once expected much later are already becoming a reality with the arrival of advanced AI systems and intelligent agents.

He said that developments in AI and large language models are already changing the way people learn, work and use knowledge. According to him, this change is also affecting the job market and creating a major shift in the way students need to prepare for their careers.

Prof. Dey stressed that education should no longer remain only knowledge-centric. He said that the learning process must increasingly become skill-centric, as practical skills and the ability to adapt to new technologies will be essential for students to remain relevant in a changing employment environment.

Dr. Manish Arora, in his address, said that Foundation Day gives an institution an opportunity to look back with gratitude at the milestones it has achieved, appreciate the contributions of everyone who has been part of its journey, and move forward with determination to face new challenges and opportunities.

He observed that the world is now going through a period of rapid technological transformation. Technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Cloud Computing, Cyber Security, Internet of Things, Data Science and other emerging digital technologies are bringing new challenges, while at the same time opening up new opportunities. He encouraged students and institutions to prepare themselves for these changes and make the best use of the opportunities created by technology.

Addressing the gathering as Chief Guest, Smt. Adhikarimayum Sharda Devi congratulated NIELIT Imphal on completing 38 years of service. She said that emerging technologies such as semiconductor technology, Artificial Intelligence, drone technology, 3D printing technology, robotic automation, digital platforms, cyber security and data science are changing the way people learn, work and live. She urged the youth of Manipur to develop skills in these areas so that they can become future-ready and globally competitive.

She appreciated the role played by NIELIT Imphal in providing quality IT education and skill development and in promoting innovation and entrepreneurship among the youth of Manipur and the North Eastern Region.  Smt. Sharda Devi also encouraged the students to think beyond seeking jobs and to work towards becoming job creators. She called upon them to make meaningful use of technology for the socio-economic development of Manipur.

She wished NIELIT Imphal continued success and expressed her support for the institution in its journey towards becoming a Centre of Excellence. One of the highlights of the celebration was the release of the official song of NIELIT Imphal by the Chief Guest.

The celebration concluded with a Vote of Thanks by Dr. Angom Buboo Singh, Sc.E & Head (Academics), NIELIT Imphal, followed by light refreshments.

item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, October 1, 2026

The Centre of Excellence on Green Hydrogen (CoE GH2) was inaugurated today at Jadavpur University, Kolkata as a part of the National Green Hydrogen Mission of the Union Ministry of New & Renewable Energy. Shri Rajesh Pandey, Chairman, Damodar Valley Corporation, graced the occasion as Chief Guest of the function and inaugurated the Centre of Excellence. The distinguished dignitaries present included Professor Dr. Chiranjib Bhattacharjee, Vice Chancellor, Jadavpur University, Shri Swapnendu Kumar Panda, Member (Technical), DVC and Professor Amitava Datta, pro-Vice Chancellor, JU.

The Centre came into being as a joint initiative of DVC, Jadavpur University, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL), supported and funded by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) and DVC. Jadavpur University is the knowledge partner, while SAIL and HURL are industry stakeholders. Mr. Arghyajit Saha, General Manager, Environment Management Division, SAIL was present as industry partner.

Selected through a nationwide process, it is one of only four such Centres pan-India approved under the National Green Hydrogen Mission of the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy,GoI which aims to make India a global hub for the production, use and export of green hydrogen.

The Centre will focus on high-pressure compression, storage and transportation of green hydrogen, and on its applications in decarbonising the power, steel and fertiliser sectors. It is expected to deliver stable and efficient green hydrogen co-firing burner systems, efficient high-pressure compression, and cleaner steel and fertiliser production, contributing to India’s clean energy transition.

item.title: CMFRI initiative gives fresh hope to declining black clam resource in Vembanad
item.description:
