The success of the stock enhancement project was marked by a harvest festival held after a 12-month culture period following the relaying of five tonnes of clam seed in a one-hectare area at Vadakkumkara in Alappuzha district. …
item.content:encoded:
Kochi, 01 October 2026:  A black clam regeneration initiative of the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CMFRI) has yielded encouraging results in Vembanad Lake, with a production reaching seven to eight times the quantity of the stocked seeds.

The success of the stock enhancement project was marked by a harvest festival held after a 12-month culture period following the relaying of five tonnes of clam seed in a one-hectare area at Vadakkumkara in Alappuzha district.

 

The black clam (Villorita cyprinoides), one of the most important fisheries resources of Vembanad Lake, accounts for more than 80 per cent of India’s total clam resources. The resource directly supports the livelihoods of more than 6,000 families, while nearly twice that number depend on allied activities associated with the clam fishery.

 

 

The initiative assumes greater significance in the wake of a sustained decline in clam resources in Vembanad due to intensive exploitation and changing environmental conditions. According to CMFRI estimates, the black clam catch from the region declined from a peak of 75,592 tonnes in 2006 to 45,601 tonnes in 2024, registering a decline of nearly 40 per cent.

Under the project, five tonnes of black clam seed were stocked in a one-hectare area in the region in September last year. During the harvest, the clams showed good growth and a survival rate of around 80–90 per cent, with the harvested stock recording about seven to eight times the quantity of the initially stocked seed. The production from the one-hectare area is expected to reach around 40 tonnes, indicating the considerable potential of planned clam stock enhancement in restoring the resource base.

 

 

The project was implemented with 100 per cent subsidy for Scheduled Caste communities under the Central Government’s Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP), with technical guidance from CMFRI and in collaboration with the Thaikkattussery Black Clam Co-operative Society.

Inaugurating the harvest, CMFRI Director Dr Grinson George said: “The stock enhancement initiative shows how scientific regeneration can help replenish the declining clam resource while providing sustained livelihood support to fishing communities”.

Besides enhancing clam availability for fishers, replenishing the natural stock can contribute to the ecological functioning and productivity of the estuarine ecosystem, where clams play an important role as filter-feeding organisms, he added.

“The relaying site, identified through scientific assessment, had no existing clam stock. Standard sampling methods and an appropriate stocking density were adopted to ensure effective stock enhancement. The successful outcome highlights the potential of scientific intervention to combine resource regeneration, ecosystem recovery and sustained livelihood support for local communities” said CMFRI Senior Scientist Dr Vidya R, who coordinated the project.

The awards will recognize outstanding contributions to the coconut sector in the following three categories:
1. Best National Coconut Farmer
2. Best Coconut Scientist/Researcher
3. Best Coconut Entrepreneur
Eligible Indian farmers, scientists/researchers and entrepreneurs may apply under the respective categories in accordance with the prescribed eligibility criteria and by submitting the required documentary evidence. Applications will be accepted online only.
The last date for submission of applications is 15 October 2026. Detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria and application forms are available on the Coconut Development Board website https://coconutboard.gov.in/docs/news/award26/award26.htm.

The awards are aimed at recognising and encouraging outstanding contributions to coconut cultivation, research, innovation, value addition, processing and entrepreneurship, and at highlighting exemplary achievements in the coconut sector. Eligible farmers, scientists/researchers and entrepreneurs may make use of this opportunity and submit their applications before 15th October 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign is being observed in Department of Telecommunications (DoT) from 17.09.2026 to 02.10.2026 with the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” exemplifying the “Whole of Society” and “Whole of Government” approach for cleanliness. The campaign facilitates large scale advocacy and citizen participation for Swachhata, cleanliness drives with focus on cleaning of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) across the country through active participation of officers and staff of the department, attached offices, subordinate offices, field units and public sector units.

Department of Telecommunications has conducted following activities during the campaign:

  1. Swachhata Pledge: Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, along with DoT officials, took the Swachhata Pledge, committing to cleanliness, hygiene and responsible civic practices.

     

  1. Jan Bhagidari advocacy drive for promoting cleanliness: The Department organized Essay Writing and Poster Making Competitions for the children of DoT employees on 23rd September 2026 at Sanchar Bhawan, celebrating the spirit of Swachhata through creativity.

     

  1. Awareness Session on Waste Management for Sanitation Workers: As part of the #SwachhataHiSeva2026 campaign, the Department of Telecommunications organized an expert awareness session on effective waste management. Shri J.B. Ravindra, Retired Joint Advisor, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, shared valuable insights on different waste management techniques and practices. The session was attended by Safai Karmacharis, empowering them with knowledge for more efficient and sustainable waste management.

  1. Safai Mitra Suraksha Shivir: Housekeeping staff was made aware of occupational hazards and provided with safety equipment and first aid-kit.

The campaign also saw enthusiastic participation from DoT, attached offices, subordinate offices, field units, and public sector units, focusing on the cleaning of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) nationwide. Various events such as cleanliness drives, awareness sessions, poster making competitions, tree plantation, Swachhata pledges and SafaiMitra Suraksha Shivirs were organised across DoT’s field offices across the country advocating campaign’s commitment to cleanliness, sanitation and safety.

The Campaign shall conclude on 2nd October 2026 with plantation of tree sapling by Hon’ble Minister of Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia with plantation of a tree sapling under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ inititative on occasion of Swachh Bharat Divas.

item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, 1 October 2026

 

The situation Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI), Kolkata following the incident of 27 September 2026 is now normal.

SRFTI is a premier national institution, with students drawn from across the country and beyond. The Institute and its students have consistently upheld high standards of excellence in film and television, and SRFTI remains committed to further strengthening its position as a global centre for cinema education.

Shri Santosh Ajmera, Vice-Chancellor, SRFTI, said that students are at the heart of the Institute, and their safety, dignity, well-being and academic journey remain the foremost priority. He stated that the incident of 27 September was unfortunate and that there can be no justification for violence within an educational institution. He assured students and their families of the Institute’s firm commitment to their safety and well-being.

The Institute is extending full cooperation to the concerned authorities and following due process. All necessary measures are being taken to strengthen campus safety and security and to ensure that such an incident does not recur.

The Vice-Chancellor appealed to all concerned to exercise restraint and refrain from relying on unverified information, videos or speculation, which may cause unnecessary apprehension and adversely affect students.

He said that the Institute is continuously engaging with students, and that the focus is now on moving forward and enabling them to resume their classes, academic activities and creative pursuits in a safe, peaceful and supportive environment.

The Vice-Chancellor acknowledged the support extended by the President, SRFTI Society; State and Central Government authorities, as well as the cooperation and understanding of the students, faculty, staff and the entire SRFTI community.

SRFTI remains committed to providing a safe and inspiring environment where every student can learn, create and realise their full potential with confidence and dignity.

item.title: Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare Organises National Workshop to Strengthen Implementation of PC&PNDT Act
item.description: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, today organised a National Workshop on Strengthening the Implementation of the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994 (PC&PNDT Act) in the national capital. The workshop brought together representatives from all 36 States and Union Territories, along with senior officials of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry…
item.content:encoded:
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, today organised a National Workshop on Strengthening the Implementation of the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994 (PC&PNDT Act) in the national capital. The workshop brought together representatives from all 36 States and Union Territories, along with senior officials of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs.

The workshop focused on strengthening regulatory compliance, enhancing digital governance and ease of doing business, addressing emerging challenges in the digital ecosystem, and sharing State-level best practices to improve implementation of the PC&PNDT Act.

Delivering the keynote address, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, emphasised the need for strict and effective enforcement of the PC&PNDT Act, complemented by sustained Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives to reinforce the equal value of the girl child.

Highlighting the opportunities and challenges arising from emerging technologies, Ms. Patnaik noted that portable diagnostic devices, online platforms and social media have significantly expanded access to healthcare and information, but can also be misused for activities prohibited under the law. She stressed that technology must be leveraged to advance healthcare and social inclusion and must not be allowed to facilitate sex selection or gender discrimination.

Highlighting the progress made in improving the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB), Ms. Patnaik noted that the national SRB has shown a steady improvement over the years. As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) Report 2024, the national SRB increased by 20 points, from 898 females per 1,000 males during 2014–16 to 918 females per 1,000 males during 2022–24. The improvement reflects the continued efforts towards effective implementation of the PC&PNDT Act, regulatory oversight and community-level interventions.

The workshop also deliberated on emerging challenges associated with the digital ecosystem, particularly online advertisements and content relating to sex selection and sex determination.

A dedicated session on Section 22 of the PC&PNDT Act highlighted the role of States and Union Territories in identifying, flagging and restricting prohibited digital content. The discussions also covered the use of the Sahyog Portal and the need for proactive coordination with digital intermediaries to address online violations and prevent misuse of technology for activities prohibited under the Act.

Deliberations were also held on standardising and strengthening State/UT PC&PNDT portals. The discussions focused on integrating digital modules for regulatory processes, monitoring and compliance to strengthen oversight while facilitating ease of doing business. Live demonstrations of digital initiatives undertaken by Telangana and Gujarat provided practical insights and enabled participating States and UTs to examine replicable models for strengthening digital governance under the PC&PNDT framework.

The workshop also provided a platform for States and UTs to share their experiences and innovative practices. Representatives from Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Jharkhand, Odisha and Tamil Nadu, among others, presented State-level initiatives and best practices. The exchange facilitated peer learning and discussions on actionable measures to further strengthen implementation of the PC&PNDT Act.

Ms. Meera Srivastava, Joint Secretary (RCH), MoHFW; Dr. Pawan Kumar, Additional Commissioner (PC&PNDT), MoHFW; senior officials from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs; and senior officials from all States and Union Territories were present during the workshop.

*****

SR

item.description:
A senior officer of the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India, is undertaking a four-days Area Officer visit to Jammu and Kashmir from September 30 to October 3, 2026, to monitor the implementation and progress of various ongoing rural development schemes in Srinagar and Anantnag districts.

item.content:encoded:
A senior officer of the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India, is undertaking a four-days Area Officer visit to Jammu and Kashmir from September 30 to October 3, 2026, to monitor the implementation and progress of various ongoing rural development schemes in Srinagar and Anantnag districts.

The visit is being led by Shri Altaf Hussain Haji, Deputy Director General, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, New Delhi, who is the designated Area Officer for MoRD schemes.

During the visit, Shri Haji also attended a training programme on Viksit Bharat Gram Panchayat (VB-GRAMG) organised by the Department of Rural Development for Block Development Officers (BDOs) of Srinagar and Ganderbal districts.  During the brief interaction, Shri Haji emphasised the need to focus on the convergence of various government schemes, enhance awareness about rural development programmes, and identify low-development Gram Panchayats (GPs) for focused interventions. He stressed that such targeted efforts would help these Panchayats progress towards becoming Viksit Panchayats, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

During the field visit along with Assistant commissioner  Rural devlopment Srinagar, Tariq Ahmad Reshi  and other local officers interacted with Self-Help Groups (SHGs) at block  Khonmoh and Qamarwari and beneficiaries and other stakeholders associated with rural livelihoods and other rural development schemes including VB G RAM G . He also interacted with members of Umeed Ka Zaika SHG, which has gained recognition in Jammu and Kashmir within a short period of three to four months.

The visiting officer observed that Self-Help Groups functioning under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) were performing remarkably well. The SHG members were found to be enthusiastic and committed towards achieving the goal of becoming Lakhpati Didis at the earliest, with aspirations of progressing further towards becoming Crorepati Didis.

Shri Haji also reviewed the implementation status of various rural development schemes in Srinagar and discussed measures to further improve their outreach and ensure that the intended benefits reach a larger number of beneficiaries.

Officials of the District Administration, Srinagar, were advised to expedite and strengthen the implementation of ongoing rural development schemes for the benefit and overall well-being of the people. The officer also stressed the need to conduct awareness programmes at the grassroots level so that rural communities are better informed about various government schemes and the benefits available to them.

Emphasis was also laid on greater convergence among different government schemes and departments to achieve targets effectively and maximise benefits for beneficiaries.

At the concluding leg of the visit in Srinagar, Shri Altaf Hussain Haji met  also officers of Rural Development, Government of Jammu and Kashmir. They discussed the achievements made in the implementation of various rural development schemes, as well as issues concerning their effective implementation.

The meeting also focused on addressing minor implementation-related issues and further strengthening the delivery of rural development programmes across Jammu and Kashmir.

*****

PU - Prabhat Upadhyay

item.content:encoded:
The many faces of Punjab, its faith, history, music, dance and living traditions, find expression in a distinctive collection of mementos featured in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026. Miniature representations of the Golden Temple, portraits of Sikh spiritual figures, Bhangra and a glimpse into Diljit Dosanjh’s global musical journey bring together timeless heritage and contemporary cultural expression.

 

 

One memento of the Golden Temple is a detailed miniature model of Sri Harmandir Sahib, while another presents the shrine within a glass dome, creating a distinctive floating effect, both reflecting the architectural and spiritual significance of the iconic Amritsar landmark.

 

 

The collection also pays tribute to Guru Nanak Dev Ji through a silver-framed portrait presented by the Gurudwara Managing Committee, Gurubagh, and Varanasi. Another poignant artwork depicts Mata Gujri Ji with the young Sahibzadas, Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, recalling their place in Sikh history and the values of courage, sacrifice and faith associated with their story.

 

 

Punjab’s vibrant cultural identity comes alive through a painting of Bhangra, capturing the movement, colour and celebratory spirit of the traditional folk dance. The collection also takes a contemporary turn with a photoprint of Diljit Dosanjh’s Dil-Luminati Tour, representing the global reach of Punjabi music and popular culture.

 

 

Another notable entry is a framed portrait of Sant Shri Sevalal Maharaj, depicting the spiritual and social reformer in a blessing posture. Completing the collection are saffron Gurdwara headscarves with golden threadwork, traditionally associated with humility and reverence in Sikh places of worship.

Together, these mementos tell a story that moves from sacred spaces and spiritual traditions to folk culture and contemporary music, offering a glimpse into the diverse cultural expressions associated with Punjab.

The PM Mementos e-Auction give people an opportunity to place their bids. Proceeds from the auction will support the Namami Gange Mission. Visit pmmementos.gov.in to place your bid.

***

M Annadurai

Kolkata, 1 October 2026

 

The Office of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, West Bengal & Sikkim, organised 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026' today at Aayakar Abasan in Kolkata, under the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, reaffirming its commitment to cleanliness, public health and environmental responsibility.

The programme was graced by Minister-in-Charge, Department of Health and Family Welfare, Givernment of West Bengal, Dr. Sharadwat Mukherjee, as the Chief Guest. The Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, West Bengal & Sikkim, IRS, Smt. Surabhi Varma Garg, presided over the event. The occasion was also attended by Madam Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Chief Commissioner of Income Tax-5, Kolkata; Smt. Paramita Mandal Biswas, Chief Commissioner of Income Tax-3, Kolkata; Shri Sreenivas T. Bidari,  Chief Commissioner of Income Tax-4, Kolkata; and Shri Shivraj B. Morey, Chief Commissioner of Income Tax-6, Kolkata, along with other senior officers, officials and Safai Mitras.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Sharadwat Mukherjee mentioned the close interlinkages between cleanliness, sanitation and public health and highlighted the importance of collective participation in building a cleaner and healthier society. Smt. Surabhi Varma Garg underscored the necessity to make Swachhata a sustained practice in everyday life and an integral part of institutional culture.

The Swachhata Pledge was administered by the Chief Guest, with participants reaffirming their collective commitment to cleanliness and responsible civic practices.

The special highlight of the programme was the felicitation of Safai Mitras, recognising their dedicated contribution towards maintaining clean and hygienic surroundings.

The programme was followed by a plantation drive under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”, the inauguration of a health camp, and a 'Shramdaan' activity. Officers, officials, Safai Mitras and other participants joined these initiatives, reinforcing the spirit of collective action towards cleanliness and environmental responsibility.

On the occasion of National Voluntary Blood Donation Day, Ministry of Defence, in collaboration with the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, organised a Voluntary Blood Donation Camp at Kartavya Bhavan-2, New Delhi on October 01, 2026. The theme of this year’s campaign was ‘One Drop of Humanity, Give Blood, Save Lives.’

The blood donation drive was conducted under the supervision of a dedicated medical team comprising two Medical Officers, two Junior Commissioned Officers and 10 Paramedical Staff (Blood Transfusion Assistants), with the requisite medical equipment and facilities in place. A total of 134 officers and officials of the Ministry of Defence participated in the drive. Prior to donation, all donors underwent counselling and health screening to ensure their safety and compliance with prescribed medical standards.

The camp highlighted the importance of voluntary blood donation and encouraged officers and officials to contribute towards saving precious lives. Chief of Defence Staff and Secretary, Department of Military Affairs General N S Raja Subramani; Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh; Secretary, Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare Smt Sukriti Likhi, along with senior officers and officials of the Ministry of Defence, participated in the camp and contributed to the initiative.

The initiative reaffirmed the Ministry of Defence’s commitment to promoting voluntary blood donation and supporting efforts to ensure the availability of safe blood for patients in need.

***

item.content:encoded:
Telecommunications Consultants India Ltd. (TCIL) today paid dividend of Rs. 43.86 crore to the Government of India for the year 2025-26. Chairman & Managing Director Shri Syed Tausif Abbas presented the dividend cheque to Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and DoNER, in the presence of Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications (DoT).

TCIL was established in August, 1978 and is under the administrative control of the Department of Telecommunications, Government of India. The Government holds 100% equity in the Company. In 2025-26, TCIL achieved an operating revenue of ₹ 3,335 Crore and earned a profit after tax of ₹ 146 Crore.

In the last 5 years, revenue of TCIL has grown by 115% (from ₹ 1,596 Crore in FY 2021-22 to ₹ 3,442 Crore in FY 2025-26). TCIL is a profit making Miniratna PSU and have paid a cumulative dividend of ₹ 4,146 Crore to the Government, including special dividend of ₹ 3,728 Crore in FY 2024-25.

TCIL is a diversified CPSE executing Projects in the field of Telecommunications & Information Technology in India and abroad. TCIL has executed projects in over 70 countries across the globe. Its overseas operations are currently in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Mauritius, Bhutan & Nepal apart from the ongoing prestigious Pan Africa e-Vidya Bharti & Arogya Bharti Network project operating in more than 15 African countries.

The Company is also executing prestigious high value Govt. of India projects of Defence NFS project, Navy OFC Projects, USOF funded APSFL & Telangana Fiber Projects, BBNL VSAT, BharatNet phase -III Project in North East, BSNL Super Edge Router Project, State Wide Area Network in Bihar and Data Centre projects for the Indian Coast Guard & in state of Chhattisgarh.

item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) organised a cleanliness drive (Shramdaan) at Transport Bhawan, New Delhi, today, as part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign. The initiative was undertaken under the campaign’s ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ call for collective participation in cleanliness activities.

The Swachhata Hi Seva campaign is being observed from September 17 to October 2, 2026, with the objective of promoting voluntarism and fostering collective action towards cleanliness. The theme of this year’s campaign is ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’.

As part of the ongoing campaign, 943 Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) have been transformed as on October 1, 2026. Further, 123 public spaces have been cleaned so far under the campaign.

Secretary, MoRTH, Shri V. Umashankar led the Shramdaan along with senior officials and employees of the Ministry. Officers and staff actively participated in the cleanliness drive, including cleaning the area outside Transport Bhawan, reaffirming the Ministry’s commitment to maintaining clean and hygienic public and workplace spaces.

On the occasion, Shri V. Umashankar and senior functionaries felicitated the sanitation workers by presenting them with shawls in recognition of their dedicated services. The Secretary appreciated their valuable contribution towards maintaining cleanliness and hygiene at the workplace and acknowledged their important role in supporting the objectives of the Swachhata campaign.

The initiative provided an opportunity for officers and employees to come together and contribute to the broader objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva. The Ministry reiterated that cleanliness is not limited to periodic campaigns but requires sustained participation and responsible practices in day-to-day life.

Under the Swachhata Hi Seva and Special Campaign 6.0, the Ministry has identified several key areas for focused action, including removal of garbage along National Highways (NHs), particularly in urban areas; refurbishment and maintenance of toilet blocks at toll plazas and other locations along NHs; comprehensive upkeep of toll plazas, including cleaning, painting, lighting and solarisation; installation of road signages and improvement of visibility of road markings; and making National Highways pothole-free, among other cleanliness and maintenance activities.

All campaign offices, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, Programme Implementation Units (PIUs), Programme Directors and other field offices, have been sensitised to undertake concerted efforts for effective implementation of the campaigns and to ensure sustained and impactful outcomes.

The progress of the campaigns is being regularly reviewed by the Joint Secretary/Secretary with the Nodal Officers of the respective campaign offices to ensure coordinated implementation and achievement of the campaign objectives.

The Shramdaan at Transport Bhawan reinforced the message of collective responsibility, dignity of work and sustained participation in building a cleaner and more hygienic workplace and public environment.

***

GDH/DS

item.title: Government of India Revises Guidelines for Issuance of Exempted FASTags for Divyangjan and PwD Vehicles
item.description: Promoting ‘Ease of living’ for the citizens and further simplifying toll-related procedures for Divyangjan & Persons with Disabilities (PwD), the Government of India has revised the guidelines for issuance and renewal of exempted FASTags for eligible Divyangjan/PwD beneficiaries. The revised framework is aimed at bringing greater uniformity in the issuance and renewal of exempted FASTag for eligible Divyangjan/PwD vehicles, while reducing the need for repeated procedural formalities. The…
item.content:encoded:
Promoting ‘Ease of living’ for the citizens and further simplifying toll-related procedures for Divyangjan & Persons with Disabilities (PwD), the Government of India has revised the guidelines for issuance and renewal of exempted FASTags for eligible Divyangjan/PwD beneficiaries. The revised framework is aimed at bringing greater uniformity in the issuance and renewal of exempted FASTag for eligible Divyangjan/PwD vehicles, while reducing the need for repeated procedural formalities. The guidelines will come into effect from 02nd October 2026.  

Under this, exempted FASTags for vehicles specially designed and constructed for use by persons with physical disabilities, as well as vehicles registered under the ownership type ‘Divyangjan’, will be issued exempted FASTag based on the percentage of disability recorded in a valid Disability Certificate, Unique Disability Identity (UDID) Card or other applicable records.

Earlier guidelines mandated renewal of exempted FASTag for Divyangjan on annual basis.  However, as per the new guidelines, validity of the Exempted FASTag will be determined by the recorded percentage of disability. FASTag issued to persons with 70% to 100% disability will be valid for five years, while those issued to persons with 40% to less than 70% disability will be valid for three years. The exempted FASTag may be renewed thereafter, subject to continued eligibility and compliance with the provisions of the National Highways Fee Rules, 2008. 

The revised provisions are aimed at making the National Highway tolling ecosystem more accessible, transparent and user-friendly for eligible Divyangjan/PwD beneficiaries, while ensuring that toll exemptions continue to be administered in accordance with the prescribed rules and eligibility requirements.

***

GDH/DS

item.content:encoded:
It was an eventful and action-oriented day at the Ministry of Coal as a series of activities were organised today under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6, bringing together the themes of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and community welfare. Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Coal, and Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Smt. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary along with senior officers and officials of the Ministry, participated in the activities.

 

The day commenced with the inauguration of an E-Waste Kiosk at the Main Entrance Lobby of GPOA-3 by Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal. The kiosk will facilitate the collection of e-waste and will remain operational till 31 October 2026, encouraging responsible disposal of electronic waste and promoting greater awareness about sustainable waste management practices.

The inauguration was followed by the “Ek Din, Ek Saath, Ek Ghanta” Cleanliness Drive along the service road near the metro exit gate and the GPOA-3 entry gate. Senior officers and officials actively participated in the drive, reinforcing the message that cleanliness is a collective responsibility and requires sustained participation.

 

Adding a humanitarian dimension to the day’s activities, a Blood Donation Camp was organised near the Entry Gate of GPOA-3. Officers and officials participated in the camp and contributed towards the noble cause of blood donation, reflecting the spirit of compassion, community service and social responsibility.

The active participation of the Ministry’s senior leadership, officers and officials gave further impetus to the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6. The initiatives brought together environmental awareness, cleanliness and community welfare, translating the spirit of collective responsibility into meaningful action.

                                               

The day’s activities reflected the spirit of collective participation and responsible citizenship, with officers and officials coming together to contribute towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and community welfare. The initiatives under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6 reaffirm the Ministry of Coal’s commitment to fostering a culture of cleanliness, sustainability and social responsibility, inspiring continued action towards a cleaner, greener and healthier India.

item.title: DACE, Manipur University Observes 5th Foundation Day, Felicitates Successful Candidates
item.description:
The Dr. Ambedkar Centre of Excellence (DACE), Manipur University, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India observed its 5th Foundation Day-cum-Felicitation Programme at the University Auditorium on Thursday, celebrating the achievements of students who have secured positions in different government services and qualified national-level examinations.
Prof. R.K. Hemakumar Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Manipur University, attended the programme as Chief Guest.…
item.content:encoded:
The Dr. Ambedkar Centre of Excellence (DACE), Manipur University, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India observed its 5th Foundation Day-cum-Felicitation Programme at the University Auditorium on Thursday, celebrating the achievements of students who have secured positions in different government services and qualified national-level examinations.

Prof. R.K. Hemakumar Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Manipur University, attended the programme as Chief Guest. Lt Gen (Retd) Konsam Himalay Singh, former Chairman of the Manipur Public Service Commission; R.K. Nimai Singh, IAS, former Commissioner, Department of Art and Culture, Government of Manipur; Prof. N. Basanta Singh, Dean, School of Engineering, Manipur University; Prof. N. Mohilal Meitei, Dean, School of Life Sciences, Manipur University; and Mayanglambam Rajkumar Singh, IAS, Deputy Commissioner, Imphal West, attended as Guests of Honour. Dr. Salam Shantikumar Singh, Programme Coordinator, DACE, Manipur University, presided over the programme.

Addressing the gathering, Prof. R.K. Hemakumar Singh stressed the importance of disciplined and honest preparation for competitive examinations. He urged aspirants to recognise gaps in their knowledge, seek guidance from experts and avoid relying on guesswork. Punctuality, regular attendance and effective use of time, he said, remain essential to serious preparation.

Appreciating the work of DACE and the achievements of its students, the Vice-Chancellor called for continued strengthening of the Centre through greater academic support, engagement of experts and improvement of the learning environment so that aspirants can compete effectively at different levels.

Mayanglambam Rajkumar Singh, IAS, Deputy Commissioner, Imphal West, urged students to treat their experiences, successes and setbacks as opportunities for reflection and growth. Recalling his earlier interactions with civil service aspirants at DACE, he said young people entering public service would have opportunities to understand existing systems and contribute towards improving them.

Drawing on examples from public service delivery, he highlighted the need to examine both the strengths and limitations of different welfare delivery mechanisms. He also spoke about the growing role of technology and artificial intelligence in governance, while stressing that technology should strengthen systems and service delivery rather than replace human judgement.

Encouraging aspirants to work wholeheartedly towards competitive examinations, Rajkumar said the experiences gathered during their preparation should help them understand their strengths and decide how they want to move forward in life.

Lt Gen (Retd) Konsam Himalay Singh congratulated the successful candidates and reminded aspirants that success should not be measured merely by securing a particular post. He linked meaningful achievement with responsibility, humility, character and service to society.

He said clearing an examination should be regarded as the beginning of a longer journey rather than its end and encouraged students to face obstacles with dedication, discipline and perseverance. Describing DACE as having the potential to serve as a “diamond-polishing centre” for Manipur’s talent, he emphasised the need for quality coaching, expert guidance and stronger infrastructure.

R.K. Nimai Singh reflected on the changing educational environment and growing competition faced by the younger generation. Drawing from his own student days, he underlined the importance of discipline, systematic preparation, time management and maintaining a balance between academics and other pursuits. He also reminded students of their responsibilities towards society and the institutions that help shape them.

Prof. N. Basanta Singh congratulated the successful candidates and appreciated the faculty and staff of DACE for the Centre’s achievements. He reminded the successful candidates that clearing a competitive examination was an important milestone, but only the beginning of their larger responsibilities. Wherever they serve, he urged them to uphold honesty and integrity and contribute meaningfully to society.

Prof. Basanta also proposed that Manipur University explore the feasibility of introducing GATE coaching through DACE, pointing out that GATE scores are used by various organisations for recruitment and other opportunities. He said such coaching could create another important avenue for engineering students and aspirants in Manipur.

Prof. N. Mohilal Meitei focused on perseverance and mental preparedness while facing competitive examinations and challenges in life. He told students that difficulties and frustration are part of the process of growth and that success often depends on how one responds to adversity.

He stressed that candidates should not allow fear, anxiety or earlier limitations to define what they can achieve. Referring to the role of DACE, he said the Centre should guide and prepare young people to move beyond barriers and open doors to wider opportunities. He congratulated the Centre on its fifth Foundation Day and the successful candidates on their achievements.

Presenting an account of the Centre’s progress and achievements, Dr. Shantikumar said 27 students of DACE have secured positions in different government services, while 16 students have qualified NET/JRF. He said the Centre chose to recognise the NET/JRF qualifiers alongside those entering government service as their academic achievement could open further opportunities in higher education.

He said DACE follows a rigorous coaching schedule, including regular monitoring of attendance and follow-up with students preparing for competitive examinations. He stressed that although coaching is provided free of cost under the scheme, students are expected to maintain discipline, regular attendance and commitment to their preparation.

Tracing the institutional journey of the Centre, Dr. Shantikumar referred to Manipur University’s engagement with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, under the free coaching initiative. He said that following an assessment of its performance, the Centre has received a further three-year extension to continue its activities.

He further said that DACE would expand its coaching initiatives under the schemes entrusted to the Centre, including coaching programmes for eligible Persons with Disabilities (PWD) candidates.

At the same time, the Programme Coordinator drew attention to infrastructure constraints faced by DACE. He said the Centre currently has only two classrooms with a combined capacity of around 80 students, limiting the number of aspirants who can be accommodated. He sought the University’s support for additional space and improvement of basic facilities, including sanitation and water supply.

Earlier, Heigrujam Premkumar Singh, faculty member of DACE, delivered the welcome address. He welcomed the dignitaries, faculty members, successful candidates, alumni, students and participants and expressed the hope that the achievements being celebrated would inspire present aspirants to dream bigger and work consistently towards their goals.

Speaking on behalf of the successful alumni, N. Malemnganbi Chanu of the Manipur Secretariat Service (MSS) recalled that she had joined DACE with a dream but also with doubts and uncertainties. She said the Centre provided not merely guidance and preparation for competitive examinations but also the confidence to keep moving forward and, most importantly, to believe in herself.

She expressed gratitude to Dr. Salam Shantikumar Singh, the faculty members and mentors for their guidance, patience and encouragement. She said the felicitation was not merely an honour but also a reminder of where her journey began, how far she had come and the people who helped her along the way.

She also thanked the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, for supporting the initiative and providing students with opportunities to prepare, grow and move closer to their goals.

The programme included the felicitation of successful candidates and recognition of faculty members associated with the Centre, along with a group song and other programme items. A booklet titled, "Success Story of Dr Ambedkar Centre of Excellence, Manipur University" was also released. Arbind Salam proposed the vote of thanks.

The fifth Foundation Day highlighted DACE’s continuing role in providing structured coaching and academic support to competitive examination aspirants while also drawing attention to the need for stronger infrastructure and wider coaching opportunities for students in Manipur.

***

        RCT

item.description:
Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Government of India, today virtually launched the auction of two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea for grant of Composite Licence, in the presence of Shri Kadam Sandeep Vasant, Joint Secretary and Administering Authority, Ministry of Mines, and other senior officials. The launch marks an important step towards unlocking India’s offshore mineral potential and strengthening the country’s long-term mineral security.
…
item.content:encoded:
Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Government of India, today virtually launched the auction of two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea for grant of Composite Licence, in the presence of Shri Kadam Sandeep Vasant, Joint Secretary and Administering Authority, Ministry of Mines, and other senior officials. The launch marks an important step towards unlocking India’s offshore mineral potential and strengthening the country’s long-term mineral security.

The two blocks Sewell Rise-01 and West Sewell Ridge-01 are located in strategically significant offshore areas and together cover an area of over 1,632 square kilometres. The blocks contain contain polymetallic nodules and crusts, which host minerals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements. These minerals are important for advanced manufacturing, clean energy technologies, electric mobility, electronics and other strategic applications.

Details of blocks put up for auction:

S. No.

Name of the Block

Offshore Region

Minerals

1

Sewell Rise -01

Southern Part of Sewell Rise, Andaman Sea

Polymetallic Nodules and Crusts

2

West Sewell Ridge -01

Off Great Nicobar Island, Andaman Sea

Polymetallic Nodules and Crusts

 

Addressing the participants, Shri Keshav Chandra highlighted the importance of offshore mineral resources as a new frontier for India’s mineral sector and noted that systematic exploration of these resources would complement efforts to enhance domestic mineral availability. He also emphasised the need for scientific, technological and environmentally responsible development of offshore mineral resources.

The Secretary urged prospective bidders, industry stakeholders and capable explorers to participate actively in the auction process and contribute towards making the initiative successful. He encouraged greater participation and investment in offshore exploration, along with the adoption of appropriate technological capabilities for responsible resource development.

The launch event was attended by senior officials of the Ministry of Mines, representatives of scientific and technical institutions, industry stakeholders, public sector enterprises, prospective bidders and members of the media.

The sale of Tender Documents commenced on October 01, 2026. The Pre-Bid Conference will be held on November 04, 2026, and the last date for submission of queries is November 13, 2026. The last date for purchase of Tender Documents is December 21, 2026, up to 17:00 hours IST, while bids can be submitted up to December 28, 2026, by 17:00 hours IST.

Detailed information on the blocks, auction terms, eligibility criteria and timelines is available on the MSTC auction platform. The auction will be conducted through a transparent electronic auction process in accordance with the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002 and the Offshore Areas Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2024, as amended from time to time.

The launch of auction of the two offshore mineral blocks marks a further step towards systematic exploration and development of India’s offshore mineral resources, with a focus on strengthening mineral security, encouraging investment and building capabilities for their responsible development.

item.description:
Goa, 1 October 2026
The Directorate General of Taxpayer Services (DGTS) and the CGST Goa Commissionerate highlighted digital-first, taxpayer-centric reform measures being undertaken through the "Bharat Sarkar Aapke Dwaar" initiative in Goa. Shri Sumit Kumar, Principal Additional Director General, DGTS, Mumbai, shared this information during a joint press conference held in Panaji today.
The Directorate General of Taxpayer Services (DGTS), Mumbai Zonal Unit, in…
item.content:encoded:
Goa, 1 October 2026

 

The Directorate General of Taxpayer Services (DGTS) and the CGST Goa Commissionerate highlighted digital-first, taxpayer-centric reform measures being undertaken through the "Bharat Sarkar Aapke Dwaar" initiative in Goa. Shri Sumit Kumar, Principal Additional Director General, DGTS, Mumbai, shared this information during a joint press conference held in Panaji today.

The Directorate General of Taxpayer Services (DGTS), Mumbai Zonal Unit, in collaboration with the CGST Goa Commissionerate, hosted the briefing at GST Bhawan, Panaji. The event marked the successful culmination of a four-day intensive outreach program across Goa aimed at enhancing taxpayer facilitation, strengthening grievance redressal, and boosting voluntary compliance.

Shri Subodh Singh, Commissioner of CGST Goa, delivered the welcome address and introductory remarks, highlighting the Commissionerate’s ongoing local initiatives and commitment to maintaining a transparent and efficient tax environment. Following the welcome, Shri Sumit Kumar, Principal Additional Director General (Pr. ADG), DGTS, Mumbai, addressed the media on key national and regional tax administration reforms.

Emphasizing the central government’s commitment to doorstep service delivery under the philosophy of "Bharat Sarkar Aapke Dwaar", Shri Sumit Kumar stated that indirect tax administration covering GST, Customs, and Central Excise is now completely digital and compliance-driven. He noted that over 99 percent of taxpayers currently have zero physical contact with the department, as registrations, tax payments, return filings, and refund claims are managed entirely online.

To address the minimal percentage of taxpayers who require operational support, a robust multi-layered grievance redressal framework remains active. Taxpayers can engage directly through email, WhatsApp messages, or formal letters to local field formations and Commissioners. Escalations handled through DGTS maintain a 100 percent resolution success rate. Furthermore, under the CPGRAMS portal monitored by the Prime Minister’s Office and the Cabinet Secretariat, the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) consistently ranks among the top three to four central government departments nationwide out of nearly 99 departments in grievance resolution quality. Statutory safeguards through RTI mechanisms and appellate authorities further ensure institutional accountability, Shri Kumar stated.

Highlighting trade facilitation innovations in Customs, Shri Sumit Kumar detailed the 'Atithi' mobile application, which allows international passengers to file necessary declarations up to three days before or after travel. He also elaborated on the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) trust-based clearance system that facilitates the seamless movement of goods without human intervention. Additionally, he shared information on schemes such as duty deferment and EMI options, which enhance liquidity and working capital availability for manufacturers.

Shri Kumar outlined the public outreach initiatives undertaken by DGTS, particularly the "Taxpayer Education On Demand" framework. Under this initiative, specialized workshops are organized for trade bodies and tax practitioners following major policy changes, such as decisions taken during GST Council meetings. Simultaneously, consumer literacy drives are being expanded across schools, colleges, and universities to raise awareness among citizens regarding valid invoices and verifiable GSTIN numbers.

Presenting local performance metrics, Shri Subodh Singh highlighted the significant revenue contributions and robust infrastructure of the CGST Goa Commissionerate. Goa currently counts 20,960 registered taxpayers who have contributed ₹1,143.87 Crores in revenue up to August for the current financial year, with the accommodation and food & beverage sectors leading tax collections. The local GST Seva Kendra situated on the ground floor of GST Bhawan in Panaji has assisted over 2,000 visitors. To support the working capital needs of businesses, online refund claims are processed within 3 to 7 days, alongside provisional refunds of up to 90 percent sanctioned swiftly for eligible taxpayers, Shri Singh stated.

The press briefing concluded the four-day outreach program conducted by DGTS from September 28 to October 1, 2026, which included internal sessions with CGST Goa officers, an industrial visit to Goa Shipyard Limited, trade awareness programs, and academic interactions at BITS Pilani (Goa Campus) and Goa Business School at Goa University.

Concluding the session, Shri Sumit Kumar urged media representatives to contact the jurisdictional commissioners to obtain official context and clarifications on policy, technical, or operational matters prior to publishing any news reports.

 

* * *

(Source: CGST, Goa) | PIB Panaji | Nana Meshram/Ambadas Yadav/Darshana Rane

item.content:encoded:
As part of the Swachhta Hi Seva 2026 campaign, a series of activities were organised at the National Media Centre (NMC), PIB Headquarters, focusing on environmental sustainability, cleanliness, sanitation and recognition of sanitation workers.

A tree plantation drive was organised on September 30 under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative. The drive aimed to promote environmental sustainability and enhance green cover while encouraging collective participation in creating a cleaner and greener environment. It also highlighted the importance of nurturing trees and protecting the environment as a shared responsibility.

Today, on October 1, a cleanliness drive was organised under the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative. The drive focused on the cleanliness and upkeep of the NMC premises and encouraged officers and officials to contribute towards maintaining a clean and hygienic workplace. It also reinforced the importance of sanitation, hygiene and collective responsibility in furthering the objectives of Swachh Bharat.

A felicitation ceremony for Safai Mitras/ Swachhagrahis/ Sanitation Workers was also organised today at the NMC. The ceremony recognised their dedicated efforts and valuable contributions towards maintaining cleanliness and sanitation at the workplace. The initiative highlighted the importance of acknowledging the role of sanitation workers and encouraging their continued contribution towards a cleaner and healthier environment.

The activities were led by the Principal Director General, PIB, with the participation of officers and officials, reaffirming the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, cleanliness and a greener and healthier future.

The series of activities reflected PIB’s commitment to the objectives of Swachhta Hi Seva 2026 and to promoting a culture of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and collective participation.

The Ministry of Jal Shakti, under the leadership of the Union Minister for Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil and Minister of State, Shri V. Somanna, organized a large-scale Shramdaan activity today at 7:30 AM at Kalindi Kunj Ghat, Okhla Barrage in New Delhi as part of the nationwide campaign for Shramdaan activity under Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026-Nirantar Prayas.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister for Jal Shakti, recalled the emphasis given by Mahatma Gandhi to “Swachhata” along with “Swantantra”, which continues to guide the nation. He told that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narender Modi, the Swachhata Andolan has achieved new heights. He expressed gratitude towards the efforts of Safai-Mitras who with their dedication help to keep the country clean. The minister also urged the citizens to make Swachhata a collective responsibility by ensuring cleanliness in their surroundings. He emphasized that cleanliness is not just a periodic event but a continuous commitment towards maintaining clean environment and river conservation.

Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, in his welcome address stated that the Shramdaan is a part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign. He reiterated that Jan Bhagidari has been an important principle of Swachhata Andolan, hence today’s shramdaan is another step towards bringing the community together, to reaffirm our commitment to Swachhata.

 

Secretary, DoWR, RD & GR, Smt. Archana Varma alongwith other senior officers and staff of the Department spearheaded the cleanliness drive.

The Shramdaan saw active participation of Senior officers& staff of 16 organizations of the Department including CWC, NMCG, NWDA, CSMRS, NDSA, NRCD, NWIC, NWM, UYRB, GFCC, CWMA, and WAPCOS, etc. More than 1,100 officials and volunteers under the Ministry of Jal Shakti actively participated in the cleanliness drive and helped in removing plastic waste, debris, and riverbank litteracross the Kalindi Kunj Ghat area. This cleanliness drive will be a continued effort leading to Swachh Bharat-Viksit Bharat.

item.title: India’s Dr. Bimal N. Patel Takes Oath as Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) at the Tribunal’s headquarters in Hamburg, Germany
item.description:
Hamburg/Gandhinagar, Dr. Bimal N. Patel , an eminent international law jurist, scholar, practitioner and institution-builder of global standing, took oath today as a Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) at the Tribunal’s headquarters in Hamburg, Germany.
Dr. Patel assumes this eminent international judicial office for a nine-year term commencing on 1 October 2026 , marking a significant milestone in a distinguished career devoted to international law,…
item.content:encoded:
Hamburg/Gandhinagar, Dr. Bimal N. Patel, an eminent international law jurist, scholar, practitioner and institution-builder of global standing, took oath today as a Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) at the Tribunal’s headquarters in Hamburg, Germany.

Dr. Patel assumes this eminent international judicial office for a nine-year term commencing on 1 October 2026, marking a significant milestone in a distinguished career devoted to international law, law of the sea, ocean governance, maritime security, legal scholarship and public institution-building.

Dr. Patel was elected on 18 June 2026 at the Thirty-sixth Meeting of States Parties to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) held at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Seven members were elected to the Tribunal at the meeting.

Members of ITLOS are elected by the States Parties to UNCLOS from among persons enjoying the highest reputation for fairness and integrity and possessing recognised competence in the field of the law of the sea. The Tribunal comprises 21 independent members, elected with due regard to equitable geographical distribution and representation of the principal legal systems of the world.

A Distinguished Career in International Law and the Law of the Sea

Dr. Patel has made extensive contributions to the development, interpretation and study of international law, with particular emphasis on the law of the sea, maritime governance, international adjudication and State responsibility. He has served as a Member of the United Nations International Law Commission (ILC) and as Chair of its Working Group on Succession of States in respect of State Responsibility, contributing to the Commission’s work on the progressive development and codification of international law.

Dr. Patel holds several prominent national and international responsibilities, including Member of India’s National Security Advisory Board; Member of the Committee on Antarctic Governance; Co-Chair of the Law of the Sea Interest Group of the American Society of International Law; Member of the High-Level Advisory Board of the International Committee of the Red Cross; and Lead Academic Adviser during India’s tenure on the United Nations Security Council in 2021–22.

Dr. Patel has also contributed to the development, interpretation and implementation of important legal and regulatory frameworks relating to India’s maritime domain, including areas concerning maritime anti-piracy, Antarctic governance, merchant shipping, private maritime security, deep seabed activities and admiralty jurisdiction.

Scholar and Institution-Builder

Alongside his work as an international legal expert, Dr. Patel has made a significant contribution to legal education and institution-building in India. He has successfully led and contributed to the development of premier national institutions, including Gujarat National Law University and Gujarat Maritime University, and currently serves as the Vice-Chancellor of Rashtriya Raksha University. His academic leadership has fostered international collaborations and capacity-building in international law, law of the sea, maritime law, national security and related areas.

A prolific scholar and publicist, Dr. Patel has authored or edited more than 25 books, besides numerous research papers and scholarly publications covering classical, contemporary and emerging areas of international law. His scholarship and Dressional engagement have consistently placed the International Law based governance of oceans, peaceful settlement of disputes and maritime cooperation at the centre of contemporary discourse.

Maritime Governance in a Changing Global Order

Dr. Patel assumes office at a time when the international law of the sea has acquired increasing significance in addressing questions relating to maritime boundaries, freedom of navigation, marine environmental protection, sustainable use of ocean resources, deep seabed activities and peaceful settlement of maritime disputes.

This broader maritime context also resonates with India’s evolving engagement with the Indian Ocean, the Global South and international maritime cooperation. In March 2025, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi articulated Vision MAHASAGAR, “Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions”, as an evolution of the SAGAR vision, with emphasis on development, capacity-building and mutual security across regions.

Against this wider backdrop, Dr. Patel’s elevation to ITLOS reflects the growing relevance of specialised expertise in the law of the sea and the vital role of international judicial institutions in advancing international law-based oceanic order.

About the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) is an independent international judicial body established under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

Headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, the Tribunal adjudicates disputes concerning the interpretation and application of UNCLOS and matters specifically provided for in other agreements that confer jurisdiction upon it. The Tribunal is composed of 21 independent members and has jurisdiction over a wide range of matters relating to the law of the sea. These include disputes concerning maritime delimitation, navigation, marine resources, protection and preservation of the marine environment, and other questions arising under the Convention.

Dr. Bimal N. Patel’s assumption of office as a Judge of ITLOS represents a distinguished milestone in his longstanding engagement with international law and the law of the sea, and also reflects India’s enduring commitment to a safe, secure, progressive and international law-based oceanic order.

**

item.title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Inaugurates E-Waste Collection Stall under Special Campaign 6 to Promote Critical Mineral Recovery
item.description:
Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy visited the park adopted by the Ministry of Mines at GPOA-3, Netaji Nagar, New Delhi, as part of Special Campaign 6. Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, planted saplings at the park in the presence of senior officials of the Ministry and reviewed the ongoing efforts towards its landscaping, beautification and development as a cleaner and greener public space.
The Ministry of Mines has…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy visited the park adopted by the Ministry of Mines at GPOA-3, Netaji Nagar, New Delhi, as part of Special Campaign 6. Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, planted saplings at the park in the presence of senior officials of the Ministry and reviewed the ongoing efforts towards its landscaping, beautification and development as a cleaner and greener public space.

The Ministry of Mines has adopted the park at GPOA-3 for planned landscaping, beautification and improvement of the surrounding area. The initiative aims to strengthen the upkeep of the public space while encouraging sustainable practices and greater ownership of shared spaces.

The Union Minister and Secretary, Ministry of Mines also inaugurated an E-Waste Collection Stall at GPOA-3, aimed at encouraging responsible collection and disposal of discarded electronic and electrical items. The initiative will create awareness about proper segregation, collection and authorised recycling of e-waste, while highlighting its potential as a source of critical minerals and other valuable materials.

The E-Waste Collection Drive will be conducted from October 2 to October 31, 2026. More than 44 office locations across the country, including over 28 locations in Maharashtra, have been identified for e-waste collection. E-waste collected through the campaign will be channelised through appropriate mechanisms for responsible recycling and resource recovery.

A key focus of the initiative is to highlight the resource value of e-waste, particularly its potential for recovery of critical minerals. Appropriate recycling and processing can help recover valuable materials, promote resource efficiency, reduce dependence on virgin resources and support the principles of a circular economy.

Under Special Campaign 6.0, identified geo heritage sites and other public spaces are also being taken up for cleanliness, upkeep and beautification. These initiatives reflect the Ministry of Mines’ focus on cleanliness, responsible resource utilisation, circular economy practices and recovery of critical minerals from secondary sources.

Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28, to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce. The absolute highest increase in MSP has been announced for Safflower at Rs.675 per quintal…
item.content:encoded:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the increase in the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for all mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28.

 

Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28, to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce. The absolute highest increase in MSP has been announced for Safflower at Rs.675 per quintal followed by Rapeseed & Mustard at Rs.413 per quintal. For Lentil (Masur), barley, gram, and wheat, there is an increase of Rs.390 per quintal, Rs.136 per quintal, Rs.83 per quintal and Rs.25 per quintal respectively.

*Refers to cost which includes all paid out costs such as those incurred on account of hired human labour, bullock labour/machine labour, rent paid for leased in land, expenses incurred on use of material inputs like seeds, fertilizers, manures, irrigation charges, depreciation on implements and farm buildings, interest on working capital, diesel/electricity for operation of pump sets etc., miscellaneous expenses and imputed value of family labour.

 

The increase in MSP for mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28 is in line with the Union Budget 2018-19 announcement of fixing the MSP at a level of at least 1.5 times of the All-India weighted average Cost of Production. The expected margin over All-India weighted average cost of production is 106 percent for wheat, followed by 96 percent for rapeseed & mustard; 92 per cent for lentil; 59 per cent for gram; 58 percent for barley; and 50 percent for safflower. This increased MSP of rabi crops will ensure remunerative prices to the farmers and incentivise crop diversification.

 

In the recent years, Government has been promoting the cultivation of crops, other than cereals such as pulses and oilseeds by offering a higher MSP for these crops.

The procurement of wheat during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3715 LMT as compared to 2254 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The procurement of 6 Rabi crops during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3921 LMT as compared to 2302 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

 

The MSP amount paid to Wheat growing famers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs. 7.31 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.56 Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The MSP amount paid to 6 Rabi crops growing farmers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs.8.36 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.65 Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

item.content:encoded:
The Union Ministry of Education has extended the last date for submission of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for the academic year 2026-27 to October 31, 2026. The extension will provide eligible students additional time to complete their applications on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and facilitate timely verification by the concerned authorities.

The revised schedule is as follows

Process

Last Date

Submission of Application

October 31, 2026

Institute Nodal Officer (L1) Verification

November 15, 2026

District Nodal Officer (L2) Verification

November 30, 2026

The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) has been open for student applications since June 1, 2026. Students are required to complete their One-Time Registration (OTR) on the portal before applying for the Scholarship. As on September 30, 2026, 88,522 fresh and 1,97,133 renewal applications had been submitted.

Students who have already submitted their applications should ensure that the applications are verified by the concerned Institute Nodal Officer (L1) by November 15 and District Nodal Officer (L2) by November 30, 2026.

NMMSS is aimed at supporting meritorious students from economically weaker sections and encouraging them to continue their education beyond Class VIII up to Class XII.

The scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year to eligible Class IX students who qualify in the selection examination conducted by the respective State/UT Governments. The scholarship is subsequently continued from Classes X to XII through renewal, subject to the prescribed academic requirements.

Eligible students studying in state government, government-aided and local body schools, receive ₹12,000 per annum, which is transferred directly to their bank accounts through DBT.

For appearing in the selection test, students must have secured at least 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in Class VII, with a 5-percentage point relaxation for SC/ST students. The parental income of the applicant should not exceed ₹3.50 lakh per annum.

The Ministry of Textiles is all set to conduct Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October to 31st October 2026 across its organisations, subordinate offices and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). The Campaign will focus on strengthening cleanliness, disposal of pending matters, efficient record management and, with special emphasis this year, Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

As part of the Preparatory Phase, the Ministry undertook extensive preparatory activities and set targets across various identified areas. The targets include disposal of 57 Public Grievances, 13 Public Grievance Appeals, 55 MP References and 26 Parliamentary Assurances. In addition, 240 cleanliness campaign sites have been identified for focused cleanliness activities. The Ministry has also identified 12,519 physical files due for review and 6,941 e-files put up for review, with a view to strengthening record management and reducing the accumulation of outdated records. As part of the Campaign, a target of 720 e-waste items has been identified for systematic collection, segregation and disposal. The identified e-waste includes Personal Computers (PCs), CPUs, I/O devices and other electronic and electrical items.

Identification and Assessment of E-Waste

As part of the preparations for Special Campaign 6, various electronic and electrical items lying unused, obsolete or found to be non-functional have been identified across the Ministry and its organisations. These items are being assessed for appropriate segregation and disposal through authorised channels, in accordance with applicable guidelines for environmentally responsible e-waste management.

The Ministry of Textiles, through concerted and coordinated efforts across its organisations, subordinate offices and PSUs, is reinforcing its commitment towards cleanliness and effective implementation of the Special Campaign 6.

As part of these initiatives, the institute’s Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA) Club spearheaded ‘Swachhata Abhiyan 2026’ in the historic and pilgrim town of Rajim, while the institute’s literary society, Literati, hosted an essay writing competition themed “Swachhata Se Samriddhi” (Prosperity Through…
item.content:encoded:
National Institute of Technology (NIT) Raipur organized multi-dimensional activities on 30 September 2026 to promote cleanliness, civic responsibility, environmental conservation, and social awareness. As part of these initiatives, the institute’s Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA) Club spearheaded ‘Swachhata Abhiyan 2026’ in the historic and pilgrim town of Rajim, while the institute’s literary society, Literati, hosted an essay writing competition themed “Swachhata Se Samriddhi” (Prosperity Through Cleanliness).

The primary objective of the cleanliness drive in Rajim was to sensitize local residents, pilgrims, and youth toward clean habits and proper waste disposal, while motivating them to maintain the hygiene of public spaces. The drive was organized under the guidance of Dr. Sudhakar Pandey, Regional Coordinator, UBA, NIT Raipur. 

Dr. Govardhan Bhatt (PI Coordinator, UBA), Dr. Deepika Agrawal and Dr. Shailendra Kumar Tripathi (Faculty In-charges, UBA Club), Mr. Vijay Verma (UBA Assistant), along with a large number of students, actively participated in the initiative.
During the visit, participants contributed voluntary labor (shramdaan) to thoroughly clean surrounding public areas and engaged in dialogue with local residents and shopkeepers. They urged the community to segregate waste, dispose of it at designated sites, curb the use of single-use plastics, and refrain from littering in open spaces. The students also took out an impactful cleanliness rally to disseminate key messages regarding solid waste management, hygienic practices, and environmental protection.

In addition with this, to encourage analytical and creative expression among youth, NIT Raipur’s Literati committee organized an essay writing competition on the theme “Swachhata Se Samriddhi,” under the guidance of Dr. Y. Vijaya Babu and Dr. Chetna S. Rajput. Students across disciplines participated actively, articulating their perspectives on sanitation, civic duties, environmental sustainability, and the indispensable role of a clean environment in building a prosperous nation.

These joint initiatives by NIT Raipur brought together community engagement, student leadership, and intellectual expression onto a common platform. The cleanliness drive in Rajim and the essay competition on campus reinforced the core ethos of the Swachh Bharat Mission, demonstrating that collective efforts and active civic participation are essential to building a healthy and prosperous India.

item.description: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj will observe Special Campaign 6.0, organised by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The Campaign seeks to institutionalise Swachhata in Government offices, reduce pendency, make public interaction with these offices smoother, and ensure collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste as per the Rules. Officers and staff of the Ministry actively participated in the cleanliness drive and Shramdaan…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj will observe Special Campaign 6.0, organised by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The Campaign seeks to institutionalise Swachhata in Government offices, reduce pendency, make public interaction with these offices smoother, and ensure collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste as per the Rules. Officers and staff of the Ministry actively participated in the cleanliness drive and Shramdaan activities held today, joining the collective effort towards a Swachh Bharat. During the Implementation Phase, beginning on 2nd October, Gandhi Jayanti, and continuing till 31st October 2026, the Ministry will take up 176 Public Grievances, 100 Public Grievance Appeals, 9 Parliamentary Assurances, 15 MP references and 4 State Government references for disposal while also generating space in the building by disposing of redundant material.

The Ministry has been an active participant in every edition of the Special Campaign since 2021. The Preparatory Phase, held from 15th to 30th September 2026, focused on ensuring the Ministry’s readiness for the Campaign. Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, visited the Divisions and Sections of the Ministry at Jeevan Bharati Building, New Delhi on 17th September 2026 to review Ministry’s preparedness for the Campaign. He encouraged officers and staff to ensure a pleasant working environment and keep the office premises clean to enhance productivity.  During the Preparatory Phase, the Ministry identified pending matters (including references from Members of Parliament, State Governments and the Prime Minister’s Office, and Parliamentary matters) for resolution. Record management was streamlined, cleanliness drive sites were selected, redundant materials were assessed for disposal, and e-waste items were identified for safe disposal under the E-Waste Management Rules. The relevant data was uploaded on the dedicated portal for the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6.0. The Implementation Phase will further reinforce the Ministry’s commitment to Swachhata, efficient governance and improved workplace management, fostering a cleaner and more productive work environment.

item.content:encoded:
Indian Naval Ship Tarkash, a frontline stealth frigate, arrived at Mombasa, Kenya, on 29 Sep 2026 for a goodwill port call as part of her deployment. The visit underscores the longstanding and multifaceted relationship between India and Kenya, two maritime nations connected by historical, cultural and people-to-people ties.

India and Kenya share a long history of maritime engagement across the Indian Ocean. As key maritime nations, both countries remain committed to fostering maritime ties and enhancing trust, understanding and interoperability between their Navies.

During the port call, personnel of the Indian and Kenya Navies will participate in a range of professional and social engagements, including interaction, cross-learning and cultural exchange. These activities will provide opportunities to share experiences and enhance interoperability.

Community outreach activities will also be undertaken, providing Naval personnel from both countries an opportunity to engage beyond the professional domain. Sports and community service activities will foster camaraderie and cultural understanding.

The port call reflects India’s commitment to maritime partnerships with friendly countries in the Indian Ocean Region and is in keeping with the spirit of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions). It is expected to further consolidate the enduring India–Kenya maritime partnership.
