The training session was attended by around 50 street food vendors and focused on essential…
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai, 1 October 2026

 

In a significant step towards strengthening food safety and hygiene practices among street food vendors, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), in collaboration with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), conducted the 57th food safety training session for street food vendors at Andheri, Mumbai, on September 30, 2026.

The training session was attended by around 50 street food vendors and focused on essential aspects of food safety, including personal hygiene, safe food handling practices, prevention of food contamination, cleanliness of food preparation areas, and hygienic storage and serving of food.

The training is part of the strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between FSSAI and BMC, under which more than 10,000 street food vendors across Mumbai are being covered through structured food safety training and awareness programmes.

The initiative aims to strengthen food safety practices at the street food level and promote safer and more hygienic food practices among vendors, thereby contributing to the objectives of the Eat Right India movement.

FSSAI and BMC will continue to undertake such capacity-building and awareness initiatives to enhance compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements among street food vendors across Mumbai.

 

* * *

item.title: From First Drop to Clean Streets
item.description:
Before the Rains, the Cities Move
As the monsoon approaches and the first rains arrive, cities across India begin preparations to address the seasonal risks associated with waterlogging, waste accumulation, and sanitation. Drains are cleaned, vulnerable locations are identified, and measures are undertaken to maintain cleanliness and public health. Under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs-led Safai Apnao, Bimaari Bhagao 2025 (SABB) campaign, urban local bodies…
item.content:encoded:
Before the Rains, the Cities Move

As the monsoon approaches and the first rains arrive, cities across India begin preparations to address the seasonal risks associated with waterlogging, waste accumulation, and sanitation. Drains are cleaned, vulnerable locations are identified, and measures are undertaken to maintain cleanliness and public health. Under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs-led Safai Apnao, Bimaari Bhagao 2025 (SABB) campaign, urban local bodies translated pre-monsoon preparedness into a coordinated cleanliness and public health effort. From 1 July to 31 July 2025, cities undertook drain cleaning, waste removal and hygiene promotion, while engaging communities through schools, neighbourhoods and other public spaces.

At the heart of the campaign are the ‘6 Swachhata Mantras’: clean hands, homes, neighbourhoods, toilets, drains and public spaces. Together, these simple practices are becoming part of a larger city-wide effort to keep the monsoon safer and healthier. And across the country, that effort is taking many different forms.

In Delhi, the campaign took the message to its streets and schools. 400 NCC girl cadets led a 3-km Pinkathon, a walkathon promoting monsoon hygiene and sanitation. The campaign saw significant on-the-ground action, including handwashing drives in 255 schools, while 206 cleaning drives covered backlanes and garbage vulnerable points (GVPs). Another 469 sanitation drives were conducted in community and public toilets (CTs and PTs). The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC) introduced ‘Manhole Ambulances’ to enhance urban safety and sanitation through swift, on-site manhole repairs. Each ambulance carries prefabricated manhole covers, repair tools, and a dedicated response team for immediate action, especially during rains. PMC repurposed old, unused municipal vehicles into functional units. Six ambulances, one per municipal zone, are operational and linked to PMC’s central control room for real-time complaint resolution. The initiative enables citizen-centric grievance redressal and ensures faster responses to manhole-related complaints.

In Navi Mumbai, a Swachhata rally was organised with the participation of over 600 students, parents, teachers, and citizens. Simultaneously, health awareness camps were held across 26 Urban Primary Health Centres, focusing on malaria and dengue prevention.  Over two days, 52 health camps were conducted, reaching more than 22,690 citizens. In Telangana, the campaign reached nearly 13 lakh households. Around 14,210 km of drains were desilted, while 4,343 km of roadside bushes were cleared. Nearly 2.5 lakh houses were covered through anti-dengue and malaria awareness drives. Health camps also benefited over 8,500 frontline workers. Meanwhile, 140 composting pits were set up in schools, encouraging young citizens to turn waste into manure.

In Chhattisgarh, the story begins with people themselves. In Pandariya, Self-Help Group members received sanitation training and were introduced to the Swachhata App. They then took part in a cleanliness drive. In Raipur, door-to-door outreach promoted hand hygiene and waste segregation, while Garbage Vulnerable Points (GVPs) were cleaned and beautified.

Northeast Unites for a Cleaner, Safer Monsoon

As the monsoon approaches, the Northeast is getting ready not by waiting for the rains, but by preparing for them. Across Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Assam, Sikkim and Tripura, the MoHUA-led SABB campaign is strengthening monsoon preparedness through collective cleanliness and disease prevention.

In Nagaland, Urban local bodies (ULBs) across six towns led school awareness activities, drain cleaning, health camps and cleanup drives. These efforts engaged nearly 5,000 people through 60 cleanliness, 30 rainwater harvesting and 40 post-monsoon awareness drives. Across the hills of Sikkim, the campaign took aim at garbage-prone areas and the risks of water- and vector-borne diseases. Students, officials and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) came together around source segregation and better waste management. Around 4,000 people participated in 100 cleanliness and 100 post-monsoon drives, alongside awareness rallies and PET bottle shredding initiatives. In Assam, towns focused on drain cleaning, garbage removal, SafaiMitra health check-ups and waste segregation. Around 5,500 people joined 200 cleanliness and 40 rainwater harvesting activities, supported by 160 organisations and NGOs.

In Tripura, ULBs strengthened waste collection, segregation and public toilet maintenance. Around 5,000 people participated in 150 cleanliness and 30 rainwater harvesting drives, alongside health camps, school rallies and sanitation initiatives. Across 47 urban notified towns in Arunachal Pradesh, efforts covered waste management, water quality and public toilet maintenance. Water treatment plants were inspected, while mass cleanliness drives targeted garbage-vulnerable points. These efforts demonstrate how cleanliness and disease prevention can be integrated into everyday community action.

From Backlanes to Clean, Vibrant Neighbourhood Spaces

A backlane refers to the space behind houses in a neighbourhood, generally characterised by limited pedestrian movement. Such areas can become vulnerable to waste accumulation and informal dumping. Recognising this, cities across Madhya Pradesh organised backlane cleaning drives with active public participation. The initiatives included the removal of encroachments and cleaning of drains to facilitate the smooth flow of rainwater during the monsoon.

In Rewa, the Municipal Corporation extended the effort beyond backlanes to improve the cleanliness and appearance of front lanes across all wards. Murals and wall paintings were created, while play equipment and musical instruments were developed using the principles of the 3Rs-Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. The walls also feature English and Hindi vowels and alphabets, numbers and multiplication tables. By integrating cleanliness with learning and recreational elements, the initiative has helped create safer, more engaging and child-friendly neighbourhood spaces.

In Agra, the Agra Municipal Corporation successfully cleaned and maintained nine backlanes across the city. The Urban Learning Internship Program (TULIP) trainees actively participated in the campaign, while local residents contributed to the cleaning and beautification of neighbourhood streets. Their participation demonstrates how community involvement can strengthen local ownership of cleanliness and support the sustained upkeep of shared public spaces.

From Safety to Opportunity

For Jyotsna Dhabde of Bhopal, access to institutional credit provided an opportunity to pursue entrepreneurship. At a Bhopal Municipal Corporation loan fair, she received a loan under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana, which enabled her to purchase a sanitation vehicle. In New Delhi, Raja, a supervisor with the New Delhi Municipal Council, shared his experience of mechanised sewer cleaning.

Raja says, “Earlier, we were compelled to enter the sewers to carry out sewer cleaning. But with the introduction of modern machines, the work is now executed using machines. In addition, being provided with safety gear such as gumboots, masks, safety glasses, helmets, and other protective equipment makes us feel safer.”

Together, these experiences illustrate efforts to make sanitation work safer, more skilled and more dignified.

The Safai Mitra Suraksha Challenge 2021 focused on health education, the provision and use of safety equipment, worker welfare and reduction of occupational risks. Under Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has emphasised the provision of protective equipment, training and safety awareness by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), to work towards zero fatalities in sanitation work.

As a pioneer in this space, Chandigarh has prohibited hazardous manual sewer cleaning since 2018. An Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU), operating under the Responsible Sanitation Authority (RSA), supports safer sanitation practices by providing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), safety gear and regular medical check-ups.

In Assam, 83 of 96 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) declared themselves SafaiMitra Surakshit Shehar in 2023. The state mapped 5,230 sanitation workers and organised 92 health camps. In Maharashtra, 246 Master Trainers were prepared during the first phase, followed by training for 1,917 sanitation workers. Uttar Pradesh supported SafaiMitras by facilitating access to credit and livelihood opportunities. Together, these measures seek to strengthen the safety, social and economic security, dignity and entrepreneurial opportunities of SafaiMitras, creating pathways from sanitation work towards sani-entrepreneurship.

From Preparedness to Community Action

As the rains arrive, the real value of pre-monsoon preparedness becomes visible on the ground. A cleared drain allows rainwater to flow freely, a clean street prevents waste buildup, and an early health camp helps communities spot and contain disease risks before they spread. At the heart of each measure is the active participation of citizens, making public health a shared responsibility.

From the hills of the Northeast to the streets of Delhi, and across communities in Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh, the campaign has taken diverse, localized forms. Yet underlying them all is a single unified truth: true monsoon preparedness is not merely about reacting to rainfall, but about preparing together —one street, one neighbourhood, and one community at a time.

https://sbmurban.org/safai-Apnao-Bimaari-Bhagao-2025
https://sbmurban.org/Back-Lanes-Cleaning

item.title: NHAI Rolls out Tamil Nadu’s First Barrierless Multi-Lane Free Flow Tolling System
item.description:
Key Highlights and Benefits:
First Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system implemented in Tamil Nadu at the Paranur Toll Plaza on the Tambaram – Tindivanam Section of NH-179B Introduces barrier-less tolling, enabling vehicles to pass through toll locations without stopping Significantly reduce human intervention in toll collection, saves fuel and time, cut down congestion, lower vehicular emissions, make toll operations more transparent and cost effective …
item.content:encoded:
Key Highlights and Benefits:

  • First Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system implemented in Tamil Nadu at the Paranur Toll Plaza on the Tambaram – Tindivanam Section of NH-179B
  • Introduces barrier-less tolling, enabling vehicles to pass through toll locations without stopping
  • Significantly reduce human intervention in toll collection, saves fuel and time, cut down congestion, lower vehicular emissions, make toll operations more transparent and cost effective
  • Promotes barrier-free and seamless commuting, enhancing ‘Ease of Travel’ for the National Highway users
  • Leverages technologies such as Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and FASTag to ensure seamless and efficient toll operations.

In a significant step towards transforming the Electronic Toll Collection system in the country, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has rolled out Tamil Nadu’s first Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) based tolling system at Paranur Toll Plaza on the Tambaram – Tindivanam Section of NH-179B. The MLFF system introduces barrier-less tolling, enabling vehicles to pass through toll locations without stopping. The system leverages advanced technologies such as Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and FASTag-based Electronic Toll Collection to ensure seamless and efficient toll operations. The initiative aligns with the Government of India’s vision of delivering citizen centric services by leveraging technology for enhancing Ease of Living and Ease of Doing Business.

MLFF :

The introduction of MLFF marks a transformational shift in Electronic Toll Collection on National Highways. By eliminating the need for vehicles to stop at toll plazas, the system will significantly reduce human intervention in toll collection system, cut down congestion, improve travel time, enhance fuel efficiency and lower vehicular emissions on National Highways.

NHAI is implementing MLFF based tolling at various National Highways across the country in a phased manner. In order to provide a faster, seamless and barrier-free travel experience, NHAI has successfully rolled out the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system at various locations in the country that includes Chorayasi Toll Plaza on Surat–Bharuch section of NH-48 in Gujarat; Mundka-Bakkarwala Toll Plaza on the Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II) in Delhi-NCR; Shahjahanpur, Daulatpura and Manoharpura Toll Plaza on Delhi–Jaipur section of NH-48 in Rajasthan; and Gharaunda Toll Plaza on the Panipat–Jalandhar section of National Highway-44 in Haryana.

For a seamless MLFF experience, National Highway users are required to maintain functional FASTag with sufficient balance to avoid Electronic Notice (E-Notice).

Implementation of MLFF has helped to strengthen the tolling ecosystem by enhancing transparency, reducing operational costs associated with setting up of physical toll plazas and improving overall efficiency in toll operations across the country.

***

GDH/DS

item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, participated in a series of activities organised under the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ campaign at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), New Delhi, today.

Addressing students, officers and staff, the Minister recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had launched the Swachh Bharat Mission in 2014 with the objective of making cleanliness a people’s movement.

“After Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the cleanliness campaign in 2014, people across the country became part of this movement. Cleanliness drives were also undertaken in offices and institutions. Today, along with students and officials at IIMC, we have taken the pledge for cleanliness. We should contribute through Swachhata Seva wherever possible, including at Anganwadi centres, temples, institutions and other public places. We have been carrying forward the cleanliness campaign since September 17. It is our collective responsibility to keep our country, institutions and offices clean,” the Minister said.

The programme commenced with the Swachhata pledge at the Institute, in which faculty members, officers, staff, students and Indian Information Service trainees participated.

The Minister also took part in the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative by planting a sapling on the IIMC campus. He interacted with students and emphasised the importance of not only planting trees but also ensuring their continued care and maintenance.

As part of the programme, the Minister participated in a one-hour Shramdaan at IIMC along with students, faculty members, officers and staff. The activity included clearing waste and construction material from the area as part of the cleanliness drive.

During his visit, the Minister also inspected newly constructed classrooms and other academic and infrastructure facilities, including the teaching block, hostel under construction and the renovated library. He interacted with students from different States and departments of the Institute.

The Minister appreciated the initiatives being undertaken by IIMC under its institutional leadership, particularly in the areas of cleanliness, environmental awareness, campus development and student participation.

Dr. Pragya Paliwal Gaur, Vice-Chancellor of IIMC , Sh. L Madhu Nag, Registrar & DG Training and  Sh. R.K Jena, Sr, Economic Advisor were present during the programme, along with faculty members, officers, staff, students and Officer trainees of the Institute.

The programme formed part of IIMC’s activities under the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign, aimed at encouraging collective participation in cleanliness, environmental conservation and responsible citizenship.

******

Mahesh Kumar/ Aparajita Priyadrashini

item.title: Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions
item.description: The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India , is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026. The survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises, thereby providing important inputs for understanding…
item.content:encoded:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026. The survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises, thereby providing important inputs for understanding emerging investment trends in the Indian economy.

1. Objective, Coverage and Method of Data Collection

The primary objective of the CAPEX Survey is to collect information on capital expenditure undertaken in the recent financial years, provisional capital expenditure in the current financial year and investment intentions for the forthcoming financial year. The information covers capital expenditure across different asset groups and industries, along with aspects relating to investment strategy, objectives, sources of financing, etc.

The survey covers selected large private corporate sector enterprises from different sectors of the economy. The survey frame is prepared using information relating to active enterprises registered with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), subject to prescribed eligibility and turnover criteria. The survey is conducted under the provisions of the Collection of Statistics Act, 2008.

Data are collected through a dedicated and secure web portal, enabling enterprises to self-compile and submit their responses online. The portal provides facilities to assist respondents in understanding the questionnaire, concepts and definitions. The present survey also provides supporting digital resources, including an instruction manual and video guide for portal navigation and self-reporting.

2. Earlier CAPEX Surveys – Key Findings and Outcomes

The National Statistical Office (NSO) conducted the inaugural Forward-Looking Survey on Private Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2024) between November 2024 and January 2025.

From this first ever CAPEX survey, the results show that during 2024-25 among the principal activity categories, ‘manufacturing’ accounts for the largest share of aggregate expenditure (43.80%). This is followed by ‘information and communication’ (15.60%) and ‘transportation and storage’ (14.00%).

 

The detailed results of the CAPEX survey are available in the CAPEX 2024 Booklet published by MoSPI:

CAPEX 2024 – Booklet on Findings of the Forward-Looking Survey

The second CAPEX survey was conducted during October–December 2025, the findings of this latest CAPEX survey (CAPEX 2025), indicated that of the provisional aggregate capital expenditure in 2025-26 among the principal activity categories, ‘manufacturing’ accounts for the largest share of aggregate expenditure (50.17%), amounting to ₹5,73,900 crore. This is followed by ‘information and communication’ (16.38%; ₹1,87,395 crore), ‘electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply’ (8.96%; ₹1,02,448 crore), and ‘transportation and storage’ (5.55%; ₹63,517 crore).

In terms of the proposed scale of CAPEX allocation, nearly 21.16% of enterprises planned to invest more than 80% of their total CAPEX in robotics while the around 78.84% stated that less than 20% of their total CAPEX would be devoted to robotics investments.

As per the estimates obtained from the latest CAPEX 2025 survey (2025-26), the actual CAPEX incurred during 2024-25 by the panel of enterprises was ₹173.5 crore per enterprise, resulting in an overall realisation ratio (RR) of 96.3%, indicating that actual expenditure was broadly in line with the investment intentions at the aggregate level.

From the data collected through the CAPEX survey-2025, the aggregated CAPEX figures (₹ crore) based on data reported by a fixed panel of 3,819 enterprises covering the years 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 show a modest growth of 1.9% over the actual CAPEX reported by these enterprises in 2024-25. This is given in graph below:

PANEL Estimates on Aggregate CAPEX (in crore)

The detailed results of the CAPEX survey are available in the CAPEX 2025 Booklet published by MoSPI:

CAPEX 2025 – Booklet on Findings of the Forward-Looking Survey

3. Launch of CAPEX 2026

Building upon the experience and outcomes of the earlier two rounds of CAPEX survey, in October 2026, NSO is launching the third CAPEX survey to further strengthen the availability of timely information on private corporate investment activity and future investment intentions.

4. Salient Features of CAPEX 2026

The present survey incorporates several features intended to improve the quality, relevance and usability of the information collected as well as to improve the user interface with the portal for submitting information.

Broad coverage of information in the survey:

  • Collection of information on past, current and future capital expenditure
  • Information on CAPEX across different asset groups and industry sectors
  • Information on investment intentions and investment strategies
  • Investment in green energy and robotics
  • Information on the objectives of investment, including capacity expansion/upgradation and other investment purposes
  • Information on sources of financing of CAPEX

Features of the web-portal:

  • Collection through a secure, dedicated web portal
  • Facility for self-compilation and online submission by enterprises
  • Digital assistance through an instruction manual, video guide and AI chatbot to facilitate portal navigation and reporting
  • Bilingual questionnaire

5. Importance of Timely Response

The quality and usefulness of the estimates generated from the CAPEX Survey depend significantly on the coverage and timely response of the selected enterprises. Information furnished by individual enterprises contributes to the compilation of aggregate indicators of private corporate investment and helps in understanding the direction and magnitude of investment activity in different sectors.

Timely submission also enables NSO to undertake the necessary validation and processing of the information within the prescribed survey schedule, thereby facilitating the timely availability of reliable statistics for policymakers and other stakeholders.

6. Appeal to the Industry

NSO, MoSPI, therefore, appeals to all selected private corporate sector enterprises to extend their full cooperation and participate actively in the CAPEX 2026 Survey. Enterprises are requested to furnish complete, accurate and timely information through the designated web portal.

Enterprises are assured of the confidentiality of their individual data, and that unit-level information will not be disseminated. While disseminating the survey results, care is taken not to release any information, which could identify the enterprise that has furnished it. While releasing the results, adequate measures are applied to prevent the publication or disclosure of any information deemed confidential. To protect the confidentiality of CAPEX investment plans of individual enterprises, unit-level data of CAPEX survey are not disseminated.

NSO, MoSPI appreciates the cooperation of all selected enterprises in making CAPEX 2026 a successful statistical exercise.

Booklet available in MoSPI website: https://www.mospi.gov.in/ Scan QR code to access MoSPI Publications/ Reports

****

Samrat

item.description:
The National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research - Ahmedabad is participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters-6.0 (SCDPM-6.0), scheduled to be implemented from 02 October to 31 October 2026, with a preparatory phase from 15 September to 30 September 2026.
The campaign aims to further institutionalize cleanliness, efficient disposal of pending matters and references, effective record management, and scientific management of e-waste across the…
item.content:encoded:
The National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research - Ahmedabad is participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters-6.0 (SCDPM-6.0), scheduled to be implemented from 02 October to 31 October 2026, with a preparatory phase from 15 September to 30 September 2026.

The campaign aims to further institutionalize cleanliness, efficient disposal of pending matters and references, effective record management, and scientific management of e-waste across the Institute.

During the preparatory phase, NIPER-Ahmedabad is undertaking a systematic assessment and identification of pending matters, records and obsolete/unusable items requiring appropriate action. The Institute is also focusing on identifying e-waste for scientific segregation, disposal and channelization through appropriate mechanisms in accordance with applicable guidelines.

The campaign will also emphasize clean and organized office and institutional spaces, efficient utilization of available resources, disposal of obsolete materials, and timely resolution of pending references. Faculty members, officers, staff and students are being encouraged to actively participate in the campaign and contribute towards creating a cleaner, more efficient and environmentally responsible institutional ecosystem.

Through SCDPM-6.0, NIPER-Ahmedabad reaffirms its commitment to Swachhata, sustainability, responsible resource management and good governance, while strengthening cleanliness and administrative efficiency as an integral part of the Institute's institutional practices.

The campaign will be carried out in coordination with the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemical and Fertilizers, New Delhi, with due emphasis on scientific and environmentally responsible disposal of e-waste and other identified waste materials.

item.title: Department of Posts Takes Special Campaign 6 to the Last Mile with Focus on Swachhata, Efficiency and Customer-Centric Services
item.description:
The Department of Posts has launched the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, which will be undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026 across its extensive nationwide network. The campaign is aimed at further institutionalising Swachhata, efficient record management, reduction of pendency and environmentally responsible waste management, with a special emphasis on the scientific management of e-waste and sustainable utilisation of departmental resources.
During Special…
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Posts has launched the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, which will be undertaken from 2nd October to 31st October 2026 across its extensive nationwide network. The campaign is aimed at further institutionalising Swachhata, efficient record management, reduction of pendency and environmentally responsible waste management, with a special emphasis on the scientific management of e-waste and sustainable utilisation of departmental resources.

During Special Campaign 5, the Department covered 1.30 lakh campaign sites, disposed of 1,00,000 public grievances, reviewed and weeded out 17,352 files and e-files, freed 23,287 sq. ft. of office space and generated ₹1.02 crore through disposal of scrap and waste material.

Building on these outcomes, Special Campaign 6 seeks to further institutionalise these practices and integrate them into routine functioning across the Department.

Key Focus Areas of Special Campaign 6

Under Special Campaign 6, the Department of Posts has set the following targets:

  • Liquidation of pendency in public grievances and appeals – target for Special Campaign 6 is resolution of 1,50,000 grievances and 1500 appeals.
  • Cleanliness campaigns at 1,35,000 sites across the country.

These targets are intended to provide a focused and measurable framework for improving efficiency, cleanliness and responsiveness throughout the Department.

Swachhata: Taking the Last-Mile Approach

The Department of Posts is adopting a last-mile approach to Swachhata, extending its efforts beyond the physical cleanliness of Post Office premises to include clean processes, greater efficiency, accountability and a cultural reorientation among personnel.

The campaign covers all categories of Post Offices, including rural Branch Post Offices (BOs), with the objective of embedding cleanliness and efficient work practices into day-to-day functioning. The initiative seeks to strengthen citizen-centricity, responsive service delivery and the overall customer experience.

Improving the Customer Experience

As part of its efforts to modernise the postal network, the Department is also focusing on the renovation and modernisation of Post Office buildings in accordance with the design manual developed in collaboration with the School of Planning and Architecture, New Delhi.

The objective is to go beyond aesthetic improvements and create Post Offices that are functional, accessible, customer-friendly and future-ready.

The Department is also opening N-Gen Post Offices, featuring clean and modern interiors and exteriors, with the objective of creating contemporary postal spaces that are more welcoming and relevant to the needs of younger customers.

Further, SPA Post Offices are being renovated and modernised to upgrade existing facilities and promote uniform branding across the postal network. These initiatives are aimed at improving functionality, accessibility and the overall experience of customers visiting Post Offices.

Jan Sampark – Dak Chaupal

Under Special Campaign 6, the Department of Posts is organising Dak Chaupal to strengthen citizen engagement and bring Government services closer to the people. The initiative focuses on Digital India, financial inclusion and Antyodaya, with emphasis on last-mile delivery. Citizens are being sensitised about financial services, insurance, DBT, Payments Bank, e-commerce and export services, along with various Government welfare schemes and their benefits.

Stamping a cleaner tomorrow, one letter at a time!

India Post introduced a Special Cancellation on Swachhata Campaign 2026 on September 17th. Spreading a vital message with every dispatched piece of mail, this special cancellation reminds us to strive for "Freedom from waste with everyone's participation".

Towards Sustainable and Institutionalised Swachhata

Special Campaign 6 reaffirms the Department of Posts commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, efficiency, sustainability and citizen-centric service delivery. The campaign seeks to sustain these practices across its nationwide network and strengthen the quality of services for citizens.

*****

AMK/AR

item.title: Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tripura Launches Digi SAPNE 3.0
item.description:
Agartala, 1 October 2026: The Digital Startup Acceleration Program for North East (Digi SAPNE) 3.0 was formally launched today by Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tripura, Prof. Dr. Manik Saha , at the Agartala Women’s College Auditorium, marking another significant milestone in strengthening the technology and startup ecosystem of the Northeastern region.
The programme was attended by Shri Pranajit Singha Roy , Hon’ble Minister for Finance, Planning & Coordination and Information…
item.content:encoded:
Agartala, 1 October 2026: The Digital Startup Acceleration Program for North East (Digi SAPNE) 3.0 was formally launched today by Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tripura, Prof. Dr. Manik Saha, at the Agartala Women’s College Auditorium, marking another significant milestone in strengthening the technology and startup ecosystem of the Northeastern region.

The programme was attended by Shri Pranajit Singha Roy, Hon’ble Minister for Finance, Planning & Coordination and Information Technology, Government of Tripura; Shri Kishor Barman, Hon’ble Minister for Higher Education, Government of Tripura; Shri Kiran Kumar Gitte, Secretary to the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tripura; Dr. Prashant Kumar Goyal, IAS, Secretary, IT & Finance, Government of Tripura; Shri Rajeshwar Singh Jenwar, Director and Head, Software Industry Promotion Division, Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India; Dr. Gopalakrishna Prabhu, Vice Chancellor, Sikkim Manipal University and Chairman, AIC-SMUTBI; and Shri Jeya Ragul Geshan B., IFS, Government of Tripura, along with startups, students, innovators and ecosystem stakeholders.

Chief Minister Highlights Role of Digi SAPNE and AIC-SMUTBI

Speaking at the launch, Hon’ble Chief Minister Prof. Dr. Manik Saha called upon young innovators to convert their ideas into useful products, services and sustainable enterprises, emphasising the important role of technology and entrepreneurship in creating employment and economic opportunities.

The Chief Minister highlighted the growing support available to young entrepreneurs through startup programmes implemented with the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and specifically acknowledged the contribution of AIC-SMUTBI in supporting startups from the Northeast through Digi SAPNE.

He noted that since the launch of Digi SAPNE, Tripura startups have benefited from the programme, with startups receiving financial support of ₹10 lakh each under Digi SAPNE 2.0. He further highlighted that Digi SAPNE 3.0 will provide grants of up to ₹80 lakh in aggregate support to high-potential startups, strengthening the pipeline of technology-driven enterprises emerging from the Northeast.

The Chief Minister emphasised that such programmes can help young people move from job seekers to job creators, while enabling startups to build scalable businesses based on local opportunities and regional strengths.

Digi SAPNE 3.0 to Focus on Emerging Opportunities

Implemented by AIC-SMU Technology Business Incubation Foundation (AIC-SMUTBI) with funding support from MeitY, Government of India, Digi SAPNE is designed to identify, mentor and accelerate early-stage startups from the eight Northeastern states.

The third edition will place particular emphasis on areas including tourism, agri-tech and Artificial Intelligence, sectors with significant potential for the Northeast and Tripura.

Through structured acceleration, mentoring, market access, investor engagement and financial support, Digi SAPNE seeks to help promising startups move from early-stage innovation towards sustainable and scalable enterprises.

MeitY Calls for Problem-led Innovation

Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajeshwar Singh Jenwar, Director and Head, Software Industry Promotion Division, MeitY, emphasised that innovation begins with identifying a problem rather than simply developing technology.

He highlighted challenges such as agricultural losses, limited access to healthcare, disaster response and drinking water as opportunities for young entrepreneurs to develop locally relevant solutions. Referring to Tripura’s floods, its GI-tagged Queen Pineapple and its substantial bamboo resources, he urged students and innovators to look at challenges around them as opportunities for entrepreneurship.

He also highlighted the example of HN Technovations, founded at Tripura University under the leadership of Prof. Harjeet Nath, which developed a portable solar and electric water purification system for disaster-relief situations. The solution was used during the Silchar floods and subsequently supplied approximately 5,000 litres of safe drinking water in two days at a relief camp in Gomati district during the August 2024 floods.

Calling upon young people to participate in the Seva First Innovation Challenge, Shri Jenwar urged them to focus on one fundamental question: “What problem can I solve?”

He encouraged students to utilise nearby college laboratories and incubation centres, build multidisciplinary teams and work closely with people who understand the problems being addressed.

₹80 Lakh Distributed to Eight Startups

A key highlight of the programme was the distribution of ₹10 lakh each to eight startups, amounting to ₹80 lakh, selected from Digi SAPNE Cohort 2.0 during the recently concluded Himalayan Investors Meet (HIM ’26) in Gangtok.

The eight startups, representing seven Northeastern states, are:

Building a Pan-Northeast Startup Ecosystem

The launch of Digi SAPNE 3.0 in Tripura reinforces the growing collaboration between MeitY, Government of India, Government of Tripura and AIC-SMUTBI to create stronger pathways for innovation and entrepreneurship across the Northeast.

The participation of startups from multiple Northeastern states and the distribution of grants to enterprises emerging from different parts of the region demonstrate the programme’s pan-Northeast approach.

Digi SAPNE seeks to create an ecosystem where entrepreneurs can build businesses rooted in the needs and strengths of the Northeast while accessing national markets, investors, mentors, technology support and institutional networks.

The programme also provides an important platform for students and young innovators to transition from ideas to enterprises and from local solutions to scalable businesses.

About AIC-SMUTBI

AIC-SMU Technology Business Incubation Foundation (AIC-SMUTBI) is an Atal Incubation Centre supported by the Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, and established in partnership with Sikkim Manipal University. AIC-SMUTBI works to strengthen the startup ecosystem across the Northeast through incubation, acceleration, mentoring, funding facilitation, market access and investor engagement.

Digi SAPNE – Digital Startup Acceleration Program for North East is one of AIC-SMUTBI’s flagship initiatives, supported by MeitY, focused on accelerating technology and digital startups from the eight Northeastern states and connecting them with opportunities at the national and global level.

item.title: Minister of Parliamentary Affairs leads “Ek Din – Ek Ghanta – Ek Saath Shramdaan” under Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026
item.description:
As part of the nationwide “Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) Campaign 2026”, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs organized “Ek Din – Ek Ghanta – Ek Saath Shramdaan” today at Navyug School, Peshwa Road, New Delhi.
The cleanliness drive was led by Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs & Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju. The event was attended by Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal; Chairman, NDMC, Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi; Additional Secretary,…
item.content:encoded:
As part of the nationwide “Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) Campaign 2026”, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs organized “Ek Din – Ek Ghanta – Ek Saath Shramdaan” today at Navyug School, Peshwa Road, New Delhi.

The cleanliness drive was led by Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs & Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju. The event was attended by Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal; Chairman, NDMC, Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi; Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. Satya Prakash; Principal, Navyug School, Ms. Meenakshi Kaushik, along with officers and officials of the Ministry, teachers and students of Navyug School.

 

The Swachhata Pledge was also administered to all the participants, who reaffirmed their commitment to cleanliness and to making Swachhata an integral part of their daily lives.

As part of the programme, Union Minister Shri Kiren Rijiju, Secretary Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal, Chairman, NDMC, Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi, and Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. Satya Prakash planted saplings in the school campus under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam Abhiyan”. The plantation activity reflected the spirit of environmental responsibility and complemented the objectives of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign.

 

Addressing the gathering, Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi, Chairman, NDMC, expressed his gratitude for the presence of the Minister and the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs at Navyug School. He thanked the Ministry, on behalf of himself and the school, for choosing Navyug School as the venue for the Swachhata Hi Seva activity and appreciated the joint efforts of all stakeholders in making the programme a success.

Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal, thanked the Navyug Cooperative Society for the smooth coordination and conduct of the programme. He highlighted the vision of Mahatma Gandhi for a clean India and recalled that on 2nd October 2014, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the Swachh Bharat Mission on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, giving a renewed impetus to the nationwide movement for cleanliness. He also noted that the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign was launched in 2017 to further strengthen public participation in the cleanliness movement.

The Secretary emphasized that Swachhata is everyone's responsibility and not merely the responsibility of the Government. He encouraged the students to take the message of cleanliness from their school to their homes and ultimately to society at large. He also underscored that the collective resolve should not be limited to making India clean, but should contribute towards building a developed, inclusive and progressive India – Viksit Bharat.

Addressing the students and participants, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs & Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju, said that although he had heard about Navyug School earlier, he was pleased to get an opportunity to visit the school and participate in the Swachhata Hi Seva programme. He interacted with the teachers and students and appreciated their participation in the cleanliness drive.

The Minister recalled that cleanliness was earlier often perceived as work meant only for sanitation workers or as a task of a lower order. He said that the launch of the Swachh Bharat Mission by the Prime Minister in 2014, including the call for cleanliness from the Red Fort, transformed cleanliness into a people’s movement and a national mission.

Emphasizing that cleanliness cannot be confined to a symbolic one-day activity, Shri Rijiju said that while “Ek Din – Ek Ghanta – Ek Saath” is symbolic of collective participation, the spirit of Swachhata has to be followed throughout the day and every day. He urged the students to continue practising cleanliness in their daily lives and carry the message from the school to their homes and communities.

The Minister thanked the Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Chairman, NDMC, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, the Principal, teachers and staff of Navyug School, officers and officials of the Ministry and all the students for their active participation and contribution to the successful conduct of the programme.

The programme witnessed enthusiastic participation of officers and officials of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, teachers and students of Navyug School, reflecting the spirit of collective responsibility and public participation in the Swachhata movement.

The event concluded with a collective resolve to make cleanliness an integral part of everyday life and to continue contributing towards a cleaner, healthier and more developed India.

***

ISA

item.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment expands “Shram Samvad” outreach across industrial clusters
item.description: The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, conducted district-level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes under “Shram Samvad” across five industrial clusters — Bhiwadi and Bhilwara in Rajasthan, East Delhi, Dehradun in Uttarakhand and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra — on September 30, 2026. The programmes brought together senior government officials, State Labour Departments, industry associations, employers, HR and legal professionals and other stakeholders to…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, conducted district-level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes under “Shram Samvad” across five industrial clusters — Bhiwadi and Bhilwara in Rajasthan, East Delhi, Dehradun in Uttarakhand and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra — on September 30, 2026. The programmes brought together senior government officials, State Labour Departments, industry associations, employers, HR and legal professionals and other stakeholders to facilitate a better understanding of the four Labour Codes, employer compliance requirements and key employment and social-security initiatives of the Government.

The Shram Samvad campaign, launched nationwide on September 28, 2026, is a 90-day outreach initiative under which the Ministry is undertaking district-level engagement across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories, with a focus on industrial clusters. The initiative seeks to bridge the gap between the legislative framework and its implementation on the ground by providing employers and other stakeholders with greater clarity on the provisions, applicability and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes.

At Bhiwadi, Rajasthan, Shri Ashutosh A.T. Pednekar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, delivered the keynote address, outlining the key provisions of the Labour Codes and the Ministry’s vision for district-level capacity building. The programme, organised in collaboration with FICCI and the Bhiwadi Manufacturers Association (BMA), was attended by more than 100 participants. Sessions covered the broad framework of the Labour Codes, employer compliance requirements, Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM), along with interactive discussions on field-level implementation and stakeholder concerns.

In East Delhi, the programme at SCOPE Minar, Laxmi Nagar, was addressed by Dr. Mahendra Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, and Shri Pandurang Pole, Secretary-cum-Commissioner (Labour), Government of NCT of Delhi. More than 100 participants from industry and the labour ecosystem attended the programme. Technical sessions focused on the new Labour Codes, their objectives and major provisions, employer compliance requirements, PMVBRY and PM-SYM.

The programme at Dehradun was organised in partnership with PHDCCI, and attended by around 90 participants, including representatives of industry associations and business establishments, employers, industrialists and professionals. Shri Govind Ram, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, provided an overview of the four Labour Codes and the employer compliance chain. Shri Venkanna Banothu, Director of Mines Safety, DGMS, and senior representatives of the Uttarakhand Labour Department also participated.

At Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, the programme was organised in collaboration with the Labour Department, Government of Maharashtra, and witnessed participation of around 200 stakeholders, including representatives of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). Shri Chaman Lal Guleria, Director, Ministry of Labour & Employment, delivered the keynote address and provided an overview of the programme. Technical sessions covered the Labour Codes and employer compliance requirements, followed by dedicated sessions on PMVBRY and PM-SYM.

At Bhilwara, Rajasthan, the Ministry, in collaboration with the Labour Department, Government of Rajasthan, organised the Shram Samvad programme with around 100 participants representing employers, industry, HR, legal and finance professionals and other stakeholders. Dr. Arvind, Director General, V.V. Giri National Labour Institute (VVGNLI), addressed the inaugural session, which focused on the importance of awareness, preparedness and compliance for effective implementation of the new labour law framework. The first technical session, conducted by Shri Sanjay Rawat, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, provided an overview of the four Labour Codes, their objectives and major reforms.

Across the five programmes, technical discussions covered the Code on Wages, 2019; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Code on Social Security, 2020; and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Sessions focused on the objectives and major provisions of the Codes, applicability thresholds and employer obligations, including wages, appointment letters, working hours, overtime, social-security coverage, workplace safety, contract labour and industrial relations mechanisms.

A key component across the programmes was the interactive Question-and-Answer sessions, enabling participants to raise practical issues relating to applicability, statutory thresholds, records and returns, employee benefits and other compliance requirements.

Senior officials and representatives of EPFO, ESIC and the Central Labour Commissioner’s office participated in the programmes across the locations, enabling stakeholders to engage directly with different arms of the labour administration on implementation and compliance-related matters.

***

 

Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander

item.title: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Launches Physical Education Professionals’ Module, Highlights Critical Role in Scientific Talent Identification at Grassroots
item.description:
Union Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya today launched the Physical Education Professionals’ Module and highlighted the critical role of PE Teachers in identifying and nurturing sporting talent at the grassroots level.
The Union Sports Minister called for the creation of a comprehensive, nationwide repository of Physical Education (PE) teachers within a time-bound framework to strengthen scientific talent identification and systematic development at the…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya today launched the Physical Education Professionals’ Module and highlighted the critical role of PE Teachers in identifying and nurturing sporting talent at the grassroots level. 

The Union Sports Minister called for the creation of a comprehensive, nationwide repository of Physical Education (PE) teachers within a time-bound framework to strengthen scientific talent identification and systematic development at the grassroots level.



 

“Physical education teachers in schools and colleges are among the first to identify sporting talent among children and youth. It is important to map their qualifications, skills and expertise to enable their effective utilisation and further development,” Dr. Mandaviya said after launching the PE Teachers Registration and Onboarding Module on the National Sports Repository System (NSRS). 

He further stated, “A nationwide talent identification campaign must adopt a scientific approach, beginning at the grassroots. Many youngsters may possess the right physical attributes and potential to become good athletes with appropriate guidance. Physical education teachers, who spend considerable time with these children, are best placed to identify such talent.”



 

Outlining the growing importance of Sports Science, Dr. Mandaviya noted that Sports Science has a key role across the sporting pathway, from talent identification and nurturing to the training of elite athletes. 

“A scientific approach to talent identification must therefore begin at the grassroots levels,” he added. 

Emphasising the need to take the initiative forward in a mission mode, Dr. Mandaviya called for a Physical Education Teachers’ Association campaign at the district level, along with registration and creation of a structured repository at the district, state and national levels. 



 

He said. “Such a repository will help map the capabilities and specialisations of PE teachers and create opportunities for those with special talents to gain exposure at the national and international levels.”

The Union Sports Minister directed that the entire repository should be created within six months and said that its progress would be reviewed in a time bound manner. He said, “The initiative should be taken forward not merely as the launch of a module, but as a mission to develop sports in the country.”

The Physical Education Professionals’ Module has been introduced under the National Sports Repository System (NSRS), a centralised digital platform for maintaining a unified repository of stakeholders associated with the Indian sports ecosystem.



 

The launch event was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Sports Authority of India (SAI), the Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE), the Lakshmibai National College of Physical Education (LNCPE), the Physical Education Foundation of India (PEFI), and other key stakeholders. 

जमीनी स्तर पर खेल प्रतिभाओं को निखारने के लिए आज NSRS पोर्टल पर 'Physical Education Professionals Module' का शुभारंभ किया। आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi जी के विजन के अनुरूप, यह पहल हमारे Physical Education शिक्षकों को सशक्त कर नए चैंपियन तराशने में मदद करेगी। मेरा सभी Physical Education Professionals से आग्रह है कि वे इस पोर्टल पर अपना रजिस्ट्रेशन जरूर करें: https://t.co/ghWowXU4zN

The Ministry of Ayush today organised a joint cleanliness activity under the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative as part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Sewa 2026 campaign. The cleanliness drive was held at the front lawn of Ayush Bhawan and was led by the Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, with Senior officials and staff of the Ministry participating in the activity.

The Ministry of Ayush is actively participating in the Swachhata Hi Sewa 2026 campaign being observed across Ministries and Departments of the Government of India from September 17 to October 2, 2026. In line with the campaign calendar, the Ministry has undertaken a range of activities focusing on cleanliness, workplace organisation, disposal of obsolete records and responsible waste management.

As part of the campaign, the Ministry has undertaken a comprehensive review of old physical files and records, with records that are no longer required being weeded out as per prescribed procedures. Electronic waste, including old computers, UPS systems, monitors and used printer cartridges, has also been segregated, with action for auction initiated in accordance with the applicable rules.

The Ministry has also organised a sports event for housekeeping staff.

The cleanliness initiatives undertaken by the Ministry during Swachhata Hi Sewa 2026 underscore the importance of collective participation in maintaining a clean, organised and hygienic workplace, while promoting systematic management of records and waste.

item.title: India’s Dr. Bimal N. Patel Takes Oath as Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) at the Tribunal’s headquarters in Hamburg, Germany
item.description:
Dr. Bimal N. Patel, an eminent international law jurist, scholar, practitioner and institution-builder of global standing, took oath today as a Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) at the Tribunal’s headquarters in Hamburg, Germany.
Dr. Patel assumes this eminent international judicial office for a nine-year term commencing on 1 October 2026, marking a significant milestone in a distinguished career devoted to international law, law of the sea, ocean…
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Bimal N. Patel, an eminent international law jurist, scholar, practitioner and institution-builder of global standing, took oath today as a Judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) at the Tribunal’s headquarters in Hamburg, Germany.

Dr. Patel assumes this eminent international judicial office for a nine-year term commencing on 1 October 2026, marking a significant milestone in a distinguished career devoted to international law, law of the sea, ocean governance, maritime security, legal scholarship and public institution-building.

Dr. Patel was elected on 18 June 2026 at the Thirty-sixth Meeting of States Parties to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) held at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Seven members were elected to the Tribunal at the meeting.

Members of ITLOS are elected by the States Parties to UNCLOS from among persons enjoying the highest reputation for fairness and integrity and possessing recognised competence in the field of the law of the sea. The Tribunal comprises 21 independent members, elected with due regard to equitable geographical distribution and representation of the principal legal systems of the world.

A Distinguished Career in International Law and the Law of the Sea

Dr. Patel has made extensive contributions to the development, interpretation and study of international law, with particular emphasis on the law of the sea, maritime governance, international adjudication and State responsibility. He has served as a Member of the United Nations International Law Commission (ILC) and as Chair of its Working Group on Succession of States in respect of State Responsibility, contributing to the Commission’s work on the progressive development and codification of international law.

Dr. Patel holds several prominent national and international responsibilities, including Member of India’s National Security Advisory Board; Member of the Committee on Antarctic Governance; Co-Chair of the Law of the Sea Interest Group of the American Society of International Law; Member of the High-Level Advisory Board of the International Committee of the Red Cross; and Lead Academic Adviser during India’s tenure on the United Nations Security Council in 2021–22.

Dr. Patel has also contributed to the development, interpretation and implementation of important legal and regulatory frameworks relating to India’s maritime domain, including areas concerning maritime anti-piracy, Antarctic governance, merchant shipping, private maritime security, deep seabed activities and admiralty jurisdiction.

Scholar and Institution-Builder

Alongside his work as an international legal expert, Dr. Patel has made a significant contribution to legal education and institution-building in India. He has successfully led and contributed to the development of premier national institutions, including Gujarat National Law University and Gujarat Maritime University, and currently serves as the Vice-Chancellor of Rashtriya Raksha University. His academic leadership has fostered international collaborations and capacity-building in international law, law of the sea, maritime law, national security and related areas.

A prolific scholar and publicist, Dr. Patel has authored or edited more than 25 books, besides numerous research papers and scholarly publications covering classical, contemporary and emerging areas of international law. His scholarship and Dressional engagement have consistently placed the International Law based governance of oceans, peaceful settlement of disputes and maritime cooperation at the centre of contemporary discourse.

Maritime Governance in a Changing Global Order

Dr. Patel assumes office at a time when the international law of the sea has acquired increasing significance in addressing questions relating to maritime boundaries, freedom of navigation, marine environmental protection, sustainable use of ocean resources, deep seabed activities and peaceful settlement of maritime disputes.

This broader maritime context also resonates with India’s evolving engagement with the Indian Ocean, the Global South and international maritime cooperation. In March 2025, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi articulated Vision MAHASAGAR, “Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions”, as an evolution of the SAGAR vision, with emphasis on development, capacity-building and mutual security across regions.

Against this wider backdrop, Dr. Patel’s elevation to ITLOS reflects the growing relevance of specialised expertise in the law of the sea and the vital role of international judicial institutions in advancing international law-based oceanic order.

About the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) is an independent international judicial body established under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

Headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, the Tribunal adjudicates disputes concerning the interpretation and application of UNCLOS and matters specifically provided for in other agreements that confer jurisdiction upon it. The Tribunal is composed of 21 independent members and has jurisdiction over a wide range of matters relating to the law of the sea. These include disputes concerning maritime delimitation, navigation, marine resources, protection and preservation of the marine environment, and other questions arising under the Convention.

Dr. Bimal N. Patel’s assumption of office as a Judge of ITLOS represents a distinguished milestone in his longstanding engagement with international law and the law of the sea, and also reflects India’s enduring commitment to a safe, secure, progressive and international law-based oceanic order.

item.description:
MY Bharat NSS Cell, Manipur University, Canchipur, Imphal, successfully organised the “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – Healthy Walk and Run” on 1 October 2026 at 7:00 a.m. at the Traffic Island, Manipur University, under the aegis of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.
The programme was organised as part of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign, which seeks to engage young people in promoting a healthy, active and drug-free lifestyle. The…
item.content:encoded:
MY Bharat NSS Cell, Manipur University, Canchipur, Imphal, successfully organised the “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – Healthy Walk and Run” on 1 October 2026 at 7:00 a.m. at the Traffic Island, Manipur University, under the aegis of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.

The programme was organised as part of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign, which seeks to engage young people in promoting a healthy, active and drug-free lifestyle. The Healthy Walk and Run was designed to create awareness among students and youth about the importance of physical fitness, healthy living, positive social engagement and collective responsibility in building a drug-free campus and a healthier society.

The programme was graced by several distinguished members of Manipur University as Presidium Members, including Prof. Ch. Ibohal Singh, Dean of Students’ Welfare, Manipur University; Prof. O. Ranjit Singh, Director, Indian Knowledge System, Manipur University; Prof. S. Opendra Singh, Head, Department of Statistics, Manipur University; Prof. Laishram Santosh Singh, Programme Coordinator, NSS Cell, Manipur University; Dr. T. Deepamanjuri Devi, Programme Officer, NSS Unit–II; Dr. Dalip Singh, Programme Officer, NSS Unit–IV; Dr. R.K. Suresh Singh, Programme Officer, NSS Unit–III; and Mr. Herojit Singh, MIT, Manipur University. A large number of NSS volunteers, invitees and representatives of the electronic and print media also participated in the programme.

At the outset, Prof. Laishram Santosh Singh, Programme Coordinator, NSS Cell, Manipur University, extended a warm and heartfelt welcome to all the distinguished presidium members, NSS Programme Officers, volunteers, invitees and members of the electronic and print media. In his welcome address, he highlighted the objectives and significance of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign and explained that the Healthy Walk and Run was not merely a physical fitness activity but also a collective movement to inspire young people to adopt healthy lifestyles and stay away from drugs and other harmful substances.

Prof. Santosh Singh further emphasised that physical activity, sports, discipline, positive peer interaction and meaningful engagement of youth can play an important role in preventing substance abuse. He stated that a physically active and socially responsible youth population is an essential foundation for a healthy and developed India. He also encouraged NSS volunteers to become ambassadors of healthy living and drug-free communities and to spread the message of the Nasha Mukt campaign among their peers, families and communities.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Ch. Ibohal Singh, Dean of Students’ Welfare, Manipur University, highlighted the importance of collective responsibility in combating drug abuse. He stressed that creating a drug-free campus is not the responsibility of any single individual or institution, but requires the active participation of students, teachers, staff, parents and the wider community. He encouraged students to make healthy choices, remain physically active and contribute positively to society.

Following his address, Prof. Ch. Ibohal Singh administered the Nasha Mukt pledge in English, calling upon the participants to remain committed to a healthy and drug-free lifestyle.

The pledge was subsequently administered in Hindi by Dr. Dalip Singh, Programme Officer, NSS Unit–IV, enabling the participants to collectively reaffirm their commitment to the objectives of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign.

After the pledge-taking ceremony, all participants assembled at the starting point for the Healthy Walk and Run. Prof. Ch. Ibohal Singh, Dean of Students’ Welfare, Manipur University, flagged off the Healthy Walk and Run, marking the commencement of the awareness and fitness activity. The distinguished presidium members led the event, followed by NSS Programme Officers, NSS volunteers, invitees and other participants.

The participants covered approximately 5 kilometres within the Manipur University campus, carrying the message of “Healthy Youth, Drug-Free Youth and Viksit Bharat.” The activity provided an opportunity for students and NSS volunteers to demonstrate their commitment to physical fitness, healthy living, discipline and social responsibility. The energetic participation of the volunteers also helped create a positive atmosphere of unity and collective action against substance abuse.

Approximately 100 participants, including dignitaries, NSS Programme Officers, NSS volunteers and invitees, took part in the Healthy Walk and Run. The programme successfully combined physical fitness with social awareness, reinforcing the message that regular physical activity and constructive youth engagement can contribute to a healthier and drug-free society.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Dr. T. Deepamanjuri Devi, Programme Officer, NSS Unit–II, Manipur University, who expressed gratitude to the distinguished dignitaries, NSS Programme Officers, volunteers, invitees, media representatives and all participants for their valuable presence and active support in making the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – Healthy Walk and Run a successful and meaningful programme.

*****

item.title: Department of Agricultural Research and Education - Indian Council of Agricultural Research’s Swachhata Hi Seva 2026: From Participation to a Viksit Bharat
item.description: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), along with its 114 Institutes, Regional Centres, Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), is participating in the fortnight-long Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign from 17 September to 2 October 2026 under the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”. The campaign is being implemented across the ICAR system in both letter and spirit, in accordance with the…
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), along with its 114 Institutes, Regional Centres, Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), is participating in the fortnight-long Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign from 17 September to 2 October 2026 under the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”. The campaign is being implemented across the ICAR system in both letter and spirit, in accordance with the prescribed five-pillar framework and the date-wise action plan. It commenced on 17th September 2026 with the Swachhata Pledge administered by the Secretary, DARE & DG, ICAR, in the presence of senior officers, including the AS&FA, and was also introduced through video conferencing to ICAR Institutes and establishments across the country.

For wider dissemination and outreach, Press releases have been issued by ICAR Headquarters on the activities undertaken under the campaign, while ICAR Institutes and establishments have also been independently undertaking publicity and outreach through local print media, display of banners and other appropriate communication channels. At both Headquarters and institutional levels, the campaign and its activities are also being disseminated through social media platforms, including Facebook, X and Instagram, thereby extending the message of Swachhata beyond the ICAR network to wider and more diverse audiences, particularly digitally engaged audiences and the younger generation, including Gen Z.

Major Activities under the Five Pillars

1.Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) and Clean Public Places

Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have undertaken identification and transformation of black and dark spots across urban and rural areas, including locations such as bus stands along highways, institutional premises, research fields and other public spaces. Cleanliness drives have been complemented by beautification and improvement of these spaces, with participation of staff, students and local communities, wherever applicable, to create visibly cleaner and more welcoming public areas.

2. Swachh Paathshala: Yuva for Swachhata

Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes, ATARIs and KVKs have actively engaged students and youth in Swachhata activities, harnessing their zeal and enthusiasm through cleanliness drives, awareness activities, demonstrations, competitions and other participatory initiatives. The emphasis has been on inculcating the values of Swachhata among young participants so that these values are imbibed as part of their everyday conduct and sustained beyond the campaign.

3. Safai Mitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir

Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have undertaken activities focused on the safety, health, dignity and social welfare of Safai Mitras. Efforts have included promoting awareness and access to social welfare schemes, including VB-GRAMG and PMAY, along with cleanliness of public toilets and other sanitation facilities. The activities also seek to reinforce Mahatma Gandhi’s message that no work is menial or insignificant, while recognising the dignity and contribution of those engaged in sanitation and cleanliness.

4. Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata

Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have promoted active participation in Swachhata activities, with a focus on environmental responsibility and the role of citizens as major stakeholders in maintaining clean public spaces. This has included cleanliness drives at Visarjan sites, riverbanks, ghats and other public areas, along with Clean Green Festivities, eco-friendly and zero-waste celebrations, composting of flower waste and offerings, and other community-oriented initiatives.

The campaign has also included a focus on Swachh Tourist Spots, with emphasis on promoting Swachhata at ASI monuments, tourist destinations and other public spaces, including through cleanliness drives and illumination of monuments with the Swachhata message. These efforts seek to draw greater public attention to the cleanliness and upkeep of heritage and tourist spaces, while encouraging responsible tourism and greater citizen participation in maintaining such places.

5. Swachhata Se Samriddhi

Under this pillar, ICAR Institutes and establishments have promoted the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle through activities such as Waste to Art, Kabaad Se Jugaad, reuse and recycling drives, plastic-free initiatives and creative utilisation of waste materials. Emphasis has also been placed on converting waste into useful and aesthetically meaningful products, promoting awareness on responsible waste management and reinforcing the message that waste can be transformed into a resource.

Documentation and Reporting

The activities undertaken across the ICAR network are being documented through daily photographs being uploaded on the SHS portal. Compiled daily reports along with photographs are being forwarded to DKMA for uploading on the ICAR website, facilitating regular documentation and dissemination of the campaign activities.

Culmination and Way Forward

The campaign will culminate on 1 October 2026 with participation in the nationwide “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” initiative through collective shramdaan and cleanliness activities, followed by the observance of Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October. The culmination will focus on showcasing transformed cleanliness target units and public spaces, undertaking appropriate cleanliness and shramdaan activities, promoting plantation and green spaces under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”, and recognising contributors, as appropriate. Through these activities, the ICAR system has sought to integrate cleanliness with public participation, youth engagement, environmental responsibility, dignity of sanitation workers and responsible waste management, while extending the message of Swachhata beyond institutional premises into communities and public spaces and reinforcing it as a sustained collective responsibility.

item.content:encoded:
Mumbai, 1 October 2026

 

The Mumbai Licensing Service Area (Mumbai LSA) of the Department of Telecommunications conducted a special cleanliness drive at Juhu Beach today. The campaign was led by Additional Director General of Telecommunications (Additional DGT), Shri Mohammad Zafar Iqbal. The programme was organised with the objective of spreading public awareness about cleanliness, and all officers and employees of Mumbai LSA participated enthusiastically.

Before the commencement of the cleanliness drive, a rally was taken out from the office to Juhu Beach under the leadership of Additional DGT Shri Mohammad Zafar Iqbal. Addressing the gathering, he emphasised the increased use of Hindi as the Official Language and called upon everyone to make cleanliness an integral part of their daily lives. The officers carried banners and placards and conveyed the message of cleanliness to the general public. Upon reaching Juhu Beach, all officers and employees participated in Shramdaan (voluntary community service), cleaned the waste lying along the beach, and took a pledge to maintain cleanliness. On the occasion, Additional DGT Shri Mohammad Zafar Iqbal distributed safety and utility kits to the sanitation workers in recognition of their valuable contribution.

Along with the cleanliness drive, Mumbai LSA also organised Hindi Pakhwada from September 15, 2026 to October 1, 2026. Various competitions, including Hindi essay writing, debate, noting and drafting, were organised during the fortnight, in which officers and employees participated enthusiastically. On the concluding day of Hindi Pakhwada, Additional DGT Shri Mohammad Zafar Iqbal presented prizes and certificates of appreciation to the successful participants.

 

(Source : Mumbai Licensing Service Area (Mumbai LSA), Department of Telecommunications)

item.title: Raksha Mantri Launches Key Digital and Financial Management Initiatives at Defence Accounts Department’s 279th Annual Day Celebration in New Delhi
item.description:
