He congratulated DAD on its nearly three centuries of service to the nation and commended its contribution to defence financial audit and management , calling it the backbone of the country's defence preparedness.
During his address, Shri Rajnath Singh called for…
item.content:encoded:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh launched various publications and digital initiatives of the Defence Accounts Department (DAD) during the celebration of its 279th Annual Day at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi on October 01, 2026. He congratulated DAD on its nearly three centuries of service to the nation and commended its contribution to defence financial audit and management , calling it the backbone of the country's defence preparedness.

During his address, Shri Rajnath Singh called for greater integration of financial systems of the Army, Navy and Air Force and stressed upon maximum digitisation, automation and transparency, with real-time updating of Management Information System data. RM urged the DAD to transition from “Annual Review of Balances” to “Any Time Review of Balances”.

Shri Rajnath Singh commended SAKSHAM, DAD’s project for digitising and integrating the Defence accounting and payment ecosystem hosted on a secure dedicated data centre and operating on the DAD WAN network. It uses the latest tech-stack with secure role-based access, enhanced validations and scalability, supporting the Department's move towards “One Nation, One Function, One Application”. RM appreciated it’s integration with the Indian Army Financial Information System for budget, approval and bill data.

Highlighting the near 100% expenditure during FY 2025–26, RM lauded the joint efforts of DAD and all three Services to achieve this milestone. Referring to the success of SPARSH data cleaning, RM suggested automating grievance redressal through a Conversational AI ecosystem covering chat, SMS, WhatsApp, email and phone calls. He also emphasised quality audit, digital data cleaning, and prompt resolution of grievances and court cases.“Our approach must be firm, fair, sensitive and responsible, especially when dealing with the legitimate dues and service rights of those who have devoted their lives to defending the nation,” said RM.

He stressed early implementation of SAMPURNA, a fully automated, end-to-end revenue procurement system envisaged to leverage data analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for a valuable decision-support system.

On the occasion, the Raksha Mantri unveiled three major initiatives aimed at strengthening the integration of Financial Information Systems of the Defence Forces, improving accounting and tracking of defence expenditure and operationalising the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system in the Ministry of Defence.

Integration of SAKSHAM with Indian Army Financial Information System

The SAKSHAM bill audit and payment system of the Defence Accounts Department has been successfully integrated with the Indian Army Financial Information System (IAFIS), facilitating digital transmission of budget, sanction and bill information between the two organisations. The integration is a major step towards complete digitisation of the Defence payments ecosystem, enabling real-time sharing of information on bill status and budget balances and completely paperless processing of bills.

Treasury Single Account System in Ministry of Defence

The Treasury Single Account (TSA) system in the Ministry of Defence was inaugurated by the Raksha Mantri for Just-In-Time release of funds to autonomous bodies under the Government of India. Operationalised through the Payment Routing and Integrated System Management (PRISM) platform, the system is fully integrated with RBI eKUBER. It will facilitate better grant management for autonomous bodies under the Ministry of Defence and provide greater visibility of accounting and expenditure.

Revamped National Compilation System

The Raksha Mantri launched the revamped National Compilation System (NCS) for Defence. The NCS is the single source for accounting and compilation of all Defence expenditure in India. The Ministry of Defence operates under a unique financial delegation framework, requiring budget allocation and expenditure tracking across various Controllers of the Defence Accounts Department across the country. The revamped NCS has been comprehensively redesigned on a new technical architecture to provide accurate budget reporting and expenditure monitoring. The system will facilitate granular reporting to the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Defence, Service Headquarters and Field Controllers, thereby aiding policy planning and better budget management.

Raksha Mantri Awards for Excellence 2026

Raksha Mantri Awards for Excellence 2026 were presented during the event to recognise outstanding achievements by teams and individuals in implementing key reforms and projects. The awards recognise innovation, professionalism and efficiency in Defence financial management and contributions towards strengthening institutional capacity and enhancing transparency in the Department’s service to the Defence Forces.

The awards acknowledged the significant role played by DAD officials across the country in successful digitization of Annual Review of Balances (ARoB) and implementation of various initiatives, including SAKSHAM & SAMAR-SETU.

SAMAR-SETU is a centralised application for management of pay and allowances of Agniveers of the Indian Army. Operating from the Central Agniveer Pay and Accounts Office (CAPAO), the system manages the pay accounts of more than 2.3 lakh Agniveers through fully system-driven automated processes.

Raksha Mantri released three publications during DAD Day 2026 including the Comprehensive Statistical Handbook on Defence Expenditure (COSHE) 2026, Raksha Lekha Bharati and the Market Intelligence Report 2025-2026. A film showcasing the success of the System for Pension Administration (Raksha), SPARSH, was also screened.

Addressing the gathering, Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) Smt Alka Nangia Arora highlighted the important initiatives undertaken by the Defence Accounts Department in current year, including major strides in the centralisation and digitisation of its core functions of internal audit, payment and accounting, financial advice and management of Defence pensions.

Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay, and Vice Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit were also in attendance, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Defence.

Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (ESW), Smt Sukriti Likhi, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay, and Vice Chief of Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit were also in attendance, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Defence.

***

VK/SR/Ruchi

item.title: Students play a pivotal role in building a clean, green and healthy Viksit Bharat 2047: Shri Pralhad Joshi
item.description: Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi today led the Shramdaan and Cleanliness Drive at Gargi College, University of Delhi, under the nationwide ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative. He also planted a sapling in the college premises under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. Interacting with students on the occasion, the Minister emphasised that cleanliness was closely linked with public health and well-being and stressed on the importance of collective participation in making…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi today led the Shramdaan and Cleanliness Drive at Gargi College, University of Delhi, under the nationwide ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative. He also planted a sapling in the college premises under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. Interacting with students on the occasion, the Minister emphasised that cleanliness was closely linked with public health and well-being and stressed on the importance of collective participation in making Swachhata a sustained habit.

The Minister emphasised on the role of students in promoting cleanliness, environmental consciousness and responsible citizenship. He encouraged them to maintain Swachhata not only in educational institutions but also in their homes and public spaces. He urged them to contribute at least 30 minutes to cleanliness-oriented activities, reiterating that individual efforts could inspire collective action and transform Swachhata into a people’s movement.

Shri Pralhad Joshi highlighted the importance of physical fitness and outdoor activities among young people. He encouraged students to participate in sports and spend time on playgrounds while maintaining a healthy balance with screen-based activities.

The Minister urged the students to contribute to the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in building a Viksit Bharat by 2047 as they were the key pillars in in translating this Vision into action and building a clean, green and healthy India, through responsible citizenship and active participation.

Vice Chancellor, University of Delhi, Prof. Yogesh Singh, faculty members of the College and senior officials of the Ministry were present on the occasion.

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes at the portrait of former Speaker, Lok Sabha, Shri G.M.C. Balayogi in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, on his Birth Anniversary, today.

Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh, Members of Parliament, former Members and other dignitaries also paid tributes at the portrait of Shri Balayogi on this occasion.

Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh; and Secretary-General, Rajya  Sabha, Shri P C Mody also paid tributes to Shri Balayogi in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan.

Shri Balayogi was the Speaker of the Twelfth Lok Sabha and he was re-elected the Speaker of the Thirteenth Lok Sabha as well.

The portrait of Shri Balayogi was painted by Shri Him Chatterjee. It is placed in the Outer Lobby, Samvidhaan Sadan  and was unveiled by the then  President of India Shri Pranab  Mukherjee on 10th February , 2014.

item.content:encoded:
Mumbai, 1 October 2026

 

Cinema takes center stage in Panaji, Goa, as the 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) returns from 20 to 28 November 2026. Bringing together filmmakers, cinema professionals, journalists and film enthusiasts from India and across the world, IFFI will celebrate the magic of storytelling, the diversity of cinematic expression and the creative spirit that connects audiences across cultures.

The festival will showcase diverse stories and perspectives through film screenings, discussions, filmmaker interactions and networking opportunities, creating a dynamic platform for ideas, conversations and collaborations. As Goa gets ready to host this grand celebration of cinema, IFFI will offer a unique space for creative exchange and meaningful engagement among the global film community.

Media professionals play a vital role in amplifying the reach and visibility of IFFI each year. Through news reports, interviews, reviews, features and digital coverage, the media helps bring the festival’s films, events and conversations to audiences across India and around the world. It helps celebrate diverse artists and their art. IFFI values the continued participation of the media in the festival which is instrumental in creating wider awareness and building public engagement with IFFI and with creative expression.

Media Accreditation Opens on 1st October

Media professionals planning to cover the 57th International Film Festival of India 2026 (IFFI) may register as Media Delegate through the official Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation portal: https://accreditation.pib.gov.in/eventregistration/login.aspx

The media accreditation window has opened today, on 1 October 2026, and the last date for registration is 15 October 2026.

Accredited media professionals will have access to various festival activities, including:

  • Film screenings
  • Panel discussions
  • Interactions with filmmakers and cinema professionals
  • Networking opportunities
  • Other activities related to festival coverage

Media delegates are advised to carefully read the accreditation guidelines before submitting their applications. Applicants must provide valid identity proof, professional credentials, active contact numbers and email addresses, along with any other supporting documents as required on the accreditation portal.

Detailed eligibility criteria and media accreditation policy can be read here.

Required Documents:

  • Photograph
  • Government Identity Proof
  • PIB or State Government Accreditation Card/ Organization’s ID + Editor’s Letter
  • Proof of work in the relevant field

Key Information

  • Festival: 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI)
  • Venue: Panaji, Goa
  • Media Accreditation Opens: 1st October 2026
  • Media Accreditation Closes: 15th October 2026
  • Accreditation Portal: https://accreditation.pib.gov.in/eventregistration/login.aspx
  • Support Email: iffi.mediadesk@pib.gov.in

Media professionals who are already registered on the portal for previous edition (56th) of IFFI, can use the same credentials to log in and update their documents as required.

Apply early to secure your place at one of Asia’s most celebrated film festivals, connect with voices shaping the world of cinema, discover stories beyond the screen and be part of IFFI’s vibrant celebration of filmmaking, creativity and culture. The first 50 successful registrations will also be eligible for a complementary workshop on Film Appreciation on 19th November 2026 in Panaji!

Furthermore, film enthusiasts who are not media persons may also register for IFFI as Delegates vide https://www.iffigoa.org/delegate-registration and enjoy the rich tapestry of films and other activities on offer at 57th IFFI 2026.

About IFFI

Born in 1952, the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is South Asia’s oldest and largest celebration of cinema. Jointly hosted by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India and the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG), State Government of Goa, IFFI brings together filmmakers, legends and emerging voices from across the world. With international competitions, cultural showcases, masterclasses and tributes, the festival celebrates diverse stories, languages and cinematic traditions against the vibrant backdrop of Goa. For more information and latest details about the 57th IFFI 2026 please visit https://www.iffigoa.org/.

 

* * *

PIB IFFI CAST AND CREW | Nikita Joshi/ Robin Singh/ Darshana Rane | IFFI 57 - 4

item.content:encoded:
ICAR-National Research Centre for Orchids (NRCO), Pakyong, Sikkim, has successfully concluded a series of activities under the "Swachhata Hi Sewa" (SHS) campaign from 17th September to 1st October 2026. The campaign was organized with the support of staff of ICAR-NRCO, 14 PIB media delegates from Bengaluru, Nagar Panchayat, Taxi Driver Association, Organic Market Groups, Rhenock and Rongli, and Pachey Panchayat, Pakyong District.

The programme commenced with a Swachhata Pledge Ceremony on 17th September 2026, in the presence of PIB Media Delegation on tour to Sikkim from Bengaluru.

As part of the campaign, the SHS team carried out daily cleanliness and awareness activities, including cleaning of office premises, residential quarters, farm areas, public places and guest houses; quiz competitions on 'Swachhata Hi Sewa' and 'Value Addition'; disposal of waste after Vishwakarma Puja; organic waste management; promotion of digital banners; waste segregation at residential quarters and office premises; home composting; waste-to-art initiatives; clean and green drives with plantation of fruit and ornamental plants for soil and water conservation; 'Kabaad Se Kala' with orchids; and display of banners at key locations.

A special drive, 'Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath – Collective Action for Voluntary Shramdaan', was also organized in collaboration with Nagar Panchayat, Taxi Driver Association, Organic Market Groups and Pachey Panchayat.

The three core pillars of the campaign were sanitation, environmental cleanliness and safe water for household use.

The programme was organized under the leadership of Dr. S.P. Das, Director, ICAR-NRCO, and Dr. L.C. De, SBA Nodal Officer, with active participation from scientists, administrative, finance and technical staff, supporting staff, Young Professionals, SRFs and other contractual staff of ICAR-NRCO, and with support from PIB officials, Nagar Panchayat, Taxi Driver Association, Organic Market Groups and Rhenock and Rongli, and Pachey Panchayat, Pakyong District, Sikkim.

The 5 th edition of KEC will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international…
item.content:encoded:
The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) is scheduled to be held from 3rd to 5th October 2026 at New Delhi, under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux”. The three-day gathering will bring together senior policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders.

The 5th edition of KEC will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries. They will contribute to the Conclave’s plenary sessions, interactive discussions and focused roundtables.

The Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) was founded by Professor V.K.R.V. Rao in 1952. Currently, Shri N. K. Singh is the President, Board of Trustees, IEG. Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra is Chairman of the Board of Governors, and Professor Sabyasachi Kar is Director of the Institute.

The Kautilya Economic Conclave is an initiative of the Institute of Economic Growth (IEG), organised in partnership with the Ministry of Finance, Government of India. First convened in 2022, the Conclave provides a forum for dialogue on contemporary economic and policy challenges.

Since its inception in 2022, the Kautilya Economic Conclave has grown into a forum for dialogue on economic and policy challenges. Earlier editions were held under the themes “Redefining the Future” (2022), “Navigating a World on Fire” (2023), “The Indian Era” (2024) and “Seeking Prosperity in Turbulent Times” (2025).

Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address on October 3, 2026. The inaugural session will examine how economic policy can build resilience without sacrificing growth, openness or institutional credibility in an environment marked by recurrent global shocks and uncertainty.

A special plenary on “Resilience in an Age of Flux: India’s Economic Priorities” will focus on how India can sustain growth, preserve macroeconomic stability and expand investment amid global fragmentation, technological disruption and recurrent shocks. Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will deliver the special address, with Amelie de Montchalin, President of the Cour des Comptes and former Minister of Public Action and Accounts of France, as discussant.

The concluding session, “India and the World: Adaptive by Design”, will be moderated by Shri N. K. Singh, President, Board of Trustees, Institute of Economic Growth. Dr. S. Jaishankar, Union Minister for External Affairs, will deliver the special concluding address, with former Singapore Foreign Minister Mr. George Yeo as discussant. The session will examine how India can remain adaptive by design, preserve strategic autonomy, widen partnerships and respond flexibly to a more contested and uncertain global order.

Technology and the digital economy will constitute another major strand of KEC 2026. Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, will deliver the keynote address at the plenary on “Connected India, Empowered Finance: Building Trusted Digital Infrastructure for the AI Economy”. The session will examine how digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and new communications networks can raise productivity while preserving competition and trust.

Union Cabinet Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will deliver the keynote address on Culture as Capital: From Heritage to Horizons on the penultimate day.

The opening plenary, “A World Priced for Risk”, will examine how energy shocks, supply-chain disruptions and the weaponisation of trade and economic access are creating renewed challenges for macroeconomic management, investment and resilience. The session will be chaired by Lord Nicholas Stern, with Shri P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivering the keynote address and Professor Michael Greenstone of the University of Chicago as discussant.

The Conclave will also feature Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, as keynote speaker in the plenary session “Kautilya and a Resurgent India: Lessons for Emerging Markets”. The session will explore the lessons that India’s economic experience can offer emerging markets and will feature José De Gregorio, former President of the Central Bank of Chile, and Muhamad Chatib Basri, former Finance Minister of Indonesia.

The role of central banks in navigating a more volatile global environment will be a key focus of the Conclave. In the plenary session “Central Banking in an Age of Flux”, Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, will deliver the special address. Chaired by Jean-Claude Trichet, former President of the European Central Bank and former Governor of the Banque de France, the session will consider how central banks can manage inflation, financial fragility, capital flows and credibility amid recurrent global shocks. Governor Malhotra’s participation will provide an important perspective on the challenges confronting monetary policy and financial stability in a rapidly changing global economy.

The agenda will address a wide range of domestic and global economic issues, including fiscal federalism, industrial policy, capital-market development, regulatory oversight, development finance and the mobilisation of domestic and foreign capital for long-term investment. Sessions will examine the institutional and fiscal principles governing Centre-State relations, the role of industrial policy in structural transformation, and the conditions required to deepen India’s capital markets and channel savings into productive risk capital.

International perspectives will form an important part of the Conclave. Sessions will examine Europe’s growth and competitiveness challenges and its economic relationship with Asia; global imbalances, debt and financial stability; structural transformation in China; and Japan’s role in economic security, technology and connectivity in the Indo-Pacific.

A dedicated plenary, “Balancing Contradictions in the Age of Flux”, will consider how India can manage competing strategic and economic relationships while preserving strategic autonomy, economic interests and room for manoeuvre. The discussion will bring together international experts on Asia, China, Taiwan and India’s global economic relationships.

Parallel sessions will further explore “The New Tech Order: Power, Platforms, AI and Regulatory Competition” and “Humans and Machines: Work, Skills and Education in the AI Age”. These discussions will focus on how artificial intelligence and strategic technologies are reshaping economic power, labour markets, skills, education and regulatory frameworks.

Other sessions will address climate resilience, reform of multilateral development banks, healthcare and global health security, urbanisation, agriculture, demographic change and the future of work. Discussions on “Feeding the Future” will examine the resilience of agriculture and food systems amid climate uncertainty and trade disruptions, while “Demography at a Turning Point” will consider the implications of ageing, fertility, migration and demographic change for labour markets and productivity.

The Conclave will also examine the transformation of global trade and investment networks. A plenary on “From Globalisation to Fragmentation: Rewiring Trade Networks” will consider how strategic rivalry, industrial policy and economic security are reshaping trade, investment and supply chains. Another session, “The New Growth Corridor: Reimagining Asia-Africa Economic Partnerships”, will focus on opportunities for deeper trade, investment, infrastructure and development partnerships between Asia and Africa.

The three-day Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and invitation-only closed-door roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment, providing opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners. The Conclave is a “by invitation only” event.

SR/KT/KMN

Speaking on the occasion, Additional Director General Smt. Shruti Patil, IIS, highlighted the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi that the Swachh Bharat Mission is a people-led movement. She emphasised that cleanliness is not a one-day activity but a continuous responsibility, and called upon officials and staff to make cleanliness a regular part of everyday life.

Smt. Patil also appreciated the efforts of the sanitation workers of CGO Towers for keeping the premises clean and hygienic. As a token of appreciation, gloves and sanitation kits were handed over to the sanitation workers in recognition of their dedicated service.

 

On the occasion, as part of the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Additional Director General Smt. The programme commenced with a welcome address by the Indian Chamber of Commerce, followed by a special address by Shri Beiseia Darlong, TCS,…
item.content:encoded:
Agartala, September 29, 2026 – The Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC), in collaboration with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), organised an interactive “Retire Smart India 2.0” NPS Awareness Session at Pragna Bhawan, Agartala, with a focus on retirement planning and enhancing awareness about pension participation.

The programme commenced with a welcome address by the Indian Chamber of Commerce, followed by a special address by Shri Beiseia Darlong, TCS, Deputy Secretary & State Nodal Officer, Finance Department, Government of Tripura, and a special address by Shri Pradeep Krishnaraj, IAS, Director, Skill Development Department, Government of Tripura. The keynote address was delivered by Shri Ruby Vinayak Bhaosagar, Assistant General Manager, PFRDA.

In the key note address, Sh. Ruby Vinayak Bhaosagar discussed on the evolving pension landscape in India and the growing significance of the National Pension System (NPS) as a flexible, digital and market-linked retirement solution were highlighted. NPS has emerged as a significant component of India’s pension ecosystem, with more than 9.93 crore subscribers and Assets Under Management (AUM) exceeding ₹17.26 lakh crore as on August 30, 2026.

The session also highlighted various reforms and initiatives undertaken to enhance the accessibility and reach of the pension system. These include the relaxation of the maximum entry age to 85 years, simplified withdrawal provisions and enhanced digital processes. Such initiatives are aimed at expanding pension coverage among diverse sections of society, including gig workers, MSMEs, farmers, women and corporates, thereby contributing towards the vision of a Pensioned Society by 2047 and the broader goal of Viksit Bharat @2047. 

Shri Nishant Anand, Manager, PFRDA, delivered a presentation on the features and benefits of NPS for individuals and corporates, highlighting its key features and role in long-term retirement planning. CA Gaurav Jain, ICAI, elaborated on the tax benefits available under NPS and addressed various tax-related aspects of pension planning. 
An interactive Question-and-Answer session was subsequently conducted, providing participants an opportunity to seek clarifications on various aspects of NPS and retirement planning. The programme concluded with a press interaction followed by a vote of thanks. 

PFRDA has been undertaking various outreach and awareness initiatives across the country to promote greater awareness about retirement planning and encourage wider participation in the pension ecosystem. PFRDA remains committed to advancing the vision of a “Pensioned Society by 2047”, wherein every citizen has access to an appropriate pension solution and enhanced financial security during old age.

About PFRDA

The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is a statutory regulatory organisation established by the Government of India with the mandate of regulating, promoting
and developing the pension sector in India. 

For more details, follow PFRDA on:

Twitter: @PFRDAOfficial
Facebook: @PFRDAOfficial
Instagram: @pfrdaofficial

item.title: National Voluntary Blood Donation Day 2026 Observed with Renewed Call for Regular Voluntary Blood Donation
item.description:
National Voluntary Blood Donation Day (NVBDD) 2026 was observed today at Swarn Jayanti Auditorium, Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC), New Delhi, with a renewed emphasis on strengthening the culture of regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation to ensure a safe, adequate and sustainable supply of blood and blood components across the country.
The national observance was organised by the Blood Transfusion Services (BTS) Division, Directorate General of Health Services (Dte.…
item.content:encoded:
National Voluntary Blood Donation Day (NVBDD) 2026 was observed today at Swarn Jayanti Auditorium, Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC), New Delhi, with a renewed emphasis on strengthening the culture of regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation to ensure a safe, adequate and sustainable supply of blood and blood components across the country.

The national observance was organised by the Blood Transfusion Services (BTS) Division, Directorate General of Health Services (Dte. GHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, in collaboration with Lady Hardinge Medical College and Associated Hospitals, New Delhi. The theme of NVBDD 2026 was “One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”

Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, presided over the programme and inaugurated the voluntary blood donation camp organised as part of the observance. The programme was attended by Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS); Dr. Himani Ahluwalia, Director, LHMC and Associated Hospitals; senior officials of Health Services; experts in Transfusion Medicine; healthcare professionals; representatives of State Blood Transfusion Councils, blood centres, voluntary organisations and educational institutions; and voluntary blood donors.

The programme commenced with the inauguration of the voluntary blood donation camp. This was followed by a Nukkad Natak and cultural performances by students of Lady Hardinge Medical College to disseminate the message of voluntary blood donation and highlight its importance in saving lives. The programme also included administration of the voluntary blood donation pledge, addresses by dignitaries and felicitation of States, organisations and stakeholders for their contribution towards promotion of voluntary blood donation. The programme concluded with the singing of the National Song followed by the National Anthem.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. M. Srinivas highlighted the importance of voluntary blood donation in ensuring an adequate and sustainable blood supply and emphasised the collective responsibility of citizens and stakeholders in strengthening voluntary blood donation.

Dr. Srinivas administered the voluntary blood donation pledge at the outset of his address and called upon citizens not only to donate blood regularly but also to create awareness and encourage greater participation in voluntary blood donation within their communities.

Acknowledging the contribution of blood donation organisations and volunteers towards the nation and humanity, Dr. Srinivas noted that around 75 per cent of blood collection in the country is through voluntary donation. He called for concerted efforts by the Government, healthcare professionals, NGOs, voluntary organisations and youth organisations to further expand voluntary blood donation and address gaps between demand and availability.

He also underscored the importance of rational and optimal utilisation of blood and its components. He called for expanding awareness on blood health beyond blood donation to include related issues such as nutrition and anaemia, particularly among women and adolescent girls.

Dr. Srinivas urged healthcare institutions, voluntary organisations and community groups to take these messages to the grassroots and contribute towards strengthening public awareness about the importance of blood, blood components and voluntary blood donation.

Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services, acknowledged the contribution of voluntary blood donors, institutions and organisations engaged in strengthening blood transfusion services across the country.

He highlighted various measures undertaken by the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, for strengthening blood transfusion services, including implementation of the National Blood Policy, strengthening of quality assurance and quality management practices, utilisation of the e-RaktKosh portal for donor registration and monitoring, development of national technical guidelines and implementation of Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives.

Dr. Krishna emphasised that systems and infrastructure, while essential, need to be complemented by sustained voluntary participation to ensure adequate availability of blood. He called for strengthening a culture of regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation, with particular emphasis on greater participation of youth.

Highlighting the human dimension of blood donation, Dr. Krishna observed that behind every unit of blood is a patient, behind every patient is a family, and behind every donor is an act of humanity. He called upon all stakeholders to contribute towards strengthening voluntary blood donation and make it an integral part of responsible citizenship.

LHMC Reaffirms Commitment to Safe and Quality Blood Services

Dr. Himani Ahluwalia, Director, LHMC and Associated Hospitals, highlighted the institution’s commitment to its core values of service, education and community responsibility and reaffirmed LHMC’s commitment to ensuring access to safe and quality blood services.

She stated that LHMC provides free treatment and transfusion support to around 700 registered thalassemia patients, making it one of the largest such services among government hospitals in the country.

Dr. Ahluwalia further highlighted the various initiatives undertaken by LHMC to promote voluntary blood donation, including regular voluntary blood donation camps, awareness campaigns, street plays and other community outreach activities.

States Recognised for Performance in Blood Collection during 2025

State Blood Transfusion Councils were felicitated during the national observance in recognition of their performance in blood collection during 2025 and their contribution towards strengthening voluntary blood donation.

Among the North-Eastern States, Mizoram secured the first position, followed by Sikkim in the second position.

Among the Union Territories, Chandigarh secured the first position, followed by Delhi in the second position.

Among the remaining States, Haryana secured the first position, Uttarakhand the second position and Punjab the third position.

The recognition acknowledges the sustained efforts of State Blood Transfusion Councils towards donor mobilisation, expansion of voluntary donor participation and promotion of voluntary blood donation.

NGOs and organisations making significant contributions towards promotion of voluntary blood donation and strengthening blood transfusion services were also felicitated. These included Thalassaemics India; Akhil Bharatiya Terapanth Yuvak Parishad (ABTYP); All India Radio; and Indian Red Cross Society, among others.

Nationwide Mega Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign

The national observance forms part of the Nationwide Mega Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign, being conducted from 17 September to 2 October 2026 across the country.

The campaign seeks to promote regular voluntary blood donation, strengthen the voluntary donor base and facilitate wider participation of citizens, institutions and communities. State and Union Territory Health Departments, State Blood Transfusion Councils, blood centres, healthcare and educational institutions, government departments, voluntary organisations and community groups are participating in the campaign.

The campaign places particular emphasis on youth participation, grassroots outreach, awareness generation and Jan Bhagidari. The e-RaktKosh portal is being utilised for donor registration and monitoring of blood collection activities. The voluntary blood donation pledge is also being promoted through digital platforms, including MyGov, to facilitate wider citizen participation.

Voluntary Blood Donation: An Essential Public Health Responsibility

National Voluntary Blood Donation Day is observed on 1st October every year to generate awareness about the importance of voluntary blood donation and encourage healthy and eligible individuals to donate blood regularly.

Blood and blood components are required for a wide range of medical interventions, including surgery, trauma care, management of severe anaemia, cancer and blood disorders, maternal care and other life-saving procedures. As blood cannot be manufactured, its availability is dependent upon the voluntary participation of eligible donors.

Regular voluntary blood donation is therefore an important contribution towards ensuring timely availability of blood and blood components for patients in need.

The theme of NVBDD 2026, “One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”, underscores the humanitarian spirit of voluntary blood donation and calls upon eligible citizens, particularly youth, to contribute towards this life-saving cause.

The observance concluded with an appeal to citizens, healthcare institutions, educational institutions, government departments, voluntary organisations and other stakeholders to sustain efforts towards regular, voluntary and non-remunerated blood donation throughout the year.

The Nationwide Mega Voluntary Blood Donation Campaign will continue up to 2 October 2026, with participating States, Union Territories, blood centres and organisations undertaking blood donation drives, donor mobilisation and awareness activities to further strengthen the culture of voluntary blood donation across the country.

*****

SR

Department of Land Resources gears up for the implementation of Special Campaign 6, announced by the Government of India, for institutionalizing swachhata and minimizing pendency in government offices from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026.

Department is ready to undertake the Campaign in its all three premises i.e. Kartavaya Bhawan-3, CGO Complex and Shivaji Stadium Annex.  During the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6  (September 15–30, 2026), efforts are focussed on identifying targets for reduction of pendencies, reviewing records, discarding e-waste items/obsolete items, and planning cleanliness initiatives.

During the last Special Campaign 5.0, Department of Land Resources achieved the following targets:

• 16 Cleanliness Campaigns were successfully conducted in the premises of the     Department

•  100% Disposal of Public Grievances and Appeals  

•  2415 files, including physical files and e-files, were reviewed for recording/weeding/closing

As part of the preparatory phase for Special Campaign 6, the Secretary, Department of Land Resources inspected the CGO Complex office on 17th September 2026 including the Record Room, and addressed staff members on the value of cleanliness.

Highlighting the Prime Minister's vision for Swachhata, Secretary noted the profound nationwide impact of the cleanliness movement. He stressed that maintaining a clean environment is a collective duty vital for a healthy and developed society—one that should extend far beyond government offices into our homes, neighbourhoods, and local communities.

To achieve this, he urged everyone to take personal responsibility for maintaining clean surroundings by properly identifying and disposing of obsolete items, e-waste, and unserviceable materials at home and workplace.  Additionally, he emphasized that reviewing, recording, and weeding out old files must be undertaken as a matter of priority.

The Department actively supports Special Campaign 6 by driving initiatives in workplace hygiene, streamlined record management, responsible waste handling, and effective space utilization.

***

SS/HR

item.content:encoded:
Indian Naval Ship Trishul arrived at Toulon, France, on 22 Sep 2026 to participate in the 24th edition of Exercise ‘Varuna’, the annual bilateral maritime exercise between the Indian Navy and the French Navy.

The ship received a warm welcome from the French Navy with a ceremonial water cannon salute. The harbour phase comprised professional, sporting and cultural engagements aimed at strengthening maritime ties and professional bonds between the two navies. The Commanding Officer, INS Trishul, called on RAdm Mackara Ouk, Deputy Commander-in-Chief for Operations (CECMED), and interacted with senior leadership of the French Navy.

The Commanding Officer, officers and crew laid wreath at the Mazargues War Memorial, Marseille, in remembrance of 205 Indian soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the World Wars. Professional engagements included cross-deck visits and exchange of operational experiences, contributing to enhanced interoperability between the two navies.

INS Trishul also hosted a cultural interaction onboard, attended by VAdm (Retd) Laurent Isnard, Deputy Mayor of Toulon, officers of the French Navy and civil dignitaries. A friendly volleyball match further fostered camaraderie between personnel of the two navies. The ship’s crew also visited French Navy ships Charles de Gaulle, Forbin and La Fayette, gaining insights into carrier operations, aviation facilities and practices followed onboard.

During the Sea Phase, INS Trishul exercised alongside French Navy units, including FDA Forbin, FLF La Fayette and SNA Suffren, as well as NH90 helicopters and Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft. Anti-submarine, anti-surface and live-firing exercises, along with cross-deck helicopter landing serials, enhanced operational coordination, interoperability and synergy between the two navies.

The visit of INS Trishul to Toulon reaffirms the strong and enduring maritime partnership between India and France and the commitment of both navies to strengthening maritime engagement, interoperability and professional exchanges.

item.title: English rendering of PM’s address at the Centenary Celebrations of UPSC
item.description:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet, Dr. Jitendra Singh Ji, P. K. Mishra Ji, T. V. Somanathan Ji, Ajay Kumar Ji, all the esteemed members of the UPSC, Chairpersons of the various State Public Service Commissions who have come from different states, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

item.content:encoded:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet, Dr. Jitendra Singh Ji, P. K. Mishra Ji, T. V. Somanathan Ji, Ajay Kumar Ji, all the esteemed members of the UPSC, Chairpersons of the various State Public Service Commissions who have come from different states, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

Before I begin today's discussion, I would like to mention an incident that occurred yesterday. The manner in which India's Captain Smita displayed patience, prudence, and courage, and as the Prime Minister of Israel said today, this Indian prevented another 9/11 from taking place. This act of valor by Smita fills every citizen of the country with pride. Today, I also spoke with his father Bhupendra Bhai, his mother Geeta Ben, and his wife Sonal. His treatment is ongoing, and today the entire world is proud of him. I appeal to the people of the country that we should all pray for Smita's long life and excellent health, and salute our brother Smita, who has enhanced India's glory.

Friends,

Today is not only a celebration of 100 years of the UPSC, but also a celebration of a legacy. It is a celebration of the aspirations that millions upon millions of young people cherish and pursue every year. It is a celebration of the trust that every Indian places in this institution. During this century-long journey, generations changed, governments changed, technology changed, and syllabi changed, yet the trust in the UPSC remains just as unwavering today, and that is one of your greatest assets. A commemorative postage stamp and coin marking this 100-year journey have just been released. A compilation of 100 important case laws has also been published. I pay my respects to all the distinguished individuals associated with this century-long journey. I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you. A little while ago, I was visiting the gallery that has been set up here, and I would encourage all of you to spend 10 to 15 minutes exploring it. I noticed a photograph from the 75th anniversary celebrations in which Lt. General Surendra Nath can be seen. Today, at the age of 90, he is present among us.

Friends,

There are many individuals who transformed this journey into a legacy of trust, introduced changes in tune with the times, and took the institution to new heights. Every one of them deserves appreciation and recognition. While looking through the gallery, I noticed that it also contains information about how Subhas Chandra Bose went through this very process in 1920. What caught my attention was that although India was under British rule at the time, there used to be a Sanskrit paper in the examination, and Subhas Babu wrote his paper in Sanskrit.

Friends,

On this historic occasion, I would also like to pay tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. After Independence, the challenge before him was not merely to keep the nation free. The challenge before him was also to govern and build a nation. The steel frame that was required for the reconstruction of the nation was provided by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He made this institution one of the principal pillars of independent India and strengthened it.

Friends,

When the foundation of this institution was laid in 1926, the priorities of that era were different. At that time, both the focus of the system and its commitment were directed towards the British Raj. After India attained Independence, the dreams of a free India and the governance needs of a free India became the central focus. Over the past decades, the UPSC has discharged its responsibilities in an exemplary manner. Much has already been said from this stage about its achievements and contributions. Therefore, I neither wish to repeat those points nor go into detail about them. Moving beyond history, we now have India's future waiting before us. One quarter of the 21st century, twenty-five years, has already passed. The next twenty to twenty-five years will be extremely important for India, for every citizen of India, and for every institution of India. Therefore, I would like to focus my discussion today in that direction.

Friends,

For a Developed India, the kind of governance the country now requires depends significantly on the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions. The young people whom you are recruiting today will play a crucial role in building a Developed India, and they themselves will be among the greatest beneficiaries of a Developed India. Keeping this in mind, we must always remember two touchstones. The first touchstone is: Nation First. The second touchstone is: Citizen First. These are the two standards against which every selection must be measured. When candidates are evaluated in this spirit, and when individuals imbued with this spirit are selected, the achievement of national goals becomes far more natural and far easier.

Friends,

India in 2047 will be very different from the India of today. India will be far more urbanized than it is today. The gap between villages and cities will narrow. The aspirations and expectations of our citizens, especially our youth, will be significantly greater. The signs of this transformation are already visible. Therefore, the question today is not merely one of service delivery. The question is also whether public services are able to keep pace with the speed of today's world of instant delivery. Are they able to move at that pace? Today, citizens do not want to wait weeks or months for a service. When AI can process thousands of documents within moments, and when governments have access to real-time data, citizens expect quick solutions. This changing mindset also demands new changes from our civil services. Therefore, we must align our selection parameters and recruitment processes with the needs of the future. We need to bring into public service those young people who are attracted not by public office, but by public service. Therefore, it is important that recruitment examinations should not merely assess how much a candidate knows. They should also assess why that young person wants to join the civil services. Because when the motivation is right, it becomes easier both to keep pace with changing public aspirations and to adapt to them.

Friends,

Many of you are familiar with the fact that whenever I meet trainee officers, I ask them to write down, right at the beginning and in their own handwriting, why they have joined the civil service. This is because responsibilities increase over time and new challenges emerge. At such moments, that small note reminds them of their original purpose. It also becomes a self-appraisal tool for them. UPSC and the State Commissions may also consider developing a similar mechanism.

Friends,

We have seen that period in the past when it was believed that the government was the ultimate guardian and provider. But today, our mantra is, "Nagrik Devo Bhava" (The Citizen is Divine). In other words, the citizen of this country is no less than a deity for us. Service to the citizen is our highest priority.

Therefore, friends,

Twenty-first-century India is moving forward with a new work culture. Its core principle is: Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance! Pro-People means working not according to the convenience of the government, but by placing the interests of citizens above everything else. Pro-Active means preparing solutions by anticipating problems before they arise, instead of acting only after problems appear. Good Governance means there should be neither absence of government, nor pressure from government, nor unnecessary influence. At both the national and state levels, we must design our selection processes in accordance with this spirit. We must provide the nation with professionals who possess the sensitivity to understand the suffering of the poor; who willingly step forward with youthful energy; who find innovative solutions to difficult challenges; who understand the needs of the nation; who ensure compliance with the law; and who can also judge whether a law is making people's lives easier or whether it is becoming an obstacle.

Friends,

We are all witnessing the rapid pace at which the times are changing and technology is evolving. The period that lies ahead is going to present society with new kinds of challenges. We are all familiar with the global debate currently taking place around AI. In such a scenario, our civil servants too will be required to work under very different circumstances. There will be situations involving information warfare, the challenge of deepfakes, concerns regarding algorithmic bias, and complex questions such as climate justice. Therefore, in our selection processes, we must also give priority to assessing complex problem-solving abilities and long-term vision, and to making deliberate efforts in that direction.

Friends,

We all know that today our nation is moving rapidly on the expressway of reforms. At such a time, our examination-conducting agencies must move quickly on reforms that are the need of the hour. One such important issue is the time taken to conduct examinations. We must not view an examination merely as an event. It is connected not only to an event but to the future and lives of young people. A delay of even a few months in examinations can become a serious challenge for them. Coaching fees, rent, transportation expenses, all of these impose a heavy burden on families. Therefore, it is extremely important that our examination system adopts the principle of time certainty. UPSC and all selection commissions across the country must ensure that, without lowering standards, we find ways to shorten our examination cycle. In fact, while I was looking at the gallery, I noticed that nearly one hundred days have already been reduced. This achievement certainly deserves appreciation, and I congratulate all of you for it.

But friends,

This is not merely an administrative reform. It is also a reform that promotes equity.

Friends,

All of you are aware of the Chief Secretaries' Conference and the DGP Conference. Over the last ten years, these have evolved into important institutional mechanisms. Under these forums, all the Chief Secretaries of the country come together for three days to deliberate and exchange ideas. Similarly, during the DGP Conference, all the Directors General of Police gather for three days to discuss issues and share experiences. One objective of these conferences is to help one state learn about, understand, and, where appropriate, adopt the best practices of another state. I have been informed that every year UPSC organizes a National Conference in partnership with State Public Service Commissions. To make this conference broader, more productive, and richer in new ideas, I am sure you are continuously thinking about giving it a new shape and a new dimension. Such efforts help institutions share their best practices with one another. At the same time, this conference should also study international best practices. Focused discussions should also be held on how technology can be used to improve the efficiency of our processes and procedures. Such efforts at cross-learning will benefit UPSC as well as every state selection commission. We must also consider standardizing procedural norms and processes. This will provide significant assistance to young people.

Friends,

Another important subject is capacity building within UPSC and the state selection commissions. This effort should continue on a sustained basis. The iGOT platform developed under Mission Karmayogi can also be used for our internal systems, for strengthening the capabilities of our teams, and for enhancing the efficiency of our institutions through these various platforms.

Friends,

You must always remember that your work is linked directly to the future of India's youth. In other words, you are an important pillar in the mission of transforming youth power into national power. Over the years, you have played a major role in advancing this mission. When UPSC was established, opportunities were more readily available to young people from large cities, economically privileged families, and prestigious institutions. Today, however, youth from villages and small towns are also entering public service. The participation of our daughters is also steadily increasing. In 1952, women constituted only 3 percent of candidates in the civil services, just three percent. Today that figure has risen to more than 30 percent. In the entire history of UPSC, there have been four women Chairpersons. The time for applause comes now. Out of those four women Chairpersons in UPSC's entire history, three have been appointed after 2014. These changes are not merely statistics; they demonstrate how greatly the scope of opportunity has expanded in our country.

Friends,

In 1976, when UPSC completed fifty years, the number of candidates appearing for examinations was far lower than it is today. Compared to that period, the number of examination aspirants has increased by more than forty-five times. In other words, today we have before us an enormous pool of talent. This is a matter of immense pride for the nation. At the same time, our responsibility has grown proportionately. When we possess such a vast talent pool, one that is the envy of the world, you are not merely selecting a candidate. You are choosing an individual who will later become a representative of the government. At the grassroots level, people will regard that individual as the government itself. Therefore, all of you bear a tremendous responsibility to select the right person.

Friends,

During its first century, UPSC has continuously strengthened its credibility and earned the trust of the nation. Now, as this institution enters its second century, it must enrich and deepen that credibility in accordance with new possibilities and new challenges. While preserving the values that have been our strength until now, we must also upgrade ourselves to meet the demands of the future. UPSC's independence, impartiality, commitment to merit, confidentiality, and fair procedures constitute its defining identity. These values must always be preserved. With this appeal, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you.

Thank you very much.

DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi. 

***

MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

item.content:encoded:
Shimla: As part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign–2026, SJVN organised a “Safai Mitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir” at its Corporate Headquarters, Shimla, today. The Shivir was inaugurated by Sh. Ajay Kumar Sharma, Director (Personnel), SJVN in esteemed presence of Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel, Director (Projects), SJVN, Sh. Pankaj Porwal, Chief Vigilance Officer, SJVN and senior officials.

On this occasion, a Special Health Camp was organised for Safai Mitras, providing them with essential health screening and medical services. A medical team from Himachal Pradesh State Health Department conducted blood tests and blood pressure check-ups and provided X-ray facilities. The initiative was aimed at promoting greater awareness of health and ensuring the well-being of Safai Mitras.

As part of the initiative, a felicitation ceremony was organised for Safai Mitras for their valuable contribution in Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign. Best-performing Safai Mitras and volunteers were honoured for their active role in housekeeping, sweeping and support services. The initiative reaffirms SJVN’s commitment to the safety, dignity, health and well-being of its Safai Mitras.

SS/NK

item.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Centenary Celebrations of UPSC
item.description: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated in the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Highlighting the profound legacy behind the centenary in his address, the Prime Minister noted that the 100-year celebration is truly a festival of the immense aspirations lived by millions of youths and the unshakable trust every Indian places in the institution. He praised the organization's enduring credibility despite changing…
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated in the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) today  at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Highlighting the profound legacy behind the centenary in his address, the Prime Minister noted that the 100-year celebration is truly a festival of the immense aspirations lived by millions of youths and the unshakable trust every Indian places in the institution. He praised the organization's enduring credibility despite changing generations, governments, technologies, and syllabi, celebrating the release of a commemorative postage stamp, a special coin, and a compilation of 100 significant case laws.

Recalling the monumental challenges faced after independence, the Prime Minister paid deep homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for establishing the vital steel frame required not just to keep the country independent, but to actively govern the newly formed nation. He praised Sardar Patel for transforming and empowering the institution into a premier pillar of independent India. “The steel frame that was needed for the reconstruction of the nation was provided by Sardar Patel,” noted Shri Modi.

Contrasting the institution's British Raj origins in 1926 with its post-independence evolution, the Prime Minister noted that the system successfully shifted its focus to fulfill the dreams of a free nation. He acknowledged that while the UPSC has excellently discharged its historical duties, the focus must now decisively pivot toward the critical next 25 years that await the country. “Therefore, today I will keep the focus of my discussion in this direction,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the critical role of selection commissions in achieving a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister emphasized that the youths recruited today will simultaneously serve as the chief architects and the primary beneficiaries of the nation's future. He mandated that every selection process must be rigorously tested against the dual criteria of prioritizing the nation and the citizen. “When candidates filled with this spirit are selected, achieving national goals will become that much more natural and easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Projecting the vastly different socio-economic landscape of 2047, the Prime Minister explained that an increasingly urbanized nation with narrowing rural-urban divides will dramatically elevate the expectations of the youth. He warned that traditional service delivery models must evolve to match the speed of an instant-delivery world where citizens demand rapid, real-time solutions powered by AI. “This changing mindset demands new changes from our Civil Services as well,” observed Shri Modi.

Urging a fundamental shift in recruitment philosophy, the Prime Minister stressed that the selection parameters must evaluate not just academic knowledge, but the underlying motivation to ensure candidates are drawn to public service rather than mere public office. He explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it significantly easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations. “Therefore, we will also have to adapt our Selection Parameters and Recruitment Process according to future needs,” asserted Shri Modi.

Sharing his personal interactions with newly inducted civil servants, the Prime Minister suggested that trainee officers should write down their original motivations to serve as a grounding self-appraisal tool when future challenges and responsibilities mount. He encouraged both the UPSC and state commissions to institutionalize similar introspective mechanisms for candidates. “UPSC and state commissions can also consider developing such a system,” remarked Shri Modi.

Discarding the archaic 'Mai-Baap' governance mindset of the past, the Prime Minister heralded a modern administrative era built on the absolute principle of 'Nagrik Devo Bhava'- treating the citizen as divine. He declared that placing the service of the citizen above all else is the absolute core of 21st-century governance. “Meaning, the citizen of the country is no less than a deity to us,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Defining the new work culture for modern administration, the Prime Minister explicitly detailed that 21st-century India is moving forward with an entirely fresh operational ethos. He stated that the fundamental principles of this new era rest entirely on three core pillars. “Its fundamental principles are Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance!” asserted Shri Modi.

Elaborating on these foundational governance principles, the Prime Minister demanded that selection processes at both national and state levels be meticulously designed to recruit professionals who proactively anticipate problems and operate without unnecessary pressure or influence. He emphasized the need for empathetic civil servants who find innovative solutions, proactively ease citizens' lives, and critically evaluate the impact of laws on the public. “We have to give the country those professionals who find innovative ways out of difficult problems,” noted Shri Modi.

Addressing the unprecedented technological disruptions facing society, the Prime Minister cautioned that future civil servants will have to navigate entirely new battlegrounds such as information warfare, deepfakes, algorithmic bias, and climate justice. He instructed recruitment agencies to adapt to these global shifts by prioritizing candidates' foresight and complex problem-solving abilities. “In such a scenario, in the selection process, we will also have to give priority to testing complex problem-solving and foresight,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the urgency of administrative overhauls, the Prime Minister insisted that examination agencies must rapidly align with the nation's broader reform momentum by adopting the principle of Time Certainty to shorten exam cycles without lowering standards. He emphasized that prolonged examinations inflict severe financial burdens, such as coaching fees, rent, and transport, on families, transforming cycle reduction into a fundamental fairness issue. “This will also be an equity reform,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Encouraging systematic institutional capacity building, the Prime Minister praised existing national conferences where state commissions share best practices, but urged them to elevate these forums by studying international standards and focusing on technological efficiency. He advocated for cross-learning and standardizing procedures to provide immense relief and clarity to participating youths across the country. “This process of cross-learning will benefit UPSC as well and will also benefit the selection commissions of every state,” noted Shri Modi.

Reiterating the absolute necessity of continuous institutional growth, the Prime Minister advised that both the UPSC and state selection commissions must relentlessly focus on their own capacity building. He recommended heavily leveraging the digital infrastructure already established under the national mission for civil servants. “The i-GOT platform created under Mission Karmayogi can be utilized for this,” remarked Shri Modi.

Reminding the officials of their profound national duty, the Prime Minister emphasized that their core mission is directly linked to transforming youth power into robust national power, celebrating how opportunities have successfully shifted from elite city-dwellers to talented youth from rural villages. He proudly noted the dramatic rise in female candidates in civil services, jumping from a mere 3 percent in 1952 to over 30 percent today, alongside the historic appointment of three out of four women UPSC Chairpersons post-2014. “These changes are not just statistics; they show how much the scope of opportunities in the country has expanded,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Pointing to the massive explosion in candidate participation since the institution's 50th anniversary in 1976, the Prime Minister noted a 45-fold increase in exam takers, representing a vast national talent pool that demands monumental responsibility from selectors. He reminded the commissions that they are not merely picking candidates, but choosing individuals who will become the very face and representative of the government at the grassroots level. “Therefore, all of you have a very huge responsibility of selecting the right person,” asserted Shri Modi.

Looking toward the institution's second century, the Prime Minister urged the commission to aggressively upgrade its operations to meet future challenges while fiercely protecting its foundational credibility. He stated that the core identity of the UPSC, its independence, impartiality, merit, confidentiality, and fair processes, must remain eternally uncompromised. “These values must always remain,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address with a forward-looking mandate, the Prime Minister expressed his profound hope that the institution will continue to thrive and adapt successfully in its new century.

item.content:encoded:
Pune, 30 September 2026

The Directorate General Resettlement (DGR), Ministry of Defence, Government of India, in association with the Vaikunth Mehta National Institute of Cooperative Management (VAMNICOM), Pune, inaugurated the DGR’s Resettlement Training Programme on “Innovations and Agribusiness Management” at VAMNICOM, Pune.

The inaugural session was graced by Brigadier Ranjan Keron, ADG South, Directorate General Resettlement, Ministry of Defence, as the Chief Guest. Dr. Suva Kanta Mohanty, Director, VAMNICOM; Dr. Sudam Adlinge, Registrar, VAMNICOM; Dr. Amit Borkar, Assistant Professor and Course Coordinator; and Dr. Arvind Darshna, Assistant Professor and Co-Coordinator of the programme, were also present. 52 Officers from the Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force participating in the programme attended the inaugural session.

Addressing the participants, Brigadier Ranjan Keron appreciated the officers for undertaking the training and encouraged them to make the best use of the knowledge, skills and insights gained through the programme. He emphasised the importance of effectively applying the learning to future professional, entrepreneurial and livelihood opportunities.

Dr. Suva Kanta Mohanty, Director, VAMNICOM, highlighted the potential of small-scale entrepreneurial activities to generate sustainable income when planned and managed effectively. Drawing upon examples from the cooperative sector, he explained how small initiatives, innovation and collective efforts can create wider economic benefits and contribute to community development.

Dr. Amit Borkar, Course Coordinator, spoke on the significance of agribusiness and value chain management, highlighting the need to identify and assess viable business opportunities. He emphasised that the programme would provide participants with practical knowledge and managerial capabilities to support their transition towards entrepreneurship, self-employment and new livelihood opportunities.

The training programme is being conducted from 28 September to 20 November 2026, with 52 participants from the Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force. The programme has been specially designed to equip Armed Forces personnel with practical knowledge and managerial skills in agribusiness, entrepreneurship, innovation and allied agricultural activities, thereby supporting their transition to meaningful entrepreneurial and self-employment opportunities after service.

The comprehensive programme covers a wide range of areas, including agribusiness opportunities, agricultural finance, government schemes, food processing, dairy, poultry, fisheries, mushroom cultivation, floriculture, apiculture, marketing, project preparation, financial management and entrepreneurship. Through these sessions, participants will gain an understanding of emerging opportunities in agriculture and allied sectors, along with the managerial, financial and entrepreneurial skills required to plan and implement viable business ventures.

The inaugural programme also witnessed the enthusiastic participation of first-year PGDM-ABM students of VAMNICOM, who contributed to the smooth conduct of the event. Miss. Bhagirathi M and Mr. Sidharth Singh served as the anchors and coordinated the proceedings of the inaugural session with enthusiasm and professionalism.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Dr. Sudam Adlinge, Registrar, VAMNICOM, who expressed his gratitude to the Chief Guest, DGR representatives, faculty members, participating Armed Forces officers and all those associated with the successful organisation of the programme.

The initiative marks a significant step towards empowering retiring and transitioning Armed Forces personnel with knowledge, skills and entrepreneurial perspectives that can help them explore sustainable livelihood opportunities in the dynamic and growing agriculture and allied sectors.

item.title: Finding New Purpose in What We Discard
item.description:
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), launched in 2014, has evolved into a broader movement for cleanliness, waste management, and behavioural change.
