Parallelly , the idea of Waste to Wealth is changing how…
item.content:encoded:
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM), launched in 2014, has evolved into a broader movement for cleanliness, waste management, and behavioural change. The mission also created space for wider citizen participation through Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS), launched in 2017 as an annual campaign for collective cleanliness action. The campaign has expanded its focus to plastic waste management, visual cleanliness, and garbage-free public spaces.

Parallelly, the idea of Waste to Wealth is changing how waste is viewed and managed across India. It treats discarded material as a resource that can be recovered, reused, and converted into value. The Government has linked this approach with circularity, resource efficiency, and sustainable waste management. Under Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban 2.0, cities are encouraged to strengthen source segregation, waste processing, and recovery of value from waste. The change is visible not only in large processing plants, but also in homes, communities, and local institutions.

A Compost Bin Brings the Change Home

For many Indian households, turning kitchen waste into compost is not a new idea. It is a practice that is finding a fresh place in today’s waste management systems. In Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, senior citizen K. Subbalakshmi has shown how this familiar habit can be adopted at home. The municipal corporation recently shared her experience to encourage more citizens to take up home composting. The wet waste generated in her kitchen is converted into compost and used in her garden, returning what would otherwise be discarded to the soil.

A similar effort began in Chandigarh during the COVID-19 pandemic. Resident Kamaljeet Kaur Deol started composting wet kitchen waste at home. What began as a household practice gradually grew into awareness activities to encourage others to adopt home composting. Her efforts have since helped inspire citizens to contribute towards a cleaner and greener city.

As these individual efforts began encouraging wider participation, the idea also found a place in organised community learning. In Siddipet, Telangana, the dedicated waste management learning centre ‘Swachh Badi’ is providing young people with hands-on exposure to practical waste management practices, from home composting to community-level composting. Building on this approach, similar centres are planned across 141 municipal areas, bringing awareness and practical learning on responsible waste management closer to communities.

What begins with a small compost bin can therefore have a wider effect. It gives new life to plants while keeping a regular stream of wet waste away from landfills. More importantly, it shows how waste management can begin where waste itself is generated.

When a Weed Becomes an Opportunity

Beyond household waste, communities are also finding uses for materials that have long been difficult to manage. In Borchila village of Assam’s Morigaon district, this approach is being applied to a plant that has become a persistent challenge for communities living around water bodies. Water hyacinth, locally known as ‘pani meteka’, is an invasive aquatic plant that spreads rapidly across water bodies. Despite its aesthetic appeal, water hyacinth has become a problematic weed, overcrowding freshwater bodies such as rivers, ponds, and lakes. Its overgrowth hampers activities like fishing, transportation, and recreation, making these water sources less viable.

However, the women of Borchila village have found a new way to turn water hyacinth into an opportunity. Instead of viewing the plant only as an unwanted growth in water bodies, they have begun transforming it into handicrafts. Supported under the Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission, the initiative has created an additional source of income for the participating women, who earn at least ₹10,000 a month through this work. What was once seen as a problem for water bodies is thus being transformed into a resource for livelihoods and enterprise. The experience demonstrates that resource recovery can extend beyond waste management to create value and livelihood opportunities. By transforming materials that might otherwise remain a burden into useful products, such initiatives can support local enterprise while promoting more sustainable use of resources.

Coconut Waste Finds a New Market

From an invasive plant being transformed into a source of rural livelihood, the focus now shifts to another material contributing to the urban waste burden. In Patna, coconut shells, fibres and other residues are being recovered and processed into useful products. The city generates around 25–30 metric tonnes of coconut shell every day, which previously added to the volume of waste reaching landfill sites. To address this waste stream, the Patna Municipal Corporation has established a processing facility in the Danapur area, creating a pathway for converting discarded coconut residues into productive resources.

Coconut Waste Processing Plant in Patna

The initiative reflects the systematic approach to waste management promoted under the Swachh Bharat Mission, where waste is increasingly viewed as a resource rather than merely a material for disposal. The facility is designed to recover useful components from coconut waste and convert them into products with applications in agriculture, horticulture, and other commercial uses. With an initial processing capacity of 10 tonnes per day, the plant is planned to operate in multiple shifts and scale up to 30 tonnes per day.

 Ropes made from coconut waste fibers

Different components of coconut waste can be recovered and put to productive use. Wet residues are processed into high-quality organic compost, while coconut fibres are converted into coir ropes with applications in construction, packaging, mats, and handicrafts. Cocopeat is another valuable output, with applications in agriculture and horticulture, including nurseries and rooftop gardens, where its use as a growing medium is gaining importance.

By recovering and processing these materials, the initiative reduces the volume of coconut waste requiring disposal and enables waste-derived products to re-enter productive use. This approach advances circular economy practices while creating avenues for local livelihoods and employment.

When Waste Becomes a Public Space

 

The idea of Waste to Wealth is also changing how cities look at discarded material. Instead of treating scrap only as waste, cities are finding ways to reuse it in public spaces and community facilities. One such approach is the creation of Waste to Wonder parks, where discarded material is given a new purpose as part of public spaces and attractions. The approach reflects the principles of a circular economy, which encourage materials to be reduced, reused, repaired, and recycled for continued use.

Chandigarh offers an early example of this approach. Its Rock Garden was created using industrial and household waste, demonstrating how discarded material can be creatively reused in a public space. The city has also developed a Waste to Wonder Park spread across 1.75 acres. Structures in the park have been created from discarded materials such as iron sheets, rods, fans, and automobile parts.

Delhi has adopted a similar approach through its Waste to Wonder Park, where industrial waste, scrap metal, and discarded automobile parts sourced from landfills are repurposed to create replicas and other structures. Beyond recreation and urban beautification, such spaces demonstrate how discarded materials can be integrated into productive and public-use infrastructure. Beyond urban beautification, the park integrates clean energy infrastructure, featuring solar trees and rooftop solar panels with a combined capacity of 50 KW. The electricity generated can be supplied to power distribution companies, creating an additional avenue for revenue generation while promoting the productive use of waste and renewable energy.

From Waste to Resource

These examples demonstrate how discarded materials can be recovered, repurposed, and returned to productive use rather than being sent directly for final disposal. Materials that would otherwise add to the waste burden can be transformed into components of public spaces, creative attractions and, in some cases, sources of economic value.

The Waste to Wealth approach begins with a shift in perspective, from viewing waste as something to be discarded to recognising its potential as a resource. Through proper segregation, recovery and processing, discarded materials can be converted into useful products, supporting cleaner communities, resource efficiency and the transition towards a circular economy.

However, the form can be filled between 8 th to 15 th October, 2026 with late fee also. item.title: Government Strengthens Implementation of PCR and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Acts through Special Courts, Victim Support, Awareness and Grievance Redressal Mechanisms
item.description:
The Central Government continues to support States and Union Territories in the effective implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, through a range of measures aimed at strengthening enforcement mechanisms, facilitating speedy trial, providing relief and rehabilitation to victims, creating awareness about statutory safeguards and promoting social harmony.
The implementation of the…
item.content:encoded:
The Central Government continues to support States and Union Territories in the effective implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, through a range of measures aimed at strengthening enforcement mechanisms, facilitating speedy trial, providing relief and rehabilitation to victims, creating awareness about statutory safeguards and promoting social harmony.

The implementation of the two Acts primarily rests with the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The Government of India, through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for implementation of the PCR Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, provides financial assistance to States and UTs for strengthening the institutional and implementation mechanisms under the Acts and Rules.

Strengthening Exclusive Special Courts for Speedy Trial

As reported by States and Union Territories, 217 Exclusive Special Courts have been established in 15 States and Union Territories for trial of offences under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. The Act also provides for designation of Courts of Session as Special Courts in districts where the number of cases is relatively lower, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

The establishment and strengthening of Exclusive Special Courts is aimed at facilitating speedy trial and effective disposal of cases under the Act and ensuring that victims have access to specialised judicial mechanisms.

Central Assistance to States and UTs

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme, the Centre released ₹392.71 crore in 2022–23, ₹535.30 crore in 2023–24 and ₹495.29 crore in 2024–25, amounting to ₹1,423.30 crore over the three financial years, to States and Union Territories.

The scheme provides assistance for strengthening of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Protection Cells and Special Police Stations, strengthening of judicial machinery, relief and rehabilitation of victims, incentives for inter-caste marriages, awareness generation and other measures for effective implementation of the Acts.

Over the same three years, 88,172, 79,667 and 99,216 victims, respectively, were reported to have received relief under the scheme.

Promoting Awareness of Legal Safeguards

The Government has accorded priority to creating wider awareness about the legal safeguards and rights available to members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Rules framed thereunder.

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme, States and UTs are supported in undertaking awareness campaigns, workshops, training programmes, awareness camps and other outreach activities to disseminate information about the provisions of the Acts and Rules.

SAMBAL – Strengthening Access to Grievance Redressal

To facilitate easier access to grievance redressal mechanisms, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the National Helpline Against Atrocities (NHAA) in December 2021, subsequently renamed SAMBAL. The initiative provides members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes with an accessible mechanism to register and track grievances relating to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The helpline is available through toll-free number 1800-202-1989 and short code 14566.

Encouraging Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages

As part of the Government’s efforts to promote social integration, equality and social harmony, financial assistance is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for inter-caste marriages where one of the spouses belongs to a Scheduled Caste.

The number of couples reported to have received incentive for inter-caste marriages increased from 14,225 in 2022-23 to 26,050 in 2024–25.

According to the latest Crime in India figures provided in the source document, 65,646 cases were registered under the Act in 2024, compared with 70,725 in 2023 and 67,633 in 2022. At the end of 2024, 3,92,006 cases were pending trial. These figures underline the continuing need for timely investigation, effective prosecution and prompt support to victims.

The Government remains committed to working with States and Union Territories to strengthen implementation of the Act and ensure access to justice for members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

item.title: Ministry of Textiles undertakes Swachhata initiatives to promote Cleanliness, Sustainability and Waste-is-Wealth practices
item.description:
The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)
As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign and under the theme “Swachhata Se Samriddhi,” – Kabaad Se Jugaad ” activity was successfully conducted at The Jute Corporation of India Limited, Bhadrak RLD, Odisha.
As part of the initiative, the team visited households and nearby local areas to collect waste materials from the community. During the interaction, people were sensitized about the principles of Reduce, Reuse and…
item.content:encoded:
The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign and under the theme “Swachhata Se Samriddhi,”– Kabaad Se Jugaad” activity was successfully conducted at The Jute Corporation of India Limited, Bhadrak RLD, Odisha.

As part of the initiative, the team visited households and nearby local areas to collect waste materials from the community. During the interaction, people were sensitized about the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (RRR), the importance of cleanliness, and the need to minimize the use of single-use plastics.

The collected waste materials were brought to the office and creatively transformed into useful and decorative items, including pen holders, dustbins, decorative articles, eco-friendly paper bags, and cloth bags made from old clothes by the employees of the corporations.

The activity received active and enthusiastic participation from all members, making it a meaningful initiative towards promoting cleanliness, sustainable practices, creative reuse of waste, and the concept of “Waste is Wealth.” The useful and decorative items created from the collected waste were also distributed among the local people, further encouraging community participation and awareness about sustainable waste management practices.

National Jute Board (NJB)

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, the National Jute Board organized a comprehensive health check-up camp for its housekeeping workers, gardeners and Safai Mitras engaged in maintaining cleanliness and hygiene in the office premises and garden areas.

The camp was conducted in collaboration with the ESIC Hospital, wherein a team of doctors and healthcare professionals carried out the necessary health examinations. The camp included general health check-ups, blood tests, ECG and other essential medical assessments to monitor the health and well-being of the workers.

The initiative reaffirmed the National Jute Board’s commitment towards the health, safety and welfare of its Safai Mitras and support staff, recognizing their vital contribution to maintaining a clean, hygienic and healthy working environment.

Development Commissioner (Handicrafts)

  • Organized a discussion and cleaning program on “Say No to Single Use Plastic” inside and outside office area with Safai mitras.
  • The activitiy ensured enhanced cleanliness of used plastic bottle and waste . Continual monitoring will be maintained to sustain these cleanliness standards.

 

Cotton Corporation of India

The Corporation organized an awareness activity across its offices on 29 September 2026 to promote the importance of Reuse and Recycle as part of responsible waste management. Employees were sensitized about reducing waste by reusing materials wherever possible and ensuring recyclable items are properly collected and recycled. The initiative aimed to encourage sustainable habits, minimize waste generation, and promote the efficient use of resources.

The activity reflects the Corporation’s commitment to environmental stewardship, sustainable practices, resource conservation, and collective action towards a cleaner and greener future.

National Insitute of Fashion Technology

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, NIFT Campuses undertook plantation and campus beautification activities under “Swachh Parv, Harit Parv / Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”. Further, under “Swachhata se Samriddhi – Waste is Wealth & Waste to Art”, initiatives were undertaken for the creative reuse of waste materials, Waste-to-Art activities, plastic recycling and reuse/recycling drives, with the objective of promoting sustainable waste management and environmental awareness.

Plantation Drive

 

Promoting use of reusable glass bottles and cups

item.description:
Head Coach of the Indian Para Swimming contingent Dr Virender Kumar Dabbas says that he expects at least four medals from his wards at the upcoming Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games to be played from October 18 to 24, 2026.
While speaking to SAI Media during the ongoing preparatory camp in SAI NCoE, Gandhinagar, Dr Virender Kumar Dabbas picked para swimmer Rohit Kumar for special praise "Rohit(Kumar), a former MARCOS commando, started swimming just one and half years back, and he is…
item.content:encoded:
Head Coach of the Indian Para Swimming contingent Dr Virender Kumar Dabbas says that he expects at least four medals from his wards at the upcoming Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games to be played from October 18 to 24, 2026.

While speaking to SAI Media during the ongoing preparatory camp in SAI NCoE, Gandhinagar, Dr Virender Kumar Dabbas picked para swimmer Rohit Kumar for special praise "Rohit(Kumar), a former MARCOS commando, started swimming just one and half years back, and he is already ranked second in Asia, he along with Himanshu Nandal and Ravi Karthik Budigina is among our best prospects. I expect this team to win at least four medals at the continental games."

Members of the Indian para swimming contingent are undergoing a preparatory camp at the SAI NCoE, Gandhinagar from September 20- October 13, 2026.

Dr Dabbas, who also serves as the Chairman of Para Swimming in the Paralympic Committee of India(PCI) said that currently the focus of the camp is on building speed,"right now we are in the tapering phase, we are focusing on speed, working on having faster starts, sharper turns, yesterday we took note of the timmings our swimmers are clocking, with the (Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games) Games so close, we have to be on the last phase of training which is the tapering phase. Swimming coaching follows a particular trajectory, first we teach technique and work on the athlete's stamina, then comes strength training, last we work on speed, without technique, stamina and strength then there will be no speed."

He explained  that if India has to emerge as a serious sporting nation then sports has to be given equal weightage as academics in schools

"Right now the government is trying to ensure that the students get two games periods per week, what will be achieved in two periods in a week?. Also during these games periods, are they actually being taught sports ?. The physical education teachers  just give a football or Volleyball to the students and that's it, they don't care to teach them anything, they have to be made accountable."
  
"I was in East Germany during the late eighties for Masters in Science of Sports Training (not Ph.D.), there students would not be promoted in schools unless they passed gymnastics and swimming tests, sports was given equal if not higher weightage than academics."

He stressed that if small children are to be developed into sports persons, the primary school teachers need to contribute in a big way 

"Every teacher at the primary level must have a certain level of proficiency in sports, if the primary teacher is well versed in sports, and knows the measurements and rules related to various sports, that will be very helpful. He will be able to utilise even a small area for sports coaching. Also considering the paucity of sports equipment, they need to innovate, one football can also be used for volleyball, handball etc. That is how sports culture will be built."

He praised the SAI, NCoE, Gandhinagar as an excellent centre for sports training "I have been coming here since long as I am a member of the Talent Identification Development Committee(TIDC), there has been a marked improvement under the stewardship of Coach Mayank Diwan and Coach Ravi Teja. The improvement is evident as the swimmers are clocking much better timings now. The centre serves high quality food, has good residential facilities and the players are supported by a sports science department. However, I feel there should be a small market inside the campus, consisting of a cafeteria with carrom, TT table where the athletes could socialise, relax and gel."

item.title: From AI to EVs: How Technology Is Transforming Urban Swachhata
item.description: On October 2, 2014, the Swachh Bharat Mission began with a simple idea: keep our surroundings clean. Avoid littering public spaces and make cleanliness a shared responsibility. What began with brooms, bins and citizen participation soon became a mass movement. Today, that movement is embracing a new generation of technology. Urban sanitation is becoming digital, sensor-enabled and electrified. Digital dashboards are making services easier to track. AI-powered robots are entering spaces too…
item.content:encoded:
On October 2, 2014, the Swachh Bharat Mission began with a simple idea: keep our surroundings clean. Avoid littering public spaces and make cleanliness a shared responsibility. What began with brooms, bins and citizen participation soon became a mass movement. Today, that movement is embracing a new generation of technology.  Urban sanitation is becoming digital, sensor-enabled and electrified. Digital dashboards are making services easier to track. AI-powered robots are entering spaces too hazardous for workers. Electric vehicles are bringing cleaner mobility to waste collection. From the broom to the bot, technology is giving Swachhata a smarter edge — creating cleaner cities, safer workplaces and more responsive services.

Raipur’s Digital Leap: Dashboard Replaces a Queue

Earlier, Raipur residents had to visit the municipal office for septic tank cleaning services. The new digital system lets residents request desludging services online, reducing the need for an in-person visit and cutting wait times.

Raipur Municipal Corporation has introduced a digital Faecal Sludge Management (FSM) dashboard prototype based on the UPYOG (Urban Platform for DeliverY of Online Governance) platform. Residents can use the system to book desludging services, make payments and track the process digitally. The platform is associated with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA) and the National Urban Digital Mission (NUDM).

The process is designed to be simple. A resident enters a mobile number or property ID, and the system automatically locates the address. A single-page form enables desludging to be booked. But the real change happens behind the screen.

Once a request is placed, the system helps track the service in real time. The “one application, one trip” approach supports better planning. Drivers upload photographs after completing the work, enabling the service to be verified digitally. The dashboard also helps the city monitor vehicles and plan resources more efficiently.  For sanitation workers, technology is also changing how hazardous work is approached. Digital monitoring supports the shift from manual sewer cleaning towards mechanised cleaning. This reduces human risk and supports safer work practices.

What looks like a simple dashboard is therefore doing more than replacing paperwork. It connects the citizen, the service provider and the municipal system on one digital platform. In Raipur, the journey from “request” to “service” is becoming a trackable digital process.

G-SPIDER: Inside the Canal, a Robot Takes Over

In the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, the Amayizhanchan Canal disappears beneath the Thampanoor railway premises.  The covered stretch has restricted vertical clearance, continuous water flow and no safe entry points for workers. Conventional cleaning methods therefore become extremely difficult in this confined space.

Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation has brought a robot to clean this difficult space. The city has deployed G-SPIDER, an AI-powered canal-cleaning system developed by Technopark-based Genrobotic Innovations, the makers of the robotic scavenger Bandicoot.

The robot uses machine vision and sensor intelligence to detect, assess, and remove accumulated waste. It adapts to different waste types, flow conditions and structural challenges in real time. Its five-degrees-of-freedom mechanism uses a biomimetic claw to pick up mixed and irregular debris. The extracted waste is then transferred directly into designated collection vehicles.

The significance goes beyond automation. G-SPIDER enhances worker safety by minimising direct exposure to toxic gases, contaminated water and hazardous waste. It can also operate during high water levels and continuous-flow conditions, supporting scheduled and systematic canal cleaning.

That makes G-SPIDER more than a cleaning machine. The deployment demonstrates how technology can enable sanitation work in environments where human entry poses significant safety risks. The model also points to wider possibilities. The Thiruvananthapuram deployment showcases a scalable and replicable approach for other high-risk canals and drainage networks.

Garbage Trucks Get an Electric Upgrade

The daily garbage collection vehicle is also becoming part of the clean-city transition. Across Guntur (in Andhra Pradesh), Chennai and Indore cities, electric vehicles are being integrated into door-to-door waste collection, combining cleaner mobility with smarter waste management.

In Guntur city, more than 200 electric autos have brought cleaner mobility to door-to-door waste collection across the city. Each vehicle is equipped with GPS tracking, allowing real-time monitoring of collection operations. The initiative eliminates the need for more than 71,000 litres of diesel annually and is estimated to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 21,000 tonnes over a decade.

Tamil Nadu’s Chennai has brought electric mobility directly into its daily waste collection system. The Greater Chennai Corporation has deployed 5,478 battery-operated e-rickshaws across all 15 zones for door-to-door collection. The vehicles travel around 40 km a day, replacing diesel-powered collection vehicles with e-rickshaws and helping reduce pollution. The fleet reduces around 41 tonnes of carbon emissions each day, amounting to an annual reduction of 15,160 tonnes.

But the change is not limited to cleaner vehicles. Each e-rickshaw has separate bins for wet, dry and hazardous waste, bringing segregation into the collection process itself. The fleet now covers 24,621 streets and more than 2.1 million households, while audio systems on the vehicles carry waste-segregation messages through neighbourhoods. The initiative also supports employment for more than 6,000 people.

Indore city in Madhya Pradesh has taken the electric transition a step further by linking waste collection with renewable energy. The city has deployed 100 electric vehicles for door-to-door collection in core areas. Real-time GPS tracking through the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) supports monitoring and service transparency. The initiative is expected to reduce annual carbon emissions by about 24,918 tonnes and save around ₹5.97 crore each year in fuel and maintenance costs.

The city has also established 20 solar charging stations, each equipped with 10 kW solar panels. Together, they can generate 800–1,000 units of green energy daily and charge 80–100 vehicles a day.  Across these cities, the garbage collection vehicle is becoming more than a means of transport. It is becoming a cleaner, connected and increasingly efficient part of urban sanitation.

The Next Chapter: Smarter, Safer Swachhata

Technology is giving urban sanitation new tools to clean smarter, work safer and respond faster. From digital dashboards and AI-powered robots to electric waste collection, these innovations are bringing technology closer to everyday Swachhata. The next chapter is about taking these innovations to more cities, adopting them in daily life, making urban sanitation cleaner, safer and more responsive.

Reference

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

item.title: Government Revises Sugar Stock Holding Norms to Prevent Hoarding and Ensure Smooth Supply to Consumers During Festive Season
item.description:
With the commencement of the new sugar season from 1st October, The Government of India has further strengthened measures to ensure adequate availability of sugar to consumers at reasonable prices during the festive season.
The Government has reduced the stock holding period for sugar dealers to 15 days and fixed the stock holding limit at 1,000 quintals, with effect from 15 October 2026 to 30 November 2026 , except in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and the State of…
item.content:encoded:
With the commencement of the new sugar season from 1st October, The Government of India has further strengthened measures to ensure adequate availability of sugar to consumers at reasonable prices during the festive season.

The Government has reduced the stock holding period for sugar dealers to 15 days and fixed the stock holding limit at 1,000 quintals, with effect from 15 October 2026 to 30 November 2026, except in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and the State of Assam.

Under the revised provisions, with effect from 15 October 2026, a sugar dealer shall:

  • Not hold sugar stock for a period exceeding 15 days  from the date of receipt of such stock.
  • Not hold sugar stock exceeding 1,000 quintals at any time and at any place across the country.
  • Considering the specific market requirements of the region, the stock holding limit has been fixed at 2,000 quintals for Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas and the State of Assam.

Kolkata sources sugar from Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka and supplies it to the eastern part of the country, including the North-Eastern region. The higher limit for Assam has been provided keeping in view geographical constraints, transportation logistics and consumer interest in the North-Eastern region.

The revised norms are aimed at ensuring that sugar is not unnecessarily accumulated in the distribution chain and that supplies move smoothly from sugar mills through dealers and ultimately reach the end consumer. The measure is particularly aimed at further curbing hoarding, discouraging speculative trading and preventing accumulation of sugar stocks by dealers. By limiting the quantity and duration for which sugar can be held, the Government seeks to facilitate an orderly movement of sugar through the supply chain and ensure its continuous availability to consumers at reasonable prices.

Retail Sugar Prices Decline by 15%

Average retail sugar prices have declined by 15 per cent from their August peak and are expected to decline further as the benefit of lower ex-mill prices passes through the supply chain. Ex-mill sugar prices have declined by approximately 28 per cent and have remained stable over the last three weeks.

The decline reflects the impact of various measures taken by the Government to ensure adequate availability of sugar and facilitate its orderly movement through the market.

The Government has reiterated that sugar mills, dealers, wholesalers and other market participants are expected to ensure continuous movement of sugar through the supply chain and prevent artificial accumulation or speculative hoarding. Wholesalers and retailers have also been urged to immediately pass on the benefit of the substantial decline in ex-mill sugar prices to consumers.

Sugar mills have already been advised to commence crushing operations in accordance with the agro-climatic conditions prevailing in their respective regions. The Union Government will continue to monitor the impact of uneven and deficient rainfall associated with El Niño conditions on sugarcane in certain sugar-producing regions and take all necessary and timely measures to maintain a balance between domestic availability, consumer interest and the interests of sugarcane farmers.

Concerned State Governments have also been advised to take suitable action regarding crushing operations based on prevailing field conditions.

The Government reiterates that sugarcane farmers and consumers are the two central pillars of India’s sugar policy. While the Government remains committed to ensuring remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers, it is equally committed to protecting consumers from unreasonable increases in sugar prices and ensuring adequate availability of sugar across the country.

***

IA/ RP

item.title: Special Gram Sabhas across India to Mark 2nd October with Discussions on Transformative Governance Reforms ; Launch People’s Plan Campaign 2026-27 ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’
item.description: Special Gram Sabhas across the country will assemble on 2nd October 2026 to discuss transformative governance reforms and initiatives that are strengthening Panchayats, improving public services and enhancing the quality of life in rural India. These special Gram Sabhas will also mark the launch of the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC) 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, under which Gram Panchayats will prepare their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) for Financial Year 2027-28 through…
item.content:encoded:
Special Gram Sabhas across the country will assemble on 2nd October 2026 to discuss transformative governance reforms and initiatives that are strengthening Panchayats, improving public services and enhancing the quality of life in rural India. These special Gram Sabhas will also mark the launch of the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC) 2026-27, “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, under which Gram Panchayats will prepare their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) for Financial Year 2027-28 through participatory and evidence-based planning. The Gram Sabha discussions will bring together citizens and local representatives to review the benefits and implementation of key Government schemes and initiatives, identify local needs and gaps and deliberate on priorities for the development of their villages.

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in collaboration with participating Ministries and Departments, Government of India is facilitating these discussions as part of a Whole-of-Government approach to grassroots development. The following schemes and initiatives will be highlighted during the Special Gram Sabhas:

  • Ministry of Panchayati Raj: Strengthening Panchayats through Finance Commission grants, capacity building under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, digital governance through eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, Own Source Revenue (OSR) initiatives, SVAMITVA and the Panchayat Advancement Index.
  • Department of Rural Development: The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), providing a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment, along with the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan for locally determined works and livelihoods.
  • Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation: Jal Jeevan Mission for rural household tap water connections and Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) for sanitation, ODF Plus and solid and liquid waste management.
  • Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation: Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain and revised watershed development norms to strengthen groundwater recharge, water conservation and water security.
  • Department of Food and Public Distribution: One Nation One Ration Card for portability of foodgrain entitlements and Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana for continued food security.
  • Department of Consumer Affairs: National Consumer Helpline and e-Jagriti to strengthen consumer awareness, grievance redressal and access to consumer justice.
  • Department of Land Resources: The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) for digitised and accessible land records, supporting secure property rights and easier access to credit and watershed development under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.

The People’s Plan Campaign has been implemented across States and Union Territories since 2018, enabling Panchayats to prepare holistic, inclusive and participatory development plans. More than 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats prepare and upload their plans on eGramSwaraj. The Panchayat Advancement Index enables Panchayats to identify achievements and gaps across key areas of local development, providing a basis for the Gram Sabha to identify priorities and take a Sankalp for the year ahead. The Gram Sabha provides citizens with a direct platform to share their experiences, feedback and suggestions on these schemes and initiatives, and to help determine local priorities. Discussions will also promote awareness of the new criminal laws, namely the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, digital transformation and strengthening of cooperatives, and initiatives for the protection and dignity of women and children, including Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. As Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 culminates, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 will also be discussed in the Gram Sabhas on 2nd October.

Citizens are earnestly invited to participate in their Special Gram Sabhas on 2nd October 2026 and contribute to the preparation of Panchayat Development Plans that reflect local needs and aspirations. Through “Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas”, Gram Sabhas will reinforce participatory governance and contribute to building Sashakt Panchayats, Atmanirbhar Panchayats and Viksit Panchayats in the larger endeavour of Viksit Bharat.

***

AA

item.title: Hindi Fortnight-2026 Concluded at the Regional Office of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Haryana
item.description: The conclusion of the Hindi Fortnight, which was ongoing since September 14 at the Regional Office of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Ministry of Labour and Employment, was marked by a prize distribution ceremony honoring the winners of various competitions held during the fortnight. Officers and employees actively participated in this grand event, during which the appeal made by the Director General, ESIC, urging all official work to be transacted in Hindi, was read out to the…
item.content:encoded:
The conclusion of the Hindi Fortnight, which was ongoing since September 14 at the Regional Office of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Ministry of Labour and Employment, was marked by a prize distribution ceremony honoring the winners of various competitions held during the fortnight. Officers and employees actively participated in this grand event, during which the appeal made by the Director General, ESIC, urging all official work to be transacted in Hindi, was read out to the gathered assembly.

Presiding over the function, Shri Hari Om Prakash, Regional Director, Haryana, stated that in Haryana, a Hindi-speaking region, it is the collective duty of all staff to execute all official work in Hindi itself. He emphasized that this approach enables the organization to reach the worker standing at the last mile who lacks awareness regarding the various benefits provided by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation.

During the ceremony, Private Secretary Ms. Meena Verma and Assistant Ms. Manisha Kalra recited spirited poems, which were greatly appreciated by the attending personnel. Under the Hindi Fortnight, competitions for Essay Writing, Noting and Drafting, Official Language Knowledge, and Elocution were organized, and the successful participants were honored with mementos and certificates.

For the valedictory event, the entire office was decorated with floral patterns (rangoli) and garlands by the female staff, filling the atmosphere of the office with beauty and fragrance.

On this occasion, the Coordination Branch was awarded the Hindi Running Shield for demonstrating the best official Hindi implementation throughout the year.
The ceremony was attended by Deputy Directors Shri Shiv Shakti Sharma, Shri Vivekanand, Shri Vivek, Smt. Poonam Bala, and Shri Brijesh Mishra, Assistant Director (Official Language), along with other officers and employees.

item.title: Ministry of Culture Gears Up for Special Campaign 6.0 launched by DARPG, with Focus on Cleanliness, E-Waste Disposal and Records Management
item.description: Ministry of Culture is actively participating in the Special Campaign 6.0 launched by DARPG, Government of India. Its Attached, Subordinate and Autonomous Organizations across the country are fully geared up to undertake the Special Drive. The Campaign started with a Preparatory Phase from 16 th to 30 th September, 2026 during which the targets for disposing and cleaning during the Campaign period have been earmarked. The implementation Phase of the campaign will start from 2 nd October,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture is actively participating in the Special Campaign 6.0 launched by DARPG, Government of India. Its Attached, Subordinate and Autonomous Organizations across the country are fully geared up to undertake the Special Drive. The Campaign started with a Preparatory Phase from 16th to 30th September, 2026 during which the targets for disposing and cleaning during the Campaign period have been earmarked. The implementation Phase of the campaign will start from 2nd October, 2026 and will continue up to 31st October, 2026. During the Campaign, special focus is being given on E-Waste disposal in Govt. Offices.

During the Preparatory Phase of the Special Campaign, Ministry along with its organizations have identified 595 sites across the country for cleanliness. Besides, Ministry has identified pending 80 MP references, 46 Parliamentary Assurances, 26 PMO references, 28 States Govt. references and 92 Public Grievances, 44 PG Appeals for disposal and redressal. Besides, 31515 physical files and 323 e-files have also been identified for review.

The activities undertaken by Ministry of Culture under the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) Campaign 2026 during September 2026, along with the upcoming activity scheduled on 02.10.2026, is furnished below:

i. Slogan-Writing Competition: A Slogan-Writing Competition on the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag” was organized for the officers and staff of the Ministry on 18.09.2026.

ii. Poster-Making Competition: A Poster-Making Competition on the theme “Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” was organized for the officers and staff of the Ministry on 22.09.2026.

iii. Nukkad Natak: A Nukkad Natak, in collaboration with National School of Drama (NSD), on themes relating to Swachhata, Heritage and Culture was organized on 23.09.2026 at the common lawn of Kartavya Bhavan-02. The programme witnessed participation of officers and staff of the various Ministries.

iv. Shramdaan Drive & Weeding out Drive: A Shramdaan Drive, in coordination with the National Archives of India (NAI), was organized on 29.09.2026 at the lawns of NAI, with active participation of officers and staff of the Ministry. Also, Inspection of Record Room in NAI was done by the Officials of Ministry to review the files as per retention schedule guidelines. Many old files were identified for weeding out.

v. “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” Shramdaan & Plantation Drive: As part of the SHS Campaign, an “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” Shramdaan & Plantation Drive, in coordination with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), will be organized on 02.10.2026 at Purana Qila, Delhi, with participation of officers and staff of the Ministry.

Further, a Training session on Records Management held on 29.09.2026 at National Archives of India

 

Daily progresses will be monitored and uploaded on the SCDPM portal hosted by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances. All Attached, Subordinate and Autonomous Organizations are enthusiastically participating in the campaign in full swing to achieve the targets set by the Ministry for the period.

***

M Annadurai

item.title: Government Committed to the Welfare and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities and Weaker Sections of Society: Sh Ramdas Athawale
item.description:
On Wednesday, Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, inaugurated the first state-level mapping programme for children with Specific Learning Disability and Autism at ITI Doon Sanskriti School, Jhajra, Dehradun. The programme was organised under the Uttarakhand State Divyang Child Campaign. Former MP Shri Tarun Vijay and MLA Shri Khajan Das were also present on the occasion.
At ITI Doon Sanskriti School, Jhajra, Dehradun, Shri Athawale interacted…
item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, inaugurated the first state-level mapping programme for children with Specific Learning Disability and Autism at ITI Doon Sanskriti School, Jhajra, Dehradun. The programme was organised under the Uttarakhand State Divyang Child Campaign. Former MP Shri Tarun Vijay and MLA Shri Khajan Das were also present on the occasion.

At ITI Doon Sanskriti School, Jhajra, Dehradun, Shri Athawale interacted with the students and reviewed the educational facilities available for children with disabilities. Around 150 students from the northeastern states and 67 students with disabilities are studying at the school, receiving education together in an inclusive academic environment. The institution is spread over approximately 13 acres of land.

Shri Athawale said that persons with disabilities may be physically challenged, but they are strong in heart and mind. Disability does not diminish a person's abilities or talent. Referring to the achievements of Indian para-athletes in the Paralympic Games, he said that persons with disabilities have won several medals, including gold medals, for the country.

Union MoS appreciated the efforts being undertaken for the education and empowerment of children with disabilities and assured all possible support from the Central Government. He also assured cooperation in seeking grants from the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to strengthen the institution. He suggested that another school could be started on the campus and additional teachers could be provided to further strengthen educational facilities.

Shri Athawale said that there are more than 2.68 crore persons with disabilities in the country and the government is committed to providing them opportunities in education, skill development, employment and social inclusion.

The Union Minister of State informed that around ₹950 crore has been allocated for various initiatives related to persons with disabilities. He emphasised the need to strengthen accessible infrastructure, education and essential support systems to enable children with disabilities to realise their full potential.

During a review meeting with officials of the Social Welfare Department of Uttarakhand, Shri Athawale also highlighted the progress of major Central welfare schemes at the national level as well as in Uttarakhand.

He said that more than 59.30 crore accounts have been opened across the country under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, including around 40.91 lakh accounts in Uttarakhand. Under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, more than 60.27 crore loans have been sanctioned across the country, while around 36.87 lakh loans have been provided to beneficiaries in Uttarakhand.

Under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, more than 10.57 crore LPG connections have been issued across the country, including around 5.05 lakh connections in Uttarakhand. Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban, around one crore houses have been constructed across the country, including approximately 43,000 houses in Uttarakhand. More than 36.87 crore LED bulbs have been distributed across the country, including around 56.73 lakh LED bulbs in Uttarakhand. As part of the government’s efforts for senior citizens, 706 old-age homes have been constructed or funded across the country, while four centres in Uttarakhand have been provided assistance.

Shri Athawale also reviewed initiatives related to de-addiction centres. He informed that 790 de-addiction centres have been established across the country. He reiterated that the government is continuously working to strengthen social security, financial inclusion and welfare services for weaker sections of society.

Shri Athawale described Uttarakhand Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami as his good friend and appreciated the development work being undertaken in the state under his leadership. He said that Uttarakhand has made notable progress under the leadership of Chief Minister Dhami.

item.title: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Seeks Surya Kiran Air Show at Lonar to Promote Maharashtra’s Tourism Potential
item.description:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, has requested Defence Minister Shri Rajnath Singh to consider organising performances by the Indian Air Force’s Surya Kiran Aerobatic Display Team at Maharashtra’s iconic tourism destinations, including Lonar Crater Lake in Buldhana district , during November 23–25, 2026.
In a letter to the Defence Minister, Shri Jadhav highlighted the…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, has requested Defence Minister Shri Rajnath Singh to consider organising performances by the Indian Air Force’s Surya Kiran Aerobatic Display Team at Maharashtra’s iconic tourism destinations, including Lonar Crater Lake in Buldhana district, during November 23–25, 2026.

In a letter to the Defence Minister, Shri Jadhav highlighted the Surya Kiran team’s reputation for precision, skill and coordinated aerial manoeuvres, noting that its performances showcase India’s aviation capabilities while inspiring public interest and encouraging young people to explore opportunities in the Indian Air Force.

Shri Jadhav particularly highlighted Lonar Crater Lake, a unique natural formation in Maharashtra’s Buldhana district that attracts visitors for its distinctive geological and environmental features. The lake is known for its saline and alkaline water and its striking crater landscape.

The Minister also drew attention to the Ajanta and Ellora Caves, globally recognised for their outstanding cultural and historical significance. Both sites are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

Shri Jadhav has requested the Defence Ministry to provide the necessary approval and issue appropriate directions to concerned authorities for organising Surya Kiran Aerobatic Display performances and associated inspirational activities at Lonar, Ajanta and Ellora on any of November 23, 24 or 25, 2026.

The proposed air show is aimed at adding a distinctive public attraction to these destinations while showcasing India’s aviation excellence and highlighting Maharashtra’s rich natural, cultural and heritage tourism potential.

***

SR/SV/SG

item.title: IIM Kashipur Concludes Hindi Month 2026 with Grand Closing Ceremony
item.description:

Winners and participants of various competitions were felicitated, and the institute’s annual Hindi magazine, ‘Jalashm’, was unveiled.
The ceremony was presided…
item.content:encoded:
The closing ceremony of ‘Hindi Month 2026’ was organised at the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Kashipur on Wednesday. The ceremony featured discussions on the contemporary role of the Hindi language and literature and marked the conclusion of various Hindi-related activities and competitions organised throughout the month. Winners and participants of various competitions were felicitated, and the institute’s annual Hindi magazine, ‘Jalashm’, was unveiled.

The ceremony was presided over by IIM Kashipur Director Prof. Neeraj Dwivedi. Prof. Shivendra Kumar Kashyap, Vice-Chancellor of Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, attended as the Chief Guest, while educationist and author Prof. Rameshwar Rai was the Guest of Honour. During the programme, Prof. Rameshwar Rai delivered a special lecture on ‘The Role of Hindi Literature and Language in Contemporary Contexts’.

During the ceremony, winners of competitions organised as part of Hindi Month were presented prizes and certificates. As per the available results, Manish Kumar Sharma secured first position in the essay writing competition. Sharad Kumar Srivastava stood first in letter writing, Saurabh Pathak in poetry writing, and Shubham Kumar in the online general knowledge competition. Participants in other categories were also felicitated for their achievements. The results of the extempore speech competition held earlier were also announced during the closing ceremony.

Chief Guest Prof. Shivendra Kumar Kashyap, in his address, linked language with an individual’s identity and emphasised the importance of the mother tongue. He said, “A person’s fundamental thoughts and dreams naturally take shape in their own language.” He drew attention to the declining use of Hindi in daily life and highlighted the need for conscious efforts to preserve the language. He also mentioned the achievements of Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, including its position in the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) rankings and initiatives related to community radio.

Guest of Honour Prof. Rameshwar Rai, in his special lecture, discussed the historical position of Indian education and languages. Referring to colonial education policies that began in 1835, he said that these policies pushed indigenous education systems and languages into the background while giving prominence to English. According to him, the impact extended beyond language to the cultural structure of society. He linked the long-term influence of the colonial system with continued cultural dependence.

Discussing the contemporary position of Hindi, Prof. Rai said that Hindi remains strong as a language of the market and entertainment, but its capacity as a language of deeper knowledge and philosophical thought is weakening. He also linked the language question with broader contemporary challenges. According to him, issues such as the uncontrolled expansion of artificial intelligence, religious conflicts and environmental degradation are not merely technological or political questions, but also involve questions of human self-awareness and connection with cultural roots. He emphasised the need for introspection and reconnecting with one’s cultural roots.

In his presidential address, Prof. Neeraj Dwivedi emphasised the practical and institutional use of Hindi. He said that modern artificial intelligence and translation technologies are continuously reducing barriers between languages, making the use of Hindi in professional work more practical than before. He advocated using Hindi with a natural sense of belonging and pride rather than adopting it merely as an obligation. On the occasion, he called upon members of the institute to increase the use of Hindi in official correspondence and day-to-day administrative work.

The annual Hindi magazine of IIM Kashipur, ‘Jalashm’, was also unveiled during the ceremony. According to the available material, Atul Kumar Srivastava contributed to suggesting the name of the magazine. The magazine was unveiled as part of the concluding activities of Hindi Month and was one of the highlights of the ceremony.

The activities organised during Hindi Month for school students and other participants provided a platform for writing, public speaking and expression in Hindi. Earlier, 27 students from 16 schools had participated in the extempore speech competition, the results of which were announced during the closing ceremony.

With the closing ceremony, the month-long activities organised under Hindi Month 2026 at IIM Kashipur formally concluded. The programme emphasised the need to use Hindi not merely as a formal language, but more effectively in daily communication, knowledge, writing and professional work.

item.title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy leads Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Cleanliness Drive; calls for collective action towards a cleaner India
item.description:
Union Minister for coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, along with Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, and senior officials of the Ministry and NDMC, participated in the cleanliness drive organised under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 at Yashwant Palace Market, Chanakyapuri, ahead of Gandhi Jayanti.
During the cleanliness drive, Shri G. Kishan Reddy interacted with sanitation workers and acknowledged their dedicated contribution towards keeping public spaces clean. He…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, along with Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, and senior officials of the Ministry and NDMC, participated in the cleanliness drive organised under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 at Yashwant Palace Market, Chanakyapuri, ahead of Gandhi Jayanti.

During the cleanliness drive, Shri G. Kishan Reddy interacted with sanitation workers and acknowledged their dedicated contribution towards keeping public spaces clean. He emphasised that cleanliness is a collective responsibility and called upon citizens to actively contribute towards maintaining clean surroundings.

The Minister called upon citizens to avoid littering and throwing garbage in drains, public spaces, roads and water bodies, and to refrain from throwing waste from buildings or other places. He stressed that maintaining cleanliness requires collective awareness and sustained public participation.

Shri G. Kishan Reddy highlighted the importance of recognising and respecting the contribution of sanitation workers, who begin their work early in the day to ensure clean surroundings for citizens. He called for greater public participation to make cleanliness an integral part of everyday life.

As part of the programme, “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” plantation was also undertaken by the Union Minister, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, and senior officials. The initiative reinforced the message of environmental responsibility and the importance of creating cleaner and greener surroundings.

The programme highlighted the spirit of Swachhata Hi Seva and the importance of collective action in keeping public spaces clean and contributing towards a cleaner and greener India.

The Union Minister expressed his appreciation to sanitation workers, officials and all stakeholders for their participation and contribution towards the Swachhata Hi Seva initiative.

***

Prajith Kumar MV

item.title: DDWS Organizes Second Follow-up Meeting to accelerate drinking water coverage in tribal areas under PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA
item.description: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, convened the second follow-up review and convergence meeting yesterday to accelerate saturation of drinking water coverage in tribal areas under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA). The meeting was chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and attended by senior officials of the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), Ministry of Tribal Affairs…
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, convened the second follow-up review and convergence meeting yesterday to accelerate saturation of drinking water coverage in tribal areas under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA). The meeting was chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and attended by senior officials of the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), State Rural Water Supply/Public Health Engineering Departments, State Tribal Welfare Departments and other concerned stakeholders.

The meeting was held as part of the follow-up process initiated after the Departmental Summit, where States and Union Territories had committed to achieving saturation of drinking water coverage in all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. Progress on these commitments was reviewed and States were advised to translate the commitments into time-bound action through closer coordination between Water Supply/PHE and Tribal Welfare Departments, ensuring that no eligible tribal village or habitation remains left out.

A dedicated provision of ₹5,000 crore under JJM 2.0 has been earmarked to address drinking water gaps in PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. In this context, the review focused on four priority areas: harmonisation of data between Tribal Welfare Departments and JJM databases, identification of uncovered villages and habitations, preparation of technically sound proposals and joint validation and certification of coverage. States and UTs were urged to complete these activities expeditiously and submit validated proposals for consideration.

Addressing the participants, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS emphasised that regular reviews of PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages should be undertaken through District Water and Sanitation Mission (DWSM) meetings chaired by the Deputy Commissioner/District Magistrate. He underscored that the DWSM should serve as the principal platform for inter-departmental coordination, validation of survey findings and identification of genuine coverage gaps requiring intervention.

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has undertaken a State-wise SurveySetu exercise, including household-level verification of Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) status. States were advised to present SurveySetu findings jointly before the DWSM through representatives of Water Supply Departments, Tribal Welfare Departments and the survey agency. Any discrepancies identified during the exercise are to be resolved through consultation and field verification, wherever required, so that a final validated database is available at the district level.

The meeting reiterated that the objective is not only to create new infrastructure but to achieve complete saturation and certification of all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. States were therefore advised to accord equal priority to certification of villages that have already achieved saturation and ensure that all eligible settlements are accurately reflected in the JJM-IMIS before submission of proposals.

States and UTs were advised to identify left-out habitations based on SurveySetu findings and validate them through the DWSM mechanism. The Rural Water Supply/PHE and Tribal Welfare Departments have been asked to jointly prepare proposals supported by self-assessed DPR Checklists duly authenticated by competent authorities. Proposals should clearly establish the justification for inclusion, avoid duplication, incorporate validated LGD codes and contain complete technical and financial details.

The Technical Division of NJJM also emphasised the need to improve the quality and completeness of DPR submissions. States were advised to ensure realistic population projections, adherence to prescribed service levels, adequate provisions for source sustainability and water security, and reasonable per-FHTC costs supported by appropriate technical justification. Particular attention was drawn towards accurate completion of DPR Checklists and proper authentication of all corrections and revisions.

Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM said that the importance of joint ownership at the State level was also reiterated. State RWS/PHE and Tribal Welfare Departments will jointly prepare and present proposals before the Joint Committee co-chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and Secretary, MoTA. At the district level, the DWSM chaired by the DC/DM will serve as the key platform for validation and decision-making, with participation of the survey agency and concerned State departments.

During the meeting, State-wise progress and observations on proposals already received were reviewed. Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Kerala and Manipur were advised to address specific observations relating to LGD code validation, DPR documentation, service levels and per-FHTC costs. Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Assam were requested to take action on observations already communicated by DDWS. Several States also shared timelines for submission of proposals, with Ladakh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh indicating that proposals covering identified PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages would be submitted during October 2026.

As part of the agreed way forward, States and UTs will establish a common validated database through harmonisation of PM-JANMAN, DA-JGUA, SurveySetu and JJM-IMIS records. Jointly validated proposals, along with duly signed DPR Checklists and requisite approvals, will be submitted for consideration by the Joint Committee co-chaired by the Secretary, DDWS and Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs. District administrations have also been advised to validate SurveySetu findings through DWSM meetings and communicate any additions or deletions identified during district-level verification to the State Government and DDWS.

The meeting reaffirmed the collective commitment of DDWS, MoTA, State Water Supply/PHE Departments, Tribal Welfare Departments and district administrations towards ensuring saturation of functional drinking water services in all eligible PM-JANMAN and DA-JGUA villages. Through data harmonisation, district-level validation, joint planning, timely submission of proposals and certification of saturation, the initiative aims to ensure that every eligible tribal village and habitation is provided with reliable and sustainable drinking water services.

***

item.description:
Shri Narendra Bhooshan, a 1992-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, has assumed charge as Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India.
Shri Bhooshan brings with him over three decades of administrative experience across the Central and State Governments, with wide exposure to energy, infrastructure, industry, agriculture, urban development, finance and land-resource management. His…
item.content:encoded:
Shri Narendra Bhooshan, a 1992-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, has assumed charge as Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India.

Shri Bhooshan brings with him over three decades of administrative experience across the Central and State Governments, with wide exposure to energy, infrastructure, industry, agriculture, urban development, finance and land-resource management. His appointment as Secretary, MoEFCC follows his tenure as Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development.

Career Background

During his career in the Uttar Pradesh cadre, Shri Bhooshan has held several senior assignments, including Additional Chief Secretary, Energy and Additional Energy Source and Technical Education. Earlier he served as Principal Secretary in the departments of PWD, Infrastructure and Industries Development, I.T. and Electronics, Science and Technology, Panchayati Raj. He has also served as Chief Executive Officer, Greater Noida Authority, besides holding other important charges. Shri Bhooshan also carries substantial field experience, having served as the District Magistrate of Mathura, Firozabad, and Udham Singh Nagar.

At the Government of India level, Shri Bhooshan has served as Deputy Director General, Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Mission Director, National Food Security Management, and Joint Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Cooperation. He has also served as Officer on Special Duty in the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

Shri Bhooshan holds a graduate degree in Electronics and a Master's degree in International Development Policy from Duke University, USA. His professional training includes programmes relating to public finance, infrastructure and climate-change preparedness.

*****

VM

item.description:
Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, will undertake a four-day visit to Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand from October 1 to 4, 2026 , during which he will attend programmes relating to senior citizen welfare, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and tribal education, besides participating in the Uttarakhand Aadi Rangotsav.
On October 1 , the Union Minister will travel to Meerut, Uttar Pradesh , where he will attend a programme organised by the Senior Citizen Welfare Association at…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, will undertake a four-day visit to Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand from October 1 to 4, 2026, during which he will attend programmes relating to senior citizen welfare, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and tribal education, besides participating in the Uttarakhand Aadi Rangotsav.

On October 1, the Union Minister will travel to Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, where he will attend a programme organised by the Senior Citizen Welfare Association at Pallavapuram. He will thereafter proceed to Ramnagar in Uttarakhand, where he will stay overnight.

On October 2, Shri Oram will attend a Swachh Bharat Abhiyan programme at Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS), Bazpur, in Uttarakhand. He will subsequently return to Ramnagar for an overnight stay.

On October 3, the Union Minister will visit Kainchidham, including a darshan at the Kainchidham Temple. He will thereafter proceed to Khatima, where he will visit Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS), Khatima. The Minister will later travel to Rudrapur for an overnight stay.

On October 4, Shri Jual Oram will attend the Uttarakhand Aadi Rangotsav at Khatima. He will return to New Delhi later in the evening.

The visit will provide an opportunity for interaction with local stakeholders and officials on matters concerning tribal education and welfare, particularly through the network of Eklavya Model Residential Schools, as well as participation in programmes aimed at social welfare and community engagement.

item.title: CISF Strikes Coal Smuggling Network at Vedkaro, Seizes 207.17 Tonnes of Coal
item.description: CISF has conducted a major operation against illegal coal storage and transportation near Charakpania village, close to Vedkaro Mines in CCL's B&K Area. Acting on secret information, a joint CISF-CCL team launched the operation under the leadership and supervision of Commandant R.P. Singh, in the presence of Deputy Commandant Gara Abhilash and Assistant Commandants K.V. Sridhar and D.K. Pandey. The suspected area was first identified through drone surveillance. The CISF raid team, Quick…
item.content:encoded:
CISF has conducted a major operation against illegal coal storage and transportation near Charakpania village, close to Vedkaro Mines in CCL's B&K Area. Acting on secret information, a joint CISF-CCL team launched the operation under the leadership and supervision of Commandant R.P. Singh, in the presence of Deputy Commandant Gara Abhilash and Assistant Commandants K.V. Sridhar and D.K. Pandey.
The suspected area was first identified through drone surveillance. The CISF raid team, Quick Response Team (QRT) and sniffer dogs then carried out a thorough search of the site. The team engaged local women and villagers with tact and dialogue, and the operation concluded peacefully, without any dispute. The search led to the seizure of 207.17 tonnes of Grade-4 coal and 4 motorcycles.

Preliminary investigation indicates the following modus operandi:

  • Coal was lifted by hand from various mining areas.
  • It was stockpiled temporarily at isolated spots, away from active mining and operational areas.
  • Motorcycles were used to move it onward, for loading into large commercial vehicles such as trucks and tipper trucks for dispatch elsewhere.

CISF is taking sustained action against illegal mining, storage and transportation under the Zero Coal Leakage campaign and the provisions of the MMDR Act, 1957.

item.title: FIEO to organise One-Day Program on Customs Schemes for Exporters in Hyderabad
item.description:
Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) is organising a one-day program on “Customs Schemes for Exporters: Benefits, Procedures and Compliances” on 9th October 2026 (Friday) at Hyderabad in association with ICICI Bank.
The program is aimed at creating awareness among exporters, manufacturers, MSMEs and trade stakeholders about key Customs schemes and facilitation measures available for international trade, with particular emphasis on benefits, eligibility, procedures,…
item.content:encoded:
Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) is organising a one-day program on “Customs Schemes for Exporters: Benefits, Procedures and Compliances” on 9th October 2026 (Friday) at Hyderabad in association with ICICI Bank.

The program is aimed at creating awareness among exporters, manufacturers, MSMEs and trade stakeholders about key Customs schemes and facilitation measures available for international trade, with particular emphasis on benefits, eligibility, procedures, documentation and compliance requirements.

The program will cover a range of important topics, including:

  • Overview of Customs Facilitation for Exporters, including the role of Customs in export promotion, ICEGATE and electronic Customs procedures, Risk Management System and faceless assessment.
  • Duty-Free Import Schemes, including Advance Authorisation, Duty Free Import Authorisation (DFIA), eligibility, conditions, application and documentation.
  • Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme, including import of capital goods at concessional/zero Customs duty, export obligations, procedures and compliance.
  • Special Customs Procedures and Facilitation, including bonded manufacturing/warehousing, exports under bond/LUT and Customs warehousing provisions.
  • Eligible Manufacturer Scheme and AEO/Customs Facilitation, covering eligibility, benefits to compliant manufacturers/exporters and procedural requirements.
  • Customs Compliance for Exporters, including Shipping Bill and supporting documents, classification and valuation, country-of-origin requirements, record keeping, audit, common errors and penalties.
  • Digital Customs and ICEGATE Services, along with interactive Q&A and case studies.

Senior officials from the Customs Commissionerate, Hyderabad will make detailed presentations on the above topics and interact with participants to address practical issues relating to Customs procedures and compliance.  Officials from Bank will also participate and address on financial opportunities.

The program is intended to provide participants with practical insights into Customs schemes and facilitate better understanding of the procedures and documentation required to effectively utilise the available facilities, said Mr. Unnikrishnan K., Joint Director General, FIEO.

For participation and other details, please contact: Mr. R. Kulkarni, Head - Telangana Chapter on 9848286640, email: kulkarni@fieo.org


About FIEO

Federation of Indian Export Organisations popularly known as 'FIEO' was set up by Ministry of Commerce, Govt of India in 1965.  FIEO is the apex body of the Government recognised Export Promotion Councils, Commodity Boards and Development Authorities in India. FIEO provides a wide range of services to exporters, including market research, trade information, export promotion activities, organizing overseas trade fairs and exhibitions, training programs, and policy advocacy.
