item.content:encoded:
On the occasion of Swachhata Hi Seva, the Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department organized a workshop on “Best out of Waste – Turning Waste into Wonder: Kabad Se Jugad” on 29th September, 2026 at the Conference Hall, Kartavya Bhawan-2.

The workshop was conducted with experts from India Aids (NGO) and N.K. Bagrodia Public School, Dwarka, Sector-4. The experts included Smt. Archana Srivastava, General Secretary, India Aids (NGO); Ms. Anjali Kharbanda, Principal, N.K. Bagrodia Public School; Ms. Baisakhi Bhattacharjee, TGT (Science) & School Social Responsibility Coordinator; Ms. Sweta Tulsyan, PGT (Geography) & Health and Wellness Coordinator, NKBPS; Ms. Vidushi Sinha, Alumni – NKBPS & Volunteer, India Aids (NGO); and Aryan Gupta, Alumni – NKBPS & Volunteer, India Aids (NGO).

The workshop was chaired by Shri G. Panmei, Joint Secretary & Legislative Counsel (JS&LC), along with other senior officers and staff members of the Department. The workshop witnessed enthusiastic participation from the officers and staff of the Department, including its attached offices, i.e., the Official Language Wing and Vidhi Sahitya Prakashan.

During the workshop, the experts explained and demonstrated various creative and practical ways of transforming waste and discarded materials into useful and innovative products. They shared simple and effective ideas for giving a new purpose to materials that are otherwise considered waste. As part of the hands-on demonstration, the experts and volunteers prepared sample articles from waste materials under the theme “Kabad Se Jugad”, showcasing how creativity, innovation, and resourcefulness can convert discarded items into useful and attractive articles. The demonstration also highlighted the importance of reusing available materials and adopting environmentally responsible practices.

The workshop concluded with a message to encourage responsible waste management, recycling, and sustainable living. The initiative reinforced the idea that, with creativity and collective effort, waste can be transformed into useful and meaningful products, thereby contributing to a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable environment.

Shri Panmei, JS&LC, emphasized the importance of adopting innovative and sustainable practices in day-to-day life and encouraged the participants to explore creative ways of making optimum use of waste materials. He appreciated the enthusiasm and involvement of the participants and highlighted that small and consistent efforts towards reuse, recycling, and responsible waste management can make a meaningful contribution towards a cleaner and greener environment.

 

 

***

Samrat/Sagar

item.title: District Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan as part of Shram Samvad Initiative
item.description: The Ministry of Labour & Employment, in collaboration with FICCI and the Bhiwadi Manufacturers Association, organised the “Shram Samvad” District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes at BMA House, Industrial Area, Bhiwadi, Rajasthan today. The programme aimed to build awareness among employers and industry stakeholders about the Labour Codes, which came into force on 21 st November 2025, and the Central Rules, notified on 08 th May 2026, while highlighting the key…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Labour & Employment, in collaboration with FICCI and the Bhiwadi Manufacturers Association, organised the “Shram Samvad” District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes at BMA House, Industrial Area, Bhiwadi, Rajasthan today. The programme aimed to build awareness among employers and industry stakeholders about the Labour Codes, which came into force on 21st November 2025, and the Central Rules, notified on 08th May 2026, while highlighting the key provisions and compliance requirements under the new framework. The programme brought together more than 100 participants from diverse sectors, including employers, industry representatives, HR professionals, legal experts, finance specialists, and other key stakeholders in the labour and employment ecosystem.

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the Government of India.

The inaugural address was delivered by Shri Yogesh Jain, General Secretary, Bhiwadi Manufacturers Association (BMA). This was followed by a keynote address by Shri Ashutosh A.T. Pednekar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, who highlighted the key provisions of the Labour Codes and the Ministry’s vision for organising the ‘District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes’ across the country.

The first technical session was conducted by Shri Om Prakash Singh, Labour Welfare Commissioner (Central), who presented a comprehensive overview of the Labour Codes, their objectives, and the major reforms introduced through the new legislative framework. The session helped participants understand the broader vision and significance of labour law reforms for both employers and workers.

The second session, conducted jointly by Shri Nitesh Bhasin, Under Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, and Shri Om Prakash Singh, Labour Welfare Commissioner (Central), focused on the key compliance requirements for employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new framework.

A Q&A session was conducted as part of the event, that encouraged active participation and engagement from attendees. Participants shared their perspectives, highlighted field-level challenges, and raised queries relating to labour welfare, employer obligations, and social security provisions, setting the stage for the subsequent technical sessions and deliberations.

The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was led by Shri Bhupendra Yadav, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). Participants were briefed on the scheme’s objectives, eligibility conditions, and benefits aimed at promoting employment generation.

The fourth session covered the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Shri Pravin P. Mohandas, Welfare Commissioner (Central), Ajmer. The session highlighted the scheme’s key features and its role in extending pension and social security benefits to workers in the unorganised sector.

The programme concluded with a second interactive question-and-answer session, during which participants engaged directly with the speakers and sought clarifications on various aspects of the Labour Codes, employer compliance, and social security schemes.

The vote of thanks was delivered by Shri Surendra Singh Chauhan, Member, FICCI Rajasthan State Council, and Past President, BMA. He urged the authorities to continue supporting initiatives that would further strengthen Bhiwadi’s position as one of the country's leading industrial hubs.

The event served as a key platform for capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and awareness generation, fostering a deeper understanding of the Labour Codes and supporting their effective implementation through informed participation by employers and industry stakeholders.

*****

Rini Choudhury/Anjelina Alexander

item.description: Union Minister for Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, will participate in the “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” collective voluntary Shramdaan being organised by the Ministry of Mines under the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign at Yashwant Place, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, on October 1, 2026. During the programme, the Union Minister will join officers, employees and sanitation workers in cleanliness activities and interact with the personnel engaged in maintaining the public space. The…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, will participate in the “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” collective voluntary Shramdaan being organised by the Ministry of Mines under the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign at Yashwant Place, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, on October 1, 2026. During the programme, the Union Minister will join officers, employees and sanitation workers in cleanliness activities and interact with the personnel engaged in maintaining the public space. The one-hour collective Shramdaan will bring together participants in a shared effort towards cleanliness and upkeep of the surrounding areas, reinforcing the spirit of Jan Bhagidari, dignity of work and collective responsibility for a cleaner and greener environment.

As part of the Ministry’s wider Swachhata Hi Seva initiatives, the Ministry of Mines has adopted a park at GPOA-3, Netaji Nagar, New Delhi, for planned landscaping, beautification and improvement of the surrounding area. The initiative will focus on developing the identified space into a cleaner, greener and well-maintained public area, while promoting sustainable practices and greater ownership of shared spaces.

The Union Minister will also inaugurate an E-Waste Collection Stall at GPOA-3, marking another important initiative under SHS 2026. The stall will facilitate the collection of discarded electronic and electrical items and encourage officials and employees to adopt responsible practices for disposal of e-waste. The initiative will also create awareness about the importance of segregation, collection and authorised recycling of e-waste.

The E-Waste Collection Drive will be conducted for one month from October 2 to October 31, 2026. During this period, officials and employees will be encouraged to bring their discarded electronic items to the designated collection point. The collected e-waste will be channelised for appropriate recycling and scientific processing through authorised mechanisms.

A key focus of the initiative will be to highlight the resource value of e-waste, particularly its potential for recovery of critical minerals and other valuable materials. Electronic and electrical products contain a range of materials that can be recovered through appropriate recycling and processing. Their recovery can contribute to resource efficiency, reduce dependence on virgin materials and support the principles of a circular economy.

The initiative is in line with the Ministry of Mines’ broader efforts to promote responsible resource utilisation, circular economy practices and recovery of critical minerals from secondary sources. By linking cleanliness with responsible e-waste management and resource recovery, the campaign will encourage sustainable practices in everyday life.

The Ministry of Mines continues to undertake various activities under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, with emphasis on cleanliness, sanitation, waste management, environmental sustainability and citizen participation. The initiatives at Yashwant Place and GPOA-3 will reinforce the Ministry’s commitment to making Swachhata a sustained collective effort and promoting a cleaner, greener and more resource-efficient future.

***

Prajith Kumar MV

item.title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Reviews Preparedness for Special Campaign 6.0
item.description:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today reviewed the preparedness and implementation timeline of Special Campaign 6.0 with the Science Ministries and Departments.
The Science Ministries and Departments have set a target of 1,500 cleanliness campaign sites under Special Campaign 6.0. The Ministry of Earth…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today reviewed the preparedness and implementation timeline of Special Campaign 6.0 with the Science Ministries and Departments.

The Science Ministries and Departments have set a target of 1,500 cleanliness campaign sites under Special Campaign 6.0. The Ministry of Earth Sciences has kept a target of 100 cleanliness campaign sites. The campaign will focus on visible cleanliness outcomes, optimum utilisation of available space, systematic disposal of obsolete material and better utilisation of Government resources.

A key thrust of the campaign will be effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste. The review also covered the scope for leveraging scientific and technological capabilities for recycling electronic waste and creating value from discarded equipment, going beyond conventional disposal. The campaign framework provides for systematic identification and item-wise reporting of e-waste and its disposal through appropriate channels, including producers, recyclers and refurbishers.

The campaign will also demonstrate the importance of actual disposal of identified obsolete electronic equipment, disposal of the same as part of the exercise. The focus is on ensuring that identified e-waste moves through the appropriate disposal and recycling chain rather than remaining accumulated in offices.

Special Campaign 6.0 will be implemented from October 2 to October 31, 2026, following the preparatory phase undertaken during September. DARPG is coordinating the campaign across Ministries and Departments through a common digital platform, with targets and progress being updated and monitored on the campaign portal.

The Minister stressed the importance of maintaining the momentum through the campaign period, adhering to the prescribed timelines and ensuring that the exercise translates into visible and measurable outcomes.

Dr. Jitendra Singh will participate in a cleanliness drive on October 2, marking the commencement of the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6.0. The drive will focus on cleanliness, segregation and scientific disposal of e-waste, shredding of old files, optimum utilisation of office space, better record management, and reduction of pendency across Government offices.

During the review, Dr. Jitendra Singh evaluated the budgetary expenditure and noted that DSIR and MoES had achieved around 50 per cent expenditure by September 30, in line with the prescribed target. The Minister appreciated both organisations for achieving the 50 per cent target and reviewed the quarter-wise trajectory of expenditure and implementation to ensure steady progress in line with the campaign timeline.

The review meeting was attended by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology (DST); Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, CSIR; Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT); and Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), besides senior officers and nodal officers of the concerned Ministries and Departments.

*****

NKR/AK

item.title: India’s emerging quantum ecosystem strengthened by enabling policy of the Modi government: Dr Jitendra Singh
item.description: India’s emerging quantum ecosystem is being strengthened by an enabling policy of the Modi government that is opening greater space for industry and the private sector to participate in frontier technologies, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said today. He said India had the scientific talent, technological capability and industry readiness, but the enabling environment provided by policymakers is now giving…
item.content:encoded:
India’s emerging quantum ecosystem is being strengthened by an enabling policy of the Modi government that is opening greater space for industry and the private sector to participate in frontier technologies, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said today. He said India had the scientific talent, technological capability and industry readiness, but the enabling environment provided by policymakers is now giving stakeholders the confidence to build and scale in quantum technologies.

Addressing PRAGATI Q-FOUNDRY 2026 – NQM Co-development and Venture Partnership Meet at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the National Quantum Mission represents a new approach in which the Government, scientific institutions, startups, industry, investors, States and strategic users are working together to build indigenous capabilities. He said India would not remain a consumer of quantum technologies developed elsewhere and is building capabilities, infrastructure, talent and enterprises to develop these technologies at home and take them to the world.

The Minister highlighted the speed of progress under the National Quantum Mission, noting that the Mission was planned for eight years, but India has already achieved 1,000-km quantum secure communication in about three years, against the 2,000-km target envisaged for the eight-year period. He said achieving half of the target in less than half the planned timeframe demonstrates the capability that has been built within the quantum ecosystem and provides confidence to move ahead with greater speed and resolve.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the National Quantum Mission has been structured as a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation effort, with four thematic hubs at IISc Bengaluru, IIT Madras, IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi, bringing together 152 researchers from 43 institutions across 17 States and two Union Territories. The hubs are working across quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing and metrology, and quantum materials and devices.

He said the progress achieved in the last two to three years shows that India now has an opportunity to become globally competitive in quantum communication and quantum sensing and self-reliant in quantum computing. The Minister said the technologies emerging from the hubs, academic institutions and startups are already providing a strong foundation for this ambition.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government’s support to startups is not limited to funding, but extends to infrastructure, mentorship, technology validation, industry partnerships and pathways to customers. He stressed that quantum startups require sustained engagement from industry and investors, including capital, technical validation, co-development, procurement and market access. He also called upon States to evaluate indigenous technologies developed by startups and explore their deployment and procurement so that promising ventures can become sustainable.

The Minister said early industry linkage is particularly important for the sustainability of quantum startups, as quantum technologies require substantial capital and long-term commitment. He said PRAGATI Q-FOUNDRY and the B2B interactions associated with it are intended to facilitate concrete outcomes such as technology validation, procurement, co-development, investment and partnerships rather than merely showcasing technologies.

The National Quantum Mission has already supported 17 startups, and nine additional startups were announced at the event, taking the total to 26. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the expansion reflects the Government’s continuing commitment to nurture quantum entrepreneurs and provide promising Indian ventures access to funding, infrastructure, mentorship and pathways to customers.

The event also witnessed the launch of flagship quantum technologies and products, exchange of MoUs and announcement of startups by Dr. Jitendra Singh. These initiatives mark the next phase of implementation under the National Quantum Mission, with the focus shifting towards testing, validation, integration, investment and deployment of indigenous technologies.

As part of the technology outcomes showcased under the Mission, one of the Technical Groups under the Quantum Communication Hub at IIT Madras successfully demonstrated a hybrid PQC-QKD link over 17 secure nodes between Chennai and Bengaluru using existing BSNL fibre. The 50ps daisy-chain timing synchronisation has also been released as an open-source solution for the research community.

The event was attended by Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member, NITI Aayog; Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India; Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology; Dr. J. B. V. Reddy, Mission Director, National Quantum Mission, along with senior scientists, entrepreneurs, investors, industry representatives and other stakeholders.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also interacted with founders of quantum startups in a roundtable discussion, taking stock of their technological progress, challenges and requirements for scaling. The interaction focused on strengthening linkages between startups, investors, industry and potential users so that promising indigenous technologies can move towards validation, adoption and deployment.

The Minister said indigenous capability in quantum processors, secure communication systems, advanced sensors, materials and devices is important for India’s technological self-reliance, particularly in critical and strategic domains. He said India must build domestic capability across the value chain while remaining globally connected and developing technologies that are internationally competitive.

Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member, NITI Aayog, said the progress under the National Quantum Mission demonstrates the importance of bringing together government, academia, startups and industry to build a strong quantum ecosystem. He said the Mission is creating the foundations for indigenous technology development and greater participation of the private sector in this emerging field.

Principal Scientific Adviser Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood said the quantum ecosystem is demonstrating that the traditional linear model of taking 10–15 years to move from fundamental science to technology is changing. He said around 52 technologies at various Technology Readiness Levels have emerged from the four thematic hubs, along with 17 financially supported startups. He stressed that deployment and procurement of indigenous technologies will be critical for making startups sustainable and creating internationally competitive products.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the success of PRAGATI Q-FOUNDRY should ultimately be measured by the technologies advanced, partnerships created, investments mobilised, startups strengthened and indigenous solutions taken into use. He called upon all stakeholders to move forward with clear commitments, timelines and responsibilities, and said the National Quantum Mission has laid the foundation for India to build globally relevant quantum technologies and national capability.

*****

NKR/AK/FT

item.title: India Showcases Justice Reforms and Global Legal Partnerships at 15th UN Congress in Abu Dhabi
item.description:
Union Minister of State (I/C) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal held meeting with UAE Minister of Justice, Mr. Abdullah Sultan bin Awad Al Nuaimi, during the 15th UN Congress highlights India’s tech-driven justice system, new criminal laws and global legal cooperation.
India showcased its efforts to build a modern, citizen-focused, tech-enabled and globally connected justice system at the 15th United Nations Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in Abu Dhabi,…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of State (I/C) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal held meeting with UAE Minister of Justice, Mr. Abdullah Sultan bin Awad Al Nuaimi, during the 15th UN Congress highlights India’s tech-driven justice system, new criminal laws and global legal cooperation.

India showcased its efforts to build a modern, citizen-focused, tech-enabled and globally connected justice system at the 15th United Nations Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in Abu Dhabi, being held under the theme, “Accelerating crime prevention, criminal justice and the rule of law: Protecting people and planet and achieving the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development in the digital age.”

Addressing the UN Congress, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal highlighted India’s new criminal laws—the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam—and their focus on technology, faster justice, forensic investigation and digital-first procedures. He also highlighted India’s digital response to cybercrime through the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, enabling faster reporting, fraud prevention and freezing of mule accounts.

Shri Meghwal reiterated India’s zero-tolerance stance against terrorism and stressed the need for global cooperation against terrorism, drug trafficking, transnational wildlife crime, illegal logging, toxic waste dumping and other organised and environmental offences.

It was also highlighted the growing India-UAE legal partnership, particularly in international arbitration and alternative dispute resolution. The partnership between India International Arbitration Centre(IIAC) and Dubai International Arbitration Centre(DIAC) is strengthening knowledge exchange, professional training, joint programmes, research and digital dispute-resolution mechanisms. DIAC handles nearly 5,000 cases worth over AED 80 billion (around USD 21.8 billion).

During his visit, Shri Meghwal also met Ms. Monika Juma, Executive Director, UNODC, to discuss cooperation against drugs and organised crime and stronger legal and judicial partnerships.

These developments reflect the deepening India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which now spans trade, investment, energy, technology, defence, education and people-to-people relations, alongside cooperation in law, justice and good governance.

India’s participation in the 15th UN Congress underlines its commitment to modern laws, digital innovation, strong institutions, effective enforcement and meaningful international cooperation—building a justice architecture equipped for a fast-changing digital world.

Effective justice today needs more than laws. It needs technology, skilled institutions, global teamwork and an unwavering commitment to fairness.

***

Samrat/Sagar

item.title: New Discovery Track for Startups and MSMEs with Financial Assistance upto ₹50 cr under PRIP Scheme announced
item.description:
In order to encourage discovery, development and commercialisation of new medicines and to support Start-ups and MSMEs, the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has announced a New Discovery track under the Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) Scheme for undertaking Pharma Innovation projects. The objective is to encourage and enable start-ups and MSMEs to venture in to high-risk innovation ecosystem for discovery of new drugs and therapies.
This new track…
item.content:encoded:
In order to encourage discovery, development and commercialisation of new medicines and to support Start-ups and MSMEs, the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has announced a New Discovery track under the Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) Scheme for undertaking Pharma Innovation projects. The objective is to encourage and enable start-ups and MSMEs to venture in to high-risk innovation ecosystem for discovery of new drugs and therapies.

This new track seeks to address a critical funding gap in early-stage novel drug discovery. Financial assistance of upto ₹50 crore per company/project/portfolio of projects will be provided, subject to a minimum co-funding of 25% of the project cost(s) from bona fide institutional investors.

This will act as large-scale risk capital to startups/ MSMEs and catalyse participation of institutional investors at an earlier stage of drug development, enabling more indigenous New Chemical Entities and New Biological Entities assets to progress from discovery towards clinical development and help build a globally competitive drug innovation pipeline.

Start-ups and MSMEs undertaking NCE/NBE projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 1, 2 or 3 are eligible to apply under this new exclusive track. The Department would support such projects to progress to higher TRLs not beyond TRL 6. The online PRIP portal is now open for submission of applications under the second call of the scheme. With a financial outlay of ₹5,000 crore, the Scheme aims to strengthen India’s pharmaceutical and MedTech research and development ecosystem by supporting startups, MSMEs and large companies to move up the innovation value chain.

Second Call Invites Applications Across the following three Priority Areas:

  1. New Medicines - including New Chemical Entities (NCEs), New Biological Entities (NBEs) and phytopharmaceutical drugs
  2. Complex Generics and Biosimilars
  3. Novel Medical Devices

Apart from the New Discovery track, applications are invited under the following two tracks:

Early Stage: Startups and MSMEs undertaking projects at TRL 1, 2 or 3, with the objective of progressing them to higher TRLs not beyond TRL 5, will be eligible. Financial assistance of up to ₹5 crore per project will be provided. Where the approved total project cost is up to ₹1 crore, no co-funding from the applicant will be required. Where the project cost exceeds ₹1 crore, half of the project cost exceeding ₹1 crore will be co-funded by the applicant.

Later Stage: Industry, startups and MSMEs undertaking projects at TRL 4, 5 or 6 to higher TRLs will be eligible. Financial assistance of up to ₹100 crore per project will be provided, subject to a maximum of 35% of the approved total project cost, with the remaining amount to be co-funded by the applicant.

Application forms and supporting guidance are available on the PRIP Portal: PRIP Portal. 

Applicants can refer to the Scheme and Scheme Guidelines, Guidance for Concept Note, Guidance for Application Form, Milestone Descriptor Catalogue, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and the Application Support Toolkit for further details.

Under the first call of the PRIP Scheme, 41 projects have been approved for around ₹1,600 crore in financial assistance. Evaluation of the remaining applications under the first round is underway, with further results to be announced over the coming month.

Applicants who had submitted projects under PRIP Round 1 have been advised not to resubmit the same project. For queries and additional guidance, applicants may write to support-prip@pharma-dept.gov.in.

*****

PC/PM

item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Labour & Employment, in collaboration with the Labour Department, Government of Maharashtra, organised a “Shram Samvad” – District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) today. The programme was organised with the objective of creating greater awareness among employers and industry stakeholders regarding the four Labour Codes, which came into force with effect from 21 November 2025, and the Central Rules notified on 8 May 2026. The programme focused on key provisions of the new labour law framework, compliance requirements, and various social security initiatives of the Government.

Around 200 participants representing diverse sectors participated in the programme, including employers, industry representatives, HR professionals, legal experts, finance professionals and other stakeholders associated with the labour and employment ecosystem.

The programme comprised a series of technical sessions aimed at providing participants with a practical understanding of the Labour Codes, employer obligations, statutory compliance requirements and key social security schemes.

The welcome address of the inaugural session was addressed by Mr. Narendra Kulkarni, Chairman, CII Marathwada Zone along with the Keynote address and Program Overview addressed by Shri Chaman Lal Guleria, Director, Ministry of Labour & Employment. The speakers highlighted the importance of awareness, preparedness and compliance among stakeholders for effective implementation of the new labour law framework.

The first technical session was conducted by Shri Krishna Kumar, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner -II, PMU, and Shri Jiv Nath Jha, Assistant Director, ESIC PMU. The session focused on the key compliance requirements for employers under the Labour Codes and provided a comprehensive overview of the four Codes, their objectives and the major reforms introduced through the new legislative framework. The participants were apprised of the broader vision underlying the labour law reforms and their significance for both employers and workers. The session also provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, with emphasis on the operational aspects of the new framework.

The second technical session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was conducted by Shri Ankur Sharma, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). The participants were briefed on the objectives, eligibility criteria and benefits of the scheme, which seeks to promote employment generation and encourage formal employment.

The third technical session covered the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Mr Vishal Amte, Deputy Labour Welfare Commissioner, (Central) Directorate General Labour Welfare. The session highlighted the salient features of the scheme and its role in providing pension and social security coverage to eligible workers in the unorganised sector.

The programme concluded with an interactive Question and Answer session, providing participants an opportunity to directly interact with the speakers and seek clarifications on various aspects of the Labour Codes, statutory compliance requirements and social security schemes.

The “Shram Samvad” programme served as an important platform for capacity building, awareness generation and stakeholder engagement, enabling employers and industry representatives to develop a better understanding of the new labour law framework and associated compliance requirements. Such outreach initiatives are aimed at facilitating informed participation of stakeholders and supporting the effective implementation of the Labour Codes.

item.description:
The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE), along with its CPSUs and Autonomous Institutes, has successfully completed the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 , launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG) for institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in Government offices. item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE), along with its CPSUs and Autonomous Institutes, has successfully completed the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6, launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG) for institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in Government offices. The Preparatory Phase was carried out from 15th September to 30th September, 2026.

During this period, the following activities were undertaken:

i. Identification and disposal of pendency under various parameters.

ii. Review, categorisation and weeding out of physical records as per extant guidelines.

iii. Conduct of cleanliness campaigns for maintaining cleanliness in the Ministry and its PSUs and Autonomous Institutes.

iv. Identification and segregation of e-waste as per MoEFCC guidelines for target setting during the Implementation Phase.

The Ministry, its two CPSUs — Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd. (IREDA) and Solar Energy Corporation of India Ltd. (SECI) — and its three Autonomous Institutes — National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) and Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy (SSS-NIBE) — actively participated in the preparatory phase.

With the successful completion of this phase, the Ministry is now fully geared up for the Implementation Phase of the Campaign, which will commence from 2nd October, 2026 and continue up to 31st October, 2026. During this period, sustained efforts will be made to achieve all identified targets and further strengthen the culture of cleanliness and efficiency in Government functioning.

Radhakrishnan today interacted with probationers of the Indian Defence Estates Service (2025 Batch) at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, and called upon them to make the best use of the opportunity to serve the nation, with dedication, integrity and a strong sense of public responsibility.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan interacted with Indian Defence Estates Service probationers (2025 Batch) at Uprashtrapati Bhavan today. He urged them to serve with integrity, firmness and a strong sense of responsibility while safeguarding defence assets and advancing… pic.twitter.com/pE8pfrdZLp

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 30, 2026

The Vice-President noted that many of them come from smaller towns, demonstrating that dedication and hard work can overcome perceived barriers. He urged them to take pride in their achievement while remaining conscious of the responsibility entrusted to them as public servants.

Highlighting the vital mandate of the Defence Estates Organisation to manage  nearly 18 lakh acres of defence land across the country, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that this responsibility involves safeguarding national assets, providing civic amenities, facilitating defence infrastructure and supporting the operational readiness of the Armed Forces.

The Vice-President appreciated the Organisation’s steps towards digital governance, particularly the e-Chhawani initiative, which has strengthened smart governance and integrated public service delivery in cantonments. He said that emerging technologies, including AI, GIS, drone surveys, satellite imagery, automated change detection and 3-D visualisation, can significantly enhance the accuracy, transparency and efficiency of defence land management.

Emphasising that technology must be accompanied by human responsibility, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said, “Technology should strengthen accountability, not replace it.” He urged the probationers to remain firm in discharging their duties, observing that technology may fail, but an officer’s sense of responsibility and firmness should not.

Referring to the rapidly changing technological and scientific landscape, the Vice-President called upon the young officers to continuously upgrade their knowledge and skills. He highlighted iGOT Karmayogi as an important platform for continuous capacity building and encouraged the probationers to remain receptive to new ideas and innovations.

Quoting the celebrated Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that learning acquires true meaning only when it is reflected in conduct. He stressed that knowledge of laws, procedures and governance frameworks must be complemented by character, kindness, integrity and ethical conduct. He also advised the young officers to obey their seniors while remaining independent of undue pressure, and to ensure timely disposal of files.

The Vice-President said that civil servants have a crucial role in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, particularly by ensuring inclusive development and taking governance to the last mile. He urged the probationers to give their best in every responsibility entrusted to them, saying that sincere service to the people is itself the greatest measure of public service.

Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, senior officers of the Ministry of Defence, and senior officers of the Indian Defence Estates Service were present on the occasion.

item.title: Electrical Emergency Preparedness Tested in Mock Drill at BSP SMS-3
item.description: Bhilai Steel Plant conducted a quarterly mock drill at Steel Melting Shop-3 (SMS-3) on September 29, 2026, to review preparedness and response procedures for handling emergency situations. The exercise was organised in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Factories Act and established occupational health, safety and environmental management requirements. The drill was held during the first shift at 11 am at the entrance area of HI Bay, Crane Substation-1, Cubicle No. 6F1. The…
item.content:encoded:
Bhilai Steel Plant conducted a quarterly mock drill at Steel Melting Shop-3 (SMS-3) on September 29, 2026, to review preparedness and response procedures for handling emergency situations. The exercise was organised in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Factories Act and established occupational health, safety and environmental management requirements. The drill was held during the first shift at 11 am at the entrance area of HI Bay, Crane Substation-1, Cubicle No. 6F1. The simulated emergency involved an electrical shock and flashover.

During the exercise, a scenario was created in which the moving contact jaws of an Air Circuit Breaker (ACB) became loose and were displaced from their position during the racking-in process. This was simulated to result in a short circuit between the phases of a charged incoming busbar, leading to a flashover. Two employees, including a Technician and a Helper, were simulated to have sustained injuries and become unconscious due to the electrical shock and flashover, requiring their safe evacuation.

Immediately after the simulated emergency was reported, the prescribed emergency response procedure was activated. The siren was sounded and the concerned departments and emergency response agencies were informed. The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Fire Brigade, Main Medical Post and Civil Defence teams responded promptly and participated in the rescue exercise. The injured personnel were provided first aid and evacuated to a designated safe area, while the unconscious employee was also evacuated through coordinated rescue efforts. As part of the drill scenario, the Main Medical Post team assessed the affected personnel and declared their condition normal.

A thorough inspection of the area was subsequently carried out to ensure that no person remained at risk. After the simulated emergency was brought under control, the Fire Brigade issued the “All Clear” signal to the Department Head. The Area In-charge then sounded the continuous siren to confirm the restoration of normal conditions.

The approximately 25-minute exercise provided an opportunity for the concerned teams to practise rescue operations during an electrical emergency, safe evacuation of injured personnel, provision of medical assistance and coordinated emergency response procedures. The main emergency exercise lasted around 10 minutes, during which all participating agencies and teams worked in close coordination.

At the review meeting held after the drill, Shri Tribhuvan Baitha, Chief General Manager, Steel Melting Shop-3, appreciated the prompt response, coordination and disciplined approach demonstrated by the participating departments and agencies. He emphasised the importance of regular mock drills in strengthening preparedness for actual emergency situations and reducing response time.

The successful conduct of the exercise was supported by Shri Rajat Sarkar, Deputy General Manager (Electrical), Steel Melting Shop-3, and Shri Umashankar Parganiha, General Manager and Departmental Safety Officer, Steel Melting Shop-3, along with the concerned teams.

The mock drill concluded successfully, demonstrating coordinated emergency response among the participating departments, adherence to prescribed safety procedures and a high level of safety awareness among employees.

item.title: Ministry of Mines to Launch Auction of Offshore Mineral Blocks in Andaman Sea
item.description:
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, will launch the auction of offshore mineral blocks tomorrow, marking an important step towards unlocking India’s offshore mineral potential and strengthening the country’s long-term mineral resource security.
Offshore mineral resources are important in the context of technological advancement, clean energy transition and resilient supply chains. Minerals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements are important inputs…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, will launch the auction of offshore mineral blocks tomorrow, marking an important step towards unlocking India’s offshore mineral potential and strengthening the country’s long-term mineral resource security.

Offshore mineral resources are important in the context of technological advancement, clean energy transition and resilient supply chains. Minerals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements are important inputs for electric mobility, renewable energy systems, advanced electronics and strategic industries. Development of domestic offshore mineral resources can therefore contribute to India’s objectives of self-reliance, resource security and sustainable economic growth.

The auction is being conducted under the provisions of the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002 and the Offshore Areas Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2024, as amended from time to time. Following amendments to the OAMDR Act in 2023, the Ministry of Mines has been empowered to auction offshore mineral blocks, enabling transparent and competitive allocation of offshore mineral resources.

The auction comprises two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea region, which will be offered for grant of Composite Licence. It is expected to encourage systematic exploration, attract investment and promote the adoption of advanced technologies for offshore mineral exploration and development.

The initiative reflects the Government’s commitment to expanding India’s mineral resource base through systematic exploration and responsible development of offshore resources. It is also expected to facilitate greater private sector participation and technological innovation in an emerging area with significant potential for meeting future industrial and strategic requirements.

The launch of the auction marks another step towards harnessing India’s offshore mineral wealth and strengthening the country’s mineral security for emerging technologies, industrial development and long-term economic growth.

***

Prajith Kumar MV

Conducted under the theme “Anchored in Trust, United at Sea”, the exercise brings together maritime forces from India and ASEAN countries for professional, operational and social engagements aimed at enhancing mutual understanding, cooperation and…
item.content:encoded:
The Second Edition of the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise (AIME-2026) commenced at Subic Bay, Philippines, on 28 Sep 2026, with the participation of Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish, along with maritime forces from ASEAN Member States. Conducted under the theme “Anchored in Trust, United at Sea”, the exercise brings together maritime forces from India and ASEAN countries for professional, operational and social engagements aimed at enhancing mutual understanding, cooperation and interoperability.

The exercise commenced with the Opening Ceremony, wherein His Excellency Shri Harsh Kumar Jain, Ambassador of India to the Philippines, graced the occasion as the Guest of Honour and addressed the participating maritime forces.

The Harbour Phase will comprise a series of professional, operational and social engagements, including Subject Matter Expert Exchanges, sporting and cultural activities, community engagement and Operational Synchronisation, followed by a Pre-Sail Brief prior to commencement of the Sea Phase.

The exercise will thereafter transition to the Sea Phase, wherein the participating maritime forces will undertake coordinated maritime exercises and operational serials. The sea phase is aimed at enhancing professional understanding, operational coordination and interoperability through practical training and coordinated activities at sea.

The participation of INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish in AIME-2026 underscores the Indian Navy’s continued commitment to strengthening maritime partnerships and promoting practical cooperation with ASEAN maritime forces. The exercise is being conducted in furtherance of India’s Act East Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

item.title: Ministry of Coal Reviews Special Campaign 6 Preparations; SECL Sets Large-Scale Cleanliness and Scrap Disposal Targets
item.description: The Ministry of Coal reviewed preparations and targets for Special Campaign 6.0 across organisations in the coal sector, with a particular focus on large-scale cleanliness activities, scrap disposal and scientific management of electronic waste. During the review, South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) presented an action plan covering 225 identified sites, with cleanliness activities planned across approximately 40 lakh square feet and a target for disposal of 3,300 metric tonnes of scrap. …
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Coal reviewed preparations and targets for Special Campaign 6.0 across organisations in the coal sector, with a particular focus on large-scale cleanliness activities, scrap disposal and scientific management of electronic waste. During the review, South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) presented an action plan covering 225 identified sites, with cleanliness activities planned across approximately 40 lakh square feet and a target for disposal of 3,300 metric tonnes of scrap.


The review meeting was chaired by Shri Sanjeev Kumar Kassi, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Coal. Representatives of Coal India Limited, its subsidiary companies, Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), NLC India Limited, Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPFO) and other concerned organisations participated in the meeting.


Special Campaign 6.0 will be conducted from 2 to 31 October 2026. The campaign places enhanced emphasis on systematic collection, segregation and scientific disposal of e-waste, besides cleanliness, scrap disposal, optimisation of office and operational space, digitalisation and reduction of administrative pendency.


During the organisation-wise review, SECL outlined its targets for the campaign. In addition to cleanliness activities at 225 sites and disposal of 3,300 metric tonnes of scrap, the company plans to review 500 physical files and weed out 200 obsolete files. It has also set targets to review 7,000 electronic files and close 3,000 e-files. The targets form part of the campaign objectives published by the Ministry of Coal through the Press Information Bureau.


The review accorded special attention to e-waste management. Shri Kassi directed participating organisations to undertake systematic identification, categorisation and assessment of electronic waste and ensure reporting in the prescribed format. He also called upon the organisations to identify and share innovative initiatives and best practices emerging from the campaign for wider adoption across the coal sector.


The meeting also reviewed media outreach and social media activities planned by participating organisations. Emphasis was placed on regular dissemination of campaign activities, achievements and replicable best practices through press releases and digital platforms to enhance public awareness and visibility of the campaign.


During the concluding discussions, Shri Kassi stressed the need for participating organisations to achieve their assigned targets well before the scheduled conclusion of the campaign on 31 October 2026, thereby allowing adequate time for verification and timely reporting. He reiterated that systematic e-waste management should remain a key priority throughout the campaign.


Shri Alok Kumar Thakur, General Manager (Civil) and Nodal Officer for Special Campaign 6, along with officials from the Materials Management and Public Relations Departments, participated in the review meeting on behalf of South Eastern Coalfields Limited.

item.title: Special Campaign 6
item.description: The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and its organisations are undertaking Special Campaign 6 in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). From 05–15 October 2026, t he Campaign will seek to translate Swachhata into sustained administrative action by promoting workplace cleanliness, optimising available space, reducing pendency and strengthening systems for effective management of records, files…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and its organisations are undertaking Special Campaign 6 in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). From 05–15 October 2026, the Campaign will seek to translate Swachhata into sustained administrative action by promoting workplace cleanliness, optimising available space, reducing pendency and strengthening systems for effective management of records, files and obsolete material. Officers and staff across the Ministry and its organisations are being encouraged to participate actively in the Campaign and contribute towards creating cleaner, more organised and efficient workplaces.

Building on the achievements of Special Campaign 5.0, concluded on 31 October 2025, MDoNER and its organisations are continuing their efforts towards cleanliness and administrative efficiency. The Campaign witnessed 36 cleanliness drives, freeing of 3,664 sq. ft. of office space, disposal of 46 public grievances and 3 VIP references, review and weeding of 217 physical files and 32 e-files, and generation of ₹7,82,814 through disposal of scrap and unserviceable items.

Under Special Campaign 6, these efforts will be further strengthened through a cleanliness drive in the office premises, corridors, common areas, staircases and surrounding areas, activities such as the Clean Desk Campaign, identification and review of old physical files/records, review and closure of eligible e-files, identification of obsolete/damaged furniture, equipment and scrap, segregation of e-waste and other scrap for disposal as per prescribed procedure, review of pending references/pendency cases for time-bound disposal.

The Campaign is expected to bring about visible and measurable improvements across the Ministry and its organisations. By combining cleanliness with systematic administrative reforms, Special Campaign 6 aims to ensure that Swachhata becomes an integral part of day-to-day office management rather than remaining a one-time exercise. MDoNER and its organisations remain committed to sustaining the improvements achieved through the Campaign and fostering a cleaner, more efficient, organised and environmentally responsible workplace.

*****

PS

BSNL Himachal Pradesh Circle is steadily expanding its…
item.content:encoded:
Shimla, September 30, 2026. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) is celebrating its 26th Foundation Day on October 1, 2026, reaffirming its commitment to provide reliable, affordable and inclusive digital connectivity. Over the years, BSNL has remained an important part of India’s telecommunication infrastructure and continues to strengthen its network to meet the growing needs of customers both  in urban and rural areas of Country.

BSNL Himachal Pradesh Circle is steadily expanding its connectivity footprint through focused network expansion, 4G rollout and Fibre connectivity. As of September 30, 2026, more than 1050 villages/locations in Himachal Pradesh have been covered under DBN-funded 4G projects, with 626 BTSs. These initiatives are helping to extend modern telecom services and supporting improved digital access across the State.

Amended BharatNet project is another important pillar in this effort, particularly for rural connectivity. Under the Amended BharatNet Programme, BSNL shall be laying about 20,000 Kms of Optical fiber cable to connect 3615 Gram Panchayats of Himachal Pradesh . More than 5500 Kms of Optical Fiber cable have already  been laid  covering about 1020 GPs to provide high-speed broadband connectivity ,helping to bring digital services and opportunities closer to citizens in remote and underserved locations.

New FTTH Plans: More Choice, Speed and Value

As part of its customer-centric initiatives, BSNL has introduced 10 new FTTH broadband plans on a pan-India basis, offering speeds ranging from 25 Mbps up to 1 Gbps. Monthly tariffs range from ₹459 to ₹4,799, excluding GST. The new portfolio provides customers with a wider choice of high-speed broadband plans suited to different usage requirements, including variety of options for choosing OTT services.

The new ₹459 Fibre Rural OTT plan has been introduced specifically for rural areas. This initiative further supports BSNL’s objective of making broadband connectivity more accessible in rural and remote areas.

BSNL has also enhanced speeds in its existing FTTH service plans. The ₹899 Fibre Value Advance plan has been upgraded from 175 Mbps to 200 Mbps, while the ₹1,299 Fibre/AirFibre Premium Plus plan has been upgraded from 250 Mbps to 300 Mbps. The new plans are effective from September 25, 2026, on a regular basis across BSNL circles.

BSNL’s Commitment to Himachal Pradesh

With continued expansion of 4G services, strengthening of Fibre infrastructure and new FTTH offerings, BSNL Himachal Pradesh Circle is working towards creating a stronger and more customer-focused digital ecosystem. The emphasis remains on reliable connectivity, wider coverage, affordable high speed broadband and improved customer experience, particularly in areas where quality digital connectivity can make a significant difference.

On this occasion, Sh. Harsh Vardhan Singh, Chief General Manager, BSNL Himachal Pradesh Circlesaid :-“As BSNL celebrates 26 years of services, our focus is firmly on building reliable & robust telecom  networks, wider 4G and Fiber connectivity, better customer experience and affordable digital services for every section of society. We remain committed to ensuring that even the remotest parts of Himachal Pradesh are connected to the opportunities of Digital India.”

SS/NK

item.title: AIIMS Raipur Strengthens Advanced Trauma Care Training for Timely Treatment of Critically Injured Patients
item.description: Raipur, September 30, 2026: Strengthening timely and coordinated treatment of critically injured patients, the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Raipur, organised a two-day Continuing Medical Education (CME) programme and workshop on Trauma Resuscitation, Anaesthesia and Critical Care (TRACC) 2026. The programme provided doctors and healthcare professionals with practical training in advanced trauma-care techniques through hands-on sessions, simulation-based learning and…
item.content:encoded:
Raipur, September 30, 2026: Strengthening timely and coordinated treatment of critically injured patients, the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Raipur, organised a two-day Continuing Medical Education (CME) programme and workshop on Trauma Resuscitation, Anaesthesia and Critical Care (TRACC) 2026. The programme provided doctors and healthcare professionals with practical training in advanced trauma-care techniques through hands-on sessions, simulation-based learning and expert-led demonstrations.

Organised by the Department of Trauma and Emergency Medicine, AIIMS Raipur, the programme brought together doctors from different medical specialties, healthcare professionals, faculty members and invited experts. The key focus was on strengthening early trauma resuscitation, advanced airway management, pain management, critical care and coordinated treatment among different medical specialties involved in the care of severely injured patients.


The programme was formally inaugurated on September 27, 2026, by Director, AIIMS Raipur, Lieutenant General Ashok Jindal (Retd.), in the presence of senior officers, faculty members, invited experts and participants. The inaugural session emphasised the importance of timely trauma resuscitation, team-based patient care, evidence-based medical practice and continuous hands-on training. Experts highlighted that clinical decisions taken during the initial stages of trauma management can have a significant bearing on the subsequent course of treatment.


On the first day, specialised hands-on workshops were conducted on ultrasound-guided nerve blocks and advanced airway management. Participants received demonstrations by experts and practised the techniques through simulation-based training under supervised conditions. The sessions focused on contemporary techniques relevant to trauma care, emergency medicine and perioperative management.


The academic sessions of TRACC 2026 covered recent advances in trauma care and their practical application in emergency and critical-care settings. Expert lectures, interactive discussions and case-based academic sessions provided participants an opportunity to discuss important aspects of trauma resuscitation, anaesthesia and critical care. The programme sought to bridge the gap between advances in medical knowledge and their effective application in real-world emergency situations.


The programme also highlighted that trauma care is not confined to a single medical specialty. Timely and effective coordination among emergency medicine, anaesthesia, surgery, critical care and other relevant specialties plays an important role in providing comprehensive care to severely injured patients. Accordingly, TRACC 2026 placed equal emphasis on knowledge sharing, practical skills and interdisciplinary teamwork.


TRACC 2026 was organised under the leadership of Dr. Debendra Kumar Tripathi, Organising Chairperson, and Dr. Pallavi Shende, Organising Secretary, Department of Trauma and Emergency Medicine, AIIMS Raipur. The programme provided a platform for doctors and healthcare professionals involved in the management of critically ill and injured patients to exchange knowledge, share clinical experiences and learn contemporary treatment approaches.


The organising committee expressed its gratitude to the invited experts, participants, delegates, collaborating institutions, hospital administration and all those who contributed to the successful conduct of the programme. The Department of Trauma and Emergency Medicine, AIIMS Raipur, reaffirmed its commitment to promoting continuous medical education, advanced clinical training and excellence in trauma and emergency care.

item.title: REGIONAL DIRECTORATE OF NSS, KOLKATA STRENGTHENS YOUTH-LED DISASTER RESPONSE THROUGH ‘NSS DISASTER MATES’
item.description:

The initiative seeks to build upon the long-standing tradition of NSS Volunteers responding to floods, cyclones and other natural calamities by providing a common identity and a coordinated platform for…
item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, September 30, 2026

The Regional Directorate of National Service Scheme (NSS), Kolkata, has initiated “NSS Disaster Mates”, a volunteer-led initiative to strengthen the participation of NSS Volunteers in disaster response, relief and community support activities. The initiative seeks to build upon the long-standing tradition of NSS Volunteers responding to floods, cyclones and other natural calamities by providing a common identity and a coordinated platform for volunteer-led humanitarian action. It aims to facilitate greater coordination among NSS Units, educational institutions and local communities during emergencies.

The first major mobilisation under NSS Disaster Mates was undertaken in response to the floods in Assam. 20 NSS Units from fourteen institutions of West Bengal participated in the initiative and collectively mobilised ₹4,07,301/- (Rupees Four Lakh Seven Thousand Three Hundred One only) towards the Assam Chief Minister’s Relief Fund.

The contribution was raised through voluntary efforts of NSS Volunteers, including contributions from their tiffin expenses and personal savings, crowdfunding activities and door-to-door campaigns.

The initiative enabled NSS Volunteers from West Bengal to extend support to communities affected by a natural calamity beyond the State, reflecting the spirit of the NSS motto “Not Me, But You.”

Building upon the experience of the Assam initiative, the Regional Directorate of NSS, Kolkata undertook “NSS Disaster Mates 2.0” to provide relief assistance to flood-affected families in Bhutni Island, Malda in coordination with the District Nodal Officer, NSS, Malda, with the participation of 55 NSS Units from fifty-five educational institutions across West Bengal.

A preliminary local survey was conducted to identify affected families and facilitate need-based distribution. On 26 September 2026, a team comprising 57 NSS Volunteers and teachers travelled to Hiranandapur village of Bhutni Island and distributed essential relief materials among 310 flood-affected families. Each relief package included essential household items such as rice, flattened rice, potatoes, sattu, soybean, chana dal, jaggery, biscuits, noodles and soap, along with a carrying bag.

The riverine geography and difficult accessibility of the area required the relief operation to be conducted through a combination of road and waterways. Relief materials and participating personnel were transported up to Manikchak Ghat, following which boats were used to reach the affected areas through Suksena Ghat, Doman Tola and Hiranandapur.

The total expenditure recorded for the relief operation was ₹1,71,311/-, including expenditure towards relief materials, transportation and logistical arrangements.

Shri Agnimeel Das, Regional Director, Regional Directorate of NSS, Kolkata, stated that NSS Disaster Mates has been conceived to provide a common identity and coordinated platform for the voluntary humanitarian action traditionally undertaken by NSS Volunteers during natural calamities. He emphasised that the initiative is intended to encourage young volunteers to remain sensitive to the needs of affected communities and contribute within their capacity whenever society faces a crisis.

He further highlighted that the response to the Assam flood initiative and subsequently to NSS Disaster Mates 2.0 in Bhutni Island demonstrates the strength of collective youth action. The participation of NSS Units from different parts of West Bengal, he noted, reflects how the spirit of “Not Me, But You” can be translated into meaningful support for communities in distress. He also underlined the objective of further strengthening a culture of preparedness, service and community solidarity among NSS Volunteers.

The NSS Disaster Mates initiative seeks to encourage NSS Volunteers to participate, as appropriate and in coordination with competent authorities, in activities relating to disaster preparedness, community awareness, emergency assistance, relief mobilisation, health and hygiene awareness, post-disaster support and community resilience.

The initiative also aims to strengthen coordination among NSS Units, Programme Officers, educational institutions, district-level NSS structures and local communities, enabling the NSS network to contribute in an organised manner during emergencies.

Through NSS Disaster Mates, the Regional Directorate of NSS, Kolkata seeks to further translate the spirit of “Not Me, But You” into coordinated community action and encourage young volunteers to contribute to society during times of need.

item.description:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Bhopal Branch Office (BPBO), organized a ‘Manak Manthan’ programme on the Draft Indian Standard “Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement — Specification (First Revision of IS 12330)” on 29 September 2026 at Hotel Park, Satna. The programme was attended by around 25 participants from the cement industry and MSME sector.
The programme commenced with the welcome address by Shri Mohammad Rizwan, Director & Head, BIS Bhopal Branch Office. He highlighted the…
item.content:encoded:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Bhopal Branch Office (BPBO), organized a ‘Manak Manthan’ programme on the Draft Indian Standard “Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement — Specification (First Revision of IS 12330)” on 29 September 2026 at Hotel Park, Satna. The programme was attended by around 25 participants from the cement industry and MSME sector.

The programme commenced with the welcome address by Shri Mohammad Rizwan, Director & Head, BIS Bhopal Branch Office. He highlighted the role of BIS in standardization, product certification, and promotion of quality culture. While explaining the objective of Manak Manthan, he emphasized the importance of obtaining practical and technical feedback from all concerned stakeholders before finalization of the standard. He also highlighted that Indian Standards not only ensure quality but also act as a bridge between industry, research institutions, and society by providing a common platform for sharing experiences, suggestions, and technical inputs.

Subsequently, Shri Hariom Meena, Scientist ‘C’/Deputy Director, BIS Bhopal Branch Office, delivered a detailed PowerPoint presentation on the key provisions of the draft standard and the changes made in the new version. The participants were briefed about the scope, objectives, and major requirements of the standard, followed by discussions on quality and compliance aspects. During the technical discussion and interactive session, participants shared their views on practical aspects related to cement the concerned standard. Discussions covered important issues such as sampling methodology, testing procedures, laboratory requirements, acceptance criteria, sample handling, documentation, and BIS certification requirements.

The discussions focused on ensuring that the standard serves as an effective guideline for administrators, policymakers, industry professionals, and end users, while incorporating field-level realities and emerging technological advancements.

The Manak Manthan programme reaffirmed BIS’s commitment towards an inclusive, transparent, and consultative standardization process for ensuring quality and reliability of products and services. The suggestions and recommendations received during the meeting will be compiled and placed before the concerned technical committee for consideration, so that the final Indian Standard effectively reflects the needs and expectations of stakeholders across the country.

***

item.title: Bureau of Indian Standards Sponsors Exposure Visits for 635 Standard Club Students to “Gatisheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0” Exhibition in Jammu
item.description: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Jammu & Kashmir Branch Office (JKBO) continued its participation in the “Gatisheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0” Exhibition held in Jammu from 28 to 30 September 2026, showcasing its initiatives in the areas of standardization, quality assurance, conformity assessment and consumer awareness. As part of its student outreach initiative, BIS sponsored exposure visits for 635 students from 25 BIS Standard Clubs over the three-day period, enabling students from schools…
item.content:encoded:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Jammu & Kashmir Branch Office (JKBO) continued its participation in the “Gatisheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0” Exhibition held in Jammu from 28 to 30 September 2026, showcasing its initiatives in the areas of standardization, quality assurance, conformity assessment and consumer awareness. As part of its student outreach initiative, BIS sponsored exposure visits for 635 students from 25 BIS Standard Clubs over the three-day period, enabling students from schools across the Jammu Region, including far-flung and hilly areas, to visit the exhibition and gain firsthand exposure to government departments, Public Sector Undertakings, government agencies and other participating organizations.

On the third day, 254 students from nine BIS Standard Clubs participated in the exposure visit. The students also visited the Jammu & Kashmir Branch Laboratory (JKBL), where they learned about gold testing, XRF technology, assaying, parting and hallmarking. The initiative provided students with an opportunity to connect classroom learning with real-world applications and understand the importance of quality, safety and standards in everyday life.

During the third day of the exhibition, Shri Saaqib Raahi, Scientist-C/Deputy Director, BIS JKBO, visited the BIS stall and interacted with visitors and students. He apprised them of the activities of the Bureau and various initiatives undertaken under the BIS Standard Club and Promotion Activities.

The BIS stall was also visited by Hon’ble Member of Parliament Shri Jugal Kishore Sharma, who appreciated the efforts of the Bureau of Indian Standards in promoting quality consciousness among young minds through its Standard Club activities and student-oriented initiatives. He appreciated the contribution of BIS towards creating awareness among students about standards, quality, safety and consumer awareness, and acknowledged the importance of such initiatives in nurturing a culture of quality consciousness among the younger generation.

Shri Ashish Dwivedi, Standard Promotion Officer, and Shri Sumit Kashyap, Consultant, BIS JKBO, briefed visitors about the Bureau’s initiatives relating to standardization, conformity assessment, quality promotion, consumer awareness, BIS certification, hallmarking, standards education and the role of standards in ensuring the quality and safety of products and services.

The BIS stall displayed awareness material on Indian Standards, ISI Mark, Hallmarking, BIS Care App, quality-conscious consumer practices and the importance of standards in everyday life. The BIS team also sensitized visitors about the role of standards in promoting quality, safety, reliability and sustainability.

The Bureau of Indian Standards, Jammu & Kashmir Branch Office, sponsored exposure visits for students associated with BIS Standard Clubs as part of its efforts to provide them with experiential learning opportunities.

Over the three-day exhibition, 635 students from 25 BIS Standard Clubs participated in the sponsored exposure visits. The initiative enabled students from different districts of the Jammu Region to visit a major exhibition and interact with representatives of various Central Government departments, Public Sector Undertakings, government agencies and other participating organizations.

The students explored different exhibition stalls and learned about the products, technologies, services, initiatives and developmental activities showcased by various organizations. The visits also helped students understand the practical application of concepts related to science, technology, quality, public services, standards and development.

The Gatisheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0 Exhibition brought together a wide range of Central Government departments, Public Sector Undertakings, government agencies, departments and other organizations on a common platform.

During the sponsored exposure visits, students visited various exhibition stalls and interacted with representatives of participating organizations. They learned about the products, technologies, services, initiatives and developmental activities showcased at the exhibition.

The exposure programme enabled students to connect their classroom learning with real-world applications and enhanced their understanding of science, technology, public services, quality, standards and developmental initiatives.

The participation of students from Doda, Rajouri, Ramban, Kishtwar, Kathua and Jammu provided them with an opportunity to experience a large-scale exhibition and interact with diverse institutions on a common platform.

The students were also facilitated to visit the Jammu & Kashmir Referral Assaying Laboratory, Bari Brahmana, Jammu, where they received information about gold testing and assaying processes, X-ray fluorescence (XRF) technology, parting processes and various hallmarking activities.

The students learned about the scientific methods used to determine the quality and purity of precious metals and understood the role of assaying and hallmarking in ensuring transparency and protecting consumer interests.

The visit further familiarized students with the importance of scientific testing, standards, conformity assessment and hallmarking in ensuring quality and consumer confidence.

The exposure visits formed an important component of BIS’s efforts to provide practical and experiential learning opportunities to students associated with BIS Standard Clubs. Such initiatives help students understand the relevance of standards, quality and safety in everyday life and encourage them to become informed and quality-conscious citizens.

The Bureau of Indian Standards continues to strengthen its engagement with schools through the BIS Standard Club Programme, providing students with opportunities to learn about standards beyond the classroom and observe their practical application in different sectors.

The participation of the Bureau of Indian Standards, Jammu & Kashmir Branch Office in the “Gatisheel Jammu & Kashmir 2.0” Exhibition, coupled with the sponsorship of exposure visits for 635 Standard Club students from 25 Standard Clubs over three days, reflects BIS’s continued efforts to promote awareness of quality, safety, reliability, conformity assessment and standardization among students and consumers across the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

*******

The Acquirer is a private limited company, incorporated under the laws of Netherlands and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Chubu Electric Power Co., Inc., Japan (CHUBU). The Acquirer is engaged in the activities related to investment, management, financing and treasury related functions for the CHUBU Group. CHUBU is a public limited company listed on recognized stock exchanges in Japan and is engaged in the business of generation, distribution and transmission of power generated through renewable sources such as solar, wind, nuclear etc., among other activities.

The Target is a public limited company incorporated under the laws of India. The Target and its various subsidiaries in India are primarily engaged in the business of sale and generation of power through renewable sources such as wind and solar.

The offering is complemented by comprehensive lifecycle service solutions through its PrimeServ organization.
