item.title: Auction of 109 Mementos Showcases West Bengal’s Diverse Cultural and Artistic Heritage
item.description:
West Bengal features prominently in the 8th PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, with 109 mementos representing a wide range of the State’s artistic, cultural, religious and heritage traditions. The collection includes traditional crafts, devotional artworks, representations of heritage sites, folk-art forms and commemorative mementos associated with notable personalities.
The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online until October 2, 2026. For details, participation and the…
item.content:encoded:
West Bengal features prominently in the 8th PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, with 109 mementos representing a wide range of the State’s artistic, cultural, religious and heritage traditions. The collection includes traditional crafts, devotional artworks, representations of heritage sites, folk-art forms and commemorative mementos associated with notable personalities.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online until October 2, 2026. For details, participation and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal at pmmementos.gov.in.

Among the prominent mementos featured in the West Bengal collection are:

 

 

 

Two mementos in the collection feature statues of Baba Lokenath, the renowned Indian spiritual leader and saint, revered for his teachings on spiritual enlightenment, yoga and devotion. One of the statues is made of ceramic, while the other is crafted in a different material.

 

Another memento features the face of Goddess Durga through Shola work, using Indian cork, a traditional material associated with West Bengal.

A memento highlights distinctive Monument of West Bengal woven in rattan cane showcases handwoven craftsmanship. The memento features intricate weave and natural texture, reflecting sustainable craftsmanship rooted in rural heritage.

This memento features a pair of hand-carved wooden Bankura Horses, representing the folk-art heritage of West Bengal. The sculptures is characterised by elongated necks, erect ears and geometric forms associated with the Panchmura artistic style.

A handcrafted Sholapith artwork depicting Maa Kali is also part of the collection. The piece features the goddess’s face, third eye and multi-tiered crown, with the ornamental elements carved from ivory-white Sholapith, a traditional material associated with Bengali heritage.

A hand-painted canvas depicting the historic Rasmancha monument in Bishnupur captures its distinctive pyramidal terracotta structure and arched galleries. The painting is signed by the artist Nibedita Nema.

The West Bengal collection further includes mementos associated with Rabindranath Tagore, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Swami Vivekananda and Satyajit Ray, along with representations of Madan Mohan Temple, Jalpesh Temple, Tarapith, Dakshineswar, Kalna’s heritage temples, Bankura’s folk traditions and Durga Puja craftsmanship.

Taken together, the 109 mementos offer a broad view of West Bengal through its devotional traditions, folk and craft practices, architectural heritage, literary and artistic legacy, and contemporary commemorative works.

***

M Annadurai

item.title: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Completes Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6
item.description:
The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has completed the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 with focused efforts towards cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending matters and strengthening of sustainable practices in the Ministry.
During the Preparatory Phase, the Ministry undertook a comprehensive review of records, pending matters and other items identified for disposal. 134 physical files and 80 e-files have been identified for review as part of the campaign.…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has completed the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 with focused efforts towards cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending matters and strengthening of sustainable practices in the Ministry.

During the Preparatory Phase, the Ministry undertook a comprehensive review of records, pending matters and other items identified for disposal. 134 physical files and 80 e-files have been identified for review as part of the campaign.

The Ministry has also identified a large number of e-waste items for disposal under the campaign. The exercise has been undertaken with a view to ensuring systematic disposal, better utilisation of office space and greater efficiency in day-to-day functioning.

The Ministry continues to promote digital and paperless functioning through various e-governance platforms, thereby reducing dependence on physical records and facilitating streamlined administrative processes.

The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 will commence from 2nd October and continue till 31st October 2026. During this phase, the Ministry will work towards achieving the identified targets, along with further strengthening of cleanliness, record management and workplace efficiency.

The Ministry remains committed to institutionalising Swachhata, efficiency and sustainable work practices in its functioning.

***

ISA

item.title: Bankers Books Evidence Act, 2026
item.description: The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 modernises India’s legal system governing admissibility of banking records as evidence. It comes into force on October 1 2026, and replaces the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891. The Act introduces a technology-neutral framework covering physical, electronic and digital records, with standardised provisions for their authentication and certification. It strengthens procedural safeguards governing the production of bankers’ books. The Act also protects bank…
item.content:encoded:
The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 modernises India’s legal system governing admissibility of banking records as evidence. It comes into force on October 1 2026, and replaces the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891. The Act introduces a technology-neutral framework covering physical, electronic and digital records, with standardised provisions for their authentication and certification. It strengthens procedural safeguards governing the production of bankers’ books. The Act also protects bank officials from routine appearance in proceedings, where the bank is not a party, solely for the purpose of proving/testifying the record of the bank. It enables extension of its provision to specified financial sector entities, supporting an evolving and increasingly digital financial ecosystem.

A Modern Legal Framework for Banking Records

The Government has undertaken reforms to strengthen India’s banking and financial sector and improve ease of doing business. These efforts also focus on modernising laws and regulations to reflect the changing needs of the economy.

The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 comes into force on October 1, 2026, and replaces the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.

The Act provides clear and updated rules for admissibility of bank records as evidence in legal proceedings. It applies to court cases, inquiries, arbitrations and investigations where banking records may be required to be produced as evidence.

Breaking Down Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026

The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 provides a modern framework for admissibility of banking records as evidence in line with contemporary digital banking practices. The Act will be used in any legal proceeding, an arbitration and any investigation or inquiry under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, or under any other law for the time being in force, in which evidence is or may be taken. As per the Act-

  • “Bank” and “banker” mean any company or corporation carrying on the business of banking, any entity or class of entities operating in the financial sector (to whose books the provisions of this Act are extended), any post office savings bank or money order office.
  • “Bankers’ books” include ledgers, day-books, cash-books, account books and all other records used in the ordinary course of business of the bank. These can be kept in written or physical form or stored in any form of data storage mechanisms

Need for the Act

The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act was framed in the colonial era of 1891, when banking systems were entirely paper-based. In the current times, India continues to progress in digitising its economy. Banking and financial transactions are largely driven by digital platforms, frequently accessible with a simple click on a mobile phone. In such a scenario, it is imperative that India’s legal framework evolves to keep pace with these advancements.

Key Features

  • The Act establishes a contemporary evidentiary framework for banking records, covering records maintained across physical and digital banking systems.
  • It enables standardised authentication and certification of bankers’ books, providing for appropriate certification of physical and electronic records.
  • The Act strengthens clarity and procedural safeguards in the production of bankers’ books. It also protects bank officials from being routinely required to produce records or testify in proceedings where the bank is not a party.
  • It provides a flexible framework for extending the law across the financial sector, as it continues to evolve in India.

The Act provides for stringent and contemporary safeguards for the secure handling and verification of electronic records as a precondition for their admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings.

 

Major Changes under the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026

The 2026 Act retains the core evidentiary framework of the 1891 law for proving banking records through certified copies of records. It modernises and strengthens the existing framework with a technology-neutral system covering electronic and digital banking records.

  • Recognition of Electronic Records as Evidence:
    • As per the new Act, an electronic or digital record of a banker’s book will be admissible, valid, and legally enforceable as evidence, subject to a few conditions which include-

(i) the said copy is a true copy of such entry or information, and correctly represents or is appropriately derived from such records

(ii) no unauthorised changes to data are detected

(iii) no tampering or other event affecting the integrity and accuracy of the system is detected

    • This change standardises the certification process and allows authentication through manual, digital, and electronic signatures.

 

  • Compelling Production of Bankers’ Books:
    • The Act provides that the contents of a banker’s book may be proved in legal proceedings through a certified copy, without requiring production of the original banker’s book.
    • Accordingly, a bank officer cannot ordinarily be compelled to produce the banker’s book or appear as a witness to prove the records, particularly where the bank is not a party to the proceedings.
    • The Act provides that a bank officer may, however, be required to appear as a witness or produce a banker’s book only pursuant to a written order of the Court recording a special cause. The Act specifies the circumstances constituting a special cause, where-

(i) accuracy or authenticity of the entry or information is uncertain.

(ii) the regularity or ordinary nature of record keeping is interrupted owing to any event.

(iii) the bank does not comply with any previous Court order about inspection or production of the certified copy of the books.

  • Extension to Other Financial Sector Entities:
    • The 1891 Act applies to entities engaged in the business of banking and any post office savings bank or money order office. The 2026 Act also retains this clause.
    • However, it further allows the Government to extend its provisions to any entity or class of entities operating in the financial sector, by notification. The Government may highlight conditions, exceptions, or modifications in the notification.

Conclusion

The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 marks a significant step towards modernising the legal framework governing banking records. By aligning evidentiary provisions with technological advancements and evolving economic needs, it strengthens the efficiency, reliability, and adaptability of India’s financial system. It reflects the Government’s continued commitment to advancing reforms that strengthen institutions and support India’s growth trajectory.

item.title: Grand and Dignified Closing of Rajbhasha Pakhwada–2026
item.description:
The Rajbhasha Pakhwada–2026 concluded with a grand and dignified closing ceremony at the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Sub-Regional Office, Gurugram. The fortnight-long observance, marked by enthusiasm, respect and a sense of belonging towards Hindi, focused on taking the Official Language beyond routine office work and connecting it with public service, dialogue and participation.
During the Pakhwada, various informative, creative and language-oriented activities were…
item.content:encoded:
The Rajbhasha Pakhwada–2026 concluded with a grand and dignified closing ceremony at the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Sub-Regional Office, Gurugram. The fortnight-long observance, marked by enthusiasm, respect and a sense of belonging towards Hindi, focused on taking the Official Language beyond routine office work and connecting it with public service, dialogue and participation.
 
During the Pakhwada, various informative, creative and language-oriented activities were organised with the active participation of officers and employees, including Hindi Noting and Drafting Competition, Rajbhasha Knowledge Competition and Hindi Speech Competition. These activities provided participants with a platform to showcase their linguistic skills and creativity while encouraging the effective and सहज use of Hindi in official work.
 
A major highlight of this year’s Rajbhasha Pakhwada was the initiative “Ek Nayi Soch, Ek Nayi Shuruaat: Rajbhasha Pakhwada with the Heroes of the Corporation.” Through this initiative, an effort was made to take Hindi beyond the confines of the office and connect it with Insured Persons and their families. A Hindi Word-Writing Competition was organised for the children of Insured Persons, and Hindi alphabet books were distributed among them. The initiative not only encouraged children to develop interest and affection for Hindi but also gave a new dimension to communication between ESIC and insured families.
 
As part of the same initiative, a dialogue programme titled “Rajbhasha Pakhwada with the Heroes of the Corporation – Hindi Dialogue for Solutions” was organised with Insured Persons. Through interaction in simple and सहज Hindi, efforts were made to understand their experiences, suggestions and expectations. The underlying objective of the initiative was to establish Hindi as a meaningful bridge between service, communication and sensitivity.
 
The closing ceremony was attended by Shri Sachin Singh, Deputy Director; Shri Naveen Kumar, Deputy Director; Shri Deepak Sharma, Deputy Director; Shri Kamalendra Kumar, Assistant Director; and Shri Pramod Kumar, Assistant Director, along with officers and employees of the office.
 
Addressing the gathering, Shri Hariom Prakash, Regional Director, said that Hindi is not only an important means of discharging official responsibilities but also a powerful medium for making public services simpler, more accessible and more effective. He emphasised that the use of Hindi should not remain confined to official correspondence, noting and drafting, but should naturally find place in the day-to-day functioning and delivery of services.
 
He stated that Rajbhasha Pakhwada provides an opportunity to reflect upon our working practices and ensure that information about ESIC services reaches the general public and Insured Persons in a language that is simple and easy to understand. The simpler and more simple the language, the more effective the communication becomes, thereby strengthening understanding and trust in the delivery of services.
 
Shri Hariom Prakash appreciated the initiative “Ek Nayi Soch, Ek Nayi Shuruaat: Rajbhasha Pakhwada with the Heroes of the Corporation”, stating that involving Insured Persons and their families in Rajbhasha activities is an important step towards connecting Hindi with public concerns and service delivery. He observed that Insured Persons are at the centre of the Corporation’s service system and that meaningful communication with them in a सहज language should form an important part of the organisation’s work culture.
 
He called upon all officers and employees to ensure that the use of Hindi does not remain limited to the Pakhwada but becomes a natural and consistent part of official work throughout the year. He emphasised that the true respect for Hindi would be reflected when the language becomes an integral part of our conduct, work practices and public service.
 
He also congratulated all officers and employees who participated enthusiastically in the various competitions and activities organised during the Pakhwada. He said that such activities not only promote interest in Hindi but also strengthen a positive, creative and participative work culture in the organisation. He appreciated the efforts of the Rajbhasha Section in organising the programmes and emphasised the need to further promote Hindi as a language of public service, dialogue and sensitivity.
 
Dr. Sweety Yadav, Assistant Director (Rajbhasha), said that this year’s Rajbhasha Pakhwada focused on taking Hindi beyond competitions and routine official work and connecting it with wider public concerns. She stated that when we communicate with Insured Persons and their families in a language that is सहज and familiar to them, language becomes more than a means of communication—it becomes a medium of trust, empathy and service. She emphasised the importance of adopting simple, सहज and effective Hindi in day-to-day official functioning.
 
During the closing ceremony, the winners of various competitions organised during the Pakhwada were felicitated with prizes and certificates. The participants expressed their enthusiasm and reaffirmed their commitment towards the promotion and effective use of Hindi.
 
The closing ceremony highlighted the message that Rajbhasha Pakhwada is not merely an annual event, but a commitment to making Hindi an integral part of work culture, public service and public dialogue. The initiatives undertaken by the Sub-Regional Office, Gurugram, this year marked a meaningful step towards taking Hindi from the office to society.
 
“Hindi comes alive not merely through words, but through dialogue;
and through dialogue, sensitivity finds its way into service.”

item.title: ECL sets the stage for action-driven Special Campaign 6

item.content:encoded:
Setting a high benchmark for operational efficiency and environmental stewardship, Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), a premier subsidiary of Coal India Limited having coal mining operations in West Bengal and Jharkhand, has successfully wrapped up the preparatory phase of the nationwide Special Campaign 6.

With a resolute focus on institutionalizing Swachhata (cleanliness), minimising administrative pendency and modernising governance, ECL has finalised comprehensive targets across all its mining areas, workshops and headquarters.

Laying the Groundwork for Cleanliness and Space Reclamation

As part of the preparatory phase blueprint, ECL identified 30 key operational sites spanning its expansive command areas for intensive cleanliness and rejuvenation drives. A major highlight of the campaign blueprint is the targeted clearance of 208,052 sq. ft. of area. By systematically removing clutter from industrial zones, office complexes and residential townships, the coal major aims to transform workspaces into safe, green and highly productive environments.

Driving Wealth from Waste: Scrap Management

Aligning with the national mission of resource optimisation and sustainable management, ECL has lined up a robust target to dispose of 850 Metric Tons of scrap material during the campaign cycle. Building on successful past asset monetisation drives—such as major scrap disposals across the Rajmahal Area, Khottadih OCP (Pandaveswar Area) and SP Mines—this initiative reinforces ECL's commitment to eco-friendly practices while unlocking substantial commercial value from unserviceable assets.

Streamlining Governance Through Digital and Physical File Review

ECL’s preparatory strategy places equal emphasis on administrative efficiency and swift workflow redressal:

  • Physical File Management: The company has targeted the review of 1,200 physical files, earmarking 1,000 obsolete files for systematic weeding out to optimize record-keeping infrastructure.
  • Paperless Governance (e-Files): Demonstrating leadership in digital adoption, ECL has set a target to review 3,800 e-files and achieve closure on 3,600 e-files, ensuring rapid inter-departmental communication, transparency, and a minimal carbon footprint.

A Culture of Continuous Improvement

Reflecting on the successful conclusion of the preparatory phase, ECL management noted that the blueprint for Special Campaign 6 represents a holistic approach to corporate governance. By combining rigorous physical cleanliness with digital agility and sustainable scrap disposal, ECL continues to champion the values of transparency, accountability and excellence in the coal sector.

****

Shuhaib T

item.title: IIT Jodhpur Uses AI to Predict Traffic, Understand Drivers and Prevent Road Accidents From predicting traffic jams before they happen to identifying risky situations before crashes occur, research at IIT Jodhpur is building a data-driven approach to understand—and improve—the way Indian traffic moves
item.description: Why does traffic suddenly slow down even when there is no accident, roadblock or visible obstruction? Why do two people travelling on the same road experience the journey so differently? And can Artificial Intelligence help predict traffic problems and make roads safer before an accident takes place? At the Transportation Systems and Traffic Modelling (TSTM) Laboratory at the Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, researchers are exploring these questions by bringing together transportation…
item.content:encoded:
Why does traffic suddenly slow down even when there is no accident, roadblock or visible obstruction? Why do two people travelling on the same road experience the journey so differently? And can Artificial Intelligence help predict traffic problems and make roads safer before an accident takes place? At the Transportation Systems and Traffic Modelling (TSTM) Laboratory at the Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, researchers are exploring these questions by bringing together transportation engineering, mathematics, Artificial Intelligence, behavioural science and data analytics. Led by Dr. Ranju Mohan, Associate Professor, Department of Civil and Infrastructure Engineering and Head, TSTM Lab, the research aims to understand transportation not merely as roads and vehicles, but as a complex system where infrastructure, technology, traffic and human behaviour continuously interact.

One of the major research directions at the laboratory focuses on understanding why traffic congestion develops and whether it can be predicted before it becomes visible on the road. Indian traffic presents a particularly complex challenge, with cars, buses, trucks, two-wheelers and other vehicles moving together, often without strict lane discipline. The researchers are developing mathematical and computational models to understand how such heterogeneous traffic behaves, how congestion begins and how traffic conditions evolve over time. These models can provide the scientific foundation for intelligent transportation systems, digital twins and future traffic-management strategies designed to make transportation networks more efficient, resilient and sustainable.

“Transportation is not simply about roads and vehicles; it is about people, behaviour, infrastructure, technology and data working together as one mobility ecosystem. Our research is focused on understanding these interactions scientifically so that transportation systems can become safer, smarter, more efficient and more responsive to the needs of people,” said Dr. Ranju Mohan, Associate Professor, Department of Civil and Infrastructure Engineering and Head, TSTM Lab, IIT Jodhpur.

The laboratory is also using technology to understand what happens behind the steering wheel. Its advanced driving simulator can recreate realistic Indian driving environments inside a controlled laboratory setting. This allows researchers to study how drivers respond to different road conditions, traffic situations and environmental factors without exposing participants to real-world danger. As part of the India–Japan collaborative JST LOTUS Project, the researchers are examining the relationship between physical road conditions and driver behaviour. Such insights can help engineers design road infrastructure that improves not only safety but also the comfort of those using it.

Another important dimension of the research looks at the experience of the traveller. The TSTM Lab studies why people choose one mode of transport over another and whether the quality of a journey influences their future travel choices. By examining travel satisfaction and travel behaviour together, researchers seek to generate insights that can help planners develop transportation systems that are efficient as well as comfortable, user-friendly, inclusive and sustainable.

At the heart of this work is data. To better understand the realities of Indian traffic, the laboratory is developing IDS JODHA, a comprehensive transportation dataset created through extensive field-data collection under diverse traffic conditions. Using Artificial Intelligence techniques, including Graph Neural Networks, researchers analyse the complex interactions among different road users, identify patterns that may not be immediately visible and extract insights into traffic behaviour. The research is intended to support the development of future intelligent transportation systems and smart-city applications.

The research goes a step further—from analysing accidents to asking whether some dangerous situations can be identified before an accident happens. Through its work on Proactive Road Safety, the TSTM Lab integrates traffic-flow modelling, driving simulation, behavioural studies and real-world traffic observations to develop methods for identifying potential risks in advance. These approaches can support safer road design, intelligent traffic management and evidence-based transportation policies.

Through this multidisciplinary research, IIT Jodhpur is working towards a transportation ecosystem in which roads are understood not merely as physical infrastructure, but as living systems shaped by vehicles, people, data, technology and the environment. The overarching objective of the TSTM Lab is to develop transportation systems that are safer, smarter, sustainable and centred on people—because improving the journey is ultimately about improving everyday life for millions of road users.

Addressing the gathering, RRM acknowledged the exemplary service, professionalism and selfless dedication of the MNS officers and highlighted the vital role played by them in supporting…
item.content:encoded:
Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth attended the closing ceremony of Centenary celebration of Military Nursing Service (MNS) at Manekshaw Centre, Delhi, on September 30, 2026. The ceremony marked the culmination of a year-long commemoration celebrating the rich legacy of the Military Nursing Service.

Addressing the gathering, RRM acknowledged the exemplary service, professionalism and selfless dedication of the MNS officers and highlighted the vital role played by them in supporting the Armed Forces Medical Services and the nation during war, natural calamity and peace times.

Director General Armed Forces Medical Services, Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja, appreciated the professional commitment, compassion and unwavering dedication of MNS officers towards their clientele, and their invaluable contribution to the Armed Forces Medical Services over the past century.

The highlights of the closing ceremony included the release of a Commemorative Coin, the memoir Steel and Grace, the centenary commemorative book titled Healing Hands & Brave Hearts: MNS@100, and the commemorative video Glimpses of a Year of Commemoration. A photo gallery depicting the history and evolution of the Military Nursing Service was also inaugurated.

Chief of Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, DGMS (Army)  Lt Gen CG Muralidharan, Vice Chief of Army Staff, Lt Gen Sandeep Jain, Addl DGMNS, Maj Gen Rachel Thomas, and other senior dignitaries from Delhi Garrison graced the occasion.

The Centenary events reaffirmed the Military Nursing Service’s commitment to its enduring values of compassion, professional excellence and service to the nation, in keeping with its Centenary theme, “Honouring the Past, Healing the Present & Inspiring the Future.”

VK/SR/Ruchi

item.title: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026, Sanitation System in Raipur to Become More Transparent and Result-Oriented
item.description: Raipur, September 30, 2026. With the effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, comprehensive changes are being made in Raipur to render the sanitation system more transparent, accountable, and result-oriented. Raipur Municipal Corporation Commissioner Mr. Sambit Mishra shared details of the key provisions of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and the preparations for their execution in Raipur during a press conference organized by the Press Information Bureau,…
item.content:encoded:
Raipur, September 30, 2026. With the effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, comprehensive changes are being made in Raipur to render the sanitation system more transparent, accountable, and result-oriented. Raipur Municipal Corporation Commissioner Mr. Sambit Mishra shared details of the key provisions of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and the preparations for their execution in Raipur during a press conference organized by the Press Information Bureau, Raipur.

Mr. Mishra stated that under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs selected 50 cities across the country under PRAGATI-50. The objective is to elevate cleanliness in these cities to a level where it is clearly visible to visitors. Raipur and Bilaspur from Chhattisgarh have been included among these selected cities. He said that in line with the vision of the Central and State Governments, efforts are being made to move beyond routine cleaning and develop a system that delivers visibly clear outcomes on the ground to advance Raipur towards becoming a world-class city.

He informed that under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, waste segregation at source has been made more comprehensive. Along with wet and dry waste, emphasis is now placed on keeping sanitary waste and special care waste separate. Sanitary waste includes items such as diapers and sanitary pads, while special care waste includes batteries, bulbs, tube lights, mercury thermometers, and other such items that require safe handling.

The Commissioner said that citizens should develop the habit of handing over waste in segregated categories. A system to collect all four categories of waste separately is also being developed within the Municipal Corporation’s collection setup. He noted that proper waste segregation at source makes the subsequent processing and disposal operations smoother and enables better recovery of useful resources from waste.

Greater Responsibility for Bulk Waste Generators

Mr. Mishra explained that the new rules outline specific responsibilities for bulk waste generating institutions and premises. Establishments generating large quantities of waste—such as large residential complexes, malls, commercial centers, institutions, hostels, and colleges—now have clearer waste management obligations.

He stated that wet waste generated within such premises should ideally be processed on-site wherever feasible. Systems such as composting or biomethanation can be adopted for this purpose. Similarly, for wastewater reuse, small-scale Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) can be installed as needed to recycle water for gardens and other suitable applications.

He added that where biogas plants are available, the respective institutions can route their wet waste to these plants through formal agreements. This will allow useful resources, such as biogas and energy, to be derived from waste.

The Commissioner emphasized that the new rules place special focus on digitization. Various stakeholders involved in waste management will be required to log their compliance details online, which will enhance transparency and accountability throughout the system.

Raipur to Be Divided into Four Clusters; Over 5,000 Beats to Be Monitored

Sharing details of the structural changes being made in Raipur's sanitation setup, Mr. Mishra stated that earlier monitoring and payment mechanisms were based on manpower numbers at the ward level. Now, Raipur city is being divided into four clusters to implement a beat-based, performance, and outcome-driven monitoring system.

He explained that distinct beats will be designated for roads, drains, parks, ponds, and other public places. For instance, a one-kilometer stretch of road, a one-to-two-kilometer section of a drain, or the perimeter around a park or pond could constitute a single beat. The designated agency will be entrusted with full sanitation responsibility for that specific beat.

He clarified that the new system will not focus on how many workers are deployed in a beat. Whether the agency utilizes manual labor or machinery, the primary goal of the Municipal Corporation will be ensuring actual, effective cleanliness in the specified area.

Before-and-after photographs of each beat's cleaning will be uploaded daily to a digital portal. The Commissioner stated that the total number of beats in Raipur could exceed 5,000. A central control center will be set up to monitor all these beats and review daily reporting.

He made it clear that the agency's payment will be linked directly to its performance and results. Deductions will be made from the payment if the expected level of cleanliness is not maintained in the assigned beat.

Real-Time Monitoring for Door-to-Door Waste Collection

During the press conference, journalists raised questions regarding the regularity of door-to-door waste collection in Raipur, as well as the monitoring and resolution of the high volume of incoming complaints.

In response, Mr. Mishra stated that the routes of door-to-door waste collection vehicles will be fully digitized. Fixed routes and schedules will be established for each vehicle. The exact time a vehicle is expected to reach a specific area or house will be tracked. Any deviation from the scheduled route or time will immediately trigger a flag in the digital system.

He explained that if a vehicle is scheduled to arrive at a household by 9:00 AM but arrives at 10:00 AM or 11:00 AM, this time delay will be registered in the system. Similarly, if a vehicle strays off its designated route, it will be tracked in real time.

He added that efforts are underway to provide citizens with a digital interface to lodge complaints. If a complaint is received regarding uncollected waste in a beat, the status of that specific beat can be inspected, and cleanliness can be verified using before-and-after photographs if necessary.

Adequate Waste Processing Capacity Available in Raipur

Addressing a question regarding Raipur's current waste management infrastructure, the Municipal Corporation Commissioner affirmed that the city possesses adequate capacity to process the volume of waste generated. He shared that remediation work at the old dump site in Sarona has been completed, and no new dump site is currently being created.

He noted that while basic infrastructure capacity exists in Raipur, monitoring has been the key gap affecting overall sanitation quality. The new beat-based system and digital tracking of door-to-door collection aim to eliminate this shortcoming.

Appeal to Citizens for Source Segregation

Mr. Mishra appealed to the citizens of Raipur to align with the spirit of the Solid Waste Management Rules and make waste segregation an integral part of their daily routine. He stated that cleanliness is not solely the responsibility of the Municipal Corporation, but a sustainable cleanliness framework can only be built through active citizen participation.

Referring to the Swachhata Hi Seva and Seva Sankalp campaigns, he urged citizens to personally contribute to maintaining cleanliness in their surroundings and set aside time to participate in sanitation drives. He concluded that waste segregation at source, responsible civic behavior, and a transparent monitoring system together will play a vital role in transforming Raipur into a cleaner and better city.

Additional Commissioner Mr. Vinod Pandey and Deputy Commissioner Mr. Jasdev Singh Babra of the Raipur Municipal Corporation were also present on the occasion.

 

*****

 

RDJ/KV/PJ/BKT

item.title: CAEPHT Concludes Three-Day PMFME Training on Meat Processing
item.description: The College of Agricultural Engineering and Post Harvest Technology (Central Agricultural University, Imphal), Ranipool, successfully concluded a three-day Beneficiary Training Programme on "Meat Processing" under the PMFME Scheme, organised from 28 to 30 September 2026 in collaboration with the Department of Food Processing Industries, Government of Sikkim. The programme trained 25 farmers from various districts of Sikkim in the preparation of value-added products such as chicken pickle, prawn…
item.content:encoded:
The College of Agricultural Engineering and Post Harvest Technology (Central Agricultural University, Imphal), Ranipool, successfully concluded a three-day Beneficiary Training Programme on "Meat Processing" under the PMFME Scheme, organised from 28 to 30 September 2026 in collaboration with the Department of Food Processing Industries, Government of Sikkim. The programme trained 25 farmers from various districts of Sikkim in the preparation of value-added products such as chicken pickle, prawn pickle and chicken sausages, along with practical exposure to micro-enterprise processing machinery, FSSAI standards, quality control, food hygiene, sanitation and packaging.

Following an internal assessment of the trainees, the valedictory session was graced by Mrs. Rashmi Kapil, Under Secretary, and Mr. Arjun Sadai, OSD, and other officials from Department of Food Processing Industries, Government of Sikkim, and Prof. N. S. Chauhan, Dean, CAEPHT. Mrs. Sangy Doma Bhutia, Trainer, motivated the participants to build confidence, take calculated risks and establish their own meat-processing units. Prof. Chauhan apprised the trainees of the academic and extension activities and custom hiring facilities of the college, and urged them to pursue entrepreneurship in meat value addition. Mr. Sadai stressed the need to channel the acquired skills into viable micro-processing enterprises in the state.

Feedback was collected from the participants to assess the effectiveness of the programme, after which certificates were distributed and the products prepared during the training were showcased. The programme was coordinated by Dr. Sujata Jena, Professor and Head, Department of Processing and Food Engineering, CAEPHT, in collaboration with Mr. Sajal Tamang and Mr. Naveen Sharma, Department of Food Processing Industries, Government of Sikkim.

item.title: Induction Programme for Newly Recruited Scientists, September 21-30, 2026 | CSIR-HRDC Campus, Ghaziabad
item.description:
The ten-day Induction Programme for Newly Recruited Scientists of CSIR was successfully organized from September 21-30, 2026 at CSIR-Human Resource Development Centre. The programme brought together thirty-eight young scientists from various CSIR laboratories across the country, providing them with a dynamic platform for learning, collaboration, and professional development.
The programme commenced on September 21, 2026 with an inspiring inaugural session that marked the beginning of…
item.content:encoded:
The ten-day Induction Programme for Newly Recruited Scientists of CSIR was successfully organized from September 21-30, 2026 at CSIR-Human Resource Development Centre. The programme brought together thirty-eight young scientists from various CSIR laboratories across the country, providing them with a dynamic platform for learning, collaboration, and professional development.

The programme commenced on September 21, 2026 with an inspiring inaugural session that marked the beginning of an enriching journey of innovation, scientific learning, and nation-building. The inaugural ceremony was formally conducted with the ceremonial lamp lighting by Dr. T. S. Rana, Head, CSIR-HRDC, Dr. Shobhna Choudhary Scientist F, CSIR-HRDC and Mrs. Preeti Chaudhary Sr. Technical Officer, CSIR-HRDC symbolizing the illumination of knowledge and ensuring a dynamic and enriching learning experience for all.

The induction programme was designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the scientific, administrative, and collaborativse ecosystem of CSIR while equipping participants with both technical expertise and behavioural competencies essential for effective scientific leadership. Throughout the programme, participants benefited from expert lectures delivered by eminent scientists and Directorate Heads from CSIR and other organisations like Dr. Vibha Malhotra Sahwney, Dr Manoj Semwal, Dr Jyoti Yadav, Dr Rama Swami Bansal, Dr Rama Swami Bansal, Dr Anirban Pal, Dr.  Debashis Bandyopadhyay Dr. Rajnish Kumar, IIT, BHU along with hands-on learning sessions and interactive discussions.

The programme also created valuable opportunities for networking and collaboration among scientists from different CSIR laboratories. Programme focused on fostering a holistic approach to professional growth through a blend of technical learning and behavioural development and enabled participants to strengthen their interpersonal skills alongside their professional competencies, preparing them to contribute effectively in multidisciplinary scientific environments. Participants explored key themes such as enhancing creative problem-solving and decision-making abilities, strengthening leadership effectiveness, and promoting innovation-driven scientific thinking. Technical sessions on AI in Drug Discovery and Development: Applications and Challenges, Technology Transfer, and Commercialisation provided valuable insights into translating scientific innovations into societal and industrial impact.

Adding a distinctive dimension to the learning experience, the programme went beyond conventional classroom instruction with a thoughtfully curated mix of interactive, experiential, and activity-based sessions that fostered active participation, collaborative learning, and professional engagement.

A key highlight was the participants’ involvement in the 85th CSIR Foundation Day celebrations at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi, providing young scientists with a unique opportunity to experience the broader CSIR ecosystem and its rich legacy of scientific excellence. Their interactions with eminent dignitaries, distinguished scientists, and professionals from leading scientific and research organisations offered valuable insights into the diverse dimensions of scientific research, innovation, and institutional leadership. The exposure not only enriched their understanding of CSIR’s multidisciplinary research landscape but also inspired them to envision their own roles in advancing scientific excellence, innovation and impactful research for the nation.

The valedictory function of the programme was held on September 30, 2026 and was graced by Prof. Manoj Kumar Dhar, Director, AcSIR as the Chief Guest. He joined the session online.  Addressing the newly recruited scientists, he motivated them to contribute actively towards innovation and impactful scientific research. He emphasised the importance of stronger collaboration between CSIR laboratories and the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research to achieve greater academic and research excellence, including a shared vision to attain the top rank among research and academic institutions.

The programme was seamlessly coordinated by Dr. Shobhna Choudhary, Scientist F and Mrs. Preeti Chaudhary, Sr. Technical Officer whose dedicated efforts ensured a vibrant, engaging, and enriching learning experience for all participants.

The successful completion of the induction programme reflects CSIR’s continued commitment towards nurturing the next generation of scientists and strengthening the nation’s scientific and innovation ecosystem through capacity building, leadership development, and collaborative research culture.

****

NKR/AK

item.title: Scientists map earliest glow of hydrogen, opening a new window to the universe
item.description:
In an international collaboration that includes researchers from India, the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment telescope (CHIME telescope) has made its first standalone detection of the glow of hydrogen from when the universe was about five billion years old, paving the way for new studies of cosmic expansion and dark energy.
The CHIME interferometric radio telescope in Canada was built to map the distribution of hydrogen gas in the early universe, allowing astronomers to…
item.content:encoded:
In an international collaboration that includes researchers from India, the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment telescope (CHIME telescope) has made its first standalone detection of the glow of hydrogen from when the universe was about five billion years old, paving the way for new studies of cosmic expansion and dark energy.

The CHIME interferometric radio telescope in Canada was built to map the distribution of hydrogen gas in the early universe, allowing astronomers to calculate its expansion and thus investigate dark energy, the mysterious force thought to be driving the universe to expand faster over time.

In a study that included CHIME collaborators at the Raman Research Institute (RRI), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the CHIME telescope has shown, for the first time, that it can detect the faint glow of hydrogen gas from deep in the universe's past using only its own data.

The breakthrough paves the way for a faster, less expensive method for scientists to study dark energy — the mysterious force thought to be driving the universe to expand at an ever-increasing rate, and one of the biggest open questions in physics. The achievement also marks a milestone for the telescope, built for this very reason. The findings are published in a paper today in The Astrophysical Journal.

Fig: A view of CHIME at night, with the Milky Way in the background Credit_ CHIME collaboration

 

“Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe and the raw material from which stars form,” said co-author Dr. Arnab Chakraborty, postdoctoral fellow at the University of Toronto who first proposed the finding. “Its faint radio emission acts like a cosmic tracer, revealing how matter is distributed across space.”

There are contradicting theories about the nature of dark energy in the astrophysical community. Using its own data, CHIME can investigate these theories independently and help prove or disprove them.

“This is a completely new technique for probing the cosmos, delivered by an instrument that was conceived, built and funded by Canadians,” said co-author Dr. Mark Halpern, professor in the University of British Columbia and CHIME principal investigator.

“CHIME is a unique instrument that scans a large fraction of the cosmos as the sky drifts over it. With no moving parts and high accuracy measurements, CHIME delivers a snapshot of what our sky looks at radio wavelengths everyday!”, added co-author Dr. Saurabh Singh, associate professor at RRI. 

Previously, CHIME had to cross-correlate its observations with galaxy survey data from other telescopes. Galaxy surveys investigate the same question, using light and focusing in fine detail. They cost millions more dollars, and they focus just on the part of the universe hot and dense enough to form stars.

By mapping the combined radio glow that hydrogen emits on its own, CHIME can explore the same questions at a greater scale, further back in time, at a fraction of the cost and without relying on anyone else’s results.

In an accompanying paper, the researchers examined what the observed signal reveals about the distribution of hydrogen in the universe.

“Our data indicate that roughly two per cent of the hydrogen in the universe was in neutral atomic form at this time, broadly consistent with other measurements” said co-author Dr. Shabbir Shaikh, postdoctoral fellow at Arizona State University. “By measuring how that hydrogen is distributed and clustered, CHIME gives us a new way to test our understanding of how galaxies form and evolve”.

The finding wasn’t a Eureka moment. The research applied new data analysis and processing techniques to find the faint signal amongst the overwhelming noise of the background universe, human technology and even the instrument itself. They then spent more than a year testing the finding to prove it was correct: it was indeed a call from the universe itself when it was about five billion years old, based on 94 nights of observation data collected in 2019.

The current measurement uses only a small fraction of the data CHIME has collected since operations began. Researchers now have nearly seven years of observations available and are working to expand the analysis to include earlier periods in cosmic history when the universe was only three billion years old. 

 

Publication Link: DOI 10.3847/1538-4357/ae9835

 

***

NKR/FT/AA

item.title: Department of Youth Affairs Gears Up for Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-Waste
item.description:
The Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports is gearing up to undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters has been organised annually since 2021 with the objective of institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible disposal of e-waste and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across Government offices.
Special Campaign 6.0 will…
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports is gearing up to undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters has been organised annually since 2021 with the objective of institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible disposal of e-waste and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across Government offices.

Special Campaign 6.0 will place particular emphasis on “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste”. The campaign is being undertaken in two phases, with the Preparatory Phase from 15th to 30th September 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

During the Preparatory Phase, the Department is undertaking identification of pending references received from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), VIPs, State Governments and matters relating to Parliament Assurances. The Department is also assessing the volume of redundant materials to be disposed of and finalising procedures for their disposal. In line with the focus of the campaign, measures are also being undertaken for effective collection and segregation of e-waste in accordance with the guidelines of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), with targets being finalised for the Implementation Phase.

The Preparatory Phase is also focusing on strengthening record management and space management practices across the Department and its organisations. These measures are aimed at ensuring systematic disposal of redundant materials, efficient utilisation of available office space and strengthening institutional practices related to cleanliness and resource management.

The Department has already undertaken measures towards effective e-waste management and digitisation of records. E-waste from Shastri Bhawan was auctioned in December 2025, generating revenue of ₹2,35,100. Further, scanning and digitisation of physical files and records was completed in January 2026.

Building on the achievements of previous years, the Department of Youth Affairs, along with its attached office, subordinate offices including field offices and autonomous body, is fully geared up to roll out Special Campaign 6.0. The Department remains committed to strengthening Swachhata practices, reducing pendency, improving record and space management, and ensuring responsible management and disposal of e-waste.

*****

Pawan Singh Faujdar

item.title: CAQM Reviews Preparedness for Stubble-Burning Prevention, Vehicular and Industrial Emission Control
item.description: The Sub-Committee on Safeguarding & Enforcement of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) convened its 26th meeting on 29.09.2026 under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM. The meeting comprehensively reviewed the status of preparedness, enforcement and compliance measures being undertaken by the concerned NCR State Governments/ GNCTD and implementing agencies for targeted abatement of air pollution across the National Capital Region…
item.content:encoded:
The Sub-Committee on Safeguarding & Enforcement of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) convened its 26th meeting on 29.09.2026 under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM. The meeting comprehensively reviewed the status of preparedness, enforcement and compliance measures being undertaken by the concerned NCR State Governments/ GNCTD and implementing agencies for targeted abatement of air pollution across the National Capital Region (NCR).

During the meeting, detailed deliberations were held on sector-specific measures and implementation of various statutory directions issued by the Commission. The Sub-committee took stock of the preparedness of Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh for implementation of Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026 and the respective action plans for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning during 2026, with the objective of complete elimination of such incidents. The review also covered measures for crop diversification, promotion of Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), utilisation of crop residue and strengthening of awareness and IEC activities among farmers.

The Sub-Committee undertook a comprehensive review of measures for abatement of vehicular pollution, including actions envisaged under Direction No. 88 dated 23.04.2025, as amended on 17.10.2025, relating to restrictions on entry of BS-IV and below transport and commercial goods vehicles into Delhi. The implementation of Direction No. 93 dated 03.06.2025 concerning migration of buses entering Delhi, including buses operating under All India Tourist Permit and other service regimes, towards cleaner modes was also reviewed.

The meeting further examined the preparedness of NCR State Governments/ GNCTD for installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) systems at Fuel/ CNG stations, in accordance with Direction No. 101 dated 15.05.2026, for enforcement of restrictions on fuelling of vehicles without valid Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) in NCR with effect from 01.10.2026. The Sub-Committee also reviewed enforcement of Direction No. 94 dated 03.06.2025, as amended on 23.12.2025, for fast-tracking cleaner mobility in services provided by motor vehicle aggregators, delivery service providers and e-Commerce entities, including compliance verification through surprise checks.

The status of enforcement against older End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, in compliance with the Supreme Court of India’s order dated 17.12.2025 was also deliberated upon, with emphasis on intensifying action for impounding and scrapping of such vehicles. Further, the sub-committee reviewed progress towards complete phasing out of diesel auto-rickshaws from NCR Districts by 31.12.2026 in accordance with Direction No. 70 dated 30.11.2022. Measures for identification and decongestion of traffic congestion hotspots/ intersections in Delhi and NCR towns were also reviewed, including deployment of Integrated Traffic Management Systems (ITMS) with ANPR-based automated challaning.

The Sub-Committee also reviewed the status of implementation of Direction No. 103 dated 19.08.2026 regarding prevention and control of air pollution from stone crushing units in NCR. Implementation of Direction No. 98 dated 20.02.2026 relating to stringent emission standards for industries across Delhi-NCR was also reviewed.

With winter season approaching, the meeting accorded focused attention on procurement of additional Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) and their deployment before commencement of the winter season, particularly for removal of dust from identified dust hotspots. 

The Sub-Committee further took stock of the Action Taken Report on incognito/surprise inspections of C&D sites, industries and DG sets, as part of strengthened compliance monitoring and enforcement of the commission’s statutory directions. The meeting also reviewed the status of timely resolution of complaints received through social media platforms and tagged by CPCB to the concerned agencies in GNCTD and NCR States, in accordance with the Directions of the Supreme Court of India.

The concerned implementing agencies were emphasized upon to ensure strict, coordinated and time-bound implementation of the commission’s statutory directions, with particular focus on preparedness for the forthcoming winter season, effective enforcement in the vehicular and industrial sectors, prevention of stubble burning, mitigation of road and C&D dust and strengthening of inspection and compliance-monitoring mechanisms across NCR.

The Sub-Committee reiterated the importance of sustained and coordinated efforts by all concerned agencies to ensure effective implementation of sector-specific measures and to strengthen enforcement mechanisms. Further, all implementing agencies reaffirmed their commitment to undertake strict, targeted and time-bound actions for effective implementation of the Commission’s Directions.

*****

VM/GS/SK

item.title: BIS Organizes MSME Meet and Manak Manthan for Fly Ash-Based Brick and Cement Sector at Satna
item.description: Satna, The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Bhopal Branch Office (BPBO), organized an MSME Meet and Manak Manthan programme for manufacturers, traders, and MSME units associated with the fly ash-based brick and cement sector at Hotel Park, Satna, on 29 September 2026. The objective of the programme was to create awareness about BIS activities and establish interaction with industry stakeholders on issues related to Quality Control Orders (QCOs), applicable Indian Standards, compliance…
item.content:encoded:
Satna,  The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Bhopal Branch Office (BPBO), organized an MSME Meet and Manak Manthan programme for manufacturers, traders, and MSME units associated with the fly ash-based brick and cement sector at Hotel Park, Satna, on 29 September 2026. The objective of the programme was to create awareness about BIS activities and establish interaction with industry stakeholders on issues related to Quality Control Orders (QCOs), applicable Indian Standards, compliance requirements, and certification procedures. Around 40 participants from the cement industry and MSME sector participated in the programme.

The programme commenced with the welcome address by Shri Mohammad Rizwan, Director & Head, BIS BPBO. He welcomed the representatives of the fly ash-based brick and cement industry, including the President and General Secretary of Vindhya Chamber of Commerce, Satna. He highlighted the role of BIS standards in promoting a quality culture and strengthening the quality ecosystem in the country. During the interaction session, participants were also apprised of the various benefits, incentives, and concessions provided by the BIS for MSME units. The discussion covered support provisions related to quality improvement, technology upgradation, and ease of doing business.

In his address as the Chief Guest, Shri Satish Sukheja highlighted the importance of such programmes in strengthening interaction and collaboration between BIS and industries. He stated that such initiatives provide an effective platform for stakeholders to understand quality-related issues, standards, and compliance requirements, and to share their suggestions for improving quality.

Shri Hariom Meena, Scientist-C/Deputy Director, BIS BPBO, delivered two technical presentations. The first presentation provided an overview of BIS activities, including standard formulation, conformity assessment, certification, promotion of standards, and stakeholder participation in the standardization process. The session also helped MSME representatives understand the available support mechanisms and utilize them effectively for enhancing quality and competitiveness.

The second presentation under Manak Manthan focused on IS 16720:2018 – Pulverized Fuel Ash-Cement Bricks — Specification. Participants were briefed about the objective, scope, and key provisions of the standard, followed by discussions on quality and compliance requirements. During the technical discussion and question-answer session, participants shared practical issues related to fly ash-based industries, including sampling methodology, testing procedures, laboratory requirements, acceptance criteria, sample handling, documentation, and BIS certification requirements.

The programme enhanced awareness among industry stakeholders regarding BIS standards and certification requirements and strengthened the compliance preparedness of MSME units. BIS BPBO reiterated its commitment to continued engagement with manufacturers, traders, and MSMEs through awareness and technical consultation programmes for effective implementation of standards.

item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal arrived in Milwaukee, United States of America, to attend the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting. He was received by , Consul General, Consulate General of India, Chicago, Dr. M. Anand Prakash, upon his arrival.

Shri Piyush Goyal interacted with CEOs and senior executives of prominent U.S. manufacturing and technology companies of the United States (U.S.) at a business roundtable hosted by the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM). NAM represents a substantial share of leading U.S. manufacturing companies, contributing significantly to the U.S. manufacturing GDP of around $3 trillion.

During the interaction, Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted that the India-U.S. economic relationship is moving beyond a traditional trade relationship and increasingly encompasses investment, manufacturing, technology, innovation, resilient supply chains and the creation of high-value capabilities in both countries.

The CEOs and senior executives shared their views on the opportunities emerging in India and their companies’ perspectives on expanding partnerships in the country. Shri Piyush Goyal stated that the Government of India is ready to facilitate companies in their operations, expansion and investments in India.

Shri Piyush Goyal also attended a reception hosted by the Business Roundtable (BRT) and NAM at the global headquarters of Rockwell Automation. He interacted with Trade Ministers from other G20 countries and senior business leaders of U.S. companies.

item.content:encoded:
By PIB Mumbai

Nagpur, September 30, 2026

Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) will celebrate its 27th Foundation Day on October 1, 2026, marking 26 years since its establishment in 2000. Over the years, BSNL has been providing telecommunications services across the country and has witnessed the transition from traditional landline networks to mobile, broadband and other digital communication technologies.

As a 100 per cent Government of India-owned Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, BSNL provides mobile, Bharat Fiber FTTH broadband, fixed-line and enterprise services. The organisation has also been associated with the expansion of telecom infrastructure in rural, remote and strategically important areas and with the implementation of national initiatives such as BharatNet.

In the Vidarbha region, the BSNL Nagpur Business Area has undertaken expansion and upgradation of its telecom infrastructure, including optical fibre deployment and Bharat Fiber services. The network covers Nagpur and adjoining areas, including industrial locations such as Butibori and Hingna, besides serving government offices, educational institutions, hospitals and other establishments.

On the occasion of the Foundation Day, Principal General Manager, BSNL Nagpur Business Area, Smt. Namratta Tiwari, extended her greetings to the employees and stakeholders of the organisation. She noted that BSNL’s ongoing network expansion, including the rollout of 4G services, is part of its continued efforts to meet the changing communication requirements of users.

item.description:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has commenced the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 from 15th to 30th September 2026, focusing on institutionalizing Swachhata , minimizing pendency, improving record management and enhancing efficiency in Government offices.
Building on the previous year’s focus on scientific management of e-waste, this year’s campaign emphasizes effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste in accordance with MoEFCC…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has commenced the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6.0 from 15th to 30th September 2026, focusing on institutionalizing Swachhata, minimizing pendency, improving record management and enhancing efficiency in Government offices.

Building on the previous year’s focus on scientific management of e-waste, this year’s campaign emphasizes effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste in accordance with MoEFCC guidelines and the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. C-MET, an autonomous society under MeitY, is undertaking the scientific management of e-waste generated by MeitY in accordance with the prescribed procedures.

As part of the preparatory phase, regular review meetings at the level of Additional Secretary and senior officers are being held to monitor progress and ensure timely implementation of campaign activities.

A comprehensive inspection of record rooms has been undertaken to identify obsolete and redundant records for weeding and strengthen record management. Nodal Officers have also been identified at the Division level for weeding of physical files, closure of e-files and identification of pending references, including references relating to Hon’ble Members of Parliament, PMO, Parliamentary Assurances and public grievances.

Identification of e-waste has already been completed, and its disposal through C-MET is underway, facilitating the optimal utilization of office space and infrastructure. MeitY is also undertaking cleanliness and space-management activities in its premises and associated offices, including the clearance and disposal of unused, redundant and discarded materials..

The preparatory phase will provide the groundwork for the implementation phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026, during which identified pendency, records and other activities will be monitored for timely disposal, closure or completion.

Through sustained monitoring and coordinated action, MeitY is committed to institutionalizing Swachhata, minimizing pendency, optimizing resources and improving efficiency in Government functioning, in alignment with the Government’s vision of a Swachh Bharat.

 

****

Vinod Kumar / Dhanya Ranjan

item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, 30 September 2026

 

As part of the NPS Diwas 2026 campaign, the NPS Sanchay Yatra will be flagged off on 1st October 2026 by the Finance Minister of India from New Delhi. In West Bengal, the Yatra will travel across various cities and districts of the State from 1st to 15th October 2026 to spread awareness about the National Pension System (NPS) and the importance of pension planning for a financially secure future.

The NPS Sanchay Yatra will commence from Kolkata on Thursday, 1st October 2026. During its visit, trained representatives will explain the features and benefits of NPS Sanchay, guide citizens on account opening and contributions, and address their queries. Awareness material will also be distributed during the campaign.

Officials of Punjab National Bank and other banks will be present to assist citizens and provide information related to NPS Sanchay and pension planning.

Citizens of Kolkata are invited to visit the Sanchay Yatra Van, learn about NPS Sanchay and take steps towards planning for a secure financial future. The campaign seeks to strengthen pension awareness among citizens and encourage greater understanding of the importance of systematic pension planning.

item.title: DGTS, Mumbai Zonal Unit Organises Outreach Programme on GST and Economic Integration at Goa University
item.description:
:Mumbai/Panaji, September 30, 2026
The Directorate General of Taxpayer Services (DGTS), Mumbai Zonal Unit, under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, in association with Goa University, organised an Outreach Programme on “GST in India: From Tax Reforms to Economic Integration” at Goa Business School, Goa University, Panaji, today.
The programme was organised in association with the…
item.content:encoded:
:Mumbai/Panaji, September 30, 2026

The Directorate General of Taxpayer Services (DGTS), Mumbai Zonal Unit, under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, in association with Goa University, organised an Outreach Programme on “GST in India: From Tax Reforms to Economic Integration” at Goa Business School, Goa University, Panaji, today.

The programme was organised in association with the Manohar Parrikar School of Law, Governance and Public Policy (MPSLGPP) and Goa Business School (GBS). It brought together faculty members, tax administration officers, students and academic scholars to promote awareness of GST, tax reforms and their role in economic integration.

The programme commenced with the Welcome Address by Sr. Prof. Purva Hegde Dessai, Dean, Goa Business School. Shri Sumit Kumar, Principal Additional Director General, DGTS, Mumbai Zonal Unit, delivered the Keynote Address. He explained the basic framework of GST and highlighted reforms aimed at simplifying compliance, reducing trade barriers, facilitating movement of goods and services and strengthening transparency in tax administration.

The technical session was delivered by CA Shridhar alias Yatish G. Pai Vernekar, Chartered Accountant, Goa. He provided practical insights into GST compliance, statutory books of accounts, electronic compliance and digital reporting.

Students and faculty from M.Com, LL.M. and MBA (Financial Services) programmes actively participated in the interactive session. The programme concluded with the Vote of Thanks by Dr. Kedar Chandrakant, Joint Director, DGTS, Mumbai Zonal Unit.

Earlier, on September 29, 2026, DGTS, MZU, in collaboration with CGST Goa Commissionerate and BITS Pilani, K. K. Birla Goa Campus, organised an outreach programme for students on emerging trends in GST, digital tax administration, data-driven taxpayer services and compliance.

With these initiatives, DGTS, MZU has conducted or participated in 54 outreach programmes since April 2026, comprising 32 Seminars/Webinars/Hybrid events and 22 Interactive Sessions. These initiatives aim to promote taxpayer awareness, voluntary compliance and stakeholder engagement.

***

item.description:
By PIB Mumbai
Nagpur
Recognised as one of the premier events of the NCC Air Wing, the All India Vayu Sainik Camp (AIVSC) brings together cadets from 17 Directorates to demonstrate their flying skills, discipline, leadership and teamwork under rigorous training standards. The Maharashtra Air Wing Contingent underwent a structured and progressive training programme through the Inter Group Competition (IGC), followed by Pre-Vayu Sainik Camp–1 (PVSC-1) and Pre-Vayu Sainik Camp–2…
item.content:encoded:
By PIB Mumbai

Nagpur

Recognised as one of the premier events of the NCC Air Wing, the All India Vayu Sainik Camp (AIVSC) brings together cadets from 17 Directorates to demonstrate their flying skills, discipline, leadership and teamwork under rigorous training standards. The Maharashtra Air Wing Contingent underwent a structured and progressive training programme through the Inter Group Competition (IGC), followed by Pre-Vayu Sainik Camp–1 (PVSC-1) and Pre-Vayu Sainik Camp–2 (PVSC-2). These successive stages provided the cadets with intensive training and opportunities to refine their skills across various domains in preparation for the national-level camp.

The backbone of Maharashtra’s preparation has been the training establishment at Headquarters Maintenance Command, Indian Air Force, Nagpur, where meticulously planned training sessions were conducted. The PI staff worked continuously to hone the cadets’ skills through sustained training, guidance and dedication. Wing Commander V. Deepika Rao, Camp Commandant, Group Captain Santosh Babu, Commanding Officer, 1 MAH AIR SQN and Wing Commander Arpan Chanda, 3 MAH AIR SQN, provided guidance and mentorship throughout the preparation.

No. 2 MAH AIR SQN, Nagpur, once again served as the launching and preparatory unit and played a significant role in the successful conduct of the training process. The unit contributed towards organising the camps, facilitating the training of the cadets, and ensuring the timely distribution of kitting and other essential items required for their participation. Its continued support and coordination contributed significantly to the systematic preparation of the Maharashtra contingent.

Major General Vivek Tyagi, ADG, NCC Directorate Maharashtra, virtually interacted with the contingent and motivated the cadets. Brigadier Manish Sharma, DDG, NCC Directorate Maharashtra and Group Captain Khushal Vyas, Group Commander, Nagpur Group also visited the camp to oversee the training.

The cadets underwent intensive training across diverse domains. Firing practice with .22 rifles and skeet shooting strengthened accuracy and endurance, while powered flying, gliding and simulator sessions prepared the cadets for the prestigious Best Pilot Competition. Aeromodelling enhanced their technical knowledge and understanding of aviation technology. Drill and tent pitching were practised with emphasis on coordination and synchronisation, while classroom sessions strengthened theoretical knowledge of aircraft systems, aviation principles and air regulations.

The Maharashtra Directorate moves forward with a contingent that embodies the core values of the NCC - discipline, resilience, precision, teamwork and commitment to excellence. AIVSC provides a demanding national platform for cadets to demonstrate their technical proficiency, leadership, teamwork and dedication.

The All India Vayu Sainik Camp 2026 commences on 30 September at Air Force Station Tambaram, Chennai. Over the next 14 days, the Maharashtra contingent will participate in a series of demanding competitions and activities. The coming fortnight will provide the cadets an opportunity to translate their intensive training, discipline and perseverance into performance on the national platform.
