item.title: NHAI to Conduct Special Quality Checks on Projects with Abnormally Low Quoted Bids
item.description: To strengthen quality control and adherence to the highest quality standards during construction of National Highway projects, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is undertaking special quality inspections of 17 under construction National Highway projects, whose bid value was lower than the estimated project cost by over 15 percent. The inspections are in addition to NHAI’s regular quality checks and are aimed at identifying any quality-related issues at an early stage so that…
item.content:encoded:
To strengthen quality control and adherence to the highest quality standards during construction of National Highway projects, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is undertaking special quality inspections of 17 under construction National Highway projects, whose bid value was lower than the estimated project cost by over 15 percent.  The inspections are in addition to NHAI’s regular quality checks and are aimed at identifying any quality-related issues at an early stage so that corrective action can be taken on time. The first round of inspections is scheduled to be completed by December 2026. NHAI will re-inspect the identified projects after 6 months with a different team of experts to ensure quality and adherence to construction standards.

17 projects selected based on specific criteria

The 17 projects have been selected using three criteria: construction cost of more than ₹500 crore, tender discount of over 15% and physical progress between 35% and 80%. These criteria help focus quality checks on projects that are at an important stage of construction and adopt an objective, data-driven approach.

The projects include greenfield and access-controlled corridors, bypasses, as well as four and six laning works in the states of Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh.

Experienced engineers to conduct inspections

In order to reinforce quality mechanism and ensure compliance, NHAI has created a pool of experts. The inspections will be carried out by specialised teams led by 39 experienced and retired engineers from various government organisations, including the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Defence and State Public Works Departments. Technical experts will also support the teams during the inspections.

Quality of construction, materials and safety to be checked

The teams will check construction work against approved drawings, technical specifications, contract conditions and project-specific quality plans. They will examine the quality of construction materials, workmanship, construction methods as well as records of sampling and testing.

The inspections will also cover road safety measures, traffic management and environmental safeguards, wherever applicable. Any work that does not meet the required standards will be identified and followed up for corrective action as per the applicable contract provisions.

The specialised inspections will also help NHAI to identify common quality issues, construction practices and areas where greater accountability is required from contractors, consultants and other project stakeholders.

The initiative is part of NHAI’s continued efforts to strengthen quality monitoring of ongoing National Highway projects and ensure timely corrective action, with the objective of developing a world class National Highway network across the country.

***

GDH/DS

item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs celebrated Hindi Pakhwada(Hindi Fortnight) with great enthusiasm from September 14 to 30, 2026. On Hindi Diwas (September 14, 2026), a message of felicitation was issued by the Union

Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs.

During the fortnight, the ministry organized various competitions, including Hindi typing, Hindi dictation, quizzes, Hindi noting and drafting, translation, and essay/poetry writing. Officials participated actively in these competitions.

During the closing ceremony organised on September 30, 2026, the Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs motivated the employees to dispose their official tasks in Hindi. He emphasized that efforts to work in Hindi should not be limited only to the Hindi Fortnight but should continue throughout the year.

 

[Dr. Satya Prakash, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs addressing the officials of the Ministry]

 

Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, in his address stated that the government's policy is not limited just to preserving the language, but aims to connect it with the mainstream of governance, administration, science, and modern technology. He urged to use simple Hindi, noting that the simpler and more comprehensible a language is, the more effective it will be.

 

[Shri Nikunj Bihari Dhal, Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs addressing the officials of the Ministry]

 

[Ministry's Hindi e-magazine "Sansadiya Sarita" released]

 

On this occasion, the Secretary released a Hindi e-magazine named 'Sansadiya Sarita', featuring creative works by the ministry's staff. It is a compilation of the creative talent and maturity of the officials of the Ministry. The e-magazine has been published on the Ministry's official website. Along with the release of the e-magazine, the Secretary also distributed prizes to the winners of various competitions.

item.title: Monthly Review of Accounts of Union Government of India upto the month of August 2026 (FY 2026-27)

item.content:encoded:
The Monthly Accounts of the Union Government of India upto the month of August, 2026 has been consolidated and reports published. The highlights are given below: -

The Government of India has received ₹13,67,709 crore (37.5% of corresponding BE 2026-27 of Total Receipts) upto August, 2026 comprising ₹8,37,921 crore Tax Revenue (Net to Centre), ₹4,54,549 crore of Non-Tax Revenue and ₹75,239 crore of Non-Debt Capital Receipts. ₹5,90,391 crore has been transferred to State Governments as Devolution of Share of Taxes by Government of India during this period which is ₹60,243 crore lower than the previous year.

Total Expenditure incurred by Government of India is ₹20,77,958 crore (38.9% of corresponding BE 2026-27), out of which ₹15,68,009 crore is on Revenue Account and ₹5,09,949 crore is on Capital Account. Out of the Total Revenue Expenditure, ₹5,14,810 crore is on account of Interest Payments and ₹1,87,037 crore is on account of Major Subsidies.

****

SR/Sri

item.content:encoded:
Durgapur, September30, 2026

 

Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal launched the PRAGATI-50 initiative to develop 50 model cities for Swachhata in New Delhi on Tuesday (September 29, 2026), alongside key technology-driven urban cleanliness projects including the 'Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre' at CSIR-CMERI Durgapur. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 (SBM-U 2.0), the PRAGATI-50 framework focuses on key performance indicators (KPIs) and digital monitoring across 50 cities in 24 States to establish visible benchmarks for urban sanitation.

Speaking at the launch ceremony, the Union Minister said “These 50 cities across 24 States will emerge as clean role model cities for the rest of the country, by going beyond their routine sanitation work to demonstrate sustained, high-performance parameters of visible cleanliness.

Highlighting the national significance of the facility, Dr. N. C. Murmu, Director, CSIR-CMERI, stated, “The Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre has been established as a national facility for research, product development, testing, validation, certification, and capacity building in sanitation technologies.”

Key Highlights of Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre

ü National Innovation Hub: Established as a national facility in collaboration with CSIR-CMERI for research, product development, testing, validation, certification, and capacity building in sanitation technologies.

ü Bridging Lab-to-Field: Accelerates the deployment of cutting-edge tech solutions, automation, and machine learning tools into active urban municipal operations.

ü Standardization & Capacity Building: Assists Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) with technical guidelines, model designs, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and GeM categorization for waste management infrastructure.

ü Circular Economy Drive: Promotes resource recovery, occupational safety, and sustainable waste processing toward the goal of garbage-free cities under Viksit Bharat 2047.

item.content:encoded:
Goa, 30 September, 2026

Goa’s international charter tourism season for 2026-27 got off to a promising start on Wednesday 30 September  with the arrival of the first international charter flight operated by Aeroflot at Goa International Airport, Dabolim.

The inaugural charter flight was welcomed with traditional Goan hospitality, featuring live Goan music, a welcome with rose petals and a cake-cutting ceremony. Shri Mauvin Godinho, Minister for Protocol, Hospitality and Legislative Affairs, Government of Goa, welcomed the arriving international passengers along with Flt Lt Akash Deep, Airport Director, representatives of the Airports Authority of India (AAI), Goa Tourism Department and other airport stakeholders.

Speaking on the occasion, Flt Lt Akash Deep, Airport Director, Goa International Airport, said that, Dabolim Airport has consistently served as a gateway that reflects Goa’s warmth, culture and hospitality. He expressed his delight at welcoming international tourists arriving on the first Aeroflot charter flight of the season.

With the commencement of the charter season, the airport has made necessary arrangements to handle the anticipated increase in international passenger traffic. Dedicated immigration counters have been strengthened, customs clearance processes streamlined and ground support services enhanced to ensure a swift and seamless experience for arriving passengers. He also reaffirmed the airport’s commitment to providing efficient services and ensuring passenger convenience.

The commencement of charter flight operations marks an important beginning to the new tourism season and is expected to further strengthen Goa’s international tourism connectivity.

The resumption of Aeroflot’s charter services has been facilitated through sustained coordination and efforts by the Airports Authority of India with the concerned civil aviation authorities, the airline and ground handling agencies.

Airports Authority of India has undertaken concerted efforts to ensure the availability of necessary operational infrastructure, efficient ground handling and smooth passenger movement for international charter arrivals at Dabolim.

Russian tourists have traditionally constituted an important segment of international visitors to Goa. The resumption of Aeroflot’s charter services is expected to provide fresh momentum to the tourism sector, benefiting hotels and beach resorts in North and South Goa, local transport operators, restaurants and other tourism-related businesses.

Goa International Airport, Dabolim, operated by the Airports Authority of India, plays an important role in connecting the State with major domestic and international destinations. Airports Authority of India continues to focus on upgrading airport infrastructure, enhancing passenger amenities and supporting the growth of the civil aviation and tourism sectors in Goa.

***

Source- Goa International Airport, Dabolim/PIB Panaji/AY/Parshuram Kor

item.title: Digital India BHASHINI Division and CAG Launch “CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad” to Enable AI-powered Multilingual Translation of Official Documents
item.description: The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India , in collaboration with the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) , today launched “CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad” , an AI-enabled document translation solution developed by BHASHINI to support the translation of official CAG documents and audit-related reports. The solution was launched during the closing…
item.content:encoded:
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), today launched “CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad”, an AI-enabled document translation solution developed by BHASHINI to support the translation of official CAG documents and audit-related reports. The solution was launched during the closing ceremony of the 74th Hindi Diwas and Hindi Pakhwada 2026 at the CAG Office, New Delhi.

 

The event was attended by Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Comptroller and Auditor General of India, along with senior CAG officials, including Shri A. M. Bajaj, Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General; Dr. Nilotpal Goswami, Additional Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General; and Shri Atoorva Sinha, Director General, as well as other officials and dignitaries.

The launch marks an important step in bringing Language AI into institutional workflows, combining BHASHINI’s multilingual language technology capabilities with the specialised language requirements of the CAG. The initiative is designed to support translation of official and audit-related documents while complementing existing institutional processes and maintaining appropriate human oversight.

CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad has been developed as a customised Language AI solution for the CAG, with a focus on supporting consistent terminology, contextual translation and quality of output. The solution provides an AI-enabled environment for translation of official documents while addressing institutional requirements relating to security, controlled access and data sovereignty.

The collaboration reflects the broader potential of Language AI to support government institutions in making official information more accessible across languages. By integrating multilingual AI capabilities into established institutional processes, the initiative seeks to facilitate wider and more efficient access to official information in Indian languages.

The programme featured a presentation on Digital India BHASHINI’s Language AI capabilities, highlighting its applications across government and public-facing services. The event also marked the formal launch of the CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad solution at the CAG Office.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, highlighted the evolution of BHASHINI across language data and AI models, applications and use cases, and the development of a sovereign Language AI ecosystem suited to India’s linguistic diversity.

He highlighted that BHASHINI currently supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, and is being applied across a growing range of public-service use cases. These include multilingual agricultural advisory, voice-enabled grievance registration and processing, and conversational services that enable access through voice and telephone-based interfaces.

Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Comptroller and Auditor General of India, emphasised the importance of ensuring that audit findings and reports reach citizens in languages they understand. He highlighted the potential of technology to facilitate access to audit information in local and regional languages, while complementing efforts to strengthen the use of Hindi and other Indian languages in official work.

Shri Nilotpal Goswami, Additional Deputy Comptroller & Auditor General (Rajbhasha), Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, said, “The fusion of artificial intelligence and communication has the potential to overcome linguistic barriers across geographies. By integrating language technology into our institutional processes, we can make communication more accessible, timely and effective, while strengthening the use of Indian languages in governance and official work. The CAG-BHASHINI initiative is an important step in bringing this convergence of language and technology into practice.”

 

BHASHINI and CAG collaborate on technology-enabled Hindi Pakhwada activities

The collaboration between CAG and BHASHINI also extended to the Hindi Pakhwada 2026 programme, organised from 14 to 29 September 2026. Alongside conventional Hindi language activities, the collaboration introduced technology-enabled language activities and games developed with BHASHINI, providing officers and employees an opportunity to engage with language technology in an interactive format.

A large number of officers and employees participated in various competitions and activities during the Hindi Pakhwada. The programme included activities related to official language usage, Hindi noting and drafting, translation, typing and other language-based skills, along with BHASHINI-enabled activities.The winners of the competitions were felicitated and awarded prizes during the closing ceremony. The ceremony also included the presentation of awards and certificates to the winners, recognising their participation and performance during Hindi Pakhwada.

The programme featured a presentation on the use of digital language technologies, along with demonstrations and activities aimed at familiarising officials with the growing role of technology in Hindi and Indian-language usage. The collaboration demonstrated how Language AI can support not only translation and official workflows, but also interactive language engagement and participation within government institutions.

The launch of CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad, together with the technology-enabled Hindi Pakhwada activities, represents a broader collaboration between CAG and BHASHINI to explore practical applications of Language AI in institutional settings. The initiative brings together language technology, human expertise and institutional requirements to support greater multilingual access to official information.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.

****

Vinod Kumar / Dhanya Ranjan

item.content:encoded:
As part of Special Campaign 6, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal & Mines, reviewed the progress and preparations of Coal India Limited (CIL) for Special Campaign 6 along with Secretary (Coal), Chairman CIL, CMDs and other Senior officers, of Subsidiaries, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and liquidating pendency, with a special thrust on ‘Waste to Wealth’ and ‘e-Waste Management’.

 

Key Highlights and Preparatory Initiatives

Promoting Cleanliness Awareness: South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL)

Cleanliness Awareness Walkathon at Vasant Vihar, Bilaspur, in which children enthusiastically participated and spread the message of cleanliness and environmental awareness.

 

Street play on the theme “Our Threshold, Our Waste” at the SECL Headquarters premises in Bilaspur. Through the street play, the importance of cleanliness, proper waste disposal, and individual responsibility for maintaining a clean and healthy environment in one’s surroundings were presented in an effective and engaging manner.

Identification of sites for cleaning: The Ministry of Coal, along with Coal India Limited and all Coal PSUs, has identified 1,565 sites for cleaning under Special Campaign 6, to be undertaken from 2 October to 31 October.

File Management: 19,499 physical files and 40,094 e-files have been marked for review to improve operational efficiency and ensure quick retrieval of records.

Ministry of Coal is geared up for achieving all targets within the stipulated timelines under Special Campaign 6, reinforcing the Government’s vision of efficient governance and transparency.

item.title: IndianOil’s Gujarat Refinery Marks 60 Years of Pioneering Excellence and Nation-Building
item.description:
IndianOil’s Gujarat Refinery is in its Diamond Jubilee year, marking six decades since its dedication to the nation in 1966. From its early years as a cornerstone of India’s indigenous refining capability, Gujarat Refinery has evolved into a major integrated refinery-petrochemicals complex, combining capacity growth with technological innovation, product diversification and an expanding focus on sustainability.
Commissioned in 1965 and dedicated to the nation on 18 October 1966,…
item.content:encoded:
IndianOil’s Gujarat Refinery is in its Diamond Jubilee year, marking six decades since its dedication to the nation in 1966. From its early years as a cornerstone of India’s indigenous refining capability, Gujarat Refinery has evolved into a major integrated refinery-petrochemicals complex, combining capacity growth with technological innovation, product diversification and an expanding focus on sustainability.

Commissioned in 1965 and dedicated to the nation on 18 October 1966, Gujarat Refinery has grown from an initial capacity of 2 MMTPA to 13.7 MMTPA, with capacity being further expanded to 18 MMTPA under the ongoing LuPech Project. The refinery expansion took place through successive rounds of debottlenecking, technology upgradation, and capacity augmentation. Over six decades, the refinery has consistently been at the forefront of technological advancements, pioneering many ‘firsts’ in the Indian refining sector — including the nation’s first Fluidized Catalytic Cracking Unit (FCCU), Hydrocracker Unit (HCU), Diesel Hydro Desulphurization Unit (DHDS) as well as the first petrochemical plant of IndianOil for producing Linear Alkyl Benzene marking IndianOil’s big-ticket entry into Petrochemicals.

Transforming Gujarat Refinery: The ₹17,825-crore Petrochemicals and Lube Integration Project (LuPech) is expanding refining capacity from 13.7 MMTPA to 18 MMTPA and integrating refining and lube oil base stocks and petrochemicals.

The past year has seen significant progress, including the commissioning of the Vacuum Distillation Unit-2, the first grassroots process unit under LuPech, the Catalytic Iso-Dewaxing Unit (CIDWU) on 15 August 2026.

The successful completion of one year of operation of IndianOil’s first Acrylic Acid and Butyl Acrylate Plant at Dumad in June 2026 is another milestone. It marks IndianOil’s entry into a new petrochemical segment, reduces import dependence and strengthens downstream industries and the MSME ecosystem.

A Legacy of Nation-Building: Since its commissioning in 1965 and dedication to the nation in 1966, Gujarat Refinery has reflected India’s industrial confidence and determination to build indigenous capabilities. Over six decades, its journey has been marked by pioneering technologies, continuous innovation and expansion into new domains, strengthening IndianOil’s refining and petrochemical capabilities while contributing to India’s growing energy self-reliance.

The refinery’s product portfolio reflects the pioneering spirit from STORM Racing Fuel, India’s first AVGAS 100 LL aviation fuel and Sulphur Bentonite, to specialised products such as defence-grade JP-5 naval fuel and NATO-grade High Flash High Speed Diesel (HFHSD). The refinery also has a Hydrogen Dispensing Facility. The Refinery added another significant milestone to this legacy with the first dispatch of Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) from Gujarat Refinery and export to international market in September 2026.

Under the LuPech Project, the Catalytic Iso-Dewaxing Unit (CIDWU), with a designed capacity of 270 KTA, is enabling Gujarat Refinery to produce high-quality Group II and Group III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) from Hydrocracker streams. The Unit has successfully commenced production of 150N and 70N grades, marking a significant step in strengthening IndianOil’s capabilities in the manufacture of high-performance lube base oils.

Advancing Sustainability: The upgraded Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB) unit with capacity of 162 KTPA (up from 120 KTPA) has become the First Refinery/Petrochemical Plant in India to Achieve CII GreenCo Silver Certification under the Green Company Rating System evaluated across nine key parameters, namely Management Systems, Energy Management, Carbon Management, Water Management, Material Resource Management, Green Supply Chain, Product Stewardship & Life Cycle Approach, Innovation for Environment, and Green Built Environment & Others.

The GreenCo Silver Certification stands as a testament to Gujarat Refinery's continuous efforts towards its pursuit of environment excellence, resource efficiency and sustainable growth.

Gujarat Refinery uses 40 MLD treated wastewater under an MoU with Vadodara Municipal Corporation.

Safety milestones: Gujarat Refinery achieved more than 65 million safe workhours under the LuPech Project while maintaining strong safety standards during this complex transformation. The Acrylics/Oxo-Alcohol project had earlier achieved 27 million safe workhours.

Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR): In FY 2025–26, Rs. 247 Lakhs was committed to CSR projects. Recent interventions include:

  • Donated 2 Anaesthesia Workstations with ventilators to SSG Hospital for enhanced capacity for OT surgeries and reduced waiting time for needy patients, with a total of 1107 ENT surgeries and General OT procedures in the last 6 Months.
  • 10 Ambulances to Vadodara Chief District Health Office and 2 ICU on Wheels, 01 Neo Natal ICU ambulance and 8 small Ambulance to Narmada (aspirational district) Chief District Health Office
  • 24 Truenat Machines for TB diagnostics in 7 districts of Gujarat
  • 3600 TB Nutrition Kits distributed via VMC
  • 5 health camps reaching 900+ villagers
  • Ultrasound & laparoscopic machines for VMC and SSG Hospital, with more than 58,000 patients from April 2024 till Aug-2026.
  • 3210 large vessels & 5 food vehicles provided to Akshay Patra Foundation
  • Partnered with Vadodara District Administration, installed 732 Rainwater Harvesting Systems in Government Primary Schools - contributing to making Vadodara the first district in India to implement such a large-scale, sustainable rainwater harvesting initiative, which was featured in Hon’ble PM’s ‘Mann Ki Baat’

CER Initiatives:

•           Beautification of 43 ponds under Amrit Sarovar Mission

•           Road construction projects in Koyali-Bajwa and Angadh village

•           Khaswadi Smashan (crematorium) renovation in Karelibagh

Education & Skilling: The IndianOil Gyanodaya Scholarship supports ITI and Polytechnic students from underprivileged backgrounds in Vadodara and Bharuch.

About Gujarat Refinery: Commissioned in 1965 and dedicated to nation in 1966, Gujarat Refinery is IndianOil’s flagship refinery, playing a catalytic role in Gujarat’s industrial growth. With a current capacity of 13.7 MMTPA, it is being expanded to 18 MMTPA under the LuPech Project. Over six decades, the Refinery has contributed to India's energy security, industrial development and indigenous technological capabilities.

About IndianOil: Ranked 130th in the Fortune Global 500, IndianOil is India's top-ranked energy PSU and one of the country's largest integrated energy companies. IndianOil operates 10 of India's 23 refineries and accounts for about 32% of the country's refining capacity. With more than 65,000 customer touchpoints, the Corporation serves millions of customers across India with a presence across petrochemicals, natural gas, alternative energy and emerging low-carbon solutions. Beyond business, IndianOil’s Nation-First ethos drives impactful social investment through CSR programmes in healthcare, education, sanitation, women empowerment, skill development, and environmental restoration.

Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place after technical and human intelligence about his movement and presence were received.
Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the…
item.content:encoded:
In an intelligence-led joint Security Forces operation, senior Lashkar-e-Toiba Commander, Musa aka Asif Fauji, was neutralized at Gurwatkalan, Khansahib PS of Budgam District, J&K. Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place after technical and human intelligence about his movement and presence were received.

Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the UT of J&K. With Musa’s killing, the entire group of four senior LeT Commanders operating in the UT since 2022, and responsible for sensational attacks, like Halan attack (Aug 2023), DKG attack (Dec 2023), Kandi attack (May 2023), Shahsitar attack (May 2024), Shiv Khori attack (June 2024), Gagangir attack (Oct 2024), Bootapathri attack (Oct 2024) and Baisaran attack (Apr 2025), stands neutralized. The three other members of the group were neutralized by Security Forces in separate encounters of Junaid Bhat (Dec 03, 2024, Dachigam), Suleman (July 28, 2025, OP Mahadev), and Yasir (Sep 04, 2026, Op Asdhar). The current encounter to neutralize Musa was part of an ongoing long-sustained operation.  

Over the past few years, all security agencies—such as the Jammu & Kashmir Police, the Indian Army, and the CAPF—have been conducting counter-terrorism operations in close coordination, yielding positive results.

*****

RK / RR / PR / PS

item.content:encoded:
Snapshot:

  • Registered manufacturing sector has recorded remarkable growth in respect of Industrial Output by 7.81%, Total Employment by 7.19%, Emoluments by 12.08% in the year 2024-25 over the previous year.
  • Over the last survey period, this sector has reported Invested capital (Fixed capital + Physical working capital) expansion by 11.10%.
  • During the same period, Net Income has increased by 9.68%, while Net Profit has also registered a growth of 7.73%.
  • The top five industries, Basic metal, Motor vehicles, Chemical and Chemical products, Pharmaceutical Products and Food Products, taken together, have contributed more than 45% of the total manufacturing GVA of the country during 2024-25.
  • Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana have emerged to be the top 5 States in respect of employment having share of more than 56% of the total manufacturing employment of the country in 2024-25.

Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released the results of Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) for the reference period April 2024 to March 2025 (i.e. financial year 2024-25) through the factsheet. In this press note, this survey has been referred to as ASI 2024-25. The field work for this survey was carried out during October 2025 to June 2026 for ASI 2024-25. A brief note about the survey ASI 2024-25 is given at the Endnote.

Annual Survey of Industries is conducted with the primary objective to provide a meaningful insight into the dynamics of change in the composition, growth and structure of various manufacturing industries in terms of output, value added, employment, capital formation and a host of other parameters. The survey data serves as an important input for policymaking, supporting compilation of National Accounts Statistics, and meets the information needs of various Ministries while enabling stakeholders to make informed decisions. The results are prepared at State and major industry level. The report is available in the website of the Ministry (https://www.mospi.gov.in).

Key highlights from ASI 2024-25 results

The registered manufacturing sector recorded broad-based growth during FY2024-25, with most of the major economic indicators—such as invested capital, input, output, Gross Value Added, employment and wages—witnessed an increase over the previous year.

Growth in Establishment, Gross Value Added and Employment Metrics:  

The total number of establishments in this sector increased from 2.60 lakhs in ASI 2023-24 to 2.67 lakhs in ASI 2024-25, representing a growth of 2.64%.  The highest number of establishments reported in Tamil Nadu (41,221), followed by Gujarat (33,084) and Maharashtra (27,379).

Chart-1: Bar chart showing the Number of factories by major States in ASI 2024-25: All India

During the same period, GVA increased from ₹2458.3 thousand crore to ₹2694.2 thousand crore, indicating sustained growth (9.59%) in industrial value addition. In terms of individual share of States in all India GVA, Maharashtra recorded the highest GVA in 2024-25, followed by Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh. Collectively, these five States accounted for more than 54 % of the total manufacturing GVA of the country. These five States accounted for 53.30 % of total establishments at all India level.

Endnote:

A brief note about the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2024-25

  1. Coverage of ASI:

The Annual Survey of Industries broadly covers the following

    1. Factories registered under Sections 2m(i) and 2m(ii) of the Factories Act,1948
    2. Bidi and cigar manufacturing establishments registered under the Bidi & Cigar Workers (Conditions of Employment) Act,1966
    3. Electricity undertakings engaged in generation, transmission and distribution of electricity, not registered with the Central Electricity Authority (CEA)
    4. Units with 100 or more employees registered in the Business Register of Establishments (BRE) prepared and maintained by the State Governments as and when such lists are shared by the respective State Governments.
  2. ASI frame and its updation

The ASI frame is based on the lists of registered factory / units maintained by the Chief Inspector of Factories (CIF) in each State and those maintained by registration authorities in respect of Bidi and Cigar establishments and electricity undertakings. The frame is being revised and updated periodically by the Regional Offices of the Field Operations Division of NSO in consultation with the Chief Inspector of Factories in the State. At the time of revision, the names of the de-registered factories are removed from the ASI frame and those of the newly registered factories are added. For the units selected in the last survey year (in this case 2023-24), relevant fields like Status Code, Frame industry (NIC 4 digit), Employee (Total persons engaged), Address etc. of frame for a given year, say, ASI 2024-25 are auto-updated dynamically based on the information collected during the last survey year.

  1. Unit of Enumeration

The primary unit of enumeration in the survey is a factory in the case of manufacturing industries, a workshop in the case of repair services, an undertaking or a licensee in the case of electricity, gas & water supply undertakings and an establishment in the case of bidi & cigar industries. The owner of two or more establishments located in the same State and pertaining to the same industry group and belonging to census scheme is, however, permitted to furnish a single consolidated return. Such consolidated returns are common feature in the case of bidi and cigar establishments, electricity and certain public sector undertakings.

  1. Data Collection Mechanism

Data for ASI are collected from the selected factories under the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 as amended in 2017 and Rules framed there under in 2011. The entire survey is conducted through a dedicated web-portal without any paper schedule. For data collection in ASI, an establishment (and not enterprise) approach is followed wherein data are collected from the selected establishments.

  1. Survey Disclaimer

Various quality checks are carried out on the data collected through this survey which is primarily record- based. Relative Standard Errors (RSE) (which is a widely accepted statistical measure of reliability of an estimate) for important parameters estimated from the survey at an overall level are small and well within the acceptable range. However, since the data presented in this result are estimated from sample survey, necessary caution may be taken while using this data.

The Factsheet for ASI 2024-25 is available on the website of the ministry (https://www.mospi.gov.in). Scan the below QR code to access the Publications/Reports

item.description: A special lecture on the topic of ‘Legal Startups and Innovation’ was organized on September 28, 2026, by the School of Criminal Law and Military Law at Rashtriya Raksha University, Lavad, Gandhinagar. The session was coordinated by Dr. Anand Kumar Tripathi, Head of the Centre for Post-Graduate Legal Studies, and moderated by Ms. V. Jayshree, Assistant Professor of Law. The keynote expert for the event was Dr. Kalpesh K. Gupta, founder of ProBono India and Startups & Law Teachers India.…
item.content:encoded:
A special lecture on the topic of ‘Legal Startups and Innovation’ was organized on September 28, 2026, by the School of Criminal Law and Military Law at Rashtriya Raksha University, Lavad, Gandhinagar. The session was coordinated by Dr. Anand Kumar Tripathi, Head of the Centre for Post-Graduate Legal Studies, and moderated by Ms. V. Jayshree, Assistant Professor of Law. The keynote expert for the event was Dr. Kalpesh K. Gupta, founder of ProBono India and Startups & Law Teachers India. Students from the fourth year of the LLB program and the LLM program primarily attended this enlightening event.

 

In his address, Dr. Gupta introduced the students to the modern concept of ‘legalpreneurship,’ explaining how new startups solve practical problems, accelerate economic growth, and create new employment opportunities. He elaborated on the country's current startup ecosystem, its various stages, and the Central Government’s startup initiatives.

He also highlighted successful ventures led by the legal community and underscored the importance of activities such as ‘pro bono’ (free) legal services for the upliftment of marginalized sections of society. The special lecture concluded successfully, marked by the students' enthusiasm, engaging discussions, and new aspirations. Ms. Jyotsna Singh, the student representative for the LLM program, successfully concluded the session, while Ms. V. Jayshree, Associate Professor (Law), delivered the vote of thanks.

item.content:encoded:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today said that in a major success in the fight against drugs 526 kilograms of methamphetamine and heroin were seized from an Iranian boat within India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and five Pakistani nationals were arrested, during a joint operation involving the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), the Indian Coast Guard, and central intelligence agencies.

In a post on X, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated, “Modi govt. is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs. In a joint operation by Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard and Central intelligence agencies, 526 kg of Methamphetamine and Heroin has been seized from an Iranian boat in India’s EEZ, 160 NM northwest of Lakshadweep and 490 NM southwest of Mumbai. Five Pakistani nationals have been arrested, with further investigation underway to identify the wider network and its intended receivers. Upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation among agencies the 16-day long operation also seized an Iranian boat.” 

Modi govt. is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs. In a joint operation by Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard and Central intelligence agencies, 526 kg of Methamphetamine and Heroin has been seized from an Iranian boat in India’s EEZ, 160 NM northwest of Lakshadweep and 490 NM southwest of Mumbai. Five Pakistani nationals have been arrested, with further investigation underway to identify the wider network and its intended receivers. Upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation among agencies the 16 day long operation also seized an Iranian boat.

— Amit Shah (@AmitShah) September 30, 2026

The operation, conducted from 14th to 30th September, reflects the strength of intelligence-led, inter-agency coordination in securing India’s maritime borders.

The Vision Document on Drug Control (2026–2029) unveiled by the Modi government provides a comprehensive roadmap to strengthen enforcement, disrupt drug networks and protect our youth and society from narcotics.

A safer, healthier and Nasha-Mukt Bharat remains our shared national resolve.

item.title: From Financial Assistance to Academic Excellence
item.description:
Financial assistance can play an important role in enabling students from disadvantaged communities to pursue higher education, overcome financial constraints and build confidence to achieve their academic aspirations. Targeted support can also create opportunities for beneficiaries to inspire others in their communities to pursue advanced education.
Minakashi, a 36-year-old PhD Research Scholar belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) community, aspired to build a career in teaching,…
item.content:encoded:
Financial assistance can play an important role in enabling students from disadvantaged communities to pursue higher education, overcome financial constraints and build confidence to achieve their academic aspirations. Targeted support can also create opportunities for beneficiaries to inspire others in their communities to pursue advanced education.

Minakashi, a 36-year-old PhD Research Scholar belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) community, aspired to build a career in teaching, research and the scientific field at a reputed university. Financial instability, however, posed a significant challenge in continuing her higher studies.

Coming from a community where access to higher education remains limited, Minakashi faced barriers related to financial resources, confidence and access to opportunities. The lack of adequate support made it difficult for many members of her community to pursue higher education with confidence.

During 2022–25, under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Minakashi received financial assistance of Rs. 11 lakh. The support enabled her to continue and complete her higher education without the burden of financial constraints.

Today, Minakashi stands as an example of how targeted financial assistance can create opportunities for academic advancement and social empowerment. Her journey has helped inspire other students from economically disadvantaged and socially marginalized communities to pursue higher education with greater confidence.

Minakshi’s experience reflects the impact of financial assistance under the NFSC Scheme in enabling students to overcome financial barriers, continue higher education and contribute to the aspirations of others in their communities.

Through the support received under the NFSC Scheme, Minakashi has transformed financial constraints into an opportunity for academic growth, while becoming an inspiration for other students to pursue higher education and work towards a more empowered future.

Talking about the financial support and its benefits, Minakshi said, “The NFSC Scheme gave me the financial support I needed to complete my PhD. Today, I am not just fulfilling my dream, but also helping other students from my community to dream bigger.”

The assistance extended through the NFSC Scheme helped Minakashi strengthen her confidence and pursue her academic goals. During her academic journey, she also contributed to educating students who aspired to pursue higher education but faced financial difficulties. Her experience encouraged students from disadvantaged communities to consider higher education as an achievable pathway.

SS-113-TAR/KV/GA/MK

item.title: Special Campaign 6.0: DIPAM Engages MSTC to Auction and Responsibly Recycle Departmental E-Waste
item.description:
As part of its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata and ensuring environmentally responsible management of electronic waste, the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has engaged MSTC Limited, a Miniratna Category-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, for the scientific collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste generated in the Department.
This step is being taken under Special Campaign 6 (2nd – 31st October 2026), which has…
item.content:encoded:
As part of its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata and ensuring environmentally responsible management of electronic waste, the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has engaged MSTC Limited, a Miniratna Category-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, for the scientific collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste generated in the Department.

This step is being taken under Special Campaign 6 (2nd – 31st October 2026), which has a special focus on “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-Waste” in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

MSTC’s specialised e-auction platform will facilitate transparent and compliant disposal of obsolete electronic equipment such as computers, printers, servers and other IT assets. The engagement will not only free up valuable office space but will also ensure that e-waste is channelled through authorised recyclers, thereby converting waste into resource while generating revenue for the Government.

DIPAM remains committed to the larger goals of Special Campaign 6 – saturation of cleanliness in Government offices, reduction of pendency, and promotion of sustainable practices across its offices.

*****

Sanjay Roy/Divya Ann Mathew

Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28, to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce. The absolute highest increase in MSP has been announced for Safflower at Rs.675 per quintal…
item.content:encoded:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the increase in the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for all mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28.

Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28, to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce. The absolute highest increase in MSP has been announced for Safflower at Rs.675 per quintal followed by Rapeseed & Mustard at Rs.413 per quintal. For Lentil (Masur), barley, gram, and wheat, there is an increase of Rs.390 per quintal, Rs.136 per quintal, Rs.83 per quintal and Rs.25 per quintal respectively.

*Refers to cost which includes all paid out costs such as those incurred on account of hired human labour, bullock labour/machine labour, rent paid for leased in land, expenses incurred on use of material inputs like seeds, fertilizers, manures, irrigation charges, depreciation on implements and farm buildings, interest on working capital, diesel/electricity for operation of pump sets etc., miscellaneous expenses and imputed value of family labour.

The increase in MSP for mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28 is in line with the Union Budget 2018-19 announcement of fixing the MSP at a level of at least 1.5 times of the All-India weighted average Cost of Production. The expected margin over All-India weighted average cost of production is 106 percent for wheat, followed by 96 percent for rapeseed & mustard; 92 per cent for lentil; 59 per cent for gram; 58 percent for barley; and 50 percent for safflower. This increased MSP of rabi crops will ensure remunerative prices to the farmers and incentivise crop diversification.

In the recent years, Government has been promoting the cultivation of crops, other than cereals such as pulses and oilseeds by offering a higher MSP for these crops. 

The procurement of wheat during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3715 LMT as compared to 2254 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The procurement of 6 Rabi crops during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3921 LMT as compared to 2302 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

The MSP amount paid to Wheat growing famers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs. 7.31 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.56  Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The MSP amount paid to 6 Rabi crops growing farmers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs.8.36 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.65 Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

item.title: Cabinet approves One Network, Smarter Traffic: Delhi Moves to Real-Time Traffic Management
item.description:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved implementation of the ITMS Project by Delhi Police at an estimated cost of Rs.1,789.52 crore, inclusive of taxes. The project will cover 42 identified traffic corridors and will be implemented in three phases over 24 months, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.
As part of the wider efforts of the Central Government and the Government of NCT of Delhi to…
item.content:encoded:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved implementation of the ITMS Project by Delhi Police at an estimated cost of Rs.1,789.52 crore, inclusive of taxes. The project will cover 42 identified traffic corridors and will be implemented in three phases over 24 months, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.

As part of the wider efforts of the Central Government and the Government of NCT of Delhi to improve traffic management, transport infrastructure and urban mobility in the National Capital, a major technology-led initiative will now be taken up through the Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS). The project will enable Delhi’s existing road network to be managed more intelligently through real-time traffic data, adaptive traffic signals, automated enforcement and integrated command-and-control systems.

Delhi has around 71 lakh active registered vehicles. Vehicular growth has substantially outpaced expansion of road infrastructure, while traffic regulation continues to depend significantly on fixed signal timings and manual intervention. The ITMS seeks to make better use of the available road capacity by enabling traffic management to respond dynamically to actual conditions on the road.

Benefits:

  • Smarter traffic signals and smoother movement: Adaptive Traffic Control Systems will dynamically adjust signal timings according to prevailing traffic conditions and coordinate signals along identified corridors, helping reduce avoidable stoppages and delays.
  • Priority for ambulances and emergency vehicles: The system will facilitate green corridors and priority movement for emergency vehicles, enabling faster passage through congested stretches.
  • Faster response to congestion and accidents: Real-time detection of congestion, slow-moving traffic and road incidents will enable quicker diversions and operational response by Delhi Police.
  • Timely information for commuters: Variable Message Sign boards and digital platforms will provide information on congestion, diversions, parking availability and traffic conditions. Information may also be shared with navigation service providers, helping commuters make better travel choices.
  • More consistent and technology-based enforcement: The system will strengthen automated detection of violations such as red-light and stop-line violations, speeding, wrong-way driving, non-use of helmets and seat belts, illegal parking and use of mobile phones while driving. AI-based analytics will also assist in identifying stolen, hot-listed and blacklisted vehicles, repeat violators and vehicles connected with hit-and-run incidents.

Integrated city-wide traffic management:

Traffic regulation, enforcement and information dissemination will be brought together on a common platform through Traffic Command and Control Centres, supported by secure Data Centre and Disaster Recovery infrastructure. The system will follow open standards and APIs to enable future integration and scalability.

The project will cover 1,092 Adaptive Traffic Control System and 1,029 enforcement locations. Implementation will be performance-driven, with each subsequent phase to be taken up after evaluation of the preceding phase against prescribed testing, commissioning, acceptance and performance parameters.

Delhi Police will implement the project through a Master System Integrator selected through competitive bidding. C-DAC will provide technical support as Project Management Consultant, including technical scrutiny, monitoring, validation and acceptance during implementation and operation and maintenance.

The ITMS will complement ongoing efforts to improve Delhi’s road and transport infrastructure by providing the technology and real-time intelligence required to use the existing road network more efficiently. The project is expected to contribute to smoother traffic movement, safer roads, quicker incident response, more effective enforcement and a more predictable travel experience for citizens.

 

****

MJPS

item.title: ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ ਬੈਟਰੀ ਐਨਰਜੀ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮਾਂ (BESS) ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ (Intra-State Transmission System) ਦੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਲਈ PM-DHARA (PM-Developing Harmonized and Accelerated Renewable-energy Access) ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ
item.description:
ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਸ਼੍ਰੀ ਨਰੇਂਦਰ ਮੋਦੀ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨਗੀ ਹੇਠ ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ PM-DHARA (PM-Developing Harmonized and Accelerated Renewable-energy Access) ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪਹਿਲਕਦਮੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ (InSTS) ਨੂੰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ​​ਕਰੇਗੀ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਰਾਜਾਂ/ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸ਼ਾਸਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 135 ਗੀਗਾਵਾਟ (GW) ਤੱਕ ਦੀ ਨਵਿਆਉਣਯੋਗ ਊਰਜਾ (evacuation) ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਜੀ ਥਾਂ ਭੇਜਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।
ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਦੀ ਲਚਕਤਾ ਲਈ ਨਵਿਆਉਣਯੋਗ ਊਰਜਾ (RE) ਡਿਵੈਲਪਰ/ਉਤਪਾਦਕ ਦੇ ਸਿਰ੍ਹੇ 'ਤੇ ਜਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ…
item.content:encoded:
ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਸ਼੍ਰੀ ਨਰੇਂਦਰ ਮੋਦੀ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨਗੀ ਹੇਠ ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ PM-DHARA (PM-Developing Harmonized and Accelerated Renewable-energy Access) ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪਹਿਲਕਦਮੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ (InSTS) ਨੂੰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ​​ਕਰੇਗੀ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਰਾਜਾਂ/ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸ਼ਾਸਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 135 ਗੀਗਾਵਾਟ (GW) ਤੱਕ ਦੀ ਨਵਿਆਉਣਯੋਗ ਊਰਜਾ (evacuation) ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਜੀ ਥਾਂ ਭੇਜਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।

 

ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਦੀ ਲਚਕਤਾ ਲਈ ਨਵਿਆਉਣਯੋਗ ਊਰਜਾ (RE) ਡਿਵੈਲਪਰ/ਉਤਪਾਦਕ ਦੇ ਸਿਰ੍ਹੇ 'ਤੇ ਜਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਸਥਾਨ 'ਤੇ 50 GWh ਦੇ ਬੈਟਰੀ ਐਨਰਜੀ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮ (BESS) ਨੂੰ ਲਗਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਵਿਵਸਥਾ ਵੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਰੁਕ-ਰੁਕ ਕੇ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਸਪਲਾਈ, ਕੰਜੈਸ਼ਨ (congestion- ਭੀੜ-ਭੜੱਕੇ), ਪੀਕ-ਘੰਟਿਆਂ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਕਟੌਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਨੌਨ-ਸੋਲਰ ਘੰਟਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਦੀ ਮੰਗ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ। ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਰਾਜਾਂ/ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸ਼ਾਸਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਏਕੀਕਰਣ ਅਤੇ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਜੀ ਥਾਂ ਭੇਜਣ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰੇਗੀ।

The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with total project outlay of Rs.1,86,405 crore, comprising 

 

ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਵਰ੍ਹੇ 2032-33 ਤੱਕ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਟੀਚਾ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਕੁੱਲ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ ਲਾਗਤ 1,86,405 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਤੈਅ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ GEC-III ਦੇ ਤਹਿਤ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀਆਂ (InSTS) ਦੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਲਈ 1,36,378 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਅਤੇ 50 GWh ਬੈਟਰੀ ਐਨਰਜੀ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮਾਂ (BESS) ਲਈ 50,000 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹਨ। ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੁੱਲ 54,082 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਦੀ ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹੈ। ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ (CFA) ਨਾਲ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਖਰਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਘਟਾਉਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਦਦ ਮਿਲੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਲਾਗਤ ਘੱਟ ਰਹੇਗੀ। ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਦਾ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਲਾਭ ਆਮ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਯਾਨੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਨਾਗਰਿਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲੇਗਾ।

 

InSTS ਕੰਪੋਨੈਂਟ ਦੇ ਤਹਿਤ ਸਾਰੇ 'ਗ੍ਰੀਨਫੀਲਡ' ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟਾਂ ਨੂੰ 'ਟੈਰਿਫ-ਅਧਾਰਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਯੋਗੀ ਬੋਲੀ' (TBCB) ਮੋਡ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਲਾਗੂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ, ਜਦਕਿ 'ਬ੍ਰਾਊਨਫੀਲਡ' ਅੱਪਗ੍ਰੇਡੇਸ਼ਨ ਅਤੇ ਨੈੱਟਵਰਕ ਨੂੰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ 'ਕੌਸਟ- ਪਲੱਸ ਬੇਸਿਸ (ਸੀਪੀਬੀ) ਅਧੀਨ ਕੀਤੇ ਜਾਣਗੇ। ਸਟੇਟ ਟ੍ਰਾਂਸਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਯੂਟਿਲਿਟੀਜ਼ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਮੁੱਖ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੀ ਏਜੰਸੀ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਟ੍ਰਾਂਸਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਸਰਵਿਸ ਪ੍ਰੋਵਾਈਡਰਸ (TSPs) TBCB ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਬਿਲਡ-ਓਨ-ਓਪਰੇਟ-ਮੈਨਟੇਨ (BOOM) ਮਾਡਲ 'ਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਨਗੇ।

 

ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ 2035 ਤੱਕ 900 GW ਦੀ ਨੌਨ –ਫੌਸਿਲ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਦੇ ਟੀਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਦਦ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ ਦੇਸ਼ ਦੀ ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀ ਊਰਜਾ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਯੋਗਦਾਨ ਪਾਵੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਰਬਨ ਫੁੱਟਪ੍ਰਿੰਟ ਨੂੰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ –ਅਧਾਰਿਤ ਅਨੁਕੂਲ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਉਤਸ਼ਾਹਿਤ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਖੇਤਰ, ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਉਦਯੋਗਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਡੇ ਪੱਧਰ ‘ਤੇ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਤੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਅਪ੍ਰਤੱਖ ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਪੈਦਾ ਹੋਣਗੇ। ਬੈਟਰੀ ਊਰਜਾ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮ (BESS) ਦੇ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਨਾਲ ਘਰੇਲੂ ਊਰਜਾ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਉਦਯੋਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਦੇ ਮੌਕੇ ਬਣਨਗੇ। ਨਾਲ ਹੀ, ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਲੈਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਰਾਜਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਚਾਲਨ, ਰੱਖ-ਰਖਾਅ ਅਤੇ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧਨ ਦੇ ਖੇਤਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਲਈ ਕੁਸ਼ਲ ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਵੀ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰੇਗੀ।

 

*****

ਐੱਮਜੇਪੀਐੱਸ/ਏਕੇ

item.title: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems
item.description:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme. This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.

item.content:encoded:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme. This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.

The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand. The scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation with in the States/UTs of India.

The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with total project outlay of Rs.1,86,405 crore, comprising Rs.1,36,378 crore for the development of Intra-State Transmission Systems (InSTS) under GEC-III, Rs.50,000 crore for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The Scheme involves a total Central Financial Support of Rs.54,082 crore. The Central Financial Assistance (CFA) will help in offsetting the Intra-State transmission charges and thus keep the power costs down. Thus, the Government support will ultimately benefit the end users – the citizens of India.

All Greenfield projects under the InSTS component will be implemented through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mode, while brownfield upgradation and network strengthening works will be executed under Cost Plus Basis (CPB). The State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agency, and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) will participate under TBCB on a Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM) model.

The scheme will help in achieving the target of 900 GW installed Non-Fossil capacity by 2035. The scheme will also contribute to long term energy security of the country and promote ecologically sustainable growth by reducing carbon footprint. It will generate large direct & indirect employment in the power sector, manufacturing, and construction industries. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing and deployment will additionally generate employment in the domestic energy storage industry. The scheme will also generate long-term skilled employment in operation, maintenance, and grid management across participating States.

 

****

MJPS

item.content:encoded:
Ka Kynhun Myntri jong ka sorkar pdeng ba la pyniaid da u Myntri Rangbahduh ka ri u Narendra Modi ka la mynjur ia ka skhim Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III). Kane ka sienjam ba kongsan kan pynkhlain ia ka India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) ban plie lad ban pynkynriah ia ka bording kaba lah ban pynthymmai haduh 135 Gigawatt (GW) ha kylleng ki Jylla/ ki Union Territory.

Ka skhim ka pynbiang ruh ban pyntreikam ia ka 50 GWh jong ki Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) ha ka jaka pynmih bording ba lah ban pynthymmai (RE) lane kano kano ka jaka kaba kongsan na ka bynta ka jingpynkylla ia ka bording ban weng ia ka jingthut, ka jingkhapngiah, ka jingpynduna ia ka por ba bun ka jingpyndonkam bad ban pynbiang ia ka jingdawa ha ka por ba lah dum. Ka skhim kan pynsuk ia ka jingpyniasoh ia ka grid bad ka jingpynkynriah ia ka bording ha ki Jylla/UT jong ka India.

Ia kane ka skhim la buh thong ban seng ha u snem mang tyngka 2032-33 ha kaba ka jingpynlut ha ka projek baroh kan long T.1,86,405 klur, kaba kynthup ia ka T.1,36,378 klur na ka bynta ban kyntiew ia ki Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) hapoh ka GEC-III (Store-III), T.50,000 klur na ka bynta ka Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) kaba 50 GWh. Kane ka Skhim ka kynthup ia ka jingkyrshan pisa jong ka sorkar pdeng baroh kaba long T.54,082 klur. Ka jingiarap pisa jong ka sorkar pdeng (CFA) kan iarap ban pyndap ia ka jingsiew na ka bynta ka jingpynpoi bording hapoh ki jylla bad kumta kan pynduna ia ka jinglut ha ka bording. Kumta, ka jingkyrshan jong ka Sorkar kan ai jingmyntoi ïa ki nongpyndonkam – ki nongshong shnong jong ka ri India.

Baroh ki projek ba thymmai kiba hap hapoh ka bynta jong ka InSTS yn pyntreikam lyngba ka rukom treikam Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB), katba ïa ki kam ban kyntiew ïa ki jingdon jingem ba la don lypa bad pynkhlain ïa ka rynsan yn pyntreikam hapoh ka Cost Plus Basis (CPB). Ki tnad pynpoi bording jong ki jylla kin long ka tnad pyntreikam, bad ki Transmission Service Provider (TSP) kin iashim bynta hapoh ka TBCB ha ka rukom treikam Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM).

Kane ka skhim kan iarap ban pynurlong ia ka thong ban buh ia ka bording Non-Fossil kaba 900 GW shuwa u snem 2035. Ka skhim kan nohsynniang ruh ia ka jingpynbiang bording jong ka ri ha ka samoi ba jrong bad kan kyntiew ia ka jingkiew ka bym ktah palat ia ka mariang da kaba pynduna ia ka jingpynmih carbon. Kan pynmih ia ki lad ioh kam ioh jam ha ka kam ba iadei bad ka Bording, ki karkhana shna tiar, bad ki karkhana shna jingshna. Ka jingshna bad jingpyndonkam ia ka Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) kan pynmih shuh shuh ia ki lad ioh kam ha ka kam pynlang bording hapoh ka ri. Ka skhim kan pynmih ruh ia ki kam kiba jrong samoi, ka jingpynbha, bad jingpyniaid ia ka grid ha kylleng ki Jylla kiba iashim bynta.

 

****

item.title: ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ ਬੈਟਰੀ ਐਨਰਜੀ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮਾਂ (BESS) ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ (Intra-State Transmission System) ਦੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਲਈ PM-DHARA (PM-Developing Harmonized and Accelerated Renewable-energy Access) ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ

item.content:encoded:
ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਸ਼੍ਰੀ ਨਰੇਂਦਰ ਮੋਦੀ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨਗੀ ਹੇਠ ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਕੈਬਨਿਟ ਨੇ PM-DHARA (PM-Developing Harmonized and Accelerated Renewable-energy Access) ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪਹਿਲਕਦਮੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੀ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ (InSTS) ਨੂੰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ​​ਕਰੇਗੀ ਤਾਂ ਜੋ ਰਾਜਾਂ/ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸ਼ਾਸਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ 135 ਗੀਗਾਵਾਟ (GW) ਤੱਕ ਦੀ ਨਵਿਆਉਣਯੋਗ ਊਰਜਾ (evacuation) ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਜੀ ਥਾਂ ਭੇਜਿਆ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ।

ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਦੀ ਲਚਕਤਾ ਲਈ ਨਵਿਆਉਣਯੋਗ ਊਰਜਾ (RE) ਡਿਵੈਲਪਰ/ਉਤਪਾਦਕ ਦੇ ਸਿਰ੍ਹੇ 'ਤੇ ਜਾਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਸਥਾਨ 'ਤੇ 50 GWh ਦੇ ਬੈਟਰੀ ਐਨਰਜੀ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮ (BESS) ਨੂੰ ਲਗਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਵਿਵਸਥਾ ਵੀ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਰੁਕ-ਰੁਕ ਕੇ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਸਪਲਾਈ, ਕੰਜੈਸ਼ਨ (congestion- ਭੀੜ-ਭੜੱਕੇ), ਪੀਕ-ਘੰਟਿਆਂ ਦੌਰਾਨ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਕਟੌਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਨੌਨ-ਸੋਲਰ ਘੰਟਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਦੀ ਮੰਗ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕੇ। ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਰਾਜਾਂ/ਕੇਂਦਰ ਸ਼ਾਸਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਦੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਏਕੀਕਰਣ ਅਤੇ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਦੂਜੀ ਥਾਂ ਭੇਜਣ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਹੂਲਤ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰੇਗੀ।

ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਵਰ੍ਹੇ 2032-33 ਤੱਕ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਟੀਚਾ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਲਈ ਕੁੱਲ ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟ ਲਾਗਤ 1,86,405 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਤੈਅ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ GEC-III ਦੇ ਤਹਿਤ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀਆਂ (InSTS) ਦੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਲਈ 1,36,378 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਅਤੇ 50 GWh ਬੈਟਰੀ ਐਨਰਜੀ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮਾਂ (BESS) ਲਈ 50,000 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹਨ। ਇਸ ਸਕੀਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੁੱਲ 54,082 ਕਰੋੜ ਰੁਪਏ ਦੀ ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ ਹੈ। ਕੇਂਦਰੀ ਵਿੱਤੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ (CFA) ਨਾਲ ਅੰਤਰ-ਰਾਜੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰਣ ਖਰਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਘਟਾਉਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਦਦ ਮਿਲੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਲਾਗਤ ਘੱਟ ਰਹੇਗੀ। ਇਸ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ, ਸਰਕਾਰੀ ਸਹਾਇਤਾ ਦਾ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਲਾਭ ਆਮ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਯਾਨੀ ਭਾਰਤ ਦੇ ਨਾਗਰਿਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਲੇਗਾ।

InSTS ਕੰਪੋਨੈਂਟ ਦੇ ਤਹਿਤ ਸਾਰੇ 'ਗ੍ਰੀਨਫੀਲਡ' ਪ੍ਰੋਜੈਕਟਾਂ ਨੂੰ 'ਟੈਰਿਫ-ਅਧਾਰਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਯੋਗੀ ਬੋਲੀ' (TBCB) ਮੋਡ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਲਾਗੂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ, ਜਦਕਿ 'ਬ੍ਰਾਊਨਫੀਲਡ' ਅੱਪਗ੍ਰੇਡੇਸ਼ਨ ਅਤੇ ਨੈੱਟਵਰਕ ਨੂੰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ 'ਕੌਸਟ- ਪਲੱਸ ਬੇਸਿਸ (ਸੀਪੀਬੀ) ਅਧੀਨ ਕੀਤੇ ਜਾਣਗੇ। ਸਟੇਟ ਟ੍ਰਾਂਸਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਯੂਟਿਲਿਟੀਜ਼ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਮੁੱਖ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੀ ਏਜੰਸੀ ਹੋਵੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਟ੍ਰਾਂਸਮਿਸ਼ਨ ਸਰਵਿਸ ਪ੍ਰੋਵਾਈਡਰਸ (TSPs) TBCB ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਬਿਲਡ-ਓਨ-ਓਪਰੇਟ-ਮੈਨਟੇਨ (BOOM) ਮਾਡਲ 'ਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਨਗੇ।

ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ 2035 ਤੱਕ 900 GW ਦੀ ਨੌਨ –ਫੌਸਿਲ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਦੇ ਟੀਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਦਦ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ ਦੇਸ਼ ਦੀ ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀ ਊਰਜਾ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਯੋਗਦਾਨ ਪਾਵੇਗੀ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਰਬਨ ਫੁੱਟਪ੍ਰਿੰਟ ਨੂੰ ਘਟਾ ਕੇ ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ –ਅਧਾਰਿਤ ਅਨੁਕੂਲ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਉਤਸ਼ਾਹਿਤ ਕਰੇਗੀ। ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਬਿਜਲੀ ਖੇਤਰ, ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਉਦਯੋਗਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਡੇ ਪੱਧਰ ‘ਤੇ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਤੱਖ ਅਤੇ ਅਪ੍ਰਤੱਖ ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਪੈਦਾ ਹੋਣਗੇ। ਬੈਟਰੀ ਊਰਜਾ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਸਿਸਟਮ (BESS) ਦੇ ਨਿਰਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਨਾਲ ਘਰੇਲੂ ਊਰਜਾ ਸਟੋਰੇਜ ਉਦਯੋਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਦੇ ਮੌਕੇ ਬਣਨਗੇ। ਨਾਲ ਹੀ, ਇਹ ਸਕੀਮ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਲੈਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਰਾਜਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਚਾਲਨ, ਰੱਖ-ਰਖਾਅ ਅਤੇ ਗਰਿੱਡ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧਨ ਦੇ ਖੇਤਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਲਈ ਕੁਸ਼ਲ ਰੁਜ਼ਗਾਰ ਵੀ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰੇਗੀ।

 

*****

ਐੱਮਜੇਪੀਐੱਸ/ਏਕੇ

item.content:encoded:
The Divisional level Dak Adalath of Thrissur Postal Division for the month of October 2026 is proposed to be held at the office of the Senior Superintendent of Post Offices, Sakthan Thampuran Nagar, Thrissur Head Post Office complex (Second floor), Thrissur-680001 on 08.10.2026 at 10.00 AM. 

The type of complaints and disputes which will be taken up in this Adalath will cover all types of grievances relating to Postal Services including Savings Bank, Money Orders etc. Complaints may be sent in a cover super scribed "DAK ADALATH - October 2026 to the address below. 

Senior Superintendent of Post Offices 

Thrissur Division, Thrissur 

680001 

The last date fixed for the receipt of petition is 06.10.2026. The complainants are requested to mention their Mobile number and eMail ID in the complaints.

item.title: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems
item.description:

This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.
The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other…
item.content:encoded:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme. This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.

The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand. The scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation with in the States/UTs of India.

The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with total project outlay of Rs.1,86,405 crore, comprising Rs.1,36,378 crore for the development of Intra-State Transmission Systems (InSTS) under GEC-III, Rs.50,000 crore for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The Scheme involves a total Central Financial Support of Rs.54,082 crore. The Central Financial Assistance (CFA) will help in offsetting the Intra-State transmission charges and thus keep the power costs down. Thus, the Government support will ultimately benefit the end users – the citizens of India.

All Greenfield projects under the InSTS component will be implemented through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mode, while brownfield upgradation and network strengthening works will be executed under Cost Plus Basis (CPB). The State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agency, and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) will participate under TBCB on a Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM) model.

The scheme will help in achieving the target of 900 GW installed Non-Fossil capacity by 2035. The scheme will also contribute to long term energy security of the country and promote ecologically sustainable growth by reducing carbon footprint. It will generate large direct & indirect employment in the power sector, manufacturing, and construction industries. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing and deployment will additionally generate employment in the domestic energy storage industry. The scheme will also generate long-term skilled employment in operation, maintenance, and grid management across participating States.

 

****

MJPS

item.content:encoded:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the increase in the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for all mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28.

Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28, to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce. The absolute highest increase in MSP has been announced for Safflower at Rs.675 per quintal followed by Rapeseed & Mustard at Rs.413 per quintal. For Lentil (Masur), barley, gram, and wheat, there is an increase of Rs.390 per quintal, Rs.136 per quintal, Rs.83 per quintal and Rs.25 per quintal respectively.

*Refers to cost which includes all paid out costs such as those incurred on account of hired human labour, bullock labour/machine labour, rent paid for leased in land, expenses incurred on use of material inputs like seeds, fertilizers, manures, irrigation charges, depreciation on implements and farm buildings, interest on working capital, diesel/electricity for operation of pump sets etc., miscellaneous expenses and imputed value of family labour.

The increase in MSP for mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28 is in line with the Union Budget 2018-19 announcement of fixing the MSP at a level of at least 1.5 times of the All-India weighted average Cost of Production. The expected margin over All-India weighted average cost of production is 106 percent for wheat, followed by 96 percent for rapeseed & mustard; 92 per cent for lentil; 59 per cent for gram; 58 percent for barley; and 50 percent for safflower. This increased MSP of rabi crops will ensure remunerative prices to the farmers and incentivise crop diversification.

In the recent years, Government has been promoting the cultivation of crops, other than cereals such as pulses and oilseeds by offering a higher MSP for these crops. 

The procurement of wheat during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3715 LMT as compared to 2254 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The procurement of 6 Rabi crops during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3921 LMT as compared to 2302 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

The MSP amount paid to Wheat growing famers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs. 7.31 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.56  Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The MSP amount paid to 6 Rabi crops growing farmers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs.8.36 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.65 Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

item.title: Shri Chouhan Approves ₹5,547.99 Crore Procurement of Pulses and Oilseeds Under PSS for Kharif 2026-27
item.description:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan has approved procurement worth ₹5,547.99 crore at Minimum Support Price (MSP) under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for the Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27 in Uttar Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. The decision is aimed at protecting farmers from a decline in market prices and ensuring remunerative returns for their produce, particularly for pulse and oilseed growers.
Shri Chouhan said…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan has approved procurement worth ₹5,547.99 crore at Minimum Support Price (MSP) under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for the Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27 in Uttar Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. The decision is aimed at protecting farmers from a decline in market prices and ensuring remunerative returns for their produce, particularly for pulse and oilseed growers.

Shri Chouhan said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the welfare of farmers, increasing their incomes and strengthening self-reliance in agriculture remain key priorities of the government. He said the government is working to ensure that farmers receive remunerative prices for their produce and that procurement mechanisms are made more transparent and accessible. Under the approved procurement plan, farmers in the three states will benefit from large-scale procurement of key pulses and oilseeds at MSP.

In Uttar Pradesh, the largest share of the approved procurement, worth ₹3,992.57 crore, has been sanctioned. This includes procurement of 4,66,000 metric tonnes of tur valued at ₹3,937.70 crore and 6,250 metric tonnes of moong valued at ₹54.87 crore at MSP.

For pulse and oilseed farmers in Karnataka, procurement worth ₹1,107 crore has been approved under PSS. This includes 1,15,500 metric tonnes of soybean valued at ₹659.27 crore, 38,250 metric tonnes of moong valued at ₹335.83 crore and 13,413 metric tonnes of sunflower valued at ₹111.90 crore.

In Telangana, procurement worth ₹448.42 crore has been approved. This comprises 62,000 metric tonnes of soybean valued at ₹353.90 crore and 10,766 metric tonnes of moong valued at ₹94.52 crore, to be procured at MSP under the Price Support Scheme.

Shri Chouhan said the decision will provide greater economic security to farmers while encouraging domestic production of pulses and oilseeds and contributing to India’s efforts towards self-reliance in pulses and edible oils. He assured that procurement arrangements at all designated centres will remain transparent and that farmers will receive payment for their produce directly into their bank accounts in a timely manner.

 

***

 

SS/MS/DK

item.content:encoded:
As part of the ongoing ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ campaign, the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Chandigarh, today organised a plantation drive under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative at Kendriya Sadan, Sector-9, Chandigarh. Six saplings were planted in the lawns of Kendriya Sadan with active participation of officers and staff members. The drive aimed to reinforce the message of environmental conservation, cleanliness and collective responsibility.

As part of Special Campaign 6.0, CBC Chandigarh felicitated three Safai Mitras for their remarkable contribution in maintaining cleanliness in the office premises. They were honoured with certificates, shields, Swachhata kits and tiffin boxes.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Pritam Singh, Director, PIB Chandigarh, said that planting a tree is not merely an environmental activity, but also an expression of gratitude towards nature and future generations. He encouraged everyone to contribute towards a greener environment by planting and nurturing trees.

Felicitating the Safai Mitras, Ms. Sapna, Deputy Director, PIB Chandigarh, said, “Cleanliness and environmental protection is not only the job of sweeping staff, it is the responsibility of each one of us to keep our surroundings neat and clean. The Safai Mitras have made a commendable contribution to the maintenance of office premises. Further, ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ provides an opportunity to contribute to a cleaner and greener society while strengthening the emotional bond between individuals, nature and their communities.

Mrs. Sheenam Jain, Assistant Director, PIB Chandigarh, emphasised the importance of nurturing the saplings after plantation. She said the true spirit of ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ lies not only in planting trees, but also in taking responsibility for their growth and survival. She urged staff members and citizens to adopt environmentally responsible practices in daily life.

Shri Ahmad Khan, Media & Communication Officer, said, “Cleanliness is a shared responsibility and must be taken care of by everyone, everywhere. It requires collective participation of citizens, institutions and communities.”

In addition to the plantation drive, the staff members also undertook a cleanliness drive in and around the premises, underlining the broader message of ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ – to maintain clean and hygienic public spaces.

The activities reflected the spirit of ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 6.0’, with participants reaffirming their commitment towards environmental sustainability, cleanliness and responsible citizenship.
