The 24 th edition of Routes…
item.content:encoded:
Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu today unveiled the Curtain Raiser for Routes Asia 2027 in New Delhi, marking a significant milestone in India's preparations to host the prestigious international aviation event. The Curtain Raiser witnessed participation from representatives of 28 embassies, along with leading aviation stakeholders, underscoring the growing international engagement and collaborative opportunities surrounding Routes Asia 2027.

The 24th edition of Routes Asia will be held from 16–18 March 2027 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, bringing together more than 115 leading airlines, representatives from 55+ countries, airports, tourism authorities and aviation stakeholders from across Asia and beyond.

Minister of Civil Aviation, Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, while unveiling the curtain raiser plaque, presented India's vision for Routes Asia 2027 under the theme “Bharat Aviation Rising: Inclusive Growth – Connecting Asia & Beyond.” He highlighted that guided by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the event comes at an opportune moment as India advances towards becoming the world's third-largest aviation market. He said, “Routes Asia 2027 is coming to the right place, at the right time, with the right opportunity! There is room for more capacity, more airlines and more routes”.

With over 166 airports and plans to develop 100 additional airports over the next decade, India's aviation sector is witnessing rapid expansion. The Minister emphasised the growing importance of the hub-and-spoke model, which can connect more cities and people with emerging markets, creating opportunities for airlines, tourism and economic growth. He also highlighted India's active bilateral aviation engagements, particularly with Southeast Asian countries, and the continued growth in international air travel, with passenger traffic recording a compound annual growth rate of 4.6%.

The Minister extended an invitation to the global aviation community to participate in Routes Asia 2027 and explore India's diverse destinations and expanding aviation opportunities. He underscored the importance of collective stakeholder efforts in connecting Tier-II cities, strengthening international hubs and developing new routes that will shape the next chapter of India's aviation journey.

India formally assumed the hosting responsibilities for Routes Asia 2027 from China West Airport Group during the closing ceremony of Routes Asia 2026 in Xi’an, China, in April 2026, with Airports Authority of India, receiving the hosting baton. The upcoming edition is expected to attract over 2,000 delegates, including decision-makers from leading airlines, airports and tourism authorities.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation, highlighted the transformative role of aviation in connecting people, facilitating trade and creating economic opportunities. Emphasising that international travel should become increasingly accessible and seamless for tourism and business, he underscored the importance of partnerships and route development in strengthening India's aviation ecosystem.

Routes Asia 2027 will provide a strategic platform for strengthening partnerships, developing new air routes and positioning India as a preferred aviation and connectivity destination. The event reinforces India's commitment to inclusive growth, international collaboration and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Divyanshu Kumar

item.title: EPFO urges employers and workers in North East to leverage enhanced social security measures
item.description:
“Enhancement of social security coverage of the workforce is a key priority of the Government of India, and employers and workers across the North Eastern Region should make full use of the facilitating schemes introduced under the Social Security Code, 2020,” said Shri Shishir Kant Jha, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, North Eastern Region, while addressing a media briefing organised at the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Regional Office, Guwahati, today.
…
item.content:encoded:
“Enhancement of social security coverage of the workforce is a key priority of the Government of India, and employers and workers across the North Eastern Region should make full use of the facilitating schemes introduced under the Social Security Code, 2020,” said Shri Shishir Kant Jha, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, North Eastern Region, while addressing a media briefing organised at the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), Regional Office, Guwahati, today.

Speaking about the enhancement of the EPF wage ceiling, Shri Jha said that the Ministry of Labour & Employment notified on September 17, 2026, an increase in the wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month. The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, thereby significantly widening social security protection for workers.

He said that existing EPFO members will continue as members and contributions already remitted at the earlier wage ceiling will remain unaffected. New entrants earning up to ₹25,000 in EPF wages will be eligible for the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS). The pension contribution under EPS will be calculated on wages up to ₹25,000, at 8.33 per cent, subject to a maximum contribution of ₹2,083 per month.

Shri Jha advised employers to review the records of employees earning between ₹15,000 and ₹25,000 per month, update their payroll records and file the Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) for enrolling new members and updating contributions of existing members in accordance with the revised wage ceiling and applicable EPFO provisions.

Shri Jha said that the Government of India has recently introduced several facilitating schemes aimed at enhancing social security coverage of the workforce. He urged employers and workers across Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and the wider North Eastern Region to make use of these schemes. The initiatives provide opportunities for employers to regularise past gaps, settle old disputes, avail incentives for employment generation and extend social security coverage to a larger section of workers, he said.

Shri Jha also highlighted the benefits of other initiatives, including the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY), Employees’ Enrolment Campaign (EEC), 2026 and VISHWAS, 2026. He encouraged employers and workers to avail themselves of these initiatives to strengthen social security coverage and facilitate employment generation and compliance.

The media briefing was also addressed by Shri Gaurav Srivastava, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, Regional Office, Guwahati, and Shri M. Ngullie, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, Zonal Office, North Eastern Region.

***

PG/BM

Scindia, in New Delhi today . The launch event, was organized by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The…
item.content:encoded:
The trailer of documentary series “The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast” was officially launched by Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in New Delhi today . The launch event, was organized by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The event was graced by  MoS MDoNER Dr. Sukanta Majumdar and  attended by senior officials of MDoNER and members of the production team.

The documentary series brings the rich culinary traditions, diverse communities, and vibrant cultural heritage of the eight states of Northeast India into sharp national focus.

Undertaken with the support of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and the North Eastern Council (NEC), the series has been implemented through the North Eastern Region Community Resource Management Society (NERCRMS) and produced by Urban Media Productions in association with Filandering Forker Media. It marks a significant cultural outreach effort by MDoNER to introduce the Northeast to a wider audience through the experiences and authentic stories of the people  of the region.

The documentary series takes viewers on a food-led journey across all eight Northeastern States, exploring the region through its cuisine, communities, and people. The series explores the culinary traditions of the NER rooted in locally available resources, intertwined with interesting facts.

The production of the series involved intraction with local communities and food producers, tracing native ingredients from their origins to kitchens and eventually to the dining table. Through these encounters, the documentary captures not only the food itself, but also the stories, traditions, and people connected to it.

The tariler turns the spotlight on northeastern states , looking at the region  through its food and the people who prepare and share it. Rather than presenting the NER through a single cuisine, the series reflects its diverse communities and distinct geographies, highlighting the localized ingredients, indigenous knowledge, and everyday practices behind a meal, with local voices carrying the narrative.

While food remains at the center of the series, the journey also brings viewers closer to the arts, culture, and landscapes of the Northeast, presenting these elements as part of the broader context in which the region’s culinary traditions have evolved. By placing food at the heart of its storytelling, The Enchanting 8 offers a window into the cultural diversity of Northeast India, connecting viewers with the region through its kitchens, ingredients, and  foodways. The launch marks the beginning of a documentary journey that brings the culinary richness of the Northeast to a wider audience.

PS

item.title: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Completes Preparatory Phase for Special Campaign 6
item.description: New Delhi, 29 September 2026: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and its organisations have undertaken extensive preparations for “Special Campaign 6,” the sixth edition of the Government of India's nationwide drive to clean government offices, clear pending work, organise old files and improve institutional efficiency. The preparatory phase of the campaign has run from 15 to 30 September 2026, ahead of the Implementation Phase, which will be carried out from 2 to 31…
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi, 29 September 2026: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and its organisations have undertaken extensive preparations for “Special Campaign 6,” the sixth edition of the Government of India's nationwide drive to clean government offices, clear pending work, organise old files and improve institutional efficiency. The preparatory phase of the campaign has run from 15 to 30 September 2026, ahead of the Implementation Phase, which will be carried out from 2 to 31 October, 2026.

Secretary, MoPSW, chaired a review meeting with the Heads of all organisations and Nodal Officers of the Ministry and its organisations to assess preparedness for the campaign. The Secretary emphasised timely action, cleanliness, disposal of pending matters, effective management of e-waste, and proper documentation of activities throughout the campaign.

As part of preparations, MoPSW and its organisations have identified several MP References, References from State Governments, Inter-Ministerial Communications, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO References, Public Grievances and PG Appeals, and Rules/Processes for simplification, along with 185 Cleanliness Campaigns, 6,605 physical files and 4,548 e-files for review and disposal during the campaign. In addition, 5,624 e-waste items have been identified for collection, segregation and disposal in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

MoPSW is coordinating with its organisations through designated Nodal Officers, with progress being reviewed regularly during the Preparatory Phase. The identified activities will now be taken forward in a time-bound manner during the Implementation Phase, from 2 to 31 October 2026, with proper monitoring and documentation of outcomes. An Evaluation Phase, assessing results and best practices from the campaign, is scheduled for 16 to 30 November 2026 under the national framework for Special Campaign 6.

Through Special Campaign 6, MoPSW and all its organisations will undertake concerted efforts towards cleanliness, environmental responsibility, efficient record management, reduction of pendency and responsive governance, with particular focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

MoPSW and its organisations are also observing ‘Swachhata Pakhwada’ from 16 to 30 September, 2026, coinciding with the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 and reinforcing its cleanliness and public participation objectives. Key activities under ‘Swachhata Pakhwada’ include ‘Shramdaan’ and cleanliness drives, cleaning of public places and community institutions, repair and renovation of toilets, awareness and IEC activities, Waste-to-Wealth exhibitions, ‘Swachhata Raths’ and rallies, cleaning of ponds, rivers and beaches, plantation drives, and elimination of single-use plastic.

***

MI/Indu

item.content:encoded:
The due date for furnishing Return of Income for Assessment Year 2026-27 is 31st October, 2026 in the case of persons mentioned at Serial No. 2 in the Table below Explanation 2 to sub-section (1) of section 139 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
 
The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has extended the aforesaid due date of furnishing of Return of Income from 31st October, 2026 to 21st November, 2026.
 
Accordingly, the 'specified date' for furnishing of the report of audit under the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961 for Assessment Year 2026-27, in the case of persons referred to at Serial No. 2 in the Table below Explanation 2 to sub-section (1) of section 139 of the Act, stands extended from 30th September, 2026 to 21st October, 2026.
 
A formal order/notification to this effect is being issued separately.

item.title: From mangroves to Pokkali fields, CMFRI backwater cruise offers close look at fragile ecology of Vembanad
item.description:
Kochi: From century-old mangroves and Pokkali paddy fields to island-based livelihoods, a backwater cruise organised by the ICAR- ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) to Kadamakkudy offered a close look at the fragile ecology of the Vembanad estuary and the need to conserve its biodiversity and natural resources.
This was part of CMFRI’s Fish Walk initiative, an outreach programme bringing science to the public through experiential tours . The…
item.content:encoded:
Kochi: From century-old mangroves and Pokkali paddy fields to island-based livelihoods, a backwater cruise organised by the ICAR- ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) to Kadamakkudy offered a close look at the fragile ecology of the Vembanad estuary and the need to conserve its biodiversity and natural resources.

 

This was part of CMFRI’s Fish Walk initiative, an outreach programme bringing science to the public through experiential tours. The cruise was held in connection with the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign and World Tourism Day in partnership with GDM Travel, a start-up focused on nature-based tourism and aquatic exploration.

The programme combined field visits, expert interactions and a cleanliness drive to spread conservation awareness and familiarise participants with the ecological processes and challenges of diverse aquatic life. Participants were sensitised to the importance of keeping water bodies free of plastic waste and the ecological risks posed by indiscriminate dumping.

The cruise, which was flagged off from Marine Drive Jetty by CMFRI Director Dr Grinson George, covered a stretch from Marine Drive to Kadamakkudy, taking participants across 15 islands, including a special visit to the mangrove habitats of Korungotta and the Pokkali fields of Pizhala. Participants, mostly students, learnt about how mangroves act as bio-shields against storm surges, coastal floodings and reduce climate impacts. The visit gave participants a first-hand experience of the unique mangrove biodiversity, including nearly century-old trees with large, robust stems. Scientists from CMFRI explained the different mangrove species found in the region and their vital ecological services, including carbon sequestration and climate-change mitigation, coastal protection and the provision of habitat and nursery grounds for aquatic life. The on-field interaction also highlighted how healthy mangrove and wetland ecosystems support fisheries and other local livelihoods, underscoring their importance as highly productive ecosystems.

A clean-up drive during the cruise drew attention to the impact of plastic and other waste on backwater habitats, while discussions focused on pollution, aquatic life, wetland conservation, cage fish farming and sustainable use of natural resources.

The Pokkali visit highlighted the traditional integration of salt-tolerant rice cultivation with seasonal fish and prawn farming, illustrating the links between the estuarine ecosystem and local livelihoods.

Beyond its scenic beauty, the cruise offered participants an opportunity to discover the lesser-known ecological wealth of the Ramsar-designated Vembanad, from diverse aquatic life including fish and molluscs to mangrove habitats and productive wetlands. It also brought into focus the traditional livelihoods, farming practices, island culture and community knowledge closely intertwined with the estuarine ecosystem. Students, nature enthusiasts, tourism professionals, teachers and researchers took part in the cruise.

Tony Chammany MLA interacted with the participants at Kadamakkudy Pokkali fields. Panchayat President M S Antony, CMFRI Director Dr Grinson George, and local body representatives were present.

The initiative was aimed at strengthening public awareness of the ecological sensitivity of the Vembanad backwaters and unique wetland ecosystems, and encouraging greater community participation in their conservation, said Dr Grinson George.

“CMFRI’s Fish Walk is designed as a series of innovative modes of exploring aquatic life and biodiversity, aimed at taking the message of conservation to a wider audience through engaging and experiential approaches,” said Dr Mirium Paul Sreeram, Coordinator of the initiative.

The institute launched the Fish Walk initiative last year and has since conducted a series of editions, each exploring coastal and marine biodiversity through different themes and experiential formats.

item.description:
Kochi: The Malayalam Science Conference 2026, aimed at taking new knowledge, discoveries and developments in science and technology to the public through Malayalam, commenced in Kochi today. The two-day conference is being jointly organised on September 25 and 26 by the ICAR–Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT), Kochi, Swadeshi Science Movement–Kerala (SSM-K), and Bharatiya Bhasha Samit, Ministry of Education, Government of India
The conference is being held on…
item.content:encoded:
Kochi: The Malayalam Science Conference 2026, aimed at taking new knowledge, discoveries and developments in science and technology to the public through Malayalam, commenced in Kochi today. The two-day conference is being jointly organised on September 25 and 26 by the ICAR–Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT), Kochi, Swadeshi Science Movement–Kerala (SSM-K), and  Bharatiya Bhasha Samit, Ministry of Education, Government of India

The conference is being held on the theme “Taking Research Knowledge to Society”, with the objective of making scientific and technological developments more accessible to the general public and strengthening science communication through the mother tongue.

Sri Jayan N., Director, Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC), ISRO, inaugurated the conference. In his inaugural address, he highlighted the importance of such conferences in creating scientific awareness and promoting scientific thinking among the younger generation. He said that it was important to nurture curiosity about science and encourage young people to explore new knowledge. As India continues to advance in areas including space science and technology, he emphasised the need for the younger generation to understand the role of science in shaping the country's future. He also noted that communicating scientific knowledge in Malayalam can make science simpler and more accessible to people.

The Conference will feature research paper presentations, expert lectures and discussions on various scientific subjects. The sessions provided a platform for researchers and science communicators to present scientific knowledge in Malayalam in a simple and accessible manner and discuss new approaches to strengthening science communication through regional languages.

The technical sessions covered a wide range of scientific disciplines, including Biotechnology; Health and Bioenergetics; Environmental Sciences and Biodiversity; Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences; and Food Security and Food Technology.

Researchers, teachers, students, science communicators, science writers and representatives from different sectors are participating in the conference. Experts and invited speakers from various academic and research institutions are delivering talks on diverse scientific topics. Around 120 participants are attending the two-day programme.

 

Dr George Ninan, Director, ICAR-CIFT, and President, Society of Fisheries Technologists (SOFTI), presided over the inaugural session. Shri P. A. Vivekananda Pai, Secretary General, Vijnana Bharati; Dr V. Sivakumar, President, Swadeshi Science Movement–Kerala; and the programme convenors, Dr Nikita Gopal, Head, Extension, Information and Statistics Division, ICAR-CIFT, and Dr Remya S., Senior Scientist, Fish Processing Division, ICAR-CIFT, also addressed the inaugural session.

item.description:

Clean and well-maintained public spaces play an important role in creating welcoming surroundings for visitors and strengthening responsible tourism. Through cleanliness drives and awareness activities, JCI…
item.content:encoded:
The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)-

On the occasion of World Tourism Day, the Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) reaffirms its commitment to promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental responsibility under the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026.

Clean and well-maintained public spaces play an important role in creating welcoming surroundings for visitors and strengthening responsible tourism. Through cleanliness drives and awareness activities, JCI encourages public participation, responsible waste management and sustainable practices to keep tourist destinations and public places clean and attractive.

JCI–Bobbili DPC under JCI–Parvathipuram Region undertook a post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness activity under theme of “Sports for Swachhata & Post-Event” Cleanliness at the Old Bobbili Riverbank, Bobbili, as part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026.” The initiative aimed to restore cleanliness and hygiene at the riverbank after the immersion activities and promote responsible waste management and environmental awareness.

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026,” Rampur Bolla DPC under Malda Region, West Bengal, conducted a cleanliness drive at the Maa Bolla Kali Temple, Dakshin Dinajpur, West Bengal, on the occasion of ‘World Tourism Day” on 27th September 2026.

Maa Bolla Kali Temple is one of the prominent religious and tourist destinations in the region, attracting a large number of devotees and visitors. The cleanliness initiative focused on maintaining a clean, hygienic and welcoming environment at the temple premises and its surrounding areas.

The drive aimed to promote Swachhata, environmental responsibility and public awareness, while encouraging collective participation towards proper waste management and the upkeep of religious and tourist destinations. The initiative reaffirmed JCI’s commitment to promoting cleanliness and sustainable practices as an integral part of community life.

Textiles Committee-

The Textile Committee conducted a nationwide Shramdaan drive, "Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath for Swachhata," across its Mumbai Headquarters and Regional Offices premises.

National Jute Board (NJB)-

As part of the observance of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the Officers and Employees of the National Jute Board organised a Book Donation Event at nearby schools, namely Chanchal Kumari Girls High School and Haridas Vidyapeeth.

During the event, students were actively engaged and sensitised about the importance of cleanliness, hygiene and maintaining a clean environment in and around their homes, schools and surrounding areas. The students were encouraged to develop responsible habits and contribute towards keeping their surroundings clean.

Books were also donated to the schools for the benefit of the students. The donated books will be made available through the school libraries, enabling students to read and share them, thereby ensuring that the resources can be accessed by a larger number of students.

The initiative combined the message of Swachhata with the promotion of reading and learning, contributing towards the development of responsible, aware and well-informed students.

National Insitute Of Fashion Technology-

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, NIFT Campuses undertook post-Ganesh Visarjan cleanliness, with proper collection and segregation of floral waste and offering materials. Flower waste was composted wherever feasible.

Cotton Corporation of India-

The Corporation organized an awareness activity across its offices on 28 September 2026 to promote the importance of Reuse and Recycle as part of responsible waste management. Employees were sensitized about reducing waste by reusing materials wherever possible and ensuring recyclable items are properly collected and recycled. The initiative aimed to encourage sustainable habits, minimize waste generation, and promote the efficient use of resources.

The activity reflects the Corporation’s commitment to environmental stewardship, sustainable practices, resource conservation, and collective action towards a cleaner and greener future.

National Handloom Development Corporation-

राष्‍ट्रीय हथकरघा विकास निगम लिमिटेड, नोएडा -  दिनांक 28 सितम्‍बर 2026 को अपराह्न 2.30 बजे “स्वच्छता ही सेवा” के अंतर्गत निगम के प्रबंध निदेशक महोदय द्वारा “एक पेड़ माँ के नाम” पर रोपित किया गया। इस अवसर पर उन्होंने पर्यावरण संरक्षण एवं हरियाली को बढ़ावा देने के लिए अधिक से अधिक पौधे लगाने तथा उनकी नियमित देखभाल करने का संदेश दिया। “एक पेड़ माँ के नाम” पहल प्रकृति माँ के प्रति सम्मान और हमारी जिम्मेदारी का सुंदर प्रतीक है। यह पौधारोपण न केवल कार्यालय परिसर को हरा-भरा बनाएगा, बल्कि सभी कर्मचारियों को पर्यावरण संरक्षण के प्रति जागरूक और प्रेरित भी करेगा

item.content:encoded:
As part of Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026, an Essay Writing Competition was organised at the Ministry of Textiles on 25 September 2026 on the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat Viksit Bharat.”

 

  • To ensure maximum reach and engagement, activities of the campaign are being shared across social media platforms amplifying the message of cleanliness.

 

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI)-

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026,” the Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) undertook various cleanliness and awareness initiatives under the themes of “Sports for Swachhata & Post-Event Cleanliness,” “Clean Public Places,” and “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy.” These initiatives aimed to promote cleanliness, hygiene, environmental responsibility, and active public participation in creating cleaner and healthier surroundings.

The JCI Regional Office–Berhampore conducted a collective cleanliness drive at the Y.M.A. (Young Men’s Association) Sports Ground, Berhampore, Murshidabad district, West Bengal.

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI), Guwahati Regional Office, in association with Uparhali DPC, organized a “Cricket Competition & Sports Ground Cleaning Drive” at Sarpara Playground, Uparhali, Kamrup, Assam. The initiative combined the spirit of sports with the message of cleanliness, encouraging community participation and promoting Swachhata as a Way of Life.

Simultaneously, the JCI Region Office -Siliguri conducted cleanliness drives at the Panjipara Football Ground and the Paschim Magurmari Primary School Playground, Dhupguri, Jalpaiguri, West Bengal.

The initiative focused on promoting cleanliness, hygiene, and environmental responsibility at public sports spaces. JCI officials and participants actively contributed to cleaning the sports ground and surrounding areas, reinforcing the importance of maintaining clean and healthy public spaces.

 

  • JCI organized a Door-to-Door Collection Drive for Used Clothes under the theme “Jan Bhagidari Advocacy. The initiative aimed to encourage community participation, promote the reuse and responsible disposal of used clothes, and create awareness about sustainable waste management practices. The drive highlighted the importance of collective participation in building a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable society.

Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Ltd-

 

Encouraged employees to avoid disposable cups, plates and cutlery and use reusable bottles / cups during meeting and official events.

 

  • CCIC organized Trimming / Pruning of trees in the premises New Delhi.

 

Textiles Committee-

The Textile Committee organized head quarter and regional office a workshop and demonstration session on the theme "Waste to Art" (featuring murals, sculptures, and decorative items) on 24 September 2026.

 HQ MUMBAI

                                               

Regional Office Kanpur                                                           Regional Office Delhi

 

Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts)-

  • Handicrafts organized Sanitation & Hygiene Standards: Deep cleaning and sanitization of washrooms and common facility areas.
  • Floor & Common Area Maintenance: Machine scrubbing, deep cleaning, and polishing of high-traffic corridors and entrance lobbies.
  • Plant & Machinery Area Upkeep: Comprehensive cleaning, dust removal, and water clearance in pump rooms, HVAC areas, electrical panel rooms, and utility zones.
  • Basement & Ramp Sweeping: Cleaning of parking areas, driveways, rooftop, ramps, and stairwells.
  • The activities ensured enhanced operational safety in technical rooms, clean common areas, and high standard sanitation facilities. Continual monitoring will be maintained to sustain these cleanliness standards.

 

 

National Jute Board (NJB)-

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign, the National Jute Board organised a cleanliness drive at Calcutta Jute Mill with the active participation of its officers and employees along with the workers of the jute mill. The cleanliness activities covered the inside and surrounding areas of the mill premises, with a focus on removal and proper disposal of accumulated waste and maintaining a clean and hygienic work environment.

During the programme, the waste management unit and dump yard of the mill were inspected to review the existing arrangements for collection, segregation, storage and disposal of waste. The need for timely disposal of waste and regular monitoring of the dump yard was emphasised to prevent accumulation and maintain cleanliness.

The initiative also promoted awareness among workers regarding cleanliness, responsible waste management and maintaining a litter-free workplace. The joint participation of the National Jute Board and jute mill workers reflected a collective commitment towards cleanliness, environmental responsibility and the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva.

item.title: India and Italy agree to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism
item.description:
The 2 nd India–Italy Joint Working Group (JWG) on Tourism was held on 29 September 2026, co-chaired by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, and Ms. Emanuela Tripi, Secretary-General, Ministry of Tourism, Italy.
The meeting brought together representatives from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of External Affairs, Embassy of India in Rome and Indian Association of Tour Operators (IATO) from the Indian side. The…
item.content:encoded:
The 2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group (JWG) on Tourism was held on 29 September 2026, co-chaired by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, and Ms. Emanuela Tripi, Secretary-General, Ministry of Tourism, Italy.

The meeting brought together representatives from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of External Affairs, Embassy of India in Rome and Indian Association of Tour Operators (IATO) from the Indian side. The Italian delegation included senior officials from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Embassy of Italy in New Delhi and ENIT (Italian National Tourism Board).

The discussions covered a broad range of areas for strengthening tourism cooperation between the two countries, including exchange of tourism data, promotion of lesser-known destinations, cine-tourism, destination twinning, skilling and capacity building, and enhanced Business-to-Business (B2B) engagement.

As a key outcome of the meeting, both sides agreed to establish focused technical groups and designate points of contact to take forward the identified areas of cooperation and facilitate sustained engagement between relevant stakeholders.

The two sides also discussed opportunities for tourism cooperation in the context of the proposed India–Italy Year of Culture and Tourism 2027, with a view to further strengthening cultural and tourism exchanges between the two countries.

The 2nd Joint Working Group meeting reaffirmed the commitment of India and Italy to deepen bilateral cooperation in tourism and create stronger institutional and industry linkages between the two countries.

item.content:encoded:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation stone of various projects worth more than ₹1,941 crore to strengthen connectivity in Delhi and make travel easier for the people of Delhi. He dedicated the Barapullah Elevated Road Phase-3, built at a cost of ₹1,635 crore, to the people of Delhi today.

In a post on X, Shri Amit Shah said, “To strengthen Delhi's connectivity and make travel easier for Delhi residents, today various projects worth more than ₹1,941 crore were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid. The Barapullah Elevated Road Phase-3, built at a cost of ₹1,635 crore, was dedicated to Delhi residents today. This will provide signal-free connectivity between East and South Delhi, making commuting smoother, providing relief from traffic jams, and saving travel time. Additionally, the foundation stones for the Modi Mill-Savitri Cinema Flyover and Loni Underpass were also laid.”

दिल्ली की कनेक्टिविटी को सुदृढ़ और दिल्लीवासियों के सफर को सुगम बनाने के लिए आज ₹1,941 करोड़ से अधिक की विभिन्न परियोजनाओं का उद्घाटन व शिलान्यास किया। ₹1,635 करोड़ की लागत से बना बारापुला एलिवेटेड रोड फेज-3 आज दिल्लीवासियों को समर्पित किया। इससे पूर्वी और दक्षिणी दिल्ली के बीच सिग्नल-फ्री कनेक्टिविटी होगी, जिससे आवागमन सुगम होगा, ट्रैफिक जाम से राहत मिलेगी और यात्रा का समय भी बचेगा। साथ ही, मोदी मिल-सावित्री सिनेमा फ्लाईओवर और लोनी अंडरपास का भी शिलान्यास किया।

item.title: Chhattisgarh’s Raipur and Bilaspur Among 50 Model Cities Identified Under PRAGATI-50 Initiative
item.description: In pursuance of the directions given by the Prime Minister during the 51st PRAGATI meeting, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has identified 50 model cities under the PRAGATI-50 initiative for demonstrating higher benchmarks of ‘Swachhata’ through targeted, Key Performance Indicator (KPI)-based action and intensive, technology-enabled monitoring under the framework of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0. Raipur and Bilaspur Municipal Corporations of Chhattisgarh are among the 50…
item.content:encoded:
In pursuance of the directions given by the Prime Minister during the 51st PRAGATI meeting, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has identified 50 model cities under the PRAGATI-50 initiative for demonstrating higher benchmarks of ‘Swachhata’ through targeted, Key Performance Indicator (KPI)-based action and intensive, technology-enabled monitoring under the framework of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0. Raipur and Bilaspur Municipal Corporations of Chhattisgarh are among the 50 cities identified under the initiative. The 50 cities across 24 States will work towards establishing higher standards of urban cleanliness through structured action, monitoring and outcome-based assessment.


The initiative aims to bring visible and sustained improvements in urban cleanliness, solid waste management, used water management, sanitation and citizen participation through a structured framework of monitoring and review within a defined timeframe.


Speaking at the launch, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal said that the 50 cities across 24 States will emerge as model cities for Swachhata for the rest of the country. He said that these cities would have to go beyond routine sanitation work and demonstrate sustained, high-performance parameters of visible cleanliness. He stated that major cities, cities of cultural importance, high tourism destinations and economic centres have been included under the initiative. Progress will be continuously reviewed through outcome-based assessments and technology-enabled monitoring. The Union Minister said that he would personally chair review meetings every two months to monitor the progress of these cities.


Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Tokhan Sahu said that over the past decade, Swachhata has evolved from a people’s movement into a way of life. He said that the new model city initiative would help cities achieve the goal of Garbage Free Cities within a stipulated timeframe and enable them to emerge as role models for other urban centres. He called upon States and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) to prepare micro-level action plans and ensure their swift and effective implementation.


Highlighting the growing convergence of youth power and technology, Shri Sahu said that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. He added that the launch of the third cohort of startups in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur also marks the achievement of the national target of onboarding and incubating 75 startups under the Mission.


Secretary, Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Satendra Singh said that efforts would be made towards ensuring better citizen experience and holistic service delivery. He highlighted that the initiative adopts a ‘City as a Whole’ approach, ensuring that all stakeholders, partners and Urban Local Bodies are included in planning and implementation.


To ensure effective monitoring, a Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation (PRAGATI)-like digital review mechanism has been established on the Swachhatam Portal. Officers from the Ministry will be assigned specific cities for regular supervision and handholding.


Recognising that sustainable urban transformation requires capacity building and continuous learning, the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban has empowered stakeholders with technical guidelines, model designs and targeted advisories. During the programme, the Standard Operating Procedure for Establishment of Secondary Collection Centre for Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste and the Guidelines for Source Segregation of Municipal Solid Waste, mandated under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, were released.


Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre
The Mission has consistently positioned research and innovation as key drivers of Swachhata. In collaboration with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research–Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-CMERI), the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre at Durgapur. It will serve as a national facility for research, product development, testing, validation, certification and capacity building in sanitation technologies.


Third Cohort of Swachhata Startups
Over the past decade, Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban has moved beyond conventional waste management towards cutting-edge, technology-driven solutions. The Mission has engaged 75 startups across the waste value chain to accelerate innovation. Continuing this entrepreneurial momentum, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, in collaboration with the Startup Incubation and Innovation Centre (SIIC) at IIT Kanpur, launched the third cohort of startups focused on pioneering solutions in sanitation and waste management. A total of 13 startups have joined the third cohort.


Dedicated WhatsApp Channel for Citizens
Taking the Swachhata App, an important interface for citizens to register complaints and seek grievance redressal, a step further, a dedicated WhatsApp channel has been launched to make it easier for citizens to lodge complaints and actively contribute to keeping their cities clean.


Swachhata Behaviour Change Digital Kosh
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal also launched the Swachhata Behaviour Change Digital Kosh, a digital repository bringing together ideas, creatives, campaigns and resources to strengthen behaviour change for a cleaner and more sustainable India. The platform will provide States, Urban Local Bodies and other stakeholders with ready-to-use communication resources, innovative campaign ideas and advocacy materials. It will facilitate knowledge sharing, replication of successful initiatives and citizen-centric communication to make Swachhata a habit and a way of life.


Reduce, Reuse and Recycle Centre at Sankalp Bhawan
As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal inaugurated a Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (RRR) Centre at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi. The initiative is envisaged as the first such centre in a Union Ministry office and will promote sustainable consumption, reuse, resource recovery and circularity in government workplaces.


India’s urban sanitation journey is being further strengthened through innovation, peer learning and capacity building to shape resilient and future-ready cities. As India moves towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the initiative seeks to advance the vision of garbage-free cities powered by scientific waste management, circular economy principles and sustainable urban systems.

******

The subject, Sandeep Mistry is wanted in Nirav Modi Scam case (PNB fraud case) registered by CBI, BSFB, Mumbai, for his involvement in a bank fraud case,…
item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, September 29, 2026

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), has successfully secured the deportation of the Red Notice subject Sandeep Mistry from UAE to India, wanted in Nirav Modi PNB Bank Fraud case.

The subject, Sandeep Mistry is wanted in Nirav Modi Scam case (PNB fraud case) registered by CBI, BSFB, Mumbai, for his involvement in a bank fraud case, involving fictitious international trade transactions. He acted as a key link between various entities, overseeing their day-to-day operations and issuing instructions through clandestine, self-deleting communication platforms to conceal evidence. He also facilitated the preparation of forged import-export documents to portray fictitious trade in diamonds, gold and pearl jewellery. Further, he, along with other accused persons, coerced dummy directors of foreign companies by threatening them with arrest, relocating them to other places, seizing their electronic devices and compelling them to sign documents falsely portraying them as genuine owners of the companies. He has also participated in siphoning off funds from the bank accounts of dummy companies in the UAE. The charge-sheet in the case has been filed before the competent court.

At the request of CBI, a Red Notice was published in July 2026 against the subject through INTERPOL channels. Subsequently, the subject was geo-located and arrested by the UAE authorities and deportation process initiated.

Notably, the Red Corner Notice against the subject was published in July 2026 and he was successfully traced, apprehended and brought back to India within a short span of approximately 2 months of publication of notice, reflecting swift and effective international coordination among the concerned agencies.

The subject arrived in Mumbai at 11.55 pm on Monday (September 28, 2026), where he was taken into custody by the officers of CBI, BSFB, Mumbai and produced before the competent court and sent to jail custody.

The CBI, as the National Central Bureau for INTERPOL in India, coordinates with all Law Enforcement Agencies in India through BHARATPOL for assistance via INTERPOL channels. More than 175 wanted criminals have been successfully brought back to India in the last few years through coordination via INTERPOL channels.

item.title: CAQM Approves Revised GRAP Schedule; Tightens Measures for Vehicles, Dust and Pollution Control
item.description:
The 30th meeting of the Full Commission of the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 28.09.2026, under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, during which the Commission approved modifications to the extant Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) Schedule for the National Capital Region (NCR).
The revised GRAP Schedule includes the following changes:
Merging repeated actions on dust measures,…
item.content:encoded:
The 30th meeting of the Full Commission of the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) was held on 28.09.2026, under the Chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, during which the Commission approved modifications to the extant Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) Schedule for the National Capital Region (NCR).

The revised GRAP Schedule includes the following changes:

  • Merging repeated actions on dust measures, MSW management and transport in Stage-I;
  • Moving actions related to DG Sets and entry of Buses (BS-IV & below) from NCR and Adjoining States from Stage-II to Stage-I;
  • Allowing minor relaxation under Action No. 1, Stage-III - including repairing of potholes;
  • Extension of restrictions on plying of BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel or below- standard LMVs (4-wheelers) to Sonipat in addition to the existing HVD Districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar;
  • Removal of exemption for BS-IV and below goods vehicles (LGVs, MGVs in Stage-III and Trucks/ HGVs in Stage-IV) carrying essential commodities in Stage-III and IV;
  • Restrictions on entry of diesel-operated BS-IV and below-standard LGVs and MGVs registered outside Delhi into Delhi has also been clearly mentioned under Stage- III;
  • Citizens Charter under each stage of GRAP has been modified with additional actions (Do’s and Don’ts);
  • Now, the revised GRAP Schedule has 25 actions in Stage-I, 8 actions in Stage-II, 10 actions in Stage-III and 5 actions in Stage-IV, Total: 48 Actions

 

The Commission also approved an amendment to Direction Nos. 11-18 dated 11.06.2021 for strengthening web portal-based monitoring of dust control measures at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites in NCR. The amendment extends the existing web-portal registration and monitoring mechanism to eligible C&D projects situated beyond municipal limits in urban areas, controlled areas, development areas/ industrial development areas, industrial areas/ zones and highway corridor zones, as applicable under the respective Statutory/ planning frameworks. The existing threshold of plot area equal to or greater than 500 square metres and other requirements under Direction Nos. 11-18 shall remain unchanged.

The Commission took note of Advisory No. 18 issued on 10.09.2026 regarding rescheduling of physical sports competitions scheduled during November-December. The Advisory reiterates that physical sports competitions scheduled in NCR during November-December should be appropriately rescheduled, keeping in view the air quality trends prevailing in the area, particularly in the interest of protecting the health of students.

The Commission took note of the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) for appointment of two full-time Technical Members in CAQM for a period of three years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. Two full-time Technical Members appointed are Shri Mukesh Sharma and Shri Trilok Singh Panwar.

The Commission was apprised of the updated status of Enforcement Task Force (ETF) decisions, inspections, closure and resumption of units. As on 17.09.2026, 1,831 violating units had been issued Closure Orders, out of which 1,479 cases had been considered for resumption post compliance and resumption orders issued accordingly. 126 cases had been transferred to SPCBs/ DPCC for further action where units were found unresponsive, permanently closed or shifted to other locations. During the period from 11.08.2026 to 17.09.2026, the ETF continued to examine cases involving non-compliance and applications for resumption of operations following corrective measures.

The Commission reviewed the progress of greening and plantation activities in Delhi- NCR against the targets fixed for 2026-27. Against the overall target of 4,60,54,740 plantations, covering trees, shrubs and bamboo, 4,13,68,929 plantations have been achieved as on 22.09.2026. Delhi has achieved 62,00,527 against its target of 58,01,386 plantations; Uttar Pradesh (NCR) has achieved 1,85,59,812 against the target of 1,71,44,900 plantations; Rajasthan (NCR) has achieved 1,16,13,092 plantations against the target of 1,07,09,754; while the achievement in Haryana (NCR) stood at 60,00,000 against a target of 1,20,00,000. The Commission emphasised continued follow-up and monitoring by the concerned authorities to achieve the stipulated targets and ensure survival of plantations.

*****

VM/GS/SK

item.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) Organized Voluntary Blood Donation Camp
item.description:
The Public Health (Urban) Division of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), in association with the Indian Red Cross Society, successfully organized a Voluntary Blood Donation Camp at its premises at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi today (29.09.2026), reaffirming its commitment to social responsibility and community welfare.
The blood donation camp was inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs. The camp was organized with the…
item.content:encoded:
The Public Health (Urban) Division of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), in association with the Indian Red Cross Society, successfully organized a Voluntary Blood Donation Camp at its premises at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi today (29.09.2026), reaffirming its commitment to social responsibility and community welfare.

The blood donation camp was inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs. The camp was organized with the dedicated efforts of Shri Ranjit Kumar Tiwary, Additional Director General (Urban Health Services), MoHUA, who lauded the enthusiastic participation of the donors and emphasized that voluntary blood donation is a noble act capable of saving countless lives and he also appreciated the profound spirit of service displayed by the participants. Appreciating the spirit of service displayed by the participants, Hon’ble MoS encouraged everyone to continue supporting such humanitarian initiatives.

 

The Blood Donation Camp received an encouraging response from the officers and staff of the Ministry. Driven by the theme "One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives," a total of 76 officers and staff members voluntarily participated in the blood donation drive, contributing to the overall success of the event.

The Ministry expresses its sincere gratitude to all the voluntary donors, the organizing team and the supporting medical staff from the Indian Red Cross Society for their valuable contribution in making the health and wellness event a success.

"Every Blood Donor is a Hero – Your Donation Can Save Lives."

 

*****

SK

item.title: SWACHH BHARAT CAMPAIGN OBSERVED IN AGARTALA MILITARY STATION
item.description:
September 29, Agartala: Demonstrating its steadfast commitment towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and operational health readiness, the Indian Army's Spear Corps organized a comprehensive educational and awareness drive for troops stationed in Agartala on 29 September 2026 as part of the nationwide Swachh Bharat Campaign.
The day-long initiative aimed to reinforce the core values of cleanliness, personal hygiene and ecological mindfulness among service personnel,…
item.content:encoded:
September 29, Agartala: Demonstrating its steadfast commitment towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and operational health readiness, the Indian Army's Spear Corps organized a comprehensive educational and awareness drive for troops stationed in Agartala on 29 September 2026 as part of the nationwide Swachh Bharat Campaign.

The day-long initiative aimed to reinforce the core values of cleanliness, personal hygiene and ecological mindfulness among service personnel, integrating environmental stewardship into daily military routine and garrison management.

The event commenced with a keynote address detailing the vision, spirit and national significance of the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026'. The talk emphasized that cleanliness is an integral component of military discipline, national pride and operational efficiency.

Dedicated interactive sessions were conducted on environmental conservation. Troops were encouraged to remain actively mindful of their daily actions and habits, highlighting how individual choices directly impact the surrounding ecology. Personnel were urged to adopt energy-efficient habits, reduce resource wastage and preserve local ecosystems.

Recognizing that healthy personnel are fundamental to military readiness, a clinical awareness session on Swachhta was also delivered by the Army's Medical Officer focusing on core operational pillars of Personal Hygiene, Sanitation & Cleanliness among soldiers.

Soldiers were also educated on modern waste management protocols centered around the core principles of Reduce, Reuse, Recycle and Recharge. Special emphasis was laid on reducing plastic waste, recycling organic materials and recharging groundwater reserves through rainwater harvesting units within military stations. An Army Official when contacted said, "Cleanliness and environmental responsibility are force multipliers that directly contribute to troop morale, health and operational readiness. Through initiatives under Swachh Bharat Campaign, the Spear Corps remains committed to leading by example in preserving our ecosystems and ensuring the highest standards of sanitation across all garrisons."

Spear Corps of the Indian Army is tasked with maintaining operational readiness and security across the North-Eastern frontier. Beyond its tactical duties, Spear Corps actively engages in nation-building, disaster relief, community development and ecological protection across the region.

*****

PS/AL

item.title: JLNHRC Takes Aanya 3.0 Leadership Learnings to the Workplace
item.description: Following the successful completion of Aanya 3.0, the Steel Authority of India Limited’s (SAIL) Women Leadership Development Programme, the first departmental-level Micro Learning Session was organised at the Jawaharlal Nehru Hospital and Research Centre (JLNHRC) of Bhilai Steel Plant. Dr. Uday Kumar, Chief Medical Officer (Medical and Health Services), was the Chief Guest, while Sanjeev Kumar Shrivastava, General Manager In-Charge (Human Resource–Learning and Development), attended the…
item.content:encoded:
Following the successful completion of Aanya 3.0, the Steel Authority of India Limited’s (SAIL) Women Leadership Development Programme, the first departmental-level Micro Learning Session was organised at the Jawaharlal Nehru Hospital and Research Centre (JLNHRC) of Bhilai Steel Plant. Dr. Uday Kumar, Chief Medical Officer (Medical and Health Services), was the Chief Guest, while Sanjeev Kumar Shrivastava, General Manager In-Charge (Human Resource–Learning and Development), attended the programme as Guest of Honour.

Aanya, SAIL’s flagship Women Leadership Development Programme, aims to strengthen leadership capabilities among selected women officers while fostering an enabling work environment that promotes diversity and inclusion. Taking this objective forward, the Micro Learning Session at JLNHRC focused on translating leadership learnings into workplace practices, particularly in the area of patient care and healthcare delivery.

The session was conceptualised and conducted by Dr. Mala Choudhary, Lead Advisor, Department of Paediatrics and Neonatology, JLNHRC, and Chief Advisor, Aanya 3.0. As a faculty member of Aanya, Dr. Choudhary carried the initiative forward in keeping with the programme’s emphasis on translating leadership learning into practical action at the workplace.

Speaking on the occasion, Sanjeev Kumar Shrivastava appreciated Bhilai Steel Plant’s initiative to sustain leadership development beyond formal training programmes and emphasised the need for regular organisation of such learning sessions. He said that such initiatives help extend the impact of learning across the organisation and strengthen leadership capabilities at different levels. This, in turn, can contribute to organisational excellence and improved healthcare services for patients.

The session, titled “Empowering Nurse Participants for Human Milk Donation – From Awareness to Action”, was attended by 20 executive and non-executive nurses of JLNHRC. The session covered identification of potential human milk donors, methods to motivate and engage donors on a sustained basis, counselling skills and measures to promote community participation. Special emphasis was placed on developing leadership capabilities among nurses and strengthening their role in promoting the health and survival of newborns.

Ms. Shweta Shabnam, Deputy General Manager (Projects), and Ms. B. Lalita, Deputy General Manager (Contract Cell, Works and Budgeting Department), both from the Aanya 1.0 batch, attended the programme as Special Guests. They shared their experiences from the leadership development programme and encouraged the participating nurses to strengthen leadership capabilities in their respective roles and contribute to positive change through their professional responsibilities.

The session was coordinated by Ms. Sushmita Patla, Deputy Manager (Human Resource–Learning and Development). Ms. Shyla Abraham, Deputy Manager (Nursing Administration), and Ms. Lata Mishra, Assistant Manager (Emergency Services), conducted the programme. The initiative marked a significant effort to take leadership development beyond the training room and translate the learning into practical workplace interventions, with a focus on patient care, nursing leadership and improved healthcare outcomes.

****


RDJ/BKT

item.title: AIIMS Raipur Hosts Guest Lecture on Climate Change and Health, Launches 7th Edition of Community Medicine Textbook
item.description:
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Raipur organised a guest lecture and book launch at the Swami Vivekanand Auditorium on Monday, bringing together senior faculty members, academic leaders, postgraduate residents, undergraduate students and other members of the institute for an academic discussion on emerging public health challenges.
The programme featured a guest lecture by Prof. Dr. Sanjay Zodpey, President, Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI), on…
item.content:encoded:
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Raipur organised a guest lecture and book launch at the Swami Vivekanand Auditorium on Monday, bringing together senior faculty members, academic leaders, postgraduate residents, undergraduate students and other members of the institute for an academic discussion on emerging public health challenges.

The programme featured a guest lecture by Prof. Dr. Sanjay Zodpey, President, Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI), on “Deciphering the Connect Between Climate Change and Health”. The lecture examined the growing interrelationship between climate change and human health and underlined the importance of strengthening public health preparedness to address emerging climate-related health challenges.

The programme commenced with lamp lighting and Saraswati Vandana in the presence of the dignitaries. Lt Gen Ashok Jindal (Retd.), Executive Director, AIIMS Raipur, formally introduced Prof. Dr. Sanjay Zodpey as the chief guest and guest speaker.

Addressing the gathering, Prof. Dr. Zodpey discussed the multifaceted health implications of climate change and emphasised the need to strengthen health systems, surveillance, preparedness and public health interventions in response to the changing environmental and epidemiological landscape. He highlighted the importance of integrating climate considerations into public health planning and healthcare delivery. Following the lecture, Prof. Dr. Zodpey was felicitated by AIIMS Raipur in recognition of his contribution to the field of public health and participation in the academic programme.

A major highlight of the event was the formal launch of the seventh edition (2026) of the Textbook of Community Medicine & Public Health. The updated edition covers contemporary developments in community medicine, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics and preventive medicine.

Prior to the launch, Dr. Aditi Chandrakar, Associate Editor, presented “What’s New in the 7th Edition?”, outlining the major additions, updates and academic features incorporated in the new edition. Lt. Col. Laxmikant Choudhary (Retd.), Associate Editor, subsequently presented an overview of the e-content and its key features, highlighting the digital academic resources accompanying the textbook.

The seventh edition was formally unveiled by the chief guest and other dignitaries, followed by a cake-cutting ceremony. The book launch was followed by academic reviews from faculty members of AIIMS Raipur. Prof. Dr. Anil K. Goel, Academic Head, School of Public Health, shared his academic assessment of the book, while Prof. Dr. Binu Mathew, Principal, College of Nursing, AIIMS Raipur, highlighted the importance of comprehensive public health knowledge for healthcare professionals and students. Representing the publisher, Mr. Ravi Vishwakarma, Manager, Content Management, presented the publisher’s perspective on the development and publication of the new edition.

The programme also recognised the research achievements of AIIMS Raipur students. Postgraduate residents who received Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) Thesis Grants and undergraduate students who received Short-Term Studentship (STS) Grants were felicitated by Prof. Dr. Zodpey for their research contributions. The recognition was aimed at encouraging evidence-based research and academic excellence among students. The dignitaries present on the dais were also felicitated. The programme concluded with the vote of thanks proposed by Prof. Dr. Eli Mohapatra, Dean (Academics), AIIMS Raipur.


****

RDJ/BKT

item.title: SAIL Chairman Addresses Large Group Interaction at Bhilai Steel Plant; Emphasises ‘My Area, My Responsibility’ and ‘Line of Fire’ to Strengthen Workplace Safety
item.description: Chairman and Managing Director of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), Dr. Ashok Kumar Panda, addressed a Large Group Interaction organised at Mahatma Gandhi Kala Mandir, Civic Centre, Bhilai, underscoring workplace safety as the foremost organizational priority. Emphasising the necessity of individual responsibility and active participation across all ranks, he engaged with officers, regular employees, contract workers, supervisors, and designated Safety Warriors of the Bhilai Steel Plant.…
item.content:encoded:
Chairman and Managing Director of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), Dr. Ashok Kumar Panda, addressed a Large Group Interaction organised at Mahatma Gandhi Kala Mandir, Civic Centre, Bhilai, underscoring workplace safety as the foremost organizational priority. Emphasising the necessity of individual responsibility and active participation across all ranks, he engaged with officers, regular employees, contract workers, supervisors, and designated Safety Warriors of the Bhilai Steel Plant.

Directing strict adherence to the principles of ‘My Area, My Responsibility’ and the ‘Line of Fire’ concept, the Chairman reiterated that the ultimate objective is zero loss of life and the safe return of every worker at the end of every shift. He insisted on zero tolerance towards unsafe practices and called for uncompromising compliance with standard operating procedures, including Permit to Work and shutdown protocols.

The event saw the presence of Shri Chitta Ranjan Mohapatra, Director In-Charge, Bhilai Steel Plant, alongside Executive Directors heading Materials Management, Finance and Accounts, Human Resources, Projects, Works, and Mines. Comprehensive presentations detailing workplace safety standards, incident prevention, and organizational safety initiatives were delivered by senior plant executives. Shri Mohapatra reinforced the necessity of collective ownership across every segment of the workforce to institutionalize continuous safe working habits. During an open floor exchange, Dr. Panda interacted directly with the workforce, reviewing their suggestions, ground-level operational challenges, and practical feedback aimed at reinforcing plant safety systems. The proceedings were conducted by Ms. Nisha Baul, Senior Manager (HR), and concluded with a formal vote of thanks delivered by Shri Prashant Ojha, Chief General Manager (HR).

Preceding the interactive session, the SAIL Chairman conducted an extensive inspection of vital production units and ongoing capital projects at the Bhilai Steel Plant to assess operational performance and expansion works. At Coke Oven Battery-8, Dr. Panda reviewed operational processes with departmental engineers to align plant efficiency with rigorous safety standards. During his review of the Plate Mill, he urged the workforce to maintain heightened situational awareness regarding moving machinery hazards in adherence to the ‘Line of Fire’ doctrine.

At Steel Melting Shop-3 (SMS-3), Dr. Panda firmly stated that safety must always take precedence over production targets, officially empowering all employees to immediately halt operations upon spotting any unsafe act or condition, while announcing that proactive safety interventions would be suitably rewarded. Concluding his visit with a comprehensive review of the Projects Department, he directed that all ongoing schemes be completed in a time-bound manner with optimal resource utilization, strong stakeholder coordination, and strategic alignment with the long-term operational needs of the plant.
 

******


RDJ/PJ

Among the prominent mementos featured is a detailed model of the Ram…
item.content:encoded:
A diverse collection of 99 mementos offers a glimpse into Uttar Pradesh’s cultural heritage, historical legacy and contemporary achievements. Featuring spiritual artefacts, traditional art, sporting memorabilia and models of major infrastructure projects. The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online till October 2, 2026. For details and participation, visit https://pmmementos.gov.in

Among the prominent mementos featured is a detailed model of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, crafted in MDF fibreboard with intricate architectural detailing.

Another memento features the Shri Guru Ravidas Janam Asthan Mandir in Varanasi, highlighting the spiritual and cultural legacy associated with Guru Ravidas.

A framed portrait of Rani Lakshmi Bai depicts the Queen of Jhansi on horseback with her son Damodar Rao, while a contemporary Sanjhi paper-cut artwork from Mathura presents a "Tree of Life with Holy Cows”. The Sanjhi piece also showcases the intricate hand-cutting technique associated with the traditional art form.

Uttar Pradesh’s sporting achievements are represented by a signed shirt belonging to para-athlete Preeti Pal, who won two bronze medals in the 100m and 200m T35 events at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.

The catalogue also features a miniature model of the Meerut Metro, commemorating the inauguration of its 26-km corridor in February 2026.

Other notable entries include a Namo Ghat Varanasi hand namaste memento, a sculptural representation of the distinctive joined hands at Namo Ghat and a Ganga Expressway model featuring Goddess Ganga alongside a miniature representation of the infrastructure project.

Together, these mementos bring different facets of Uttar Pradesh into focus, from its traditions and history to its achievements and landmarks.

***

M Annadurai

item.title: NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities”- an initiative under NITI Aayog’s State Support Mission (SSM)
item.description: NITI Aayog organised a national workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities” on 28th September 2026, in collaboration with the Golap Borbora State Institute of Panchayat & Rural Development (GBSIPRD), Government of Assam. The workshop focused on strengthening Panchayats as institutions capable of driving inclusive growth, effective public service delivery, and sustainable development at the grassroots, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.…
item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog organised a national workshop on “Viksit Panchayat: Connecting People, Places, Resources and Opportunities” on 28th September 2026, in collaboration with the Golap Borbora State Institute of Panchayat & Rural Development (GBSIPRD), Government of Assam. The workshop focused on strengthening Panchayats as institutions capable of driving inclusive growth, effective public service delivery, and sustainable development at the grassroots, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

The one-day National Workshop was inaugurated by Shri Atul Bora, Minister, Panchayat & Rural Development Department, Government of Assam, as the Chief Guest; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, as the Guest of Honour; Dr. Ravi Kota, Chief Secretary, Government of Assam; and Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development.

The inaugural session highlighted the importance of decentralised governance, spatial planning, capacity development, digitalisation, and convergence for advancing Viksit Gram Panchayats. The deliberations focused on four key areas: decentralised and spatial planning, grassroots capacity development, spatial planning for priority sectors, and integration of spatial planning into the GPDP process.

Participants discussed the constitutional foundation of Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and Part IX of the Constitution. Discussions also focused on clearer activity mapping, adequate financial resources, appropriate staffing, greater decision-making authority, Gram Sabha participation, and institutional accountability. The workshop emphasised the need to move from a sectoral to a spatial and integrated approach to local development. GIS, geospatial data, village master plans, and digital platforms were discussed for identifying local resources, infrastructure gaps, land-use patterns, and development opportunities. Integrating spatial information with GPDP, eGramSwaraj, and Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) was highlighted as a means of strengthening evidence-based and convergence-oriented planning.

Capacity development and institutional strengthening were also central to the deliberations. Participants emphasised equipping elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries with skills in data interpretation, investment prioritisation, resource mobilisation, convergence, and outcome monitoring. Discussions covered devolution, activity mapping, District Planning Committees, digital and hybrid learning, competency development, and last-mile technical handholding. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam (Member, NITI Aayog) called for a shift from sectoral planning to a spatial planning approach, with greater emphasis on human and social capital and the development of local economic clusters.

The workshop identified priorities including clearer functional devolution and activity mapping, improved fiscal resources and own-source revenue mobilisation, stronger capacity and technical support, operational District Planning Committees, and greater convergence across departments and schemes. It also highlighted the need to strengthen the use of spatial and administrative data in GPDPs, Gram Sabha and community participation, and rural-urban planning at the district level.

item.description:

item.content:encoded:
Udhampur has witnessed a revolutionary transformation over the last 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the development of infrastructure and public facilities across different sectors. This was stated by the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today.

The Minister was addressing a gathering while holding a Public Darbar at Tikri near here, where he interacted with members of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), several public delegations and local citizens, and listened to their issues, grievances and demands.

 

The Public Darbar was attended by Deputy Commissioner Minga Sherpa led senior officers of various district administration departments, representatives of PRIs and members of several delegations. The local leaders were led by BJP. District President Arun Gupta and others.


 

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the efforts of the Deputy Commissioner Minga Sherpa and the district administration team, and said that the administration's efforts would contribute to taking Udhampur to new heights.


 

Several issues were resolved on the spot and instructions issued for speedy redressal of some of the issues raised by the public.

 

 

Aimed at addressing cleanliness and sewage-related issues in Udhampur city, 9 crore rupees are being exclusively allocated for sewage maintenance in Udhampur, while 4 crore rupees for rejuvenation, the Minister said adding that further funds would be sanctioned after assessment of the damages and the requirements on the ground, with the objective of finding a long-term solution to the sewage problem.

 

 

The Minister said that Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, to commemorate 20 years of PM Sh Narendra Modi as the continuous head of government, aims at strengthening public service delivery through direct engagement with people. He said the campaign provides an opportunity to take government initiatives closer to the people, understand issues at the grassroots and facilitate their timely resolution through coordinated efforts of the administration and concerned departments.

 

Highlighting Aangan Milan Seva programme the Minister said that this initiative is aimed at strengthening community participation at Anganwadi centres and connecting families with services relating to maternal and child health, nutrition and welfare schemes. The initiative, being organised from September 25 to October 7, also provides a platform to recognise the contribution of Anganwadi and ASHA workers and to encourage greater participation of parents and the community in activities concerning children and families.

 

During the Public Darbar, Dr. Jitendra Singh interacted with PRIs and several delegations and listened to their issues, grievances and demands. He said that the Public Darbar is an effort to resolve the issues of the people through direct interaction and directed various departments of the district administration to undertake fast-track action on the issues raised.

 

Senior officers from several line departments, including the Public Works Department (PWD), PMGSY and other departments, were present during the interaction. The officers assured that the grievances raised by the public would be examined and necessary action taken for their early resolution.


 

Issues relating to mobile connectivity and water supply, including water pumps, were also raised during the Public Darbar. The Minister directed the concerned departments to examine these issues and take necessary measures for their resolution.

 

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the efforts of the Deputy Commissioner and the district administration team and said that the administration's efforts would contribute to taking Udhampur to new heights.

 

The Public Darbar was attended by senior officers of various district administration departments, representatives of PRIs and members of several delegations.
