item.content:encoded:
Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign started in DSIR and its organizations i.e in CEL, NRDC, CSIR and its laboratories across the country on 17th September, 2026 with the Pledge taking ceremony by Dr. (Mrs) N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, DSIR cum DG, CSIR urging officials and staff to actively participate in the campaign and contribute towards cleanliness and hygiene.

Under the guidance of Secretary, DSIR cum DG, CSIR, the nodal officer of the Campaign in the Department, Shri Surinder Pal Singh, Joint Secretary geared up all the organizations under the Department to make the campaign successful. As a part of the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, an awareness session on the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, was conducted at CSIR-Institute of Microbial Technology (CSIR-IMTECH), Chandigarh wherein the key provisions of the SWM Rules, 2026, was explained to the housekeeping and horticulture staff. The four-way segregation of solid waste at source was demonstrated and emphasized the need to shift from the conventional approach of “Collect and Dump” to “Segregate, Process and Recover” for effective and sustainable waste management. As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, a “Carry Your Own Bag” awareness drive was also organized on September 19, 2026, The initiative aimed to encourage citizens to adopt sustainable practices by carrying reusable bags and reducing the use of single-use plastics. During the drive, a demonstration of four-way source segregation of waste, in accordance with the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, was also conducted to promote responsible waste disposal and enhancement of public awareness.

As a part of the campaign, a “Safai Mitra Swasthya Shivir” was organised at the CSIR-CIMAP Dispensary on 26 September 2026. Around 50 sanitation workers from CSIR-CIMAP, Lucknow, and the Staff Colony underwent a comprehensive medical check-up during the camp.

Under Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026, thematic art competition was organized for the employees of DSIR in Technology Bhavan. A lecture on “Awareness on Solid Waste Management” was also organized at KV RRL, Jorhat for the students.

  ’Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ was organized under the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign wherein plantations were done with a view to Green India and Clean India.

item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, September 28, 2026


The Union Minister of Coal & Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, reviewed the activities, achievements and future roadmap of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) today at a meeting held in the city. The review focused on strengthening India’s mineral security, accelerating exploration of critical and strategic minerals, adoption of advanced technologies and ensuring outcome-oriented exploration.

 

The meeting was organised in the gracious presence of Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Smt. Varsha Ashok Aglawe, Director General, GSI and senior officials of the Ministry of Mines and GSI. During the review, the Union Minister was apprised of GSI’s overall achievement and action plan including region-wise exploration achievements, ongoing programmes, emerging exploration opportunities, technological capabilities and future plans, with particular emphasis on critical and strategic minerals.

During Field Season 2026-27, GSI is undertaking around 500 mineral exploration projects, including approximately 300 projects focused on critical and strategic minerals. GSI is also intensifying exploration for concealed and deep-seated mineral deposits through integrated geological, geophysical and geochemical investigations and advanced exploration techniques. GSI is simultaneously undertaking studies in natural hazards, glaciology, geotechnical investigations, offshore exploration and geoinformatics.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Reddy emphasised that mineral security is a key national priority and called for accelerated exploration in prospective areas and faster progression of high-potential mineral occurrences from discovery to resource establishment and mineral development. He stressed timely completion of projects and outcome-oriented exploration so that GSI’s scientific expertise is translated into actionable geoscientific outputs supporting domestic mineral supply chains, reducing import dependence and contributing to India’s clean-energy transition and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, emphasised the need for a technology-driven faster and integrated approach to mineral exploration, leveraging multidisciplinary geoscientific datasets, advanced analytical capabilities including digital scanning of legacy cores and inter-agency collaboration. He also stressed strengthening the exploration-to-resource pipeline so that suitable mineral blocks can be taken forward for auction and contribute to long-term mineral security.

Director General, GSI, Smt. Varsha Ashok Aglawe, in her welcome address highlighted GSI’s roadmap for further strengthening critical-mineral exploration in onshore and offshore domains, exploration of concealed mineralisation and adoption of advanced technologies. The roadmap includes wider application of AI/ML, 3D/4D geological modelling, Pan-India magneto telluric survey and development of a country-wide subsurface critical-mineral potential map. GSI is also undertaking 58 Geoinformatics and Data Analysis projects during Field Season 2026–27, including initiatives involving AI/ML and integration of geoscientific datasets through the National Geoscience Data Repository and Next Generation Portal.

A comprehensive presentation on GSI’s activities, achievements, major thrust areas and future roadmap was made by Shri Pradeep Singh, ADG (PSS), followed by region-wise presentations by heads of the region covering exploration programmes, scientific capabilities, laboratory and analytical facilities, application of emerging technologies and future plans.

During the review meeting, Shri Reddy also unveiled two commemorative volumes of GSI; “Earth Beneath Our Feet” and “Earth Without Lines”, showcasing the organisation’s more than 175-year scientific journey and geoscientific legacy. While Earth Beneath Our Feet traces GSI’s contribution to India’s geoscientific knowledge and national development, Earth Without Lines documents its geoscientific work and scientific engagements across several countries and regions in the Indian subcontinent and beyond.

 

SSS/Kol/

item.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for ‘Team Agriculture’ to Make India a Global Food Basket
item.description: On the second day of the National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan chaired a session attended by Agriculture Ministers and senior officials from various states. Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said that under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Centre and states must rise above party politics and work in the spirit of ‘Team Agriculture’ to…
item.content:encoded:
On the second day of the National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan chaired a session attended by Agriculture Ministers and senior officials from various states. Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said that under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Centre and states must rise above party politics and work in the spirit of ‘Team Agriculture’ to ensure the country’s food security and improve farmers’ livelihoods. “Governments and political parties come and go; parties are formed and dissolved, but the country and its farmers are eternal,” he said, stressing that the platform was not about politics but about finding practical ways to improve agriculture and advance the interests of farmers. Shri Chouhan also highlighted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, farmers’ interests have been accorded the highest priority in every major policy decision and international agreement. At the conference, Shri Chouhan handed over financial sanction letters worth more than ₹1200 crore to Agriculture Ministers of 10 states under the Prime Minister Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY). Union Ministers of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, ICAR Director General Dr. M. L. Jat, along with senior officials from the Centre and states, scientists and representatives of various agricultural institutions, were present at the conference.

More than ₹ 1200 crore sanctioned to 10 states under PM-RKVY

Under PM-RKVY, sanction letters were distributed to 10 states, including ₹290 crore for West Bengal, ₹198 crore for Haryana, ₹181 crore for Chhattisgarh, ₹154 crore for Arunachal Pradesh, ₹114 crore for Bihar, ₹104 crore for Karnataka, ₹75 crore for Mizoram, ₹64 crore for Himachal Pradesh, ₹58 crore for Jharkhand and ₹43 crore for Punjab.

Shri Chouhan said the Union Government was not limiting itself to policy formulation, but was also ensuring timely availability of resources to states so that implementation of schemes could begin on the ground without delay.

Agriculture growth rate rises to 4.5 per cent

Highlighting the country’s agricultural performance, Shri Chouhan said that since 2015, the agriculture growth rate has increased from 3 per cent to 4.5 per cent. The average annual increase in foodgrain production has also more than doubled, rising from around 40 lakh tonnes earlier to 84 lakh tonnes per year. He further noted that in just two years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, rabi foodgrain production recorded an unprecedented increase of 205 lakh tonnes. He attributed this historic growth to the collective efforts of state agriculture departments, scientists and farmers.

 

Monthly virtual reviews with states to strengthen cooperative federalism

Announcing a new mechanism to further strengthen cooperative federalism, Shri Chouhan said that, on the lines of weekly reviews conducted at the Centre, regular monthly virtual review meetings with states would now be held to continuously assess progress. At the state level, a strong State Agriculture Team will be constituted by bringing together the Agriculture Minister, Agriculture Secretary, state agricultural universities, ICAR institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), ATMA, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), progressive farmers, processors, exporters and nodal officers of the Government of India. At the district level, monthly meetings will be held involving the Collector, Deputy Director of Agriculture (DDA), ATMA, KVKs, ICAR scientists, bankers and farmers.

 

Annual calendar for pre-season agriculture interface meetings

To ensure advance preparation for agricultural campaigns, Shri Chouhan announced an annual calendar for interface meetings. For the Kharif campaign, district-level meetings will be held on May 10 and state-level meetings on May 17 every year. Similarly, for the Rabi campaign, district-level meetings will be held on September 10 and state-level meetings on September 17 every year. In addition, a one-day special meeting will be organised across the country on a common date, bringing together Agriculture Ministers, officials and agricultural scientists simultaneously to discuss issues concerning farmers.

 

‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from October 22 to November 30

Emphasising the need to protect soil health and the environment, Shri Chouhan called for a nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from October 22 to November 30 this year. Scientists and all key stakeholders will actively participate in the campaign. Based on Soil Health Cards, the campaign will promote balanced use of fertilisers to protect soil fertility and beneficial insects. He also called for large-scale promotion of pulse cultivation in rice fallow areas of eastern India, particularly in Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal, after the paddy harvest.

 

Rabi preparations to focus on soil moisture, water availability and crop protection

As part of preparations for the current rabi season, Shri Chouhan stressed that recommendations on crops and improved seeds should be based on soil moisture and water availability. He directed states to put in place effective arrangements to protect crops from diseases and pests, ensure saturation of all eligible farmers with Kisan Credit Cards (KCCs) and conduct transparent Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) under the crop insurance scheme. He also emphasised that state ministers should personally undertake regular reviews of the implementation of departmental schemes.

 

Strict action against spurious inputs, end to forced tagging

Stating that the availability of seeds and fertilisers in the country is adequate, Shri Chouhan directed states to take strict legal action against fake fertilisers, spurious seeds and sub-standard pesticides. He also directed that forced tagging be completely eliminated. Calling for agriculture to become more sustainable and remunerative, he urged states to adopt natural farming, integrated farming systems and crop diversification in mission mode.

 

Government working on multi-pronged strategy to ensure remunerative prices for farmers

Shri Chouhan said the government is pursuing a multi-dimensional strategy to ensure that farmers receive fair and remunerative prices for their produce. The strategy includes strengthening post-harvest management, scientific warehousing and marketing systems. He said that 100 per cent assured government procurement of tur, urad and masoor at MSP would be undertaken, with arrangements for payment within 48 hours. In line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, he said India would also leverage the new market opportunities emerging from international Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to connect Indian agricultural products, fruits, vegetables and foodgrains with global markets. This, he said, would help farmers secure better returns for their produce and enable India to emerge as a major ‘food basket’ for the world.

*****

SS/MS/DK

item.title: IndiaAI Regional Dialogue on AI Innovation and State Partnerships (West Bengal Chapter)
item.description:
Kolkata, September 28, 2026
The IndiaAI Mission under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, today convened the inaugural Regional IndiaAI Workshop-cum-Review with the States at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata hosted by Government of West Bengal, bringing together senior government officials and representatives from West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand and Sikkim for focused discussions on strengthening State-level AI capabilities…
item.content:encoded:
Kolkata, September 28, 2026


The IndiaAI Mission under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, today convened the inaugural Regional IndiaAI Workshop-cum-Review with the States at the New Town Convention Centre, Kolkata hosted by Government of West Bengal, bringing together senior government officials and representatives from West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand and Sikkim for focused discussions on strengthening State-level AI capabilities and identifying pathways for collaboration with the IndiaAI Mission. The Workshop was hosted in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal.

The Workshop marks the beginning of a proposed series of regional Government-to-Government engagements aimed at enabling States to leverage the capabilities and initiatives of the IndiaAI Mission for AI-led governance, public service delivery and institutional capacity building.

The IndiaAI Mission is developing a comprehensive National AI Ecosystem spanning areas including Datasets, AI Compute, Innovation, Centres of Excellence, Application Development, FutureSkills and Safe & Trusted AI. The State Governments play a vital role as catalysts in translating these national capabilities into sector-specific and citizen-centric applications based on their local priorities, institutional capacities and data resources.

Against this backdrop, the Regional Workshop series has been conceived as a structured platform for interaction between the IndiaAI Mission and State Governments, with a focus on understanding State-level requirements, identifying areas for convergence and developing pathways for sustained collaboration.

Senior Leadership Sets the Context for State – IndiaAI Collaboration

The inaugural session featured an Inaugural Address by Dr. Kalyan Chakraborti, Hon'ble Minister-in-Charge, Departments of Information Technology & Electronics, Science & Technology and Biotechnology, and Food Processing Industries & Horticulture, Government of West Bengal, followed by a Keynote Address by Shri Shubhanjan Das, Secretary, Department of Information Technology & Electronics, Government of West Bengal, on the State's implementation priorities and way forward, and a Special Address by Shri Saurabh Vijay, CEO, IndiaAI and CEO, UIDAI, on the Vision, Ambition and Priorities of the IndiaAI Mission.

Sharing West Bengal's perspective on AI-led governance, State-level innovation and collaboration Dr. Kalyan Chakraborti, Hon’ble Minister in Charge, Departments of Information Technology & Electronics, Science & Technology and Biotechnology, and Food Processing Industries & Horticulture, Government of West Bengal, said:

“This workshop is bringing together 5 states on a common platform to review AI readiness, exchange experiences, and discuss opportunities for collaboration. Platforms like these are important because the development of AI cannot be viewed from just the perspective of technology. It requires coordination among government, academia, research institutions, industry, startups and the wider ecosystem within.”

Highlighting the IndiaAI Mission's vision and the vitality of States participation Shri Saurabh Vijay, CEO, IndiaAI Mission and CEO, UIDAI, said:

“While Western tech models rely heavily on centralization controlled by just a few companies, our strength lies in democratization. I invite more states to adopt AIKosh as our shared, empowering platform. With data sets steadily growing since its launch, we are making strong progress and continuing to strengthen India’s AI ecosystem.”

Emphasizing the State's implementation priorities and roadmap for AI integration Shri Shri Shubhanjan Das IAS, Secretary, Department of Information Technology & Electronics and Department of Fisheries, Aquaculture, Aquatic Resources & Fishing Harbour, Govt. of West Bengal, said: “Today's thematic sessions are going to be of considerable benefit and provide rich insights for every participating state, and I firmly hope that the government of India will help us, guide us, and handhold us in our journey towards a very strong AI ecosystem of eastern India.”

Focused Deliberations across Key IndiaAI Priorities

Following an overview of the IndiaAI Mission's Seven Pillars and State engagement framework, the Workshop featured Thematic Sessions focused on areas directly relevant to State-level AI adoption:

  • The FutureSkills Pillar: Examined AI talent development, skilling priorities, State-level capacity building, academia-industry partnerships and opportunities for convergence, along with updates on Data Labs and inputs for accelerated implementation.

  • The AIKosh Pillar: Focused on datasets, AI models and resources, data sharing, State datasets and opportunities for State-level adoption and contribution. The discussions also brought together representatives from government, academia, C-DAC and the Centre of Excellence ecosystem.

  • The Startup Financing Pillar: Explored the startup ecosystem, State-specific opportunities, pathways for participation and updates on the development of Centres of Excellence.

  • The Application Development Initiative: Focused on potential use cases across sectors, enabling AI deployment in priority areas and strengthening the adoption of safe, trusted and responsible AI solutions.

  • AI Talent Mission and State Support: Examined areas of institutional and State-level support, bringing together representatives from State departments, higher and technical education, academia and the wider technology ecosystem.

The Programme also included a stakeholder interaction with startups, academic institutions and ecosystem partners, enabling wider discussion on opportunities and challenges in building AI capabilities and applications.

The Workshop concluded with a Special Session on “AI with the Conscience: The Responsible and Ethical Way Forward”, followed by the Way Forward and Key Takeaways from the Workshop.

From Regional Dialogue to Sustained State Collaboration

The Kolkata engagement is envisaged as the first step in a broader series of Regional IndiaAI Workshops with State Governments. The proposed framework seeks to establish a structured Government-to-Government mechanism through which State priorities can be mapped against IndiaAI resources and initiatives, including AIKosh, Data & AI Labs, Centres of Excellence, AI compute and infrastructure, FutureSkills, fellowships and AI applications.

The engagements are intended to move beyond awareness-building towards identification of State-specific Use Cases, Datasets, Infrastructure Requirements, Talent Needs, Institutional Capabilities and concrete areas of collaboration. The Workshop format also provides a mechanism for identifying State Nodal Officers and defining follow-up actions for continued engagement.

The Kolkata Workshop included representatives from West Bengal as well as neighbouring States including Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand and Sikkim, providing a Regional Platform for sharing priorities and identifying opportunities for convergence.

Building India's AI Ecosystem through Collaborative Federal Engagement

The Regional Workshop Series represents a collaborative approach to strengthening India's AI Ecosystem by connecting the national capabilities being developed under the IndiaAI Mission with the priorities, institutions, datasets, talent and implementation capacity available across States.

As the Series progresses across regions, these engagements are expected to provide a foundation for sustained collaboration, knowledge exchange and coordinated implementation between the IndiaAI Mission and State Governments. Together, such efforts can help create a more connected and distributed AI ecosystem, enabling States to develop and deploy AI solutions that respond to local priorities while contributing to India's broader national AI ambitions.

Through continued collaboration between Government, Industry, and Academia, the IndiaAI Mission strengthens India's AI Ecosystem contributing to our Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

*****

Vinod Kumar / Dhanya Ranjan

item.title: Two-Week Refresher Course on Leadership and Academic Administration Concludes at Manipur University
item.description:
The two-week Multidisciplinary Refresher Course on “Leadership, Academic Administration, and Legal Excellence in Higher Education”, organised by the UGC Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centre (MMTTC), Manipur University, under the Ministry of Education, Government of India, concluded with a valedictory function at the MIMS Auditorium on Monday.
Held from September 16 to 28, the course brought together faculty members and university officials from Manipur and outside the State. A total…
item.content:encoded:
The two-week Multidisciplinary Refresher Course on “Leadership, Academic Administration, and Legal Excellence in Higher Education”, organised by the UGC Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centre (MMTTC), Manipur University, under the Ministry of Education, Government of India, concluded with a valedictory function at the MIMS Auditorium on Monday.

Held from September 16 to 28, the course brought together faculty members and university officials from Manipur and outside the State. A total of 53 participants, comprising teachers and administrative officers, have attended the refresher course. The programme covered leadership, academic administration, legal issues, communication, mental well-being, financial management, interpersonal relations and emerging technologies in higher education.

Prof. M. Premjit Singh, Registrar, Manipur University; Prof. Laishram Rajendrakumar Singh, Finance Officer; Prof. R.K. Bhubon Singh, Director, MMTTC; and Prof. Ch. Ibohal Meitei, Programme Coordinator and Director, Manipur Institute of Management Studies, attended the valedictory function as presidium members.

Presenting a brief report of the course, Prof. Ch. Ibohal Meitei said the success of such training should ultimately be reflected in changes in participants’ outlook, professional interaction and approach to institutional responsibilities. He stressed continuous self-improvement and said the programme had incorporated role plays, group discussions, presentations and case studies alongside academic sessions.

Registrar Prof. M. Premjit Singh said multidisciplinary refresher courses could expose academics and administrators to ideas beyond their specialised fields and help refresh their thinking and professional capabilities.

Finance Officer Prof. Laishram Rajendrakumar Singh highlighted trust and accountability, resourcefulness and teamwork as essential attributes of effective leadership. He urged participants to translate the knowledge gained during the programme into action in their respective institutions.

Prof. R.K. Bhubon Singh said the MMTTC had attempted to cover diverse dimensions of academic administration and legal issues within the two-week programme. Responding to participant feedback, he said the Centre would explore specialised programmes on areas such as examination, evaluation and question-setting.

During the feedback session, participants appreciated the multidisciplinary and experiential nature of the course, its range of resource persons and opportunities for interaction among academics and administrators from different institutions. Suggestions were also made for incorporating field activities, examination-related training and greater interaction with practitioners in future programmes.

Certificates were distributed to the participants during the valedictory function. The programme concluded with remarks and a vote of thanks by Prof. R.K. Bhubon Singh.

***

                    RCT

item.title: Ministry of MSME and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation Sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register
item.description:
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been exchanged between Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), to institutionalize a mechanism for sharing relevant data for the development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register (SBR).
The MoU was signed by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Dalip Singh, Additional Director General, MoSPI, in the presence…
item.content:encoded:
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been exchanged between Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), to institutionalize a mechanism for sharing relevant data for the development and strengthening of the Statistical Business Register (SBR).

The MoU was signed by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Dalip Singh, Additional Director General, MoSPI, in the presence of senior officers from Ministry of MSME and MoSPI.



 

Objectives of the MoU:-

-The MoU sets the terms and understanding between the Ministry of MSME and MoSPI in relation to the sharing of unit-wise data of the Udyam Registration available with MSME  Department through APIs. The two-way API shall provide data for preparation of National Statistical Business Register (NSBR).

-The MoU will facilitate a structured framework for sharing relevant information from the Udyam Registration ecosystem of the Ministry of MSME with MoSPI. The information will contribute to improving the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information used for statistical purposes.

 



Statistical Business Register (SBR): An Overview

-The Statistical Business Register (SBR) is a central and regularly updated database of registered statistical units engaged in economic activities within a defined geographical territory.
It captures businesses, enterprises, establishments & other relevant economic units, key characteristics of economic units and relationships between different units.


- The SBR serves as foundational infrastructure for the economic statistics system to improve the coverage, consistency and reliability of business information by identifying the target population for economic surveys, supporting survey sample selection, enabling the production of business demography statistics, providing a common framework for business demography-related information, and facilitating integration and consistency across different data sources.

***

Sunil Kumar Tiwari

item.title: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to Undertake Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Cleanliness of National Highways and Toll Plazas
item.description:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) will undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with a special focus on improving cleanliness and upkeep of National Highways (NHs) and Toll Plazas. The campaign will also focus on reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible disposal of e-waste and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across organisations under the administrative control of the Ministry.
The campaign is being…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) will undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with a special focus on improving cleanliness and upkeep of National Highways (NHs) and Toll Plazas. The campaign will also focus on reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible disposal of e-waste and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across organisations under the administrative control of the Ministry.

The campaign is being implemented in two phases. The Preparatory Phase, being undertaken from 15th to 30th September 2026, focuses on identification of targets and preparatory activities for cleanliness drives, disposal of obsolete items and other activities to be undertaken during the main campaign period commencing from 2nd October 2026.

Under Special Campaign 6.0, focused efforts will be undertaken for garbage removal along National Highways, particularly in urban areas; refurbishment of toilet blocks at Toll Plazas and other locations along NHs; cleaning and maintenance of functional toilets; and overall improvement in the upkeep of Toll Plazas. The campaign will also cover cleaning, painting, improved lighting and solarisation of Toll Plazas, installation and improvement of road signage, enhancement of visibility of road markings, and making National Highways pothole-free, among other activities.

As part of the campaign, the Ministry has identified a 50-km stretch of National Highway, including one Toll Plaza, for focused intervention. Officers from the Headquarters will be deputed to inspect the identified stretches and assess the impact of the cleanliness and improvement measures. The nominated officers will visit the assigned stretches, identify and geo-tag deficiencies, and continuously monitor the progress of rectification works. They will also ensure timely resolution of the identified deficiencies and improvement in cleanliness, safety and overall upkeep of the National Highway during the campaign period.

The Ministry has sensitised all Campaign Offices, including Headquarters, Regional Offices, Programme Implementation Units, Programme Directors and other field offices, to undertake concerted efforts for effective implementation of Special Campaign 6.0 and ensure visible and sustainable outcomes.

Nodal Officers have been nominated for organisations under the administrative control of the Ministry to coordinate and oversee implementation of the campaign within their respective organisations and regularly report progress to the Ministry. The Joint Secretary (Coord.) has been nominated as the Nodal Officer for overall coordination of Special Campaign 6.0 across the Ministry and its organisations.

The progress of Special Campaign 6.0 is being regularly reviewed by the Joint Secretary (Coord.) with the Nodal Officers of the Campaign Offices. The Secretary, MoRTH, is also regularly reviewing the progress of the Preparatory Phase during the weekly Senior Officers’ Meetings.

Through Special Campaign 6.0, the Ministry is endeavouring to ensure cleaner, safer and better-maintained National Highways and Toll Plazas, while strengthening efficiency, record management and workplace practices across its organisations.

***

GDH/DS/HJ

item.title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs and IGNCA Sign MoU for Preservation, Documentation and Promotion of Tribal Cultural Heritage
item.description:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous trust under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 28, 2026, for the preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal cultural heritage.
The MoU was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Ms. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous trust under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 28, 2026, for the preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal cultural heritage.

The MoU was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Ms. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior officials of the Ministry. Dr. K. Anil Kumar, HoD, IGNCA, and other senior officials of IGNCA were also present on the occasion. The partnership brings together the Ministry’s tribal research ecosystem and network of Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) with IGNCA’s academic, archival, research and curatorial expertise.

The MoU aims to establish an institutional framework for collaboration between MoTA and IGNCA for the systematic preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal tangible and intangible cultural heritage. It seeks to leverage the expertise and resources of both institutions to document, protect and disseminate tribal arts, music, languages, oral traditions, folklore, crafts, customary practices and traditional knowledge, while creating wider platforms for their recognition and promotion.

Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, appreciated the initiative to preserve and promote India’s rich tribal cultural heritage, and underlined the importance and significance of the collaboration. She highlighted that the partnership would contribute significantly to tribal empowerment and the wider promotion and recognition of India’s diverse tribal cultural traditions.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ganesh Nagarajan, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, said, “This MoU provides an important institutional framework for bringing together the strengths of MoTA and IGNCA to preserve and promote India’s rich and diverse tribal cultural heritage.”

India’s tribal communities have a rich diversity of arts, music, musical instruments, crafts, cuisines, languages, oral traditions, folklore, customary practices and traditional ecological knowledge. Much of this heritage is living and community-based. The collaboration will provide an institutional framework for the systematic identification, documentation, digitisation, publication and dissemination of vanishing tribal arts, music, musical instruments, tribal cuisines and other cultural traditions.

The partnership will also support the identification, protection and promotion of endangered tribal languages, oral traditions, indigenous art forms and folklore. Another key area of cooperation will be the development of dedicated galleries and digital museums showcasing tribal arts, artefacts and the historical contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle. Youth camps in educational institutions and other centres of learning will be supported to promote awareness of tribal cultural values, sustainable conservation practices and the diversity of tribal customary practices and culture.

Dr. K. Anil Kumar, HoD, IGNCA, said, “this is a crucial collaboration between MoTA and IGNCA to preserve, document, and promote India's rich and diverse tribal tangible and intangible cultural heritage. The partnership will also support establishment of digital archives, and designing state-of-the-art interactive tribal museum galleries including dedicated showcases highlighting the contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle.”

The collaboration will facilitate wider dissemination of tribal cultural heritage through exhibitions, museums, publications, digital platforms, cultural festivals and knowledge-sharing initiatives, while creating greater visibility for tribal scholars, artists, artisans, performers and traditional knowledge holders at national and international platforms.

*****

RN/

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) actively participated in …
item.content:encoded:
The Government of India has announced the launch of Special Campaign 6, to be conducted from 2nd–31st October 2026, with the preparatory phase from 15th–30th September 2026. The campaign will focus on institutionalising cleanliness in Government offices, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management, effective space utilisation and enhancing workplace experience.

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) actively participated in Special Campaign 5.0 with a strong emphasis on cleanliness, records management, space optimisation and disposal of pending references across its offices and institutions. During the campaign, more than 1,836 cleanliness drives were conducted. The Ministry disposed of 3 references from Members of Parliament, 7 Parliament Assurances, 307 Public Grievances and 27 Public Grievance Appeals.

As part of the record management initiatives, 1,250 files were reviewed and 466 files were weeded out. In addition, 658 e-files were reviewed, out of which 266 e-files were closed. These efforts resulted in freeing approximately 4,000 square feet of office space through weeding out of files and disposal of scrap. The disposal of scrap also generated revenue of approximately ₹7.58 lakh.

The collective efforts of MSDE and its attached, autonomous, subordinate and field offices contributed towards creating cleaner and more efficient workplaces, improving record management and optimising available office space. The campaign also strengthened awareness regarding the importance of maintaining a clean office environment and responsible disposal of waste.

In preparation for Special Campaign 6, MSDE has initiated preparatory activities and is coordinating with the nodal officers and stakeholders of its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations and field institutions. The nodal officers are being sensitised regarding the key focus areas of the campaign, including cleanliness, disposal of pending references, efficient record management, e-waste management in accordance with the applicable E-Waste Management Rules, 2022, space management and enhancement of workplace experience.

The Ministry is committed to carrying forward the momentum generated during Special Campaign 5.0 and contributing significantly to the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through sustainable cleanliness practices, effective disposal of pendency, responsible e-waste management, improved record management and creation of cleaner, more efficient and better-utilised workspaces.

item.title: Two officials apprehended for seeking illegal gratification to facilitate FCRA registration
item.description:
Acting on specific information received by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Special Cell of Delhi Police, in coordination with central agencies, apprehended two government officials in New Delhi on 28 September 2026. The two officials, one working as a Senior Accountant and the other as an Accountant, had allegedly approached an association and sought illegal gratification in return for facilitating its pending FCRA registration.
One of the officials is presently posted in the…
item.content:encoded:
Acting on specific information received by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Special Cell of Delhi Police, in coordination with central agencies, apprehended two government officials in New Delhi on 28 September 2026. The two officials, one working as a Senior Accountant and the other as an Accountant, had allegedly approached an association and sought illegal gratification in return for facilitating its pending FCRA registration.

One of the officials is presently posted in the Foreigners Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs, while the other, presently posted in a Pay & Accounts Office, had earlier served in the Foreigners Division. Preliminary questioning indicates that they were in contact with certain associations for facilitating their registration and renewal in lieu of illegal gratification. Further investigation is in progress.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has zero tolerance towards corruption, and appropriate legal as well as departmental action is being taken in the matter. All FCRA-related services are delivered online through the FCRA portal, and no intermediary, agent or individual is authorised to facilitate any FCRA service.

*****

RK/RR/PR/PS

Ka WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, kaba la long ha Shanghai, China, naduh ka 23 haduh ka…
item.content:encoded:
Ka National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) ka la ïoh ïa ka jingjop kaba khraw ha ka WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026 kaba 48, ha kaba ki samla pule bad ki riew shemphang jong ka NIFT ki la mihkhmat ïa ka India ha ki bynta ba kongsan jong ka riam ka beit bad ki sap saindur thymmai, kynthup ïa ka Fashion Technology, Digital Interactive Media Design, Retail Sales and Visual Merchandising

Ka WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, kaba la long ha Shanghai, China, naduh ka 23 haduh ka 26 Nailur 2026, ka la wanrah lang ia palat 1,400 ngut ki samla kiba ïakhun na kylleng ki 68 tylli ki ri bad ki thaiñ ha ki 64 tylli ki sap treikam. Ka India ka la ïashim bynta ryngkat bad ka kynhun kaba heh tam jong ka kaba don 70 ngut ki nongïakhun ha kylleng ki 63 tylli ki sap, da kaba ïoh ïa ka kyrdan kaba 10 da ki 6 tylli ki takma rupa bad 20 tylli ki Medal for Excellence.

Ha kane ka jingïalang, ka NIFT ka la mihkhmat ha ki saw tylli ki bynta jong ka jingtbit—Ka Fashion Technology, Visual Merchandising, Retail Sales bad Digital Interactive Media Design. Ka jingïashim bynta ka pyni ïa ka bynta kaba nang kiew jong ka jingpule ia ka riam ka beit ha ki bynta jong ka jingsaindur, ka kam digital bad ki bynta ba iadei bad ki sap ha ka kam jingdie. Ka jingïashim bynta jong ka NIFT ka la noh synñiang shibun sha kane ka jingjop, ha kaba ki nongïashim bynta jong ka ki la ïoh 2 tylli ki takma rupa bad ka Medal for Excellence ha ki lai tylli ki thup jong ka jingtbit.

Ka Fashion Technology ka la long ka bynta kaba la slem bha jong ka jingïashim bynta jong ka NIFT ha WorldSkills, ha kaba ka Institute ka la ïashim bynta ha kane ka skill naduh u snem 2011. Ha Shanghai 2026, ka Vidhi Niravkumar Suthar, ka samla ba la pyndep ïa ka Fashion Design na ka NIFT Gandhinagar, ka la mihkhmat ia ka India ha ka Fashion Technology bad ka iohpdiang ia ka Medal for Excellence.

Ka Vidhi ka la iaid lyngba ia ka prokram ai jinghikai kaba saw bnai ha NIFT New Delhi hapoh ka jingialam jong ka Prof. (Dr.) Monika Gupta, ka riewshemphang na India, bad ka kynhun ai jinghikai jong ka NIFT.  Ka Prof. Gupta, kaba don ka jingshemphang ha ka Fashion Design bad WorldSkills, ka la ai ka jingpynkhreh kaba jur, ka jingai jinghikai bad ka jingialam lynti ha baroh ka por jong ka jingai jinghikai. Ka prokram ka la pynleit jingmut ha kaba pynkhlain ia ka jingtbit ha ka kam teknikal, ka jinglong kaba thikna, ka jingbud ryntih ia ki rukom trei jong ka pyrthei bad ka jinglah ban iakhun hapoh ki jinglong jingman jong ka jingiakop WorldSkills.

Ha ka Digital Interactive Media Design, u Kovid Ajay Gangrade na ka NIFT Mumbai u la ioh ia ka takma rupa, katba ka Saniya Joshi na ka NIFT Panchkula ka la ioh ia ka takma rupa ha ka Retail Sales. Ki jingjop jong ki kilong kiba kongsan bha namar ka Retail Sales bad ka Digital Interactive Media Design kidei napdeng ki jait jingtbit ba thymmai bad kiba dang mih kiba la ban jur ha ka WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, kaba pyni ïa ka jingkylla jong ka jinglong jong ki kam kaba iadei bad ka riam ka beit bad ki kam saindur bad ka jingïasoh kaba nangkiew jong ka teknoloji, ki rynsan digital bad ka jingshem jong ki nongthied bad kane ka bynta.

 

Ka jingïashim bynta jong ka NIFT ka la don ruh ha ka kam Visual Merchandising, ha kaba ka Anuja Ajay Vare na ka NIFT Bengaluru ka la mihkhmat ïa ka India ha kane ka bynta.

Na ka bynta ka NIFT, ka jingiaid lynti jong ka WorldSkills ka pyni kham palat ban ia ka jingiashim bynta ha ka jingiakop jong ka pyrthei. Ka ai ia ki samla pule ia ka jingshai shaphang ki jinglong jingman jong ka kam ha ka pyrthei, ki teknoloji kiba dang mih, ki rukom treikam jong ka pyrthei bad ki jingkhmih lynti ha kane ka kam. Ka jingshem ka plie lad ruh ia ka NIFT ban iai pynkhlain ia ki rukom ai jinghikai jong ka bad ban pyniasoh ia ki rukom treikam ba bha tam ha ka pyrthei ha ka rukom hikai bad ka jingkyntiew ia ki jingtbit.

Ka jingjop jong ki nongiashim bynta na ka NIFT ha ka WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 ka pyni ia ka jingshimkhia ba iai bteng jong kane ka jaka pule ban kyntiew ia ki riew shemphang kiba la pynkhreh ban iashim bynta ha ki kyrdan ba ha khlieh duh jong ka pyrthei, katba ka wanrah lang ia ka kam kaba iadei bad ka riam ka beit, ka teknoloji, ka jingstad, ka jingdie bad ki jingtbit ha ki kam digital.

Ka NIFT ka la kitbok kitrwiang ia ki samla pule, ki riewshemphang, ki nongai jinghikai, ki ophisar, ka tnat Kam Jain bad baroh kiba iadon bynta ha ka jingpynkhreh bad ka jingiashim bynta ha ka WorldSkills Shanghai 2026.

item.title: NIFT Students Make a Mark at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 with Two Silver Medals and a Medal for Excellence
item.description:
The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) has recorded a significant achievement at the 48 th WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026 , with NIFT students and experts representing India across key fashion and creative skill areas, including Fashion Technology, Digital Interactive Media Design, Retail Sales and Visual Merchandising.
WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, held in Shanghai, China, from 23 to 26 September 2026 , brought together more than 1,400 young competitors from…
item.content:encoded:
The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) has recorded a significant achievement at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026, with NIFT students and experts representing India across key fashion and creative skill areas, including Fashion Technology, Digital Interactive Media Design, Retail Sales and Visual Merchandising.

WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, held in Shanghai, China, from 23 to 26 September 2026, brought together more than 1,400 young competitors from around 68 countries and regions in 64 Skills. India participated with its largest-ever contingent of 70 competitors across 63 skills, securing 10th position with 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence.

In the event, NIFT was represented in four skill areas—Fashion Technology, Visual Merchandising, Retail Sales and Digital Interactive Media Design. The participation reflected the expanding role of fashion education across creative, digital and retail-oriented skill domains. NIFT’s participation contributed significantly to this achievement, with its participants securing 2 Silver Medals and a Medal for Excellence across three skill categories.

Fashion Technology has been a longstanding area of NIFT’s participation at WorldSkills, with the Institute participating in the skill since 2011. At Shanghai 2026, Ms. Vidhi Niravkumar Suthar, a Fashion Design graduate from NIFT Gandhinagar, represented India in Fashion Technology and received a Medal for Excellence.

Ms. Vidhi underwent an intensive four-month training programme at NIFT New Delhi under the guidance of Prof. (Dr.) Monika Gupta, Indian Expert, and the NIFT training team. Prof. Gupta, who has extensive experience in Fashion Design and WorldSkills, provided intensive preparation, mentoring and guidance throughout the training period. The programme focused on strengthening technical proficiency, precision, adherence to international standards and the ability to perform under WorldSkills competition conditions.

 

In Digital Interactive Media Design, Mr. Kovid Ajay Gangrade from NIFT Mumbai won a Silver Medal, while Ms. Saniya Joshi from NIFT Panchkula won a Silver Medal in Retail Sales. Their achievements are particularly significant as Retail Sales and Digital Interactive Media Design are among the new and emerging skill categories highlighted at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, reflecting the changing nature of the fashion and creative industries and the growing integration of technology, digital platforms and customer experience with the sector.

 

NIFT’s participation also extended to Visual Merchandising, with Ms. Anuja Ajay Vare from NIFT Bengaluru representing India in the skill.

For NIFT, the WorldSkills journey represents more than participation in an international competition. It provides students with exposure to global occupational standards, emerging technologies, international benchmarks and industry expectations. The experience also enables NIFT to continuously strengthen its training methodologies and integrate global best practices into its academic and skill-development ecosystem.

The success of NIFT participants at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 demonstrates the Institute’s continued commitment to developing professionals equipped to compete at the highest international levels, while bringing together fashion, technology, creativity, retail and digital skills.

NIFT congratulated its students, experts, trainers, officials, Ministry of Textiels and all those involved in their preparation and participation at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026.

*****

MAM/VN

item.title: NFC Achieves Record 81-Day Manufacturing Cycle for Steam Generator Tubes
item.description:
Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC), a Unit of the Department of Atomic Energy under the Government of India, is executing the manufacture of Steam Generator Tubes for the upcoming fleet-mode 700MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) being constructed by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) / National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC).
The Steam Generator (SG) Tubes are being supplied by NPCIL to its vendor as a free-issue material. Previously, these tubes were…
item.content:encoded:
Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC), a Unit of the Department of Atomic Energy under the Government of India, is executing the manufacture of Steam Generator Tubes for the upcoming fleet-mode 700MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) being constructed by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) / National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC).

 

The Steam Generator (SG) Tubes are being supplied by NPCIL to its vendor as a free-issue material. Previously, these tubes were imported, and NFC has emerged as a single supplier of these critical tubes for indigenous nuclear applications. Initially, the cycle time for the supply of these SG tubes was 180 days, while with the improvements in the number of productivity, recovery and quality, the cycle time for supply of each set has been reduced over a period of time.

NFC has manufactured the 12th set of SG tubes in a record span of 81 days and supplied to NPCIL on September 28, 2026. This reflects NFC’s enhanced manufacturing capabilities and commitment to meeting critical delivery schedules for the Nuclear Power Programme.

 

With this consignment, NFC has completed the supply of SG tubes for three of the ten reactors sanctioned under the fleet-mode programme. So far, NFC has supplied approximately 58,000 tubes for 23 Steam Generators for India’s civil Nuclear Power Programme, including reactors outside the fleet-mode programme.

 

 The consignment was flagged off by Shri Praveen Bhatt, Vice President & Head of Nuclear Business, Heavy Engineering Division, M/s. L&T, in the presence of Dr. Komal Kapoor, Chairman & Chief Executive, NFC.

Congratulating the NFC team on this achievement, Shri Praveen Bhatt appreciated the efforts made in ensuring the timely availability of these critical components for Steam Generator manufacturing and consistently delivering high-quality tubes meeting the stringent requirements of nuclear applications. Further, he expressed confidence in continued collaboration between L&T and NFC to address future requirements.

 

 Dr. Komal Kapoor stated that NFC continues to take up challenging assignments and successfully develops & manufactures several critical and strategic products of national importance, meeting stringent specifications and quality requirements in line with international standards. Dr. Kapoor emphasized NFC’s continued commitment to support India’s Nuclear Power Programme through indigenous manufacturing capabilities and technological excellence.

 

As envisaged by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, these efforts contribute to strengthening indigenous manufacturing capabilities and support the national goal of achieving 100GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047.

This year, the Government-wide Campaign will also place special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.
As part of Special Campaign 6.0, the Government of India has laid particular emphasis on field and outstation offices providing…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tourism gears up for the implementation of Special Campaign 6.0, being undertaken by the Government of India from October 2 to October 31, 2026, with a focus on Swachhata and reducing pendency across Government. This year, the Government-wide Campaign will also place special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

As part of Special Campaign 6.0, the Government of India has laid particular emphasis on field and outstation offices providing public services, in addition to Ministries/Departments, their attached and subordinate offices, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings. The Campaign is being conducted in two phases — a Preparatory Phase from September 15 to September 30, 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from October 2 to October 31, 2026.

In line with the Campaign framework, the Ministry of Tourism convened a preparatory meeting on September 16, 2026, with its Programme Divisions, Institutes and Domestic Offices to identify targets for implementation. The preparatory activities include mobilising offices, officers and ground functionaries; identifying pending references and cleanliness campaign sites; assessing redundant material for disposal; planning for efficient space management; disposal of scrap; record management; and identifying measures for effective collection and segregation of e-waste.

The Ministry had recorded significant outcomes during Special Campaign 5.0, with 92,749 sq. ft. of space freed and ₹12.69 lakh earned through scrap disposal. In addition, 4,700 physical files were weeded out and 1,100 electronic files were closed. A total of 413 Swachhata Campaign programmes were conducted across the country.

Building on the achievements of the previous campaign, the Ministry of Tourism remains committed to the successful implementation of Special Campaign 6.0 and to further strengthening cleanliness, efficient record management and reduction of pendency across its offices.

*****

item.title: IIT Gandhinagar, Suzuki R&D Center India to explore advanced materials, sensing and micro-mobility technologies
item.description:
Technologies ranging from Ground Penetrating Radar, nano-carbon materials and sensing to safety and connectivity will be among the areas explored under a new research and innovation collaboration between the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) and Suzuki R&D Center India Private Limited (SRDI), the research and development arm of Suzuki Motor Corporation in India.
Formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 28, 2026, the collaboration will explore…
item.content:encoded:
Technologies ranging from Ground Penetrating Radar, nano-carbon materials and sensing to safety and connectivity will be among the areas explored under a new research and innovation collaboration between the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) and Suzuki R&D Center India Private Limited (SRDI), the research and development arm of Suzuki Motor Corporation in India.

Formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 28, 2026, the collaboration will explore technologies relevant to Suzuki’s micro-mobility initiatives, while creating avenues for student projects, internships, recruitment, research and engagement with start-ups through IITGN’s Research Park.

“The future of mobility will be shaped not just by vehicles themselves, but by the technologies behind them, from advanced materials and sensing to safety and connectivity. For our students and researchers, the opportunity is to see how ideas move from the lab to address real-world challenges and applications. This collaboration with Suzuki R&D Center India can create those connections while opening new possibilities for our students, researchers and start-up ecosystem,” said Prof Amit Prashant, Dean, External Relations, IIT Gandhinagar.

Mr Taku Sumino, Executive General Manager, Technology Strategy, highlighted the importance of industry–academia collaboration, skill development, and the role of partnerships in addressing emerging challenges, including environmental sustainability. "Through this partnership, Suzuki will advance technological research and development, as well as talent exchange, with IIT Gandhinagar. My particular focus is on friction reduction technologies, which will enable higher fuel efficiency and greater electric efficiency, and bring us closer to Suzuki's vision of minimising energy consumption," he said.

For students, the collaboration could translate into opportunities beyond conventional classroom and laboratory exposure. The MoU provides for exploring internships, project-based engagements and recruitment of students, researchers and engineers by SRDI and the wider Suzuki group, alongside skill-development and capability-building initiatives.

The collaboration will also connect Suzuki with IITGN’s start-up,  incubation and Research Park ecosystem. Through this MoU, the two organisations will explore co-creation programmes, workshops and opportunities on emerging technologies.

The two organisations may also undertake joint research projects and sponsored research, exchange scientific and technical information, organise technical workshops and discussions, facilitate industrial visits, and engage faculty, researchers and experts. Individual projects will be taken up through separate agreements between the two organisations..

The three-year MoU provides a broad framework for collaboration rather than committing the institutions to any specific project. The agreement itself does not involve any financial commitment, with funding and other project-specific terms to be decided separately, where applicable

item.title: Literacy for All
item.description:

Literacy is a foundation of national development. India has made significant strides in improving its…
item.content:encoded:
India’s Literacy Leap: Charting the Path to Full Literacy

Literacy is a foundation of national development. Beyond being an indicator of educational progress, it enables individuals to access opportunities, participate in the economy, and engage meaningfully in society. UNESCO recognises literacy as a fundamental human right and a significant driver of achieving equality, justice, inclusion, and respect for the rule of law. India has made significant strides in improving its literacy rate over the past eight decades. In 1947, the country’s overall literacy rate stood at just 14%, while female literacy was remarkably low at 8%. India has undertaken several initiatives over the years to improve literacy and strengthen its education system. The government introduced the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to reform education at all levels and develop a skilled, adaptable, and future-ready workforce.

 

What is Literacy?

The Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, for the first time defines Literacy as “the ability to read, write, and compute with comprehension, i.e., to identify, understand, interpret and create, along with critical life skills such as digital literacy, financial literacy, etc.” It considers 95% literacy in a State/Union Territory as equivalent to full literacy.

 

In a global context, UNESCO defines Literacy as the ability to read, write, and use numbers, as well as to use digital materials to solve problems in an increasingly technological and information-rich environment-a foundational skill that is central to individuals’ engagement in work, learning, and life. It is an essential component of the right to education and a prerequisite for enjoying other human rights.

 

Measuring Progress in Literacy and Education

India’s literacy rate has made remarkable progress since 1951, increasing from 18.32% in 1951 to 74.04% in 2011. Male literacy rose from 27.15% to 82.14%, while female literacy increased significantly from 8.86% to 65.46%.

The urban literacy rate increased from 34.59% in 1951 to 84.1% in 2011, while the rural literacy rate rose from 12.10% to 67.8%. Between 2001 and 2011, rural female literacy grew by 26%, compared with 10% for rural males, reflecting significant gains in female literacy.

According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025, the literacy rate in urban areas reached 89% for those aged 7 years and above, and 88% for those aged 5 years and above. Among urban residents aged 7 years and above, literacy reached 93.1% for males and 84.8% for females. In rural areas, the literacy rate among those aged 7 years and above was 77.4%, and 76.4% for those aged 5 years and above. Among the rural population aged 7 years and above, the literacy rate was 84.8% for males and 70.3% for females. The overall Literacy rate of the country is 81.1 % as per this survey.

To complement literacy gains, the government has also taken measures to improve school enrolment, retention, and progression. Notable improvements in Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER), transition, and retention rates have been noted since 2014-15. According to the UDISE+ Report (2025-26):

  • School Enrolment: Over 24.72 crore students were enrolled in schools.
  • Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER): Stood at 42.8% at the Foundational stage, 91.7% at the Preparatory stage, 89.6% at the Middle stage, and 71.7% at the Secondary stage.
  • Dropout rates were 1.8% at the Preparatory stage, 3.6% at the Middle stage, and 7.0% at the Secondary stage.
  • Retention rates stood at 98.5% for Foundational, 91.1% for Preparatory, 83.7% for Middle, and 51.9% for Secondary stages.
  • Transition rates improved, with 99.2% progressing from the Foundational to the Preparatory stage, 93.8% from Preparatory to the Middle stage, and 88.3% from Middle to the Secondary stage.

The transition rate refers to the percentage of students who successfully move from one level of education to the next.

Participation in higher education has expanded significantly over the past decade:

  • Enrolment increased from 3.42 crore in 2014-15 to 4.50 crore in 2023-24.
  • GER increased from 23.7% to 30% over the same period.
  • Higher education out-turn increased from 88.28 lakh in 2014-15 to over 1.09 crore in 2023-24.

Higher education out-turn refers to the total number of students who pass out of higher education institutions in a given academic year.

The increase in women’s participation, alongside the inclusion of SC, ST, and other disadvantaged groups, reflects enhanced access and equity. It reflects continued improvement in access to higher education, supporting NEP 2020’s target of attaining a 50% higher education GER by 2035.

Key Government Initiatives for Advancing Literacy

India’s approach to literacy has evolved from basic reading and numeracy to broader competencies needed to participate in a rapidly changing economy and society. In line with NEP 2020, the Government has introduced initiatives such as ULLAS and NIPUN Bharat to expand access, strengthen learning outcomes, promote inclusion, and support lifelong learning.

ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) 

ULLAS - Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram: ULLAS, or the New India Literacy Programme (NILP), is a centrally sponsored initiative. It aligns with NEP 2020. It focuses on empowering adults aged 15 years and above who missed formal schooling. The programme provides functional literacy, numeracy, critical life skills, and lifelong learning opportunities. This promotes the social integration of the target group and encourages their contribution to national development.

ULLAS’s vision is ‘Jan Jan Saakshar’, empowering every individual through literacy. It follows the spirit of ‘Kartavya Bodh’ (Duty). It promotes volunteerism and Janbhagidari, or community participation, to achieve universal literacy.

ULLAS follows a hybrid learning approach. The ULLAS App, available on iOS and Android platforms, has teaching-learning material in 27 languages. Under the scheme, learners and volunteers are identified by surveyors at the district- or block-level. They may include school teachers, civil society workers, ASHA workers, and Anganwadi workers. Surveyors conduct door-to-door surveys to identify non-literate individuals and potential volunteer teachers. In the next stage, learners are connected with a Voluntary Teacher to support and guide the students in registering on the ULLAS App.  Training, orientations, and workshops are conducted through face-to-face and online modes. Learners access learning materials and develop foundational literacy and numeracy skills. They then appear for the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test (FLNAT), followed by evaluation and certification.

ULLAS’s Progress and Impact: The scheme aims to cover 5 crore learners during 2022-27 with a financial outlay of ₹1,037.90 crore. ULLAS has about 4.03 crore registered learners and over 52.20 lakh volunteers. To date, more than 3.3 crore learners have participated in the FLNAT.

Ten (10) States/UTs have declared themselves fully literate between 2024 and 2026. These include Ladakh, Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Sikkim, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir. ULLAS is expanding adult literacy through community participation, reaching millions of learners while advancing India’s goal of universal literacy.

NIPUN Bharat: (National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy)

Launched in July 2021, under the aegis of Samagra Shiksha, the initiative focuses on strengthening early learning and supporting continued academic development. It seeks to achieve universal foundational literacy and numeracy by 2026-27, ensuring that every child acquires foundational skills by Grade 2. The mission focuses on the Foundational Stage of ages 3 to 8 years.

In addition, the Government has undertaken several initiatives to increase enrolment and improve retention in schools. Key initiatives include Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI (Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India), PM e-VIDYA, and PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman).

  • Samagra Shiksha focuses on enhancing school effectiveness and ensuring equal opportunities for schooling to improve learning outcomes. The scheme is aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG-4) on education. It was introduced by subsuming the three erstwhile schemes-Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education (TE). The scheme promotes equitable, inclusive, and quality education, with a focus on foundational learning, teacher development, and vocational integration.
  • Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) seeks to strengthen more than 14,500 exemplar schools across the country. The scheme focuses on the holistic and well-rounded development of students by fostering an equitable, inclusive, and joyful learning environment that addresses diverse backgrounds, multilingual needs, and varied academic abilities.
  • PM e-VIDYA is a comprehensive initiative that brings together various efforts related to digital, online, and on-air education to provide multi-mode access to learning. The initiative is expected to benefit nearly 25 crore school-going children across the country.
  • PM POSHAN is a centrally sponsored scheme that provides one hot cooked meal to 11.20 crore students enrolled in Bal Vatikas and Classes I to VIII across 10.36 lakh government and government-aided schools on all school days. The scheme aims to provide nutritional support and encourage greater school participation among students.

Together, these initiatives create an enabling environment that enhances enrolment, retention, and learning outcomes. They also address literacy across age groups and learning stages, strengthening foundational education, adult literacy, and lifelong learning.

Literacy for Viksit Bharat and Sustainable Development

The SDGs provide a comprehensive framework for promoting a more equitable, inclusive, and sustainable future for all. Literacy and education are central to SDG 4, which seeks to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for all. Literacy is positively associated with GDP and per capita income and contributes to economic growth and national development. For India, achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat requires a literate, educated, and skilled population.

Beyond education, literacy contributes to women’s empowerment, equality, inclusion, and the realisation of human rights, while enhancing employability, productivity, innovation, and economic participation. Education and skills can also enable participation in green jobs, support the circular economy, and contribute to environmental sustainability. Thus, progress in literacy can create multiplier effects across the SDGs, supporting inclusive, sustainable, and broad-based development.

Looking Ahead: Advancing Literacy for All

India’s literacy journey since Independence reflects a wider transformation in nation-building and human development. Literacy today extends beyond reading and writing. It enables learning, livelihoods, empowerment, and meaningful participation in society. Initiatives such as NEP 2020, ULLAS, and NIPUN Bharat are broadening this vision. They connect foundational learning with adult education, lifelong learning, and future-ready skills. Aligned with SDG 4, these efforts reinforce India’s commitment to inclusive and equitable development.

As India moves towards Viksit Bharat, sustained implementation remains essential. Greater attention to regional and gender disparities will help ensure that the benefits of literacy reach every section of society. A literate, skilled, and empowered population can become a strong foundation for a more inclusive, productive, and sustainable Viksit Bharat.

item.title: Union Environment Minister hands over India’s first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme to Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation and a Bamboo Farmer from Odisha
item.description: Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today handed over the first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), in New Delhi. The event was organised by the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal, as the scheme's operating agency. Senior officers of the MoEFCC along with senior officers of various States Forest Departments, representatives of certification bodies and industry attended the event. …
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today handed over the first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), in New Delhi. The event was organised by the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal, as the scheme's operating agency. Senior officers of the MoEFCC along with senior officers of various States Forest Departments, representatives of certification bodies and industry  attended the event.

PRAMAN certificates were presented to the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC) for its plantations over an area of 33,000 hectares, and to Shri Govind Mohapatra, a farmer associated with Odisha Bamboo Development Agency (OBDA). The plantations underwent a rigorous field and management audit before certification. The certificates mark the culmination of the processes established since launch of IFWCS by the Ministry in December 2023, signifying its transition from a policy framework to field-level implementation across both forest plantations and tree-based farming.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav described PRAMAAN as a vital instrument for Indian producers, exporters and forest-based enterprises to meet emerging global regulatory requirements, including due-diligence and responsible deforestation-free timber sourcing norms adopted by major international markets. As global trade increasingly links market access to verifiable sustainability credentials, he said, PRAMAAN positions India not merely to comply, but to lead in the sustainable forest management and tree outside forest management systems, under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Vocal for Local and Act Global’. He expressed happiness that several State Forest Departments, Forest Development Corporations, farmers and industries have applied for Forest Management, Tree Outside forest Management and Chain of Custody certification and the same are in various stages of process.

The Minister highlighted that PRAMAAN’s accreditation architecture, benchmarked against international certification frameworks, ensures that certification issued under the scheme carries recognition from both domestic and global buyers and regulators. He noted that the PRAMAAN’s forest management certification is anchored in the principles of the National Working Plan Code (NWPC) 2023 ensuring that certification is built on a foundation of forest management audited by third-party rather than voluntary self-declaration alone. 

Emphasising that PRAMAAN is as much a livelihood mission as a trade instrument, the Minister said that by bringing rural and tribal communities, small holder farmers, and forest-dependent communities into a structured and verifiable certification system, the certification scheme opens new income pathways to compliant and premium markets without adding to the compliance burden on producers. He added that women Self Help Groups and marginal landholders engaged in NTFP collection and processing, farm and agroforestry and any tree-based agriculture system stand to benefit.

Placing the initiative with a wider national vision, Shri Yadav stated that PRAMAAN reflects India’s broader journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. It signifies a developed India that combines economic growth with ecological stewardship and that is recognized globally not just as a producer of sustainable goods but a leader in sustainable governance. The Minister complimented IIFM and the ministry, and concluded by calling upon the certification bodies, state forest departments, tree growers, farmer producer organisations, farmer producer companies, Industries, institutions, to strengthen their participation in PRAMAAN so that India’s forests, and the communities who depend on them are positioned at the centre of the next generation of global sustainable trade.

About PRAMAAN

PRAMAAN (Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of sustainable Management practices for Agroforestry And Natural forestry resources) is a nationally accepted, credible, and transparent framework for certification of forests, wood and non-timber forest products with the mission to promote linkages to domestic and international markets for certified forests and agroforestry products. The IFWCS-PRAMAAN certificate enhances the social, and ecological values of India’s forests, agroforestry systems and the Indian wood-based industries. 

The Forest Management certification is assessed against the Indian Forest Management Standard, which are part of the National Working Plan Code 2023.  The core principle of certificate rests on independent audit by certification bodies accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) under the Quality Council of India, rather than on self-declaration alone. PRAMAAN’s accreditation architecture is benchmarked against international frameworks, ensuring recognition among domestic and global buyers and regulators.

item.description:
