item.description:
Kochi, 28 September 2026: The CSEZ Facilitation Centre, “Suvidha”, established at the CSEZ Administrative Building, Kakkanad, was inaugurated today by Smt. Hemalatha IAS, Development Commissioner, Cochin Special Economic Zone (CSEZ).
The Facilitation Centre has been established as a single-window facilitation platform to provide guidance and support to investors, SEZ units and Export Oriented Units (EOUs) in Karnataka and Keralam, and to facilitate their…
item.content:encoded:
Kochi, 28 September 2026: The CSEZ Facilitation Centre, “Suvidha”, established at the CSEZ Administrative Building, Kakkanad, was inaugurated today by Smt. Hemalatha IAS, Development Commissioner, Cochin Special Economic Zone (CSEZ).

 

 

The Facilitation Centre has been established as a single-window facilitation platform to provide guidance and support to investors, SEZ units and Export Oriented Units (EOUs) in Karnataka and Keralam, and to facilitate their interaction with the Office of the Development Commissioner, CSEZ.

 

The Centre is intended to strengthen investor facilitation by providing assistance relating to approvals, clearances, compliance requirements, procedural guidance and liaison with concerned stakeholders. It will also serve as a convenient point of contact for entrepreneurs and existing units seeking assistance in connection with their operations under the SEZ and EOU schemes.

 

The inauguration was attended by Shri K. K. Pillai, President, CEPZ Industries Association and Regional Chairman, EPCES; Shri Anilkumar P. C., Secretary, CEPZ Industries Association; and Smt. Supriya P, Regional Director, EPCES, along with officials of CSEZ.

 

The establishment of the Centre is part of the initiatives of CSEZ towards strengthening ease of doing business, improving accessibility to facilitation services and providing responsive support to the business community.

 

The Facilitation Centre will work towards creating a more accessible and coordinated interface between investors, SEZ/EOU units and the concerned authorities, thereby supporting investment, exports and employment generation in the jurisdiction of CSEZ. 

 

***

item.title: NIT Raipur Launches Hindi Pakhwada with Annual Fest ‘Aavahan 2026’
item.description:
Rajbhasha Committee of the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Raipur on Monday inaugurated its annual Hindi festival, ‘Aavahan 2026’, marking the beginning of a series of literary, cultural, creative and outdoor activities aimed at promoting the use and appreciation of Hindi among students.
The inaugural ceremony was attended by Dr. Narendra D. Londhe, Registrar, NIT Raipur; Dr. Manoj Chopkar, Dean (Student Welfare); and Dr. Dharm Pal, Associate Professor, Department of…
item.content:encoded:
Rajbhasha Committee of the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Raipur on Monday inaugurated its annual Hindi festival, ‘Aavahan 2026’, marking the beginning of a series of literary, cultural, creative and outdoor activities aimed at promoting the use and appreciation of Hindi among students.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by Dr. Narendra D. Londhe, Registrar, NIT Raipur; Dr. Manoj Chopkar, Dean (Student Welfare); and Dr. Dharm Pal, Associate Professor, Department of Chemical Engineering. The programme was conducted under the guidance of the faculty in-charges of the Rajbhasha Committee Dr. Sanjay Kumar, Dr. Sharada Nandan Raw and Dr. Vikas Kumar Vidyarthi.

The programme began with Saraswati Vandana, followed by the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by the dignitaries. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Sharada Nandan Raw emphasised the relevance of Hindi in various spheres of everyday life and said that the language serves not only as a medium of communication but also as an important symbol of national unity.

Dr. Narendra D. Londhe highlighted the significance of Hindi Pakhwada and said that the observance reflects the rich cultural heritage and traditions of India. He extended his best wishes for the successful conduct of ‘Aavahan 2026’. Dr. Manoj Chopkar underlined the importance of regional and national languages in the holistic academic and personal development of students.

The festival will feature a range of activities, including Varga Paheli (Crossword), Prashnotari (Quiz), Kavita Vachan (Poetry Recitation), Khazane Ki Khoj (Treasure Hunt) and Andhamod. The inaugural day also featured a student-led street play, ‘Samaj Ka Darpan’, along with the creative Chitra Katha Lekhan (Storytelling through Pictures) competition.

The event provided students with a platform to demonstrate their creativity, knowledge, teamwork and communication skills. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Dr. Vikas Kumar Vidyarthi.


******

RDJ/BKT

item.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit the United States to Participate in G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting
item.description:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will visit the United States of America from 29 September to 5 October 2026. Shri Goyal will participate in the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting to be held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 30 September and 1 October 2026, at the invitation of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR).
The Meeting will bring together Trade Ministers of G20 members. India will engage constructively with all G20 members and work towards a rules-based, open,…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will visit the United States of America from 29 September to 5 October 2026. Shri Goyal will participate in the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting to be held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 30 September and 1 October 2026, at the invitation of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR).

The Meeting will bring together Trade Ministers of G20 members. India will engage constructively with all G20 members and work towards a rules-based, open, inclusive, transparent, equitable and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organization at its core, while ensuring adequate policy space for developing countries. On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal will hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts. The engagements will focus on expanding opportunities for farmers, fishermen, women entrepreneurs, startups, MSMEs and other enterprises.

Shri Piyush Goyal will also engage bilaterally with his counterpart from the United States as part of ongoing efforts to advance a balanced and mutually beneficial India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and finalise an interim deal in line with the Joint Statement of 7 February 2026.

In Milwaukee and Chicago, Shri Goyal will meet chief executives of leading American companies in manufacturing, consumer goods, agri-business, retail and technology, and participate in roundtables with businesses, startups and innovative companies. He will highlight the opportunities India offers as a manufacturing and investment destination and invite American companies to deepen their partnerships with Indian enterprises.

In Chicago, Shri Goyal will pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi on Gandhi Jayanti and Swami Vivekananda. He will also interact with professional associations representing the Indian community.

The visit is expected to further strengthen the trade and investment partnership between India and the United States and deepen India’s engagement with its G20 partners.

 

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Abhijith Narayanan/ Ishita Biswas

item.title: Hindi Journalism Must Act as an Effective Bridge in the Journey of Schemes 'From File to Field'
item.description: After the announcement of any government scheme, its real impact begins when information about it reaches the intended beneficiary. Translating the complex language of a scheme into simple language easily understood by the common man, and delivering it in the correct context, is the vital link that completes the journey of government schemes "from file to field." Hindi journalism can play the role of an effective bridge in this process. These views were expressed by Ms. Sudha Shrimali, Business…
item.content:encoded:
After the announcement of any government scheme, its real impact begins when information about it reaches the intended beneficiary. Translating the complex language of a scheme into simple language easily understood by the common man, and delivering it in the correct context, is the vital link that completes the journey of government schemes "from file to field." Hindi journalism can play the role of an effective bridge in this process. These views were expressed by Ms. Sudha Shrimali, Business Editor of Navbharat Times, during a special lecture organized on the occasion of Hindi Month.

At the beginning of the program, Additional Director General Shri Siddharth Bodke welcomed Ms. Sudha Shrimali and felicitated her for the special lecture.

Speaking on the topic "Role of Hindi Journalism in Taking Government Schemes to the Masses – In the Context of Viksit Bharat 2047", Ms. Shrimali stated that presenting government information in Hindi is not merely a task of translating words. It is far more important to understand the objective, spirit, and context behind the information and present it according to the needs of the public. When accurate information reaches people in a simple and useful format, it ceases to be mere information and becomes a driver of public participation.

Ms. Shrimali noted that whenever a scheme is announced, basic questions arise in the mind of an ordinary citizen—what is the scheme, who will benefit from it, what are the eligibility criteria, and how can one avail of the benefits? The responsibility of journalism is to provide direct and clear answers to these questions. Citing examples like the Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme, she stated that the headline and presentation of news should be such that a reader can understand at a single glance why the scheme is relevant to them and how they can benefit from it.

She added that the world of information is evolving rapidly today. Alongside newspapers, audio programming, social media, and other digital platforms have developed the capacity to disseminate information on government policies and schemes far more widely than before. In such times, the foremost responsibility of the media is to maintain credibility. Simple, fact-based information can bridge the communication gap while minimizing the spread of rumors and misleading information.

She also emphasized that the flow of information should not be a one-way channel from the government to the media and then to the public. The role of the Press Information Bureau is equally crucial in conveying media feedback back to the government. Through queries, reactions, and ground-level insights gathered from journalists and media organizations, information gaps can be identified and addressed.

Regarding the role of journalism in the era of Artificial Intelligence, she remarked that instead of viewing AI strictly as a challenge, it should be embraced as an auxiliary tool that makes a journalist's work more effective. Technology can assist in information analysis, presentation, and wide distribution, but the ultimate responsibility for ensuring the truth and credibility of information will always rest on journalism.

Ms. Shrimali stated that while information on government schemes should be engaging and useful, its aim should not be to glorify schemes, but to convey their core intent and benefits to the public in simple language. The widespread understanding of Hindi and the expanding reach of digital media render this approach even more effective. From this perspective, Hindi Journalism can play a pivotal role in linking the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 with a broad campaign of public participation.

Director General (West Zone), Press Information Bureau, Smt. Smita Vats Sharma, in her address, stated, "In today's digital era, there is an overload of information. Therefore, our continuous effort is to curate data and information for journalists and present it in an extremely simplified manner. For the convenience of journalists, we attach PIB backgrounders alongside press releases and write detailed captions for photographs so that journalists working in far-flung areas can easily grasp the background. Additionally, to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the topic, social media links and live-streaming links are also shared with the release."

This special lecture was organized by the Press Information Bureau, Mumbai, on the occasion of Hindi Month under the guidance of Director General Smt. Smita Vats Sharma. On this occasion, officers and staff from the Press Information Bureau and the Central Bureau of Communication across the zone joined the lecture online. At the conclusion of the event, Director, PIB Bhopal, Shri Manish Gautam, expressed his gratitude to Ms. Sudha Shrimali.
 

*******


RDJ/KV/PJ

item.content:encoded:
Tamil Nadu is represented by 31 mementos in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, showcasing the state’s spiritual traditions, art, craftsmanship, historical legacy and sporting achievements.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online till October 2, 2026. For details and participation, visit https://pmmementos.gov.in

Notable mementos from Tamil Nadu include:

Among the notable mementos is an Auspicious Framed Footprint from Kanyakumari, presented by the Vivekananda Rock Memorial. The piece is associated with Sri Padhaparai, which is traditionally believed to bear the footprints of Goddess Kumari

A memento of Sant Shri Ramanujacharya Ji features an intricately detailed depiction of the philosopher and theologian in a teaching pose, reflecting his spiritual and intellectual legacy.

The collection also includes a Thiruvalluvar Chariot, a handcrafted model inspired by the traditional temple chariots of Tamil Nadu.

 

The sporting memorabilia includes a badminton racket associated with para-badminton player Nithya Sre Sivan, who won a medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, and a signed racket of Thulasimathi Murugesan, who won silver in badminton singles at the Paralympics.

 

The collection also features shoes associated with Mariyappan Thangavelu, a three-time Paralympic medallist in high jump.

 

Tamil Nadu’s devotional and artistic traditions are represented by a metallic Nataraja statue, depicting Lord Shiva in his cosmic dance.

 

A Tanjore-style Veena artwork, embellished with gold foil and Kundan stones, is another notable piece.

Other prominent entries include a traditional Tanjore painting of Lord Murugan, a gold-foil depiction of Lord Murugan, a framed devotional work featuring Sri Sowmya Narayana Perumal, and a brass presentation memento depicting the Madurai Meenakshi Amman Temple. Traditional textiles are also represented by South Indian angavastras featuring zari and woven borders.

The 31 mementos together offer a glimpse into Tamil Nadu’s diverse cultural landscape, bringing its spiritual traditions, classical art, craftsmanship, historical figures, textiles and sporting achievements to the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026.

item.title: FSSAI West Region to Launch ‘Know Your Food Label’ Initiative across Schools in Mumbai
item.description:
Mumbai, 28 September 2026
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), West Region, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, is set to launch the ‘Know Your Food Label’ awareness initiative across schools in Mumbai to promote food-label literacy among school-going children and enable them to make informed food choices.
The initiative will sensitise students to important information provided on packaged food labels, including…
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai, 28 September 2026

 

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), West Region, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, is set to launch the ‘Know Your Food Label’ awareness initiative across schools in Mumbai to promote food-label literacy among school-going children and enable them to make informed food choices.

The initiative will sensitise students to important information provided on packaged food labels, including ingredients, nutritional information, allergens, date marking, FSSAI licence details, food preference symbols and other mandatory declarations. Through age-appropriate and interactive learning activities, students will be encouraged to develop the habit of reading, understanding and evaluating food labels before making food choices.

The Mumbai launch will mark the first phase of the initiative. The programme will subsequently be expanded in a phased manner to schools in other areas under the jurisdiction of FSSAI West Region, with the objective of creating a wider network of food-label literate young consumers.

The initiative assumes significance in the context of the growing emphasis on nutritional awareness and literacy among children. The importance of nutritional literacy among the young population has also been highlighted by the Supreme Court in its recent proceedings concerning front-of-package labelling.

Recognising children as important influencers within their families and communities, the initiative seeks to create a multiplier effect by enabling students to take the message of informed food choices from schools to their homes and communities.

Through the ‘Know Your Food Label’ initiative, FSSAI West Region aims to equip the next generation with practical knowledge about packaged food labels and encourage a culture of safe, healthy and informed food choices.

 

* * *

item.description:
The second India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group (JWG) meeting was held in New Delhi on September 28, 2026.The two countries held discussions on a wide range of areas of mutual interest, including military training and capacity building, service-to-service engagements, maritime security, cyber training, defence industry collaboration and enhanced institutional cooperation between the Armed Forces of India and Fiji.
India reiterated the importance accorded to Fiji and the Pacific…
item.content:encoded:
The second India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group (JWG) meeting was held in New Delhi on September 28, 2026.The two countries held discussions on a wide range of areas of mutual interest, including military training and capacity building, service-to-service engagements, maritime security, cyber training, defence industry collaboration and enhanced institutional cooperation between the Armed Forces of India and Fiji.

India reiterated the importance accorded to Fiji and the Pacific Island Countries in its vision of a free, open, inclusive and secure Indo-Pacific. Both sides expressed satisfaction at the growing bilateral defence engagements and reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cooperation in mutually beneficial areas. 

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Amitabh Prasad, Joint Secretary (International Cooperation), Ministry of Defence and Mr. Mason Smith, Permanent Secretary for Defence & Veterans Affairs, Fiji. Mr. Smith also met Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh on the sidelines of the 2nd India–Fiji Bilateral Joint Working Group Meeting. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral defence and maritime cooperation, including opportunities for greater defence industry collaboration.

As part of efforts to expand specialised military training cooperation, the Fijian delegation is scheduled to visit Kochi on 29–30 September 2026. The delegation will inspect facilities at the Southern Naval Command to formalise advanced naval training cooperation and professional aviation training modules, enhancing technical proficiency and operational synergy between the two maritime forces.

Prior to the commencement of the official bilateral talks, Mr. Smith paid solemn tribute to India's fallen soldiers at the National War Memorial, New Delhi. The Fijian delegation also visited the DPSU Bhavan at the World Trade Centre, New Delhi, where it was briefed on India's indigenous defence manufacturing capabilities. The visit highlighted advancements under the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' initiative, with a focus on exhibition displays and advanced Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality (AR/VR) simulation facilities that replicate real-world battlefield conditions.

India and Fiji share close and friendly relations, underpinned by historical, cultural and people-to-people ties. The meeting provided an opportunity to consolidate the existing defence partnership and identify new avenues for cooperation. Both sides agreed to maintain regular engagements and work towards further deepening bilateral defence cooperation.

SR/Ruchi

The initiative is aimed at strengthening safety standards, practices, accident prevention and safety awareness across the steel industry.
The Council will be headed by the Secretary, Ministry of Steel , as Chairman and will include senior officials of the Ministry, Chief…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Steel, Government of India, has decided to set up a Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) as an apex-level industry safety body under the administrative control of the Ministry of Steel. The initiative is aimed at strengthening safety standards, practices, accident prevention and safety awareness across the steel industry.

The Council will be headed by the Secretary, Ministry of Steel, as Chairman and will include senior officials of the Ministry, Chief Executives of integrated steel producers, and representatives of key technical and statutory organisations including the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS), Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and recognised steel technology institutions.

The SISC will assess the safety situation in the steel industry, facilitate studies and improvements in safety practices, approve industry safety standards and recommended practices, and review serious accidents, accidents and near-miss incidents. It will also provide directions for strengthening safety awareness, training and preventive measures.

To provide technical and professional support to the Council, a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (SISD) will be established. The Directorate will have expertise in areas including process safety, blast furnaces, steel melting, rolling mills, coke ovens, refractory systems, electrical and mechanical safety, occupational health, fire engineering and disaster management.

The SISD will oversee implementation of the Council's decisions, undertake periodic safety audits and reviews, maintain and disseminate accident and near-miss information, conduct investigations into serious safety incidents, review emergency preparedness and safety training programmes, and develop and issue Steel Industry Safety Standards, Recommended Practices and Guidelines suited to Indian conditions.

The establishment of SISC and SISD represents an important institutional step towards promoting a stronger safety culture, improving prevention of industrial accidents and advancing consistent safety practices across India's steel industry.

***

AG

item.title: IMTECH Celebrates 85th CSIR Foundation Day
item.description: The 85 th Foundation Day of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) was celebrated with great enthusiasm today at the CSIR–Institute of Microbial Technology (IMTECH), Chandigarh, commemorating over eight decades of excellence in scientific research, innovation and nation-building. Prof. Gobardhan Das, Member, NITI Aayog and alumni of CSIR-IMTECH graced the occasion as the Chief Guest, while Prof Javed Iqbal, Former Director, CSIR-NIIST and Chairman, Incor Renovis Laboratories,…
item.content:encoded:
The 85th Foundation Day of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) was celebrated with great enthusiasm today at the CSIR–Institute of Microbial Technology (IMTECH), Chandigarh, commemorating over eight decades of excellence in scientific research, innovation and nation-building. Prof. Gobardhan Das, Member, NITI Aayog and alumni of CSIR-IMTECH graced the occasion as the Chief Guest, while Prof Javed Iqbal, Former Director, CSIR-NIIST and Chairman, Incor Renovis Laboratories, was the Guest of Honour. Among other dignitaries, Dr. Srinivas Lanka, Mentor, Elix Global & Member, Research Council, CSIR-IMTECH and Dr. Moez Sanaa, CEO & Founder of International Food Risk Analysis Consortium (IFoRAC) were also present on this occasion.

This Foundation Day address was delivered by Prof. Gobardhan Das on “The Journey of Indian Civilization” and expressed confidence in India’s emergence as a leading global power by 2047 and encouraged young researchers to contribute actively to the nation’s progress. Prof. Das described CSIR-IMTECH as a Centre for Global Talent that nurtures researchers capable of contributing to science and society at the global level. He encouraged young scholars to pursue a clear vision, believe in their abilities and face challenges with determination. He highlighted India’s growing economic stature and its role as a global pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturing hub, citing vaccine production and international supply during COVID-19 as examples of its capabilities. The lecture captivated the auditorium with its brilliant and inspiring delivery, leaving the entire audience deeply engaged from start to end.

Prof. Javed Iqbal, delivered a Technical Foundation Day Lecture on Furan Macrocycles, stem-cell-to-neuron conversion and transcriptomic validation. His talk demonstrated a simple, gene-free chemical approach that can turn stem cells into functional brain cells using specially designed ring-shaped molecules. Validated through genetic sequencing, this breakthrough opens new possibilities for studying and treating complex brain disorders such as Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease.

On this momentous occasion, “SUVIDHA” web portal was launched which is an indigenous CSIR-IMTECH’s in-house digital job-card platform for all service related requests. CSIR-IMTECH Laboratory Safety Manual was also released by the dignitaries. The purpose of the manual is to create and spread awareness regarding safety and emergency procedures, prevent injury, occupational illness, environmental release, damage to equipment and interruption of operations at CSIR-IMTECH. As part of the celebrations, CSIR-IMTECH also felicitated its retirees and employees who have completed 25 years of their service. The institute also recognized efforts wards of CSIR-IMTECH staff for their outstanding performances in various academic, essay, quiz, drawing and sporting events held at the state and national level. As part of Foundation Day, institute's alumni also joined the celebrations along with Open Day for the general public and students to get a glimpse of the facilities, infrastructure and showcase scientific prowess of CSIR-IMTECH. More than 750 school and college students across different states got a chance to interact with scientists and researcher; fostering a scientific temperament among budding students.

Dr. Alka Rao, Director, CSIR-IMTECH while welcoming the guests and faculty to CSIR's Foundation Day apprised the audience with the contributions and commitments of CSIR for the vision of making India a developed nation in 2047. Speaking at the occasion she said, “To every researcher, student, industry partner, and regulator looking for an honest, capable scientific partner—our doors are open.” Dr. Rao reaffirmed CSIR-IMTECH’s commitment to serving as a dedicated implementation partner in advancing the vision of NITI Aayog and the Government of India, translating scientific knowledge into meaningful benefits for society”.

CSIR-IMTECH is a national center for excellence in microbial sciences and was established in 1984 under the aegis of CSIR. IMTECH’s vision and mission are to create translational ecosystem strengthened by fundamental discoveries and to address unmet healthcare and industrial needs with state-of-the-art processes and platforms.

item.content:encoded:
A four-day training program on "Basic Project Management" was organized at BMDC, Sector-7, by the Human Resource Learning & Development (HR-L&D) Department of Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP) in collaboration with SAIL-MTI, Ranchi. The primary objective of the program was to provide participants with a foundational understanding of project management processes, alongside practical insights into project planning, execution, resource management, and review mechanisms to ensure more effective implementation of plant projects.

Attending the inaugural session as the Chief Guest, Executive Director (Projects), BSP, Shri Prabir Kumar Sarkar emphasized the necessity of systematic project management processes to achieve superior project outcomes. He laid special emphasis on the timely execution of projects and the efficient utilization of available resources.

On this occasion, General Manager In-Charge and Head of Department (HR-L&D), Shri S. K. Srivastava highlighted the importance of continuous capacity building in strengthening organizational effectiveness. Meanwhile, former Executive Director (Projects), ISP & DSP, Shri Amit Ranjan Dasgupta shared his extensive experience in executing large-scale projects and stressed the value of disciplined project planning and structured review mechanisms.

A total of 31 participants from various departments of BSP underwent training during the program. Technical sessions were conducted by expert faculty, including former Executive Director (Projects), ISP & DSP, Shri Amit Ranjan Dasgupta; General Manager (Projects), BSL, Shri Sudhir Kumar; Chief General Manager (Projects), BSP, Shri Anurag Upadhyay; and Assistant Manager (Safety), Propane Plant, BSP, Shri A. Nagendra.

The program was coordinated by General Manager (HR-L&D), BMDC, Shri Saurabh Varshney and Manager, SAIL-MTI, Ranchi, Shri Nageshwar Rao. The inaugural session was conducted by Shri Nageshwar Rao, while the vote of thanks was delivered by Shri Saurabh Varshney. The practical insights and knowledge gained during the training will assist officials in the effective, qualitative, and systematic execution of plant projects.

item.description:

Agriculture programme at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research–National Institute of Biotic Stress Management (ICAR-NIBSM), Raipur, showcased innovative models for converting waste into useful products and resources as part of the ongoing “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag – Swachh Bharat – Viksit Bharat” campaign here today.
The student-centric “Waste to Wealth” model demonstration highlighted the potential of waste segregation, recycling,…
item.content:encoded:
Students of the Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) Agriculture programme at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research–National Institute of Biotic Stress Management (ICAR-NIBSM), Raipur, showcased innovative models for converting waste into useful products and resources as part of the ongoing “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag – Swachh Bharat – Viksit Bharat” campaign here today.

The student-centric “Waste to Wealth” model demonstration highlighted the potential of waste segregation, recycling, reuse and value addition, while promoting the principles of a circular economy and responsible resource management. The exhibits featured innovative approaches to utilizing household waste, agricultural residues and biodegradable materials, demonstrating how scientific thinking, appropriate technology and community participation can help transform waste into valuable resources.

Addressing the gathering, ICAR-NIBSM Director Dr. P. K. Rai appreciated the enthusiasm and creativity of the students and emphasized that waste management should extend beyond cleanliness to include resource recovery and sustainable utilization. He said the “Waste to Wealth” concept underscores the need to view waste not merely as material to be discarded but as a potential resource. He encouraged the students to develop their ideas into practical, scalable and locally relevant solutions that can contribute to sustainable agriculture, environmental protection and a cleaner society.

The programme provided students with a platform to demonstrate their scientific creativity while creating awareness about sustainable lifestyles and responsible waste management. It also highlighted the role of individual participation, innovation and community action in advancing the objectives of a clean and developed India.

Dr. Pankaj Sharma, Dr. K. K. Mondal and Dr. Daisy Bansandrai, Joint Directors, along with Dr. S. K. Sharma and Dr. K. C. Sharma, Principal Scientists, were present on the occasion and interacted with the participating students. The programme was coordinated by Dr. Shravani Sanyal, who facilitated the student presentations and model demonstrations.

item.content:encoded:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, is undertaking Special Campaign 6 with a focused approach towards promoting cleanliness, improving office spaces, reducing pendency and strengthening record management across its offices and field formations.

The preparatory phase of the campaign (15.09.2026- 30.09.2026) is being carried out to identify the pending VIP references, public grievances, PG appeals which shall be resolved during the implementation phase of the campaign (2.10.2026 – 31.10.2026). During the campaign period, attention shall be given to cleanliness and upkeep of office premises, disposal of obsolete and redundant records, weeding out of files as per prescribed procedures, and resolution of pending references and grievances.

During the campaign special focus shall be on identifying the maximum number of e-waste and disposal of the same in conformity of the procedures prescribed under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

As part of the campaign, the Department of Telecommunications offices and its field units are identifying areas requiring focused attention and undertaking measures to improve the overall working environment. Emphasis is also being placed on systematic management of physical and electronic records, efficient utilization of office space and adoption of good practices for maintaining cleanliness on a sustained basis.

The campaign provides an opportunity for various formations of the Department to review existing processes, identify areas for improvement and institutionalise practices that contribute to a more efficient and responsive public administration.

The Department of Telecommunications remains committed to strengthening transparency, efficiency and citizen-centric service delivery through continuous improvement in its administrative processes.

item.title: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan Calls for Data-Driven Planning, Timely Procurement and Scientific Monitoring for Rabi Season 2026
item.description: Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today called upon States to complete preparations for the Rabi season through coordinated planning, scientific assessment and close field-level monitoring. Addressing the two-day National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026 in New Delhi, he said that amid climate change, erratic rainfall and water constraints, food security and higher farm incomes would require data-driven planning and…
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today called upon States to complete preparations for the Rabi season through coordinated planning, scientific assessment and close field-level monitoring. Addressing the two-day National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026 in New Delhi, he said that amid climate change, erratic rainfall and water constraints, food security and higher farm incomes would require data-driven planning and stronger Centre-State coordination rather than conventional approaches. The conference, organised by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Pusa, was attended by Union Ministers of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Atish Chandra, Director General, ICAR, Dr. M.L. Jat, senior officials from the Centre and States, Principal Secretaries and Directors of Agriculture, Vice-Chancellors of State Agricultural Universities, heads of ICAR institutes, and representatives of KVKs, ATMA and other stakeholders. In his inaugural address, Shri Chouhan said Rabi 2026 is an important phase in advancing the vision of a self-reliant and developed India. The conference, he said, is aimed at strengthening Centre-State coordination, raising agricultural production and productivity, promoting sustainability and preparing a coordinated, outcome-oriented strategy for enhancing farmers’ incomes.

 

 

Water Budget Must Guide Crop Planning

Shri Chouhan identified the water budget as one of the most important parameters for Rabi planning, asking every State and district to assess the water available for irrigation before finalising crop plans. Areas with limited water availability should prioritise less water-intensive crops such as pulses and oilseeds, while areas with assured irrigation can plan other crops accordingly. He said rainfall has remained below normal, although not to an extent that would severely affect water availability at the national level. However, water shortages in some States remain a concern. States must assess water availability and soil moisture in vulnerable areas and make arrangements for irrigation in advance. “There should be no situation where a crop requiring more water is sown and adequate water is subsequently unavailable, resulting in crop losses,” he said, stressing that preparations must begin immediately as the Rabi sowing window is approaching. Rainfed areas, in particular, require careful planning as the availability of soil moisture largely determines the crop choice and outcome.

 

 

Centre to Undertake Ground Assessment of Drought-Hit Areas

Expressing concern over drought conditions in Maharashtra and Karnataka, Shri Chouhan said nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected and the State has declared drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions. He said a Central team would undertake a ground assessment in Karnataka on October 3, while a Central team would also be sent to Maharashtra. Shri Chouhan said he would personally visit the affected States with his team and assured that, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Central Government stands firmly with farmers during the difficult situation. He also said that Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh would need crop plans based on water availability and soil moisture. Separate strategies should be prepared for rainfed and irrigated areas. Delayed sowing, he cautioned, can affect germination as well as productivity, making timely sowing and advance preparation essential.

 

Timely Availability of Quality Seed a Key Priority

Calling seed the most critical link in Rabi preparations, Shri Chouhan asked States to determine immediately which varieties are best suited to specific regions and agro-climatic conditions. He expressed concern that some States neither place seed demands in adequate time nor lift the required quantities, resulting in delays in distribution. In some cases, valuable seed varieties reach farmers after the sowing window and are subsequently sold at prices comparable to ordinary grain. He called for a complete roadmap covering seed demand, procurement, lifting and distribution. With senior ICAR scientists and experts present at the conference, States should jointly identify the most suitable varieties for different regions and conditions. He also called for an assessment of which varieties released by agricultural institutions have gained adoption and which have not, followed by targeted farmer awareness and extension efforts. This exercise, he said, should be completed scientifically during the two-day conference.

 

Push for Pulses and Oilseeds, Backed by Assured Markets

Shri Chouhan urged States to promote pulses and oilseeds, particularly in areas that remain fallow after paddy cultivation. These crops require relatively less water and are central to the national objective of achieving self-reliance in pulses and edible oils. He asked every State to finalise by September 29 its Rabi plan indicating the area to be brought under pulses and the crops to be promoted, including chana, masoor and mustard. At the same time, he stressed that production planning must be accompanied by assured market arrangements. Farmers should have confidence that their produce will be procured on time. “If there are areas where nothing is grown after paddy, this is an opportunity to encourage farmers to take up pulses,” he said, calling for immediate action by the States.

 

Procurement Planning Must Be in Place in Advance

Shri Chouhan said procurement arrangements must be planned alongside production so that farmers have confidence in the market. If State governments are unable to undertake procurement on time, Central nodal agencies NAFED and NCCF will undertake direct procurement from farmers. However, States must provide the necessary support, including timely facilitation of mandi-related requirements and other arrangements, to ensure that procurement is not delayed. He said the Centre has approved proposals on a large scale for procurement of pulses and oilseeds under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) and urged States to make full use of the mechanism. He also pointed out that some States submit procurement proposals but subsequently do not undertake the purchase. States, therefore, must prepare a complete procurement roadmap covering seed availability, distribution, production and market arrangements. Shri Chouhan also suggested that States consult farmers while preparing seed plans and make effective use of the network of Krishi Vigyan Kendras.

 

Balanced Fertiliser Use and Expansion of ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’

Shri Chouhan called for greater emphasis on balanced use of fertilisers, noting that if one bag is sufficient for a crop, there is no reason to apply two. Excessive application raises cultivation costs and can affect soil health. He urged States to extend the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, launched during the Kharif season, to Rabi as well. He cited the experience of southern States where fertilizer use has declined without affecting production, and called for these experiences to be shared and replicated. States should encourage farmers to adopt balanced fertiliser application with support from agricultural scientists, he said, adding that the Centre is ready to provide scientific assistance wherever required. Shri Chouhan also stressed the need for timely availability and distribution of fertilisers. Just as seed must reach farmers before sowing, fertilisers must also be available at the right time. He referred to pilot initiatives based on Farmer ID to strengthen distribution and ensure that fertilisers reach genuine farmers while preventing diversion and black marketing. He said the Centre is currently spending around ₹2 lakh crore on fertiliser subsidy, while farmers continue to receive fertilisers at subsidised prices, including urea at ₹266 per bag and DAP at ₹1,350 per bag. Ensuring balanced use of this subsidised input, he said, is also a responsibility of the States. The ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, he said, is not only about reducing excessive fertilizer use but also about protecting soil health, beneficial organisms and the productive capacity of farmland for future generations.

 

Natural Farming: Focus on Branding, Marketing and Certification

Shri Chouhan said farmers are increasingly prepared to adopt natural farming and registration has also progressed, but States must now focus on branding and marketing of natural farm products. Citing Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, he said these States have developed brands for natural farming products and established their market identity, helping them command better prices. States should also ensure that certification does not become a barrier for farmers and that natural products receive appropriate market recognition.

 

Farmer Credit Card and Farmer ID Need Greater Coverage

Shri Chouhan said around 9.54 crore farmer families have been covered under the PM-KISAN scheme, but the coverage of Kisan Credit Cards remains inadequate in several areas, particularly among small and marginal farmers. He asked States to identify areas where KCC coverage remains low and examine bottlenecks in loan sanctioning at the banking level so that farmers can access credit in time for agricultural investment. He clarified that the objective is not to push farmers towards borrowing, but to ensure that farmers who need timely capital for agriculture have access to institutional credit. On Farmer ID and AgriStack, Shri Chouhan congratulated States for the progress made and called for completing the remaining work at a faster pace, including land parcel-related work. A robust digital foundation, he said, will help resolve farmers’ problems and enable more efficient delivery of government schemes. He also stressed that tenant farmers and farmers cultivating land at different locations must not be left out of the Farmer ID framework and called for coordinated efforts to bring them into the system.

 

Weekly Monitoring of Crops, Disease and Market Prices

Shri Chouhan called for weekly monitoring in every State of crop conditions, sowing progress, germination, pest and disease attacks and market prices. He said real-time information would enable authorities to identify emerging problems and take corrective action without delay. The Agriculture Department and relevant agencies should maintain close surveillance of the situation on the ground. He said the Ministry also conducts weekly reviews at the national level covering crop conditions, market rates and disease outbreaks, enabling timely intervention wherever required.

On this occasion, Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Atish Chandra emphasised that, amid changing weather patterns, uneven rainfall and moisture-related challenges in rainfed areas, it is essential to promote agricultural diversification, sustainable farming  and research-based agricultural practices.

He further emphasised the need to take concrete steps to enhance farmers’ incomes and realise the goal of self-reliant agriculture through initiatives such as ‘Per Drop More Crop’, soil health management, modern agricultural infrastructure, robust market mechanisms and digital agriculture solutions, ensuring their reach to the last mile.

Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, Dr. Mangi Lal Jat in his address identified self-reliance, crop diversification, climate-resilient and sustainable agriculture, digital agriculture, and risk mitigation as key priorities for the upcoming Rabi campaign. He emphasised promoting oilseed and pulse production, with a special focus on crop diversification through targeted strategies in rice-fallow areas. He said that this would require the development of a comprehensive technological package covering everything from crop and suitable variety selection to quality seeds, mechanisation, biological solutions and seed treatment.

Dr. Jat informed that during the upcoming season, large-scale demonstrations of green ammonia are planned across 10,000 acres in 37 districts of six states.

 

Two-Day Conference to Shape Rabi Action Plan

The two-day National Agriculture Conference brings together senior officials from the Centre and States, ICAR scientists and the Agriculture Ministry’s teams. The first day will feature three rounds of thematic group discussions covering self-reliance and diversification; sustainability and climate-resilient agriculture; and digital agriculture, infrastructure, financing and risk management. On September 29, Shri Chouhan will hold detailed discussions with Agriculture Ministers of the States. The deliberations will cover the weather outlook for the Rabi season, fertiliser availability, the Digital Agriculture Mission, Farmer Registry, missions on pulses and edible oils, the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, marketing reforms, and planning through ATMA and KVKs, among other issues. The concluding session will consolidate the outcomes of the discussions and prepare a robust action plan for increasing Rabi production, empowering farmers and advancing the vision of a self-reliant and developed India. Agriculture Ministers from the States will also have an opportunity to share their experiences, priorities and suggestions on agricultural development and Rabi preparedness. Inputs from the States and the outcomes of the thematic discussions are expected to contribute to a coordinated and outcome-oriented strategy for Rabi Campaign 2026.

***

SS/MS/DK

item.title: Second JDC meeting between India and Ethiopia held in Addis Ababa
item.description: The second Joint Defence Cooperation meeting between India and Ethiopia was held today, September 28, 2026, in Addis Ababa. The two countries discussed areas of mutual interest in the fields of military training, military exercise, medical cooperation, peacekeeping and defence industries. Both sides agreed to expand and deepen defence cooperation activities through exchange of personnel from training institutes, exploring avenues for joint ventures in defence production, delegation visits and…
item.content:encoded:
The second Joint Defence Cooperation meeting between India and Ethiopia was held today, September 28, 2026, in Addis Ababa. The two countries discussed areas of mutual interest in the fields of military training, military exercise, medical cooperation, peacekeeping and defence industries. Both sides agreed to expand and deepen defence cooperation activities through exchange of personnel from training institutes, exploring avenues for joint ventures in defence production, delegation visits and experience sharing interactions.

This visit marks a pivotal step in India-Ethiopia defence relations and reinforces both side’s commitment to work together. It is also part of the institutional mechanism set up through signing of the Defence Cooperation MoU in February 2025 by the Defence Ministers of both the countries. The 1st JDC was held in New Delhi in October 2025. 

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Sanjay Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Defence and Major General Teshome Gemechu, Director General for Defence Foreign Relations & Military Cooperation, Ethiopia. The Indian delegation comprised officers from the Department of Defence and Air Headquarters. Shri Devesh Uttam, Ambassador of India to Ethiopia, also participated in the meeting. 

Ethiopia is an important defence partner of India and the partnership started way back in 1958. During the visit of Prime Minister of India to Ethiopia in December 2025, the bilateral relationship between the two countries was elevated to the level of ‘Strategic Partnership’. 

 ***

SR/NJ

item.title: Assam Launches Comprehensive Multi-Agency Strategy to Implement Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
item.description:
Key Features of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
SWM Rules, 2026 supersede the 2016 Rules and come into force from April 1, 2026 . Four-stream segregation at source—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste—is mandatory. Bulk Waste Generators must ensure environmentally sound collection, transportation and processing, with Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) introduced. Environmental compensation will…
item.content:encoded:
Key Features of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026

  • SWM Rules, 2026 supersede the 2016 Rules and come into force from April 1, 2026.
  • Four-stream segregation at source—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste—is mandatory.
  • Bulk Waste Generators must ensure environmentally sound collection, transportation and processing, with Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) introduced.
  • Environmental compensation will apply under the Polluter Pays principle for non-compliance.
  • A Centralised Online Portal will enable end-to-end monitoring, registration, reporting and audits.
  • MRFs (Material Recovery Facilities) are formally recognised for waste sorting.
  • Landfilling is restricted to non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste.
  • Legacy dumpsites will undergo time-bound biomining and bioremediation.
  • Special provisions cover hilly areas and islands, including tourist user fees and decentralised waste management.

 

The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 which came into effect from April 1, 2026. In this regard, a joint press conference was held by the Assam Pollution Control Board, Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) and Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin), Assam today.

 

Dr. Arup Kumar Mishra, Chairman of Pollution Control Board Assam, delivered an elaborate address on the statutory framework of the rules and the progress of its implementation in Assam.  Dr. Mishra emphasized that waste management is no longer the exclusive mandate of pollution control boards, but a collective operational duty for all local bodies, institutions and citizens. Highlighting recent directives from the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bhopal Municipal Corporation v. Dr. Subhash C. Pandey & Ors. (Civil Appeal No. 6174 of 2023), Dr. Mishra noted that the court's mandates now apply nationwide to all twenty-eight State Pollution Control Boards. He explained that while materials like plastics and discarded tires have historically created major environmental menaces, the 2026 framework strictly prioritizes avoiding landfills and treating organic biodegradable waste as a valuable resource.

 

Elaborating further on the operational mandates, Dr. Mishra highlighted the foundational requirement of four-stream waste segregation at source, requiring every household, establishment and institutional generator to store wet biodegradable waste, dry recyclables, securely wrapped sanitary waste and special care waste—such as CFL bulbs, expired medicines, batteries, tube lights, and syringes—in separate containers before handing them over to authorized collectors. He underlined strict duties imposed on Bulk Waste Generators meeting statutory thresholds, such as a floor area of 20,000 square meters or more, daily water consumption of 40,000 liters, or waste generation of 100 kgs/day. Such entities must mandatorily register on the CPCB centralized portal, process wet waste through on-site composting or biomethanation, fulfill Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR), and file annual returns by June 30 every year.

 

Warning against unscientific disposal, Dr. Mishra cited Rule 5(1)(f), which strictly prohibits throwing waste in municipal drains, dumping on roadsides, or open burning, while noting that wet waste and construction waste are barred from sanitary landfills, reserving landfill space strictly for inert and residual waste. Dr. Mishra also emphasized that existing legacy dumpsites must undergo biomining and bioremediation under time-bound action plans, citing Lakhimpur as a successful benchmark for scientific legacy waste disposal in Assam.

 

Presenting the operational roadmap for urban implementation, Shri Sabyasachi Kashyap, Mission Director of Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban), detailed the concrete steps taken across Assam's urban centers. He highlighted the promotion of a circular economy based on the principles of reduce, reuse and recycle, alongside the development of Compressed Bio-Gas plants in 5 major cities across Assam through public-private partnerships with Oil India Limited to convert waste into clean energy. Following the Supreme Court's directives, detailed infrastructure audits are being conducted across all 96 urban local bodies, while Town and Country Planning authorities are integrating mandatory SWM specifications and composite pits into building permissions for new constructions. Shri Kashyap further reported that 59 urban local bodies have mapped their legacy waste sites, 561 garbage-vulnerable points out of 651 have been transformed and dedicated cleanliness measures have been instituted across 198 identified high-footfall tourist and pilgrimage spots. He added that citizen grievances are being actively resolved through the integrated Swachhtam digital platform.

 

Complementing the urban strategy, senior officials from Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) highlighted the rural implementation framework designed to ensure comprehensive coverage across Assam's countryside. They outlined the systematic management of rural waste streams, focusing on the decentralization of biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste processing through community compost pits established across villages. To enforce structured governance at the grassroots level, a formal Gaon Panchayat Order will be promulgated in every village on October 2, establishing localized waste management rules. Furthermore, Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) is deploying digital tracking systems for waste collection vehicles to ensure transparent and reliable door-to-door collection across rural habitations.

item.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality along the Delhi-Agra Highway route and Agra-Delhi Railway route under Delhi LSA, during the month of July 2026
item.description:
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality along the Delhi to Agra via Yamuna Expressway passing through Dankaur, Jewar, Tappal, Surir, Javara, Baldeo, Khandauli, Kuberpur etc. and Agra to Delhi passing through Raja Ki Mandi Jn, Mathura Jn, Chata, Kosi Kalan, Palwal, Ballabhgarh, Faridabad etc. under Delhi LSA.
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted along the Delhi-Agra Highway route and Agra-Delhi Railway…
item.content:encoded:
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality along the Delhi to Agra via Yamuna Expressway passing through Dankaur, Jewar, Tappal, Surir, Javara, Baldeo, Khandauli, Kuberpur etc. and Agra to Delhi passing through Raja Ki Mandi Jn, Mathura Jn, Chata, Kosi Kalan, Palwal, Ballabhgarh, Faridabad etc. under Delhi LSA.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted along the Delhi-Agra Highway route and Agra-Delhi Railway route under Delhi LSA, during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc.  In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across Highway drive – 183.4 Km, Hotspot location – 01 and Railway Drive – 188 Km during 16th Jul 2026 to 17th Jul 2026 in Delhi LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test.

4. Drive test routes: The map provides overview of drive test routes indicating, hotspot test, highway and railway drive route as per the legends shown on the map.

Figure-1: Drive test routes

 

Key Parameters Assessed

(a) Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).

(b) Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).

(c) Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls.

(d) Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate.

The overall mobile network performance on Delhi to Agra via Yamuna Expressway Highway route (Delhi LSA) for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

    1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 180/13960 for Airtel, 4876/12619 for BSNL, 145/13268 for RJIL and 44/13327 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
    1. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 2/65 for Airtel, 16/68 for BSNL, 1/66 for RJIL and 0/66 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
    2. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 16/63 for Airtel, 2/57 for BSNL, 0/68 for RJIL and 18/68 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
    1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 135.33 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.10 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 213.68 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 46.48 Mbps for VIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 17.62 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 3.38 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 20.62 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 13.70 Mbps for VIL (5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-I.

The overall mobile network performance on Agra to Delhi Railway route (Delhi LSA) for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 326/11709 for Airtel, 5264/10895 for BSNL, 286/11697 for RJIL and 224/11728 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/60 for Airtel, 12/60 for BSNL, 3/63 for RJIL and 2/62 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  3. Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i) Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 44.23 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 9.99 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 82.68 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 47.48 Mbps for VIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 13.32 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 5.07 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 10.14 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 12.31 Mbps for VIL (5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

Locations of Dropped Calls can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-II.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: -

  1. Highway - The areas covered on the highway drive are Delhi to Agra via Yamuna Expressway passing through Dankaur, Jewar, Tappal, Surir, Javara, Baldeo, Khandauli, Kuberpur etc. under Delhi LSA.
  2. Hotspot - The hotspot location, capturing stationary user experience is The Food Street - Food Court - Yamuna Expressway - Vrindavan Cut.
  3. Railway - The areas covered on the Railway drive are Agra to Delhi passing through Raja Ki Mandi Jn, Mathura Jn, Chata, Kosi Kalan, Palwal, Ballabhgarh, Faridabad etc. under Delhi LSA.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in.  For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.ca@trai.gov or Regional Office of TRAI at Delhi RO can be contacted on telephone No. +91-11-20907772.

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Mumbai Branch Office, organised a Seminar-cum-Manak Manthan Programme on the Wide Circulation Draft for revision of IS 14772:2020 – Boxes and Enclosures for Electrical Accessories for Household and Similar Fixed Electrical Installations — General Requirements today at the BIS Mumbai Branch Office, Powai.
The programme was organised to apprise stakeholders of the key changes proposed in the…
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai, 28 September 2026

 

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Mumbai Branch Office, organised a Seminar-cum-Manak Manthan Programme on the Wide Circulation Draft for revision of IS 14772:2020 – Boxes and Enclosures for Electrical Accessories for Household and Similar Fixed Electrical Installations — General Requirements today at the BIS Mumbai Branch Office, Powai.

The programme was organised to apprise stakeholders of the key changes proposed in the draft revised standard and the applicable testing requirements, besides providing a platform for obtaining their views, suggestions and comments on the draft.

The programme commenced with a welcome address by Shri Anurag, Scientist-C, BIS, who welcomed the participating stakeholders and highlighted the importance of stakeholder participation in the standardisation process.

Technical sessions were conducted by Shri Rushikesh Ghodake, Scientist-C, Mumbai Branch Office, BIS, covering the key changes proposed in the draft revised standard and the testing requirements related to IS 14772:2020.

The technical sessions were followed by a Stakeholder Interaction and discussion, during which participants shared their views, suggestions and comments on the proposed revision and testing requirements.

The Seminar-cum-Manak Manthan Programme provided an important platform for interaction between BIS and stakeholders and facilitated meaningful discussions on the proposed revision of the Indian Standard. The inputs received from stakeholders will support the standardisation process and contribute towards the effective implementation of the revised requirements.

BIS continues to engage with industry and other stakeholders through such Manak Manthan programmes to promote wider participation in the development and revision of Indian Standards and to strengthen the quality and standardisation ecosystem.

 

* * *

item.title: Ministry of Mines Strengthens E-Waste Collection Drive under Special Campaign 6 to Promote Circular Economy and Critical Mineral Recovery
item.description:
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, is strengthening its E-Waste Collection Campaign under Special Campaign 6 with a focus on responsible e-waste management, resource recovery and promotion of a circular economy.
The campaign is being coordinated and implemented through the Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research Development and Design Centre (JNARDDC), Nagpur, designated as the Nodal Agency for the campaign, in association with the Material Recycling Association of India (MRAI).…
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, is strengthening its E-Waste Collection Campaign under Special Campaign 6 with a focus on responsible e-waste management, resource recovery and promotion of a circular economy.

The campaign is being coordinated and implemented through the Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research Development and Design Centre (JNARDDC), Nagpur, designated as the Nodal Agency for the campaign, in association with the Material Recycling Association of India (MRAI). Collection and awareness activities are being undertaken at multiple locations by offices and organisations associated with the Ministry of Mines.

More than 44 office locations across the country have been finalised for the campaign. In Maharashtra alone, more than 28 locations have been identified for e-waste collection. The widespread participation of offices and organisations reflects the coordinated efforts being undertaken to promote responsible collection and disposal of e-waste. The Ministry of Mines office in New Delhi is also one of the identified collection locations under the campaign. E-waste collected at various participating locations will be channelised for responsible recycling and resource recovery through appropriate mechanisms.

E-waste is not merely a waste stream but also a potential source of valuable secondary resources. With several electronic products containing minerals and metals that are important for modern technologies, recycling and recovery from e-waste can contribute to resource efficiency and strengthen the circular economy for critical minerals. Responsible recycling can help recover valuable materials, reduce pressure on primary mineral resources and promote sustainable utilisation of resources.

As part of the preparatory activities for effective implementation of the campaign, JNARDDC has conducted virtual coordination meetings with designated Nodal Officers of various offices and organisations under the Ministry of Mines, including the Geological Survey of India (GSI), Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM), National Institute of Rock Mechanics (NIRM), National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO), Hindustan Zinc Limited (HZL), Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Limited (MECL) and Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL).

The Ministry and its field offices and organisations are also undertaking awareness activities, campaigns and competitions to encourage greater participation among employees and stakeholders. These activities aim to promote awareness about responsible e-waste disposal and encourage reuse, repurposing and recycling of discarded electronic and electrical products, wherever feasible.

Through the campaign, the Ministry is promoting Jan Bhagidari in resource conservation and encouraging responsible practices for the collection, segregation, recycling and recovery of materials from e-waste. The initiative also reinforces the broader objectives of Special Campaign 6 towards sustainable resource management, environmental responsibility and a circular economy.

***

Prajith Kumar MV

item.content:encoded:
In a major relief to the commuters of Andhra Pradesh, the Indian Railways has approved a new tri-weekly train service between Machilipatnam and Kurnool City via Vijayawada of South Coast Railway, providing an additional rail connectivity option between coastal and central parts of Andhra Pradesh.

The approved Machilipatnam-Kurnool City Express will cover a distance of 499 km. It will depart from Machilipatnam at 16:55 and reach Kurnool City at 05:45 the next day. In the return direction, the Kurnool City-Machilipatnam Express will depart from Kurnool City at 09:30 and reach Machilipatnam at 21:35 the same day.

The Machilipatnam-Kurnool City Express will operate on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, while the Kurnool City-Machilipatnam Express will operate on Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday.

Major Stations to be Connected

The new train will have commercial stoppages at:

  • Gudivada
  • Vijayawada
  • Narasaraopet
  • Vinukonda
  • Donakonda
  • Markapur Road          
  • Cumbum
  • Giddalur
  • Diguvametta
  • Nandyal
  • Betamcherla
  • Dhone

The new service will provide an additional travel option for the passengers of Andhra Pradesh and strengthen connectivity between Machilipatnam, Vijayawada and Kurnool City, while also improving access to several towns and cities along the route.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/Dr. Nayan Solanki /Vikas Jha

item.title: Indian Railways Approves ₹122 Crore for 6 km Barbil–Bolanikhadan Doubling Project of South Eastern Railway
item.description:
Indian Railways has approved the 6 km Barbil-Bolanikhadan Doubling Project of South Eastern Railway at a completion cost of ₹122 crore, strengthening rail infrastructure on an important mineral movement corridor.
Doubling to Support Growing Freight Traffic
The project will facilitate additional freight traffic of 8.9 MTPA on this stretch after commissioning of the project. The doubling will also help reduce delays to freight trains.
The Barbil-Bolanikhadan section…
item.content:encoded:
Indian Railways has approved the 6 km Barbil-Bolanikhadan Doubling Project of South Eastern Railway at a completion cost of ₹122 crore, strengthening rail infrastructure on an important mineral movement corridor.

Doubling to Support Growing Freight Traffic

The project will facilitate additional freight traffic of 8.9 MTPA on this stretch after commissioning of the project. The doubling will also help reduce delays to freight trains.

The Barbil-Bolanikhadan section has been identified under the “Energy, Mineral and Cement Corridor” of Indian Railways. The existing section is a single-line section and currently carries about 9 MTPA, comprising about 6 loaded rakes per day of originating iron ore traffic. The traffic is entirely for high-grade ore and pellets moving from SAIL’s Bolani mines and private sidings (Rungta, Khatau Narbheram) to major steel plants and ports.

Meeting Future Freight Requirements

Doubling this 6 km stretch, ahead of the full realisation of SAIL’s mine expansion and port/plant capacity additions, will help to prevent the capacity constraints in the designated mineral corridor.

The approved work will support the growing freight requirements, improve rail connectivity for movement of iron ore to steel plants and ports, and strengthen rail capacity as mining, industrial and port activities expand in the region. It will also strengthen the Energy, Mineral and Cement Corridor and support smoother movement of freight on this important route.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/Dr. Nayan Solanki /Vanshita Jaiswal

item.description:

The approved project will extend Kavach 4.0 coverage across the identified balance sections of Varanasi Division, strengthening the safety infrastructure available for train operations.
Strengthening Railway Safety…
item.content:encoded:
In a significant step towards strengthening railway safety through indigenous technology, Indian Railways has approved the provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 614.75 Route Kilometres of Varanasi (BSB) Division of North Eastern Railway at a total cost of ₹223 crore.

The approved project will extend Kavach 4.0 coverage across the identified balance sections of Varanasi Division, strengthening the safety infrastructure available for train operations.

Strengthening Railway Safety with Indigenous Kavach Technology

Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system designed to enhance operational safety. It helps prevent Signal Passing at Danger (SPAD), automatically applies brakes when required and supports safer train movement by monitoring train operations.

The approved work will further strengthen train protection infrastructure across the balance sections of Varanasi Division. The initiative will contribute to safer and more reliable train operations and support Indian Railways’ ongoing efforts to expand the deployment of indigenous Kavach technology across its network.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/Dr. Nayan Solanki /Vanshita Jaiswal

The milestone reflects growing acceptance of the Annual Pass among private vehicle owners for providing a seamless and economical travel option on the National Highways and Expressways.
Applicable on about 1,150 fee plazas on National Highways and National Expressways, the Annual Pass eliminates the…
item.content:encoded:
Reflecting strong adoption among National Highway users, the ‘FASTag Annual Pass’ has crossed the significant milestone of one crore passes issued after its launch on 15th August 2025. The milestone reflects growing acceptance of the Annual Pass among private vehicle owners for providing a seamless and economical travel option on the National Highways and Expressways.

Applicable on about 1,150 fee plazas on National Highways and National Expressways, the Annual Pass eliminates the need to frequently recharge FASTag through one-time fee payment of Rs. 3,075 for one year validity or 200 toll plaza crossings. The pass is applicable for all non-commercial vehicles with a valid FASTag. The annual pass gets activated on the existing FASTag linked to the vehicle after payment of one-time fee payment through Rajmargyatra App.

The growing uptake of the FASTag Annual Pass reinforces its effectiveness in promoting seamless and economical travel on National Highways across the country.

 

***

GDH/DS
